contenido: INTRODUCTION CYRIL OF JERUSALEM AND HIS CATECHESES Adult catechesis in the great century of patristics The golden century of patristics is the period between the councils of Nicaea and Chalcedon (325-451). It is, of course, the period in which the literary activity of the Fathers of the Church reaches the highest levels. In part, this notable writing activity responds to theological discussions and the interest in combating what the Church was classifying as heresies. Also in the 4th century, the first two ecumenical councils were held, that of Nicea, in the year 325, and the First of Constantinople, in 381. The council of Nicea established in its Creed the identity of nature (hamousia) of the Son with the Father: the Son is homoousios with the Father, "of the same nature" as the Father, with the characteristics that the Nicene Creed also declares. In the fight against Arianism, the figure of Athanasius, bishop of Alexandria, stands out above all. Arius had maintained a similarity, but not identity of nature between the Son and the Father. For its part, the First Council of Constantinople (c. 381), although it is in line with Nicaea, further develops the latter's creed, especially in relation to the Holy Spirit, the Church, baptism, the resurrection of the dead and eternal life. Due to the continuity and relationship between both councils, the Creed or Symbol approved by the First Council of Constantinople is usually called Nicene-Constantinopolitan and has appeared since then in the Roman liturgy, the most widespread in the entire Church. On the other hand, in the 4th century the Church continued to practice adult baptism, although the baptism of children born to Christian parents became more and more frequent. Although the 3rd century is the time in which the catechumenate of adults reached its greatest height, it is in the 4th century when there is a greater abundance of literary testimonies of this classic type of catechization. In reality, along with an incipient decline in pastoral activity, perhaps because we are no longer in the glorious and heroic times of persecution, progress has been made in the study and theological exposition of Christianity. The 4th and 5th centuries will also be, both in the East and in the West, although with different characteristics, the time of the greatest theological disputes. Nicaea and Constantinople developed their confessions of faith, also called symbols.

But along with the symbols of these councils, many others11 were also created, before or after them. These creeds were like a "rule of faith", in such a way that those who professed them could be considered Christians in the proper way: they professed a "right opinion" or orthodoxy. Creeds have always been hallmarks of Christian communities. The creeds had extraordinary importance and that is why the Church has preserved them. As they were very tight formulations, they expressed with typically Greek terminological precision, especially what refers to the ontology of God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Other statements were added to these, which were also part of the deposit

Cf. S. SABUGAL, Credo. The faith of the Church. The symbol of faith: History and interpretation. Zamora (Ediciones Monte Casino), 1986 J.N.D. KELLY, Primitive Christian creeds, Salamanca, Trinitarian Secretariat, 1980.

of faith, about the Church, baptism and the second coming of Christ. Some brief explanations can be given of the importance of the statements of the symbols of faith. If, for example—to mention the fundamentals of Nicaea's statements—it were affirmed that Christ is not of the same nature or substance as the Father (the Latins, with complete accuracy, immediately translated "consubstantial with the Father"), a state of subordination and dependence as creaturely of the Son to the Father would be admitted, which would make Jesus Christ not in reality the Son of God, savior and redeemer of man, but at most an instrument that God uses or perhaps as a kind of God. second-rate, all of which would lead to the absurdity of destroying Christianity. On the other hand, and for similar reasons, it was necessary to immediately add a third article on the Holy Spirit to the Creed. But it is not about explaining all the details now. It is necessary to say that, in the whole of the catechumenate and the catechesis leading to baptism, the praxis of the Church led it to deliver, traditio, the Creed, traditio Symboli, to those who asked for baptism. In this delivery of the Creed, the Symbol (or content, which is what the word originally means) of faith was entrusted to the catechumen, when baptism was almost time. This delivery of the Church's faith took place during Lent and ended with the return, redditio Symboli, which ended a few days before Easter with the public profession of the Christian faith. At Easter, the catechumens who had professed their faith through the Symbol received baptism and the anointing of the Holy Spirit (confirmation). Logically, in that same celebration they were fully incorporated into the Eucharist, beyond listening to the proclaimed word of Scripture (what was later called "Mass of the catechumens" and to which they could already attend before baptism). With the baptism received at Easter, the door was opened to the newly baptized, neophytes, to participate in the entire liturgy. The entire period framed by the traditio and the redditio Symboli was occupied by an intense stage of catechization. In the catechesis of Saint Cyril of Jerusalem, the first of them,
Procatechesis, and the following eighteen, are catechesis on the Creed and they go through each
one of his articles. Five mystogogic catechisms are then added, which will be discussed later, delivered before the newly baptized during the week of Easter.

Cyril of Jerusalem Cyril of Jerusalem, declared a doctor of the Church in 1882, was bishop of the city for a long period. He was born around the year 314 in Jerusalem or its surroundings. He was a man of broad culture, as evidenced by his use of language, philosophy and his knowledge—in the molds of the time—of natural sciences. He must have been very well gifted for oratory. His best-known work is precisely these Catechisms, delivered in Jerusalem in the year 347 or 348. Between these dates and the year 351 his ordination as bishop of Jerusalem must be placed, so it is not known with certainty whether he gave the catechisms while he was already a bishop or just a priest. But from some time around the year 350 and until his death, on March 18, 387, he occupied the episcopal see of Jerusalem. However, those almost forty years were often

agitated in the life and ministry of Cyril. In fact, several complex circumstances arose: he received episcopal ordination from the Arian bishop of Caesarea, Acucio, which aroused suspicion of Arianism in his person for some. The text of the Catechesis, as can be seen, nullifies these suspicions, but there were those who felt strongly about them because Cyril does not mention Arius in the catechesis nor does he use the famous adjective homoousios so characteristic of Nicaea. Conflicts, on the other hand, broke out between the aforementioned Acacius and Cyril. A synod of Jerusalem deposed him in 357. Rehabilitated in 359, he was exiled a second time, by the work of Acacius, in 360. A couple of years later he was able to return again to Jerusalem, where he resumed his tasks until in 367 he was sent by Emperor Valens into exile for the third time. Only eleven years later, in 379, under Emperor Theodosius, he was able to return again to Jerusalem, where he carried out the ministry until his death in 387. In 381 he had participated in the First Council of Constantinople. The Catechesis We are not before a creative theologian, but before a catechist, an excellent expositor and a disseminator of the dogmatic conscience of the Church in the era of catechumenal catechesis. It is, in the first place, catechesis on the Creed, using the one that seems to have been in use in Jerusalem, which is also reproduced after catechesis V. It is, in general, the order of the statements of the Symbol that indicates the theme of the catechesis. Procatechesis and
catechesis I-III put the listeners before the situation in which they find themselves, making available

way already very close to the reception of baptism and as those who will first have to make public profession of their faith in God the Father, Son and Holy Spirit. An overview of Christian beliefs is given, on the other hand, by Catechesis IV, on the "ten dogmas." In it the virginal conception of Christ, his resurrection, the coming judgment, what refers to body and soul and the resurrection of the dead, in addition to the value of the Holy Scripture, complete what in the
Catechesis VI-XVII will be the Christian image of the God in whom we believe. Two catechesis, XVI and

XVII, they are dedicated to the Holy Spirit. The XVIII exposes the resurrection of the dead and eternal life. Cyril's Catechesis is a very precise indicator of the development achieved in the middle of the 4th century by ecclesiastical dogmatic consciousness. At that time the Church perfectly articulated, already in Nicea as it will also do in more detail in I Constantinople, the statements of a faith that with the development of theology has known how to objectify itself and has known how to account for why the events of salvation, based on Scripture and preaching, have been and are in a certain way. On the other hand, the last five catechesis are mystagogic, that is, they lead to the understanding of the "mysteries" (sacraments) that the newborns to the new life, "neophytes", have just experienced effectively when they receive them in the celebration of Easter. The five mystagogic catechesis are dedicated to Baptism, Confirmation and Eucharist, which make up Christian initiation. These catechesis constitute a very valuable liturgical testimony. As a whole, then, this work by Cyril constitutes one of the most important catechetical documents of the patristic era. Given the importance that the development of the different Creeds had, but that they were essentially identical, the general structure of the Catechesis that will be found here is very logical. On the other hand, the detail with which Scripture is cited is surprising. The excellent connection of the plot development, although it sometimes leads Cirilo to certain digressions that may not be necessary, allows us to perceive an extraordinary agility in the management of the

Writing. Perhaps a reader who knows Paul's theology and its central axes in depth: Christocentrism, Christian anthropology, sin and grace, faith and justification, etc., will miss a greater influence of the Apostle in Cyril's expositions. But Cyril is rather a witness of how far the dogmatic conscience of the Church had reached, in which it had been necessary to consume too much energy in Christological and Trinitarian disputes. Finally, some observations about this edition. It goes without saying that the epigraphs do not belong to the text of the Catechesis. On the other hand, many explanatory notes have been introduced, of uneven length but in any case very frequent. Sometimes they are philological in nature, but more often they refer to content. The translation work has been done on the Latin version, published together with the Greek original in volume 33 of Migne's Patrologia graeca, (often cited: PG 33, plus the indication of the corresponding column). An effort has been made, however, to keep the Greek text in mind when the Latin version, otherwise excellent, lost some nuance. The observations frequently found in the Migne on the state of texts and codices have also been taken into account. It should be taken into account that the original was properly transmitted orally. The stenographers, as is common in pieces of classical oratory, copied as best they could what was being said in a very lively, direct and, at times, somewhat colloquial style. As for the biblical quotations, an attempt has been made to follow the text of the Spanish version of the Jerusalem Bible. The notes from that same Bible have also often been very useful, and sometimes have even been quoted literally. Sometimes, however, especially in passages from the Old Testament, Cyril's recourse to the Greek version of the LXX made it inevitable to translate according to that version. However, in many cases the texts translated by the Jerusalem Bible from the Hebrew original have been maintained. For the references of acronyms, chapters and verses, the data, generally very precise, contained in the edition of the Graeca Patrology have been very useful.
CATECHESIS OF OUR FATHER SAINT CYRIL, ARCHBISHOP OF JERUSALEM
Procatechesis, or word prior to the catechesis, of our holy Father Cyril, archbishop of

1. They already exhale, illuminating2, the smell of happiness. They are now looking for higher quality flowers to weave the celestial crowns. They already give off the fragrance of the Holy Spirit. They are already in the lobby of the royal palace: I hope they are also introduced by the King himself! The flowers have already sprouted from the trees: let us hope that the ripe fruit will also bear. Previously they have given the name3, now they are called to the militia. Have the lamps in your hands to go out to look for your wife: you have the desire for the celestial city, the good purpose and the logical hope. For he is true who said: "For those who love God, everything contributes to good." For God is generous in doing good and, for the rest, awaits the sincere will of each one; That is why the Apostle adds: "To those who have been called according to his plan." When there is a sincere purpose, it causes you to be called; But if you only have your body ready, but you are absent with your mind, you will waste time. Do not go to baptism just out of curiosity

2. Simon Magus also approached baptism on one occasion, but he did not feel enlightened: and he actually bathed his body in water, but he did not let the Spirit illuminate his heart; the body went down into the pool; but the soul was not buried with Christ nor was it resurrected together with him. I put this case as an example so that you don't fall. For all this happened to them in image5 and has been written for the teaching of those who live to this day. Let none of you become intrigued with the things of grace so that no germ of bitterness troubles you. Let none of you come in saying: let's see what the faithful do; once inside, I'll see what they do. Do you think you will see without you being seen? Or do you think that you will find out what is done there, but that God will not search your heart? Enter the banquet with the appropriate dress. The translation "illuminandos" is preferred, those who are to be illuminated, because it responds to the meaning of the Greek expression, is a literal translation of the Latin version and actually refers to those who, with baptism at the next Easter, would receive the maximum illumination of their lives. The expression is common among the Fathers to designate those who would receive baptism in a few weeks (for example, the following Easter). Reference to the inscription of the name, a prerequisite for the beginning of Lenten catechesis on the creed. Cf Rom 8,28. 1 Cor 10:6.

3. It is said in the gospels that someone went to browse at a wedding, but entered wearing an inappropriate dress, settled down and ate. The husband had allowed it. But seeing everyone's white clothes, the appropriate thing would have been to dress the same way. And he really ate the same foods as the others, but he differed in his dress and intention. So the husband, although magnanimous, was a man of judgment. And as he walked around looking at each of the diners, he focused his attention not on the fact that they were eating but on the way they behaved. Seeing a stranger dressed in a suit that was not for a party, he said to him: "Friend, how did you get in here?"6 In what dress? With what conscience? It may be that the doorman has not prohibited it due to the owner's generosity. Also ignore the fact that you did not know what dress you had to wear to the banquet. But, once inside, you see the resplendent dresses of the diners. Shouldn't you have learned from your own observations? Shouldn't you have entered in the correct way to be able to exit properly? But you came in unexpectedly and you were also expelled unexpectedly. (The owner) orders his servants: "Tie his feet," because he entered recklessly with them; "bind his hands," with which he did not know how to put on a resplendent garment, and "throw him into the outer darkness" 7, for he is unworthy of the wedding banquet. You see what happened to that man; So look carefully at your things. Stand straight

4. In fact we are ministers of Christ and we welcome anyone and, acting as a doorkeeper, we clear the entrance. It may be that you enter with a sinner's soul stained in mud. You entered, you were admitted, your name was inscribed. Do you realize the venerable aspect of the Church? Do you see the order and discipline? Do you see the reading of the canonical Scriptures, the constant memory of the people indicated in the ecclesiastical catalogues, the order and formality in teaching. They should teach you both respect for the place and contemplation of what you see. Better if you leave now in a timely manner, then enter at a much more opportune time. If you now entered with the inner garment of greed, you must enter again with another; Take off and do not cover yourself with the dress you wore. Strip yourself, I beg you, of debauchery and filth and cover yourself with the resplendent stole of modesty. I warn you before the husband of souls, Jesus, enters and examines the garments. You have time at your disposal: you are granted the penance of forty days; You have a great opportunity to undress and wash, and to dress again and enter. But if you remain in the evil purpose of your soul, the fault will not be with the one who is warning you: do not expect to receive grace. The water will welcome you, but the spirit will not welcome you. Whoever becomes aware of his own wound will receive a balm; If anyone is down, he will get up. Let no one among you be like the aforementioned Simón, let there be no simulation, nor interest in inopportune inquiries. The Church itself will purify your intention

5. It is possible that you are also guided by another pretext. Sometimes it happens that a man comes here to win the love of a woman or something similar: and the same can also be said in reverse. Likewise, perhaps it is the servant who wanted to please his master, or a friend his friend. But I accept the attraction of this bait and welcome you, even if you come with a crooked intention, Mt 8:28. Mt 22,13. with the good hope that you will be saved. Maybe you didn't know where you were coming from or what the network was that caught you. You fell into the nets of the Church: you will be caught alive; don't run away; It is Jesus who has set the hook for you, and not to destine you to death, but to, by giving you over to it, recover you alive: for it is necessary that you die and rise again, if what the Apostle said is true: "Dead to sin, but alive to justice"8. Die to sins and live to righteousness; do it from today.

6. Consider with what dignity Jesus gives you. They called you catechumen because the echo of an external bell resounded in you: you heard in hope, but you did not see9, you heard the mysteries, but without understanding them; You heard the Scriptures, although without understanding their depth. It is no longer necessary to make anything resonate in your ears, since only the sound exists inside you: since the Spirit that dwells in you 10 makes your heart a divine dwelling. When you hear what is written about the mysteries, you will understand what you did not know. And don't think that what you will receive is of little value. Well, since you are a miserable man, it will be God who will give you a name. Listen to Paul when he says: “God is faithful”11. Listen to the other passage of Scripture: “God faithful and just”12. Seeing this in advance, the psalmist said on behalf of God and foreseeing that men would receive a name from God: "I said: they are all gods and sons of the Most High." 13. But beware of bearing a distinguished name for a crooked purpose. You have entered the fight, endure the effort of the race; You don't have another similar opportunity14. If what was proposed to you was the wedding date, wouldn't you get busy preparing the banquet, leaving other things behind? Will you be able to take care of the physical, forgetting about the spiritual, just when you are preparing your soul to consecrate it to the heavenly husband? There is only one baptism

7. It is not possible to receive baptism15 a second or third time, because if that were the case, one could say: what went wrong once, I will fix it another time. Well, if once it went wrong, things cannot be fixed16, because "the Lord is one, faith is one, and baptism is one"17. Only heretics are baptized again when in reality this baptism has not been given. Cl Rom 6,11,14, cf. 1 Pe 2,24. The Greek original is more expressive, but the translation must necessarily betray the exact meaning. The Greek "catechumen" comes from the Greek "echos", echo. In fact, semantically, a catechumen is one in whom an echo is made to resonate. Catechesis, an abstract noun, is the action of making something resonate within the listener. The resonance here is that of the announcement of the message of salvation in Jesus Christ. Cf. Rom 8,9.11; I Cor 1,9. Cf I Cor 1,10. Dt 32,4. Salt 82.6. Kairos is translated as "opportunity"; the opportune time of salvation (Cf. 2 Cor 6,2). With this, the catechetical period that is about to begin is presented as an extraordinary possibility of salvation for the catechumen. Baptism, Greek here loutron, washing. With all this the fundamental statement is that baptism cannot be repeated. Eph 4,5 Good disposition I encourage you

8. But God asks of us something other than a good disposition of mind. Do not say: How will my sins be forgiven? I answer you: with what you want and believe. What is simpler than this? But if your lips express the desire, but your heart does not express it, know that he who can judge is knowledgeable of the hearts. Abandon from this day all evil; that you do not utter thick words with your tongue; May your eye no longer sin nor your thoughts wander between vain realities. Perseverance in catechesis

9. Let your feet be ready for catechesis. Receive exorcisms with good spirit: when being insufflated or exorcised, may this serve for your salvation. He thinks that gold is something infected and adulterated, mixed with various materials such as copper, iron and lead18. What we desire is gold alone, but without fire it cannot be purged of the foreign elements mixed with it: thus, the soul cannot be purified without exorcisms, which are of divine origin and deduced from the Scriptures. Your face was covered with a veil so that your mind could be more attentive and so that your scattered gaze would not also cause your heart to be distracted. But even if the eyes are veiled, nothing prevents the ears from receiving the help of salvation. For as those who expurgate gold by blowing into the fire with fine instruments melt the gold that is inside the crucible, and by fanning the flame they achieve better results19, so the exorcised expel their fear thanks to the divine Spirit and revive their soul housed in their body as in a crucible. In this way the hostile devil flees, but salvation is established and the hope of eternal life remains. The soul, freed from sin, obtains salvation. Let us therefore remain in hope, brothers; Let us strive and wait so that the God of all things, seeing the purpose of our mind, cleanses us from sins, allows us to hope for the best in our things, and grants us a healthy penance. God is the one who has called and you are the one who has been called. Persevere in catechesis

10. Although our later oratory will be more extensive, may your spirit never falter. For you will receive weapons against enemy powers; You will receive weapons against the heretics, the Jews, the Samaritans and the Gentiles. You have multiple enemies: receive multiple darts, because you will have to fight against many; You have to learn how to defeat the Greek, how to fight against the heretic, against the Jew and against the Samaritan20. The weapons are prepared, and the sword of the Spirit is fully ready21. The hands must fight valiantly to fight the battle of the Lord, to defeat the powers that oppose, so that you remain undefeated from all the schemes of the heretics. The exposition will be progressive Cf. Ez 22,18. Cf catechesis 16, n. 18; cf infra, no. 15. The four classes of enemies represent different ways of religiously or ideologically opposing the truth of the Gospel. Cf Mt 26, 41; Eph 6,17.

11. But I give you some advice. Learn what is said and keep it forever. Do not think that these are the usual homilies: they are quality and worthy of faith. But if there is something in them on a given day that is not said, we will learn it the next day. But the doctrine, neatly expounded, concerning the baptism of regeneration,22 when will it be transmitted again if it is neglected today? Think it's time to plant trees; If we do not dig and penetrate to the bottom, when will it be possible to plant again correctly what has already been planted wrong on one occasion? Think that catechesis is a building; If we do not dig and lay the foundation, and if the structure of the house is not properly and properly secured, so that nothing is loose or cut and the building becomes ruins, all the work done will be useless. It is advisable to place one stone in an orderly manner next to another and place one angle in front of another; By removing the projections, a proportionate building will emerge. In the same way, we bring you here like the stones of knowledge: we will have to hear what refers to the living God; what refers to the trial; It is necessary to hear about Christ and about the resurrection. Many other things are also said in an orderly manner that are now mentioned dispersedly, but which will be explained in their proper place. You must understand these things unitarily, relating previous and subsequent statements in memory. Otherwise, the architect will build well, but the building will be fragile and ready to fall. Keep the secret of what you hear

12. When a catechesis is given, if a catechumen asks you what the doctors said, do not say anything to the outside world24. It is the mystery and hope of the future life that we transmit to you. Keep the secret from the one who gives you his gifts. Let no one ever tell you: what harm does this cause you if I also have to learn it? Because the sick also usually ask for wine; But if it is given when it should not, it causes delirium, which causes a double evil: the patient dies and the doctor is criticized. The same thing happens to the catechumen who hears from someone who has faith in the mysteries: the catechumen suffers from delirium (because not knowing what he has heard, he denigrates him by making him an object of ridicule), but at the same time the faithful is condemned as a traitor. You are already on the divide; Try not to speak recklessly. It is not that what is said is unworthy of being told, but that certain things should not be entrusted to some. You were also a catechumen, and I did not tell you what I said here; When you know from your experience the sublimity of what is taught, then you will clearly understand that the catechumens should not hear all that yet. Pay attention to all the details

13. All those who have been registered have been conceived as sons and daughters of the same mother. When you enter shortly before the time of the exorcisms, each of you should speak regarding peri toû loutroû tês palingenesías, liter. "about the washing of regeneration" or, perhaps even better, about the "new birth" or the "new being brought forth." For the first time in catechesis it is stated that baptism is a washing in which man is born again. In the customary homilies mentioned above. Cf cat. 5,12 and cat. 6.29. Cirilo considers that the situation of the catechumen and the illuminand is very different. This is, according to what was said in the introduction, a different stage, since in the period from the beginning of Lent to the Easter season, these catechisms were pronounced, which attempt to provide an experience (and knowledge) of the most intimate mysteries of faith. The imposition of not telling anything outside does nothing more than put the discipline of the arcane into practice. Deep down it is admitted that even those who are beginning to be catechized for Christian initiation are not capable of vitally assimilating at this moment what will be the content of the catechesis of this last Lent and the Easter season. to piety. And see if any of you are missing. When you are invited to a banquet, will you not wait for him who is invited along with you? And if you have a brother, won't you seek what is good for that brother? Do not then investigate what does not concern you, nor be interested in what happens in the city or in the town, nor in what the emperor, the bishop or the priest does. Look up: this is what your “kairós” asks for25. Enough already; know that I am God!26. If you see some faithful idle and free of worries, it is because they feel safe, they are aware of what they have received and they have grace with them. You are still in doubt as to whether or not you will be admitted; do not imitate the carefree27, for you must not abandon fear.

14. When the exorcism is performed, while those who are to receive it approach, let the men be together with the men and the women with the women. With this I refer to Noah's ark, in which were Noah and his sons, his wife and his sons' wives 28. And although the ark was one, with its door closed, everything was arranged with decency. Likewise, even if the church is closed and you are all inside, everything is separated so that men are with men and women with women, so that what is meant to be help for salvation does not become an occasion for perdition. For although it is beautiful to sit next to each other, the danger of confusion must be far away. And then, the men sitting down, have some useful book in their hands. Let one read and the other listen. If you don't have a book, one pray and the other talk something useful. The group of virgins is also grouped together, who must chant or read, but in silence: their lips must speak, but their voices must not reach other people's ears. I do not tolerate that the woman speaks in the assembly29, and the married woman also acts in a similar way: that she prays and moves her lips, but her voice is not heard, imitating what Samuel said that salvation from a benevolent God springs from the barren soul30, since that is what Samuel is referring to. Maintain interest

15. I will see the interest of every man and the piety of every woman. Let the mind be inflamed with piety, since each soul will be molded. Humble and crush the hardness of infidelity, let the superfluous slag of the iron be removed, leaving only what is pure: let the rust be lost so that the noble material appears. May God show you on some occasion that night and the darkness turned into light of which it is said: "Not even the darkness itself is dark for you, and the night is bright as the day"31. The door to paradise will then be opened to each of you32. Then they will enjoy the waters full of fragrance and bringing them Christ. May they then perceive the call of Christ and the force of divine realities33. Now look upward with the open eyes of your mind: contemplate in your minds the choruses of the Cf. above, note 13, Cf. also on kairos the vocabularies and manuals of biblical theology. Psalm 26:11. Cyril is fully aware that a lot is at stake for whoever will stop being a catechumen and join the group of those who have faith. Once one is “faithful” (has faith), one can rest in that faith. But he who has not received baptism should not live in carelessness. The Migne edition PG 33,354, note 9, comments: «Cyril does not blame the faithful because they are without worries. It only says that, once they have received baptism, they are now free from the concern that must exist in the not yet baptized about their future. Cf Gen 7,9. Cf 1 Tim 2,12; 1 Cor 14:34. Reference to the episode of Anna's supplication, I Sam I, 10 ff. Ps 139:12. Vid., cat. 19, no. 9. Vid. cat. 3, nos. 3 and 13. angels, to the Father lord of all things on his throne, to the only begotten Son seated with him at his right hand and to the Spirit present with them, and to the thrones and dominions as servants. And imagine that each of you has already achieved salvation. Your ears will have heard it: desire to hear that beautiful voice with which the angels will acclaim you when you receive salvation: "Blessed is he whose guilt is forgiven, and his sin is covered!"34. They will then enter as stars of the Church resplendent in their bodies and souls. Exhortation to the process you are going to enter

16. And the baptism of which we speak is truly something great: ransom of captives, forgiveness of sins, death of sin, new birth of the soul, luminous clothing, holy indelible seal35, vehicle to heaven, delights of paradise, means to the kingdom, gift of adoption as children. For the rest, keep in mind that the dragon watches those who pass by along the road: make sure it doesn't bite you for your infidelity; He sees the many who are saved and looks for someone to devour36. You approach the Father of spirits37, but it is necessary to go through that dragon. How will you avoid him? Shod your feet with zeal for the gospel of peace 38, so that even if the tooth sinks into you, it does not hurt you: have faith within you and a firm hope. Put your shoes on well so that you can enter to the Lord even if the access is occupied by the enemy39. Prepare your heart to receive the teaching and to participate in the holy mysteries. Pray frequently so that God gifts you with the celestial and immortal mysteries, and do not leave him day or night. And when sleep leaves your eyes, let your mind be occupied with prayer. If you see that some clumsy thought assaults your soul, may the idea of ​​judgment help you, which will remind you of salvation; Keep your mind busy learning so that it forgets depraved thoughts. If you see someone saying to you: Will you go in there to go down to the water? Doesn't the new city have bathrooms?40, know that the sea dragon plots these things against you41; Do not listen to the voices of those who salute you. Cf Ps 65, 3b-4: «Until you all flesh comes with its guilty works; "The weight of our rebellions overcomes us, and you erase them." By "seal" is translated the Greek expression sfragis, from which theologians will later deduce the doctrine of sacramental "character", which expresses, applied to baptism and with the nuances specific to this sacrament, that whoever is baptized is the property of the one who has sealed him, Jesus Christ. With "character" a guarantee of the salvation received in baptism is also expressed. Cf in this regard, in addition to the treatises on the sacraments of baptism, confirmation and orders, also the biblical dictionaries: art. Seal, in X. LEON-DUFOUR, Vocabulary of biblical theology, Barcelona, ​​ed. revised, 1973, 841-842. Cf. 1 Pe 5,8.

Hebrews 12:9 contrasts, in the entire verse, the situation prior to the encounter with Jesus Christ, which marked the beginning of the catechumenate, and the new reality that one is about to enter upon completing Christian initiation: «Moreover, we had our fathers according to the flesh, who corrected us, and we respected them. Wouldn't we rather submit to the Father of spirits to live? Cf Num 27,16; 2 Mac 3:24 speaks of God as "the Sovereign of Spirits and of all Power." Cf. Eph 6,15 (and its context). Cf. cat. 1, no. 5. It refers to public baths then recently built in the city of Jerusalem. In any case, the question is intended as a possible mockery of the candidate for baptism on the part of those who thought that, since baptism was nothing superior to human baths, the city had better facilities than the baptismal pools of the churches. The expression implies baptism of immersion. Without going into further details now, cf, on "the sea dragon", the allusions of Is 27,1, Jb 3,8, Apoc 12,3 (where the "great red Dragon" is a reference to Satan). Cf. also Gen 3:15, in the context of the first announcement of the Gospel. That is why Cyril's statement here carries with it the announcement of a God who is ultimately victorious over the devil as man's personal enemy. speak, but to the God who acts42. Guard your soul so that you cannot be taken by tricks, so that, holding on to hope, you may become heirs of eternal salvation.

17. Truly we announce and teach these things as men: do not build this building of ours with hay, straw and stubble, to avoid suffering damage if it should burn. Do the work with gold, silver and precious stones43. I tell you, but it is up to you to get to work, it is God who must finish it. Let us strengthen our mind, let us put our soul in tension, let us prepare our hearts: our life depends on it, because we await eternal realities 44. But God is powerful (who has searched their hearts and has perceived who is truthful and who is false) to protect the sincere and make faithful the hypocrite and the dissembler. Well, God can make the unfaithful faithful by showing him his heart. May he be the one to erase the protocol that exists against you45 and forget your previous crimes, enlisting you in the Church and making you his soldiers while he girds you with the weapons of justice: may he fill you with the heavenly realities of the new Covenant and grant you eternally the indelible seal4647 of the Holy Spirit: in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom be glory forever and ever47. Amen. Cf. cat. 3, no. 3; cat., 17, n. 35. Cf. 1 Cor 3 12-15. Cf. cat. 1, no. 5. Cf Col 2,14; "He canceled the charge against us, the one with the prescriptions with their unfavorable clauses..." Cf. what was said in note 36. The edition of the catechesis in PG 33 contains a final note "to the reader", the text of which states: "Show these catechesis to those who are to be enlightened to those who are to receive baptism and to those who have already received it. But do not give them in any way to the catechumens and to those who are not Christians, otherwise you will have to give an account to God. And if you make a copy of a copy of them, do so as in the presence of God” (PG 33, 365366). CATECHESIS I INVITATION TO BAPTISM Delivered in Jerusalem, it contains an introduction to those approaching baptism. The starting point is Isaiah 1:16: "Wash yourselves, purify yourselves, put away the misdeeds of your souls from before my eyes"48. God awaits you. You are already disciples of the new Covenant and participants in the mysteries of Christ, now by vocation, but soon also as a gift: make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit 49 so that the inhabitants of heaven may rejoice.

For if, as the gospel says, "there will be joy over a single sinner who converts,"50 how much more will the salvation of so many souls not move the inhabitants of heaven to joy? Having entered a wide and beautiful path, walk cautiously along the path of piety. For the only begotten Son of God is fully prepared for your redemption and says: "Come, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you relief."51 Those who wear the pernicious garment of their offenses52 and are oppressed by the chains of their sins, listen to the voice of the prophet who says: "Wash yourselves, purify yourselves, put away the iniquities of your soul from before my eyes"53, so that the choir of angels will acclaim to you: "Blessed is he who is forgiven of his guilt, and his sin is covered." 54. Those who have recently lit for the first time the lamps of faith55, hold them in your hands without them fading, so that he who once by faith opened paradise to the thief on this most holy mountain of Golgotha56 may also grant you to sing the wedding song. New birth from sin to new man

2. If anyone is now a slave to sin, prepare by faith for the liberating regeneration of filial adoption. And having abandoned the fatal servitude of sins, once dedicated to the sweet service of the Lord, he will be judged worthy of enjoying the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom. Undress yourselves through the confession of the old man, which is corrupted by the By these introductory words and by the content itself, it is observed that the present catechesis is an invitation to baptism. Ez 18,31b. Lk 15,31. Mt 11,28. Cf. Procatechesis, n. 3; cat. 15, n, 25. Again Is 1,16. Psalm 32,1. It is a characteristic penitential psalm. Procat., 1, already pointed out: "Have the lamps in your hands to go look for your wife." The present catechesis alludes to that same fact again; The catechumens who were soon to receive baptism carried lighted lamps. Cf Lk 23,43. lusts of error, to put on the new man, who is renewed by the knowledge of him who created him57. Receive by faith the earnest of the Spirit58 so that you may be received into the eternal mansions59. Come (to receive) the spiritual seal so that you may be favorably recognized by its owner60. They will be numbered in the holy and faithful flock of Christ so that, as they were once separated to his right hand, they may now obtain the eternal life that has been prepared for them. Those who still suffer the harshness of their sins (like that of hairy skin) will remain standing on the left, since they have not yet had access to the grace of God, which is given through Christ in the laver of regeneration. But I am not referring to the regeneration of bodies, but to the new birth of the soul by the Spirit. For bodies are generated by visible parents, but souls are born again through faith; since "the Spirit blows where he wants" (Jn 3:8)61. If you are considered worthy, it will be permissible for you to hear: "Well done, good and faithful servant" (Mt 25:21), which will happen when your conscience cannot accuse you of simulation at all. Prepare to listen to God

3. If any of those here believe that they can tempt the grace of God, they deceive themselves and ignore the power of things. Have a sincere mind, man, free from deception for the sake of him who searches hearts and entrails (cf. Ps 7:10; Jer 11:20). Those who enlist soldiers examine their age62 and their bodies; Thus, when God enlists souls, he examines the wills and, if someone lives in hypocrisy, he rejects them as unsuitable for a true militia. But if he finds him worthy, he grants him his grace very quickly 63. He does not give what is holy to dogs (cf. Mt 7:6), but when he sees an honest conscience, he confers on it the healthy and admirable seal64 feared by demons and recognized by angels; so that those flee expelled, but these embrace him as through family kinship. Therefore, those who receive that spiritual and healthy seal must also make personal efforts. Just as those who use a pen to write or an arrow also have to make efforts, so grace needs the efforts of those who believe. From the catechumenate to the fruits of faith Cf Eph 4:22-25; Col 3:10. Cf 2. Cor 5,5. Cf Lk 16,9. Cf. Procatechesis, note 36. Cf. cat. 15, no. 25. In the frequent concrete allusions, now to Jn 3:8, but constantly with the mention of the new birth, etc., the full influence of Jn 3:1-21, Jesus' conversation with Nicodemus, in the catechisms of Cyril is seen. Basically, this implies the very common idea in patristic catechesis that through faith and baptism man is engendered anew: Christian initiation as the creation of a new humanity. It can also be translated as "the measures." Vine. cat. 3, no. 1. In this same catechesis, no. 2, mention has already been made of this "spiritual seal...". Mention has also been made of the previous note 36 and cat. 15, no. 21. We will not insist on this again, just remember that the ed. de Migne, PG 33,373 again mentions the similarity between the "seal" and the "character of baptism" with the marks printed on cattle to distinguish who their owners were, or also with the signs engraved with hot iron on soldiers. A certain crudeness in the comparison allows us to understand in a quite plastic way that the baptized will now be a servant only of Christ.

4. You do not receive corruptible weapons but spiritual ones. You will be introduced into a rational paradise, receiving a new name that you did not have before (probable allusion to Apoc 2,7b,17c)65. Before you were a catechumen, now you will be called faithful66. You are transplanted into good olive groves, from a wild olive tree to a good olive tree (cf. Rom 11:24); from sins to righteousness, from dirt to purity. You are made partaker of a holy vine: if you abide in the honey, you will grow like a fruitful branch; but if you do not remain, you will be consumed by fire. Therefore, let us bear fruit worthily. May the same thing not happen to us as to that fruitless vine, lest, when Jesus comes, he curses it for its sterility (cf. Mt 21:10). May everyone, instead, pronounce these words. "But I, like a green olive tree in the house of God, trust in the love of God forever and ever" (Ps 52:10). It is not a sensitive olive tree, but an intelligible one, a bearer of light. His own thing is to plant and water (cf. perhaps 1 Cor 3:6); but it is up to you to provide the fruit. Therefore, do not despise the grace of God: guard it piously when you receive it. Recognize sins to change your life

5. The present tense is confession time. Confess everything you did, in word or deed, both night and day. Recognize it in the acceptable time, and receive the heavenly treasure on the day of salvation (cf. 2 Cor 6:12). Enter with interest in exorcisms. Be assiduous in catechesis and record in your memory what is said there. For it will not be spoken only so that you can hear it, but so that you can seal what you have heard through faith67. Eliminate all human concerns from your thoughts, for this is a race with your own soul. Completely abandon what is of the world. Well, it's about small things; On the other hand, the gifts of the Lord are great. Abandon what is before you and have faith in what is to come. For so many years you have lived endlessly in the orbit of the world. Will you not dedicate yourself for forty days to prayer for your soul? “Surrender and know that I am God,” says the Scripture (Ps 46:11). Stop talking many useless things and stop murmuring or listening with pleasure to those who murmur 68. Show yourself rather quickly and ready to supplication. Show, by the practice of a more austere life, the strength and nerves of your soul. Cleanse your cup (cf. Mt 23:26) so that more abundant grace can fit into it; For the forgiveness of sins is given to all equally, but the communion of the Holy Spirit is granted according to the measure of each person's faith (Rom 12:6). If you work little, you will receive little; but if you do much, your reward will be much. You run for yourself, look at your own convenience. Forgiveness of others and fidelity in attending assemblies The note inserted in the aforementioned edition of PG 33, col. is reproduced here in full. 374; «"You will be introduced into a new rational paradise, receiving a new name." I can hardly resist thinking that here two passages of the Apocalypse are alluded to, c, II, v. 7: "To the victor I will give to eat of the wood of life, which is in the paradise of my God," and v. 17: "To the victor I will give a white stone, and engraved on the stone a new name." Well, although Cyril does not use the book of Revelation as canonical, he mentioned some of its statements in his catechesis. He affirms that paradise must be opened to the baptized, cat. 13:9, when, having made the renunciations, looking from the west and turned towards the east, he makes a pact with Christ. But he is grafted into the true olive tree that is Christ when he is anointed before baptism with the exorcised oil, cat. 20, no. 3.

In Christ we are, finally, grafted as in a vineyard when through baptism we commune (cat. 19, n. 7) with his death and his burial (by which the true vine has been planted in the earth, cat. 14, n. 11)». Cf Procat., n. 4; cat. 5, no. 1. Cf in this catechesis, no. 6, procat., no. 17. Cf. Procat., no. 16.

6. If you have something against someone, forgive them. You are going to receive forgiveness of sins: it is necessary that you also forgive those who sinned against you. Otherwise, how would you dare to say to the Lord: Forgive me my many sins when you do not even forgive a few things to someone who is your fellow servant (Mt 18:23-35)? Show interest in the synaxis69, and not only now when members of the clergy demand that interest from you, but also once you have received grace. For if it is good and praiseworthy before you receive it, will it cease to be good after it has been granted? If before you were grafted you had to be carefully watered and cared for, wasn't this much better once planted? Fight for your own soul, especially these days. Feed your soul with spiritual reading, because the Lord has prepared a spiritual banquet for you. You too say with the psalmist: «The Lord is my shepherd, I will lack nothing: he has placed me in the tent, in the sheepfold. He leads me to the still waters and comforts my soul” (Ps 23:1-3). With this the angels will rejoice at the same time and Christ himself, the great high priest, seeing the purpose of your will confirmed, offering himself to all of you, will say to the Father: "Here are me and the children that God has given me" (Is 8:18 and Hebr 2:13), and he will guard you all as pleasing to him. To him be glory and power forever and ever. Amen. Assemblies or sacred meetings. CATECHESIS II INVITATION TO CONVERSION Delivered in Jerusalem, it deals with conversion and forgiveness of sins, and about the enemy. The basic reading is from Ezekiel 18:20b-21: «The righteous man will have his righteousness imputed and the wicked his wickedness will be imputed. As for the wicked, if he turns away from all the sins he has committed, observes all my precepts and practices right and justice, he will certainly live, he will not die."70 Reality of sin

1. Sin is a fearsome reality and iniquity is a very serious disease of the soul: it cuts its nerves and also disposes it to eternal fire. Evil occurs when there is free delight, a germ that voluntarily leads to evil. The prophet already clearly points out that sin is committed spontaneously and freely: «I had planted you from the select stock, all legitimate seed. "Well, how have you changed into a bastard vine branch?" (Jer 2:21). The planting is good, but the fruit is bad, bad because of free will: the one who planted is free from guilt, but the vineyard will be destroyed by fire; planted for good, it produced evil for its own delight. For, according to Ecclesiastes, "God made man simple, but he complicated himself for many reasons" (Eccl 7:29). And the Apostle says: "We are His workmanship, created... for good works" (Eph 2:10). For the creator, being good, created "in order to good works," but the creature turned to evil of its own accord. According to this, sin is a grave evil. But it is not irremediable: it is serious for those who remain in it. But it is easy to heal the one who rejects it in conversion. Imagine that someone has fire in their hands. No doubt he will burn himself as long as he retains the coal, but if he throws it away from him, he eliminates the cause of his burning. But if someone thinks that he is not burned when he sins, the Scripture says to that person: "Can a man put fire in his lap without his clothes burning?" (Prov 6:27). Thus, sin burns the nerves of the soul. The origin of sin within man

2. But someone will say, What is sin? Is it an animal, an angel or a demon? What produces it?71. Pay attention well: it is not an enemy that invades you from outside, but something that springs from yourself. “Look your eyes straight” (Prov 4:25) and you will not experience passion. Have what is yours, do not take over what belongs to others and there will be no plunder in you. Remember the judgment and there will be no The subject of catechesis is the conversion that is required before baptism. Catechesis exhorts the penitence that the article of the Creed calls for "a single baptism of conversion for the forgiveness of sins." Cf. on this particular cat. 18, no. 22. It is also necessary to point out that in certain codices it is said "it is about conversion and the forgiveness of sins", but in the frontal explanation of the topic "about the enemy" is not added, that is, the devil. In fact, the examination of catechesis clarifies that the theme is essentially conversion and the forgiveness of sins, with the devil being nothing more than a secondary theme here. Cf cat. 4, no. 21. fornication nor adultery nor murder nor anything that is sinful. But if you forget God, you will begin to think evil and do what is unlawful. The devil and sin

3. But not only you are the origin and author of what you do: there is also a depraved instigator, the devil72. He tempts everyone, but he cannot deal with those who do not consent. That is why Ecclesiastes says: "If the spirit of him who has power comes upon you, do not abandon your post." 73. Close your door and make him flee away from you so that he does not cause you harm. But if you indifferently give in to the libidinous thought, opposing your spirit, it will plant its roots in you, bind your mind and drag you to the cave of the wicked. And if you say: I am faithful, evil desires will not be able to overcome me, although I frequently have them in my mind. Are you perhaps unaware that the root that remains attached to the stone for a long time always ends up breaking it? Don't even accept the germ, because it will shatter your faith. Root out evil before it flourishes, lest, acting negligently from the beginning, you later have to think about the fire (cf. Jer 23:29) and the ax (Mt3:10). Cure eye inflammation in time, so that you don't go blind and then seek a doctor.

4. The first cause of sin is the devil, the origin of evil. This was not said by me, but by the Lord: "For the devil has sinned from the beginning."74 Before him no one sinned. But he did not sin by force of nature75, as if he had been forced to sin (in that case, whoever had done so to him would have incurred a sin), but, created good, he became a devil taking his name from his actions76. For, having been an archangel77, he has subsequently been called the devil (or slanderer, Satan), having later been considered so by virtue of the thing itself. Satan is, therefore, the same as an adversary78. The proofs are not provided by me, but by the prophet Ezekiel: "You were the seal of a masterpiece and a crown of beauty, begotten in the divine paradise" (Ez 28,12 var.). And a little further down: "You were perfect in your conduct from the day of your creation until the day iniquity was found in you" (28:15)79. This did not come to you from outside, Cat. 4, nos. 21, 24. Ecl 10:4, which completes the advice with the words: "that phlegm frees us from serious errors." It is the Jerusalem version of the Bible, and the verse itself seems to be an advice of prudence in the face of errors of authority. The interpretation made by the text of the catechesis assumes another different context, that of temptation, but the intention is valid: to remain firm in the difficulties of temptation. In reality the phrase is not from the Gospel, but from 1 Jn 3:8: "Whoever commits sin is from the Devil, because the devil sins from the beginning. "The Son of God appeared to destroy the works of the devil." But along a similar line there is in Jn 8:44, put in the mouth of Jesus, this statement: «This man (the devil) was a murderer from the beginning, and did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him; When he tells a lie, he says what comes from within him, because he is a liar and the father of lies. Probably, by denying the possibility of sinning "by force (better, "by necessity") of nature", as if sin were an ontological demand of the devil's being, Cyril is thinking of the affirmation in this regard widespread among Gnostics and Manichaeans (cf. PG 33, 386, note 8). The Greek word diabolos means "slanderer", "detractor", "accuser", functions that it performs on and against man. This idea of ​​the angelic origin of the devil is also repeated in Cyril, for example, in cat. 8, no. 4. Also possible variant: "Satan means devil" (or slanderer).

In fact, in the Greek versions of the Bible the Hebrew expression "Satan" is often translated as diabolos. The prophetic oracle refers properly to the fall of the king of Tyre. In fact, the entire passage, Ez 28, 1-19, is an oracle-poem against him. A note from the Jerusalem Bible at 28:11, where the prediction of the aforementioned fall begins, states: "By a spontaneous accommodation, Christian tradition has often applied this poem to the fall of Lucifer." but you yourself gave birth to evil. A little further down he points out the cause: «Your heart has been filled with your beauty, you have been wounded by the multitude of your sins, yes, by your sins. I have thrown you to the ground" (28,17 var.). The Lord says the same thing in the Gospel in the same sense: "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven" (Lk 10:18). You see the consonance between both Testaments. When he fell, he dragged many with him. To those who follow him he suggests evil desires, from which adultery, fornication and any kind of evil follow. Because of him, our first father Adam was expelled from paradise and he exchanged it, from which admirable fruits sprouted, for a land that offered him thorns. Hope for the sinner

5. So, someone will say, have we perished deceived? Will there be no salvation? We fell, can we get up? (Jer 8,4). We have been blinded, can we regain our sight? We are limping, is there no hope that we will ever walk properly? I will say in summary: Can we not rise after having fallen? (cf. Ps 41:9) Is it that he who raised Lazarus, with a stench of four days already (Jn 11:39), will not also raise you alive? He who shed his precious blood for us will free us from sin so that we do not give up on ourselves (cf. Eph 4:19)80, brothers, falling into a state of despair. It is a bad thing not to believe in the hope of conversion. He who does not wait for salvation accumulates evil without measure; but he who waits for healing is easily merciful to himself. Likewise, the thief who does not expect to be amused goes to the point of insolence; but, if he waits for forgiveness, he often ends up doing penance. If even a snake can shed its skin, shall we not shed sin? Even the land that produces thorns becomes fertile if it is cultivated with care: Can we ever obtain salvation again? Nature is, therefore, capable of recovery, but for this voluntary acceptance is necessary. Mercy and love of God towards the sinner

6. God loves men, and not in small measure. Do not say then: I have been a fornicator and an adulterer, I have committed great crimes, and this not only once but very frequently. Will he forgive me, or rather forget about me? Listen to what the psalmist says: “How great is your goodness, Lord!” (Ps 31:20). Your accumulated sins do not overcome the multitude of God's mercies. Your wounds cannot beat the experience of the supreme doctor. Simply surrender to him in faith; tell the doctor your illness; You also say with David: "Yes, I confess my guilt, I am grieved for my sin" (Ps 38:19). And what is also said will be fulfilled in you: "And you have forgiven the malice of my heart" (Ps 32:5)81.

7. Do you, who have recently come to catechesis, want to see God's love for man? Do you want to contemplate the kindness of God and the enormity of his patience? Look at the case of Adam. He is the first man that God created, and he sinned: could he not warn him that next This version of Eph 4:19 is closer to the Vulgate's translation of the verse, examining which and its context the Pauline idea is perceived that, deprived of contact with Christ, man ends up falling into a situation of debauchery that harms the human being himself as such: Eph 4:17. It is an idea similar to Rom 1,18-32. The entire Psalm 32 is important as an expression of forgiveness after the recognition of sin. Verse 5, in its entirety, states: “I acknowledged my sin to you, and I did not hide my guilt; I said, "I will confess my transgressions to Yahweh." And you absolved my guilt, you forgave my sin. would die? But look what the God who loves men so much does. He throws him out of paradise (because because of sin he was not worthy to live there). And he places it in any place outside of there (cf. Gen 3:24), so that, seeing where it has fallen from and where it has been thrown, it may then achieve salvation through conversion. Cain, the first man given to light, became a fratricide; schemer of evil, author and cause of murders, and first envious, he later removed his brother from the middle. What penalty is he condemned to?: "You will be a vagabond and a wanderer on earth" (Gen 4:12). The sin was great, but the punishment was light.

8. And this was truly the clemency of God, but still small compared to what followed. Well, think about what happened in Noah's time. The giants sinned and evil spread greatly over the earth (cf. Hos 4:2)82. Because of her the flood was caused: in the five hundredth year God issued his threat (cf. Gen 6:13)83. Don't you think that God's kindness extended for a hundred years when punishment could have been inflicted at once? He lengthened everything to make room for the conversion. Don't you see the goodness of God? Not even those men, if they had then regained their senses, would have noticed that they lacked divine mercy. God's goodness is greater than sin

9. Let us now speak of those who have been saved through conversion. There will be those among women who will say: I am a prostitute, I have been an adulteress, I have stained my body with all kinds of lust. What possibility of salvation exists? Observe, woman, the case of Rahab, for there is salvation for you too. For if the one who engaged in open and public prostitution obtained her salvation through conversion, will not the one who once abused her body before having received grace obtain salvation through penance and fasting? Realize how he was saved, because he simply said: "Yahweh, your God, is God in heaven above and on earth beneath" (Jc 2:11)84. Out of modesty, he did not dare to say that it was his. But if you want to receive the testimony collected in the Scriptures about their salvation, you have it written in the Psalms: "I count Rahab and Babylon among those who know me" (Ps 87:4). Great is the kindness of God, who in the Scriptures remembers even prostitutes. And he doesn't just say "I count Rahab and Babylon," but he added "among those who know me." Thus, men and women can obtain salvation through conversion.

10. And even if all the people had sinned, this does not surpass divine kindness. The people had made a calf, but God did not repent of his mercy. Men denied God, but God did not deny himself (cf. 2 Tim 2:13). «Then they exclaimed: "These are your gods, Israel"» (Ex 32,4); and yet, according to their way of acting, the God of Israel protected them. Nor were the people the only ones who sinned, for Aaron, the high priest, also sinned. Moses, in fact, says: «Yahweh was also violently against Aaron. The iniquity spread over Israel, according to Hosea, is referred to here in the edition of PG 33,391, note 62. But we should rather think of Gen. 6,1-4, a passage on which the general note of the Jerusalem Bible has undoubted synthetic value. The mention of the year "five hundred" and "six hundred" refers to years of Noah's life, if Gen 5:32 and 7:6 are taken literally. The Jerusalem Bible comments on this verse: «Rajab was saved by his faith, Heb 11,31, and justified by his works, James 2,25. This foreigner, who with her faith and charity achieves the salvation of her entire house, has become among the Fathers the image of the Church. irritated... I also interceded then on his behalf and God forgave him" (Dt 9,20). Already Moses, pleading on behalf of the sinful high priest, softened the wrath of God. And Jesus, the only Son who prays for us, will not appease God? It did not prevent Aaron, despite his guilt, from becoming high priest. Will it hinder you, because you come from the Gentiles, from entering into salvation? Do penance likewise, O man: grace will not be denied you. He then adopts a blameless life: God truly loves men and no one can explain his clemency on the basis of his personal dignity: even if all the languages ​​of men were put together, they could not even explain a part of his kindness, that is, not even a part of what has been written about the kindness of God towards men. But we also do not know how much he forgave the angels, since he also forgives them, since there really is only one who is without sin, the one who frees us from it, Jesus85. But enough has been said about angels. The example of David's conversion

11. But if you wish, I will also present you other examples that refer to us: think of the blessed David, a clear example of conversion. He sinned gravely when, after going to bed, he walked around the terrace in the afternoon, looking carelessly and falling into his human weakness (cf. 2 Sam 11:2). He committed the sin, but when he confessed it, the brilliance of his soul did not completely disappear. The prophet Nathan appeared, who diligently corrected him and was the doctor of his wounds (cf. 2 Sam 12:1-1 5a). «The Lord is angry and you have sinned»86. A private person said this to the king. But the king, despite the dignity of the purple, was not outraged. For he did not take into account who was speaking, but rather the one who had sent him to him. He was not blinded by the cohort of soldiers that surrounded him, for he thought of the army of the angels of the Lord and trembled "as if he saw the invisible one." And he answered the messenger, or rather, the God who sent him: "I have sinned against the Lord" (2 Sam 12:13). You see the king's submission and confession: Had someone declared him convicted? Were there many who knew about the crime? The event had occurred quickly, but the prophet had soon appeared as the accuser. As soon as the offense has occurred, the sin is confessed. When he was recognized clearly and simply, he was healed very quickly. For the prophet Nathan, who had warned him, immediately told him: "Yahweh also forgives your sin" (ibid). Observe how the God who loves men changes very quickly. He says, however: "By provoking (God), you have provoked the enemies of the Lord" (2 Sam 12:14, according to versions). You had many enemies because of justice, but chastity protected you. But when you have neglected this protection, you have your enemies standing to rise up against you. This was the way the prophet consoled him.

12. But the blessed David, despite having heard that "God has forgiven your sin," did not neglect to do penance even though he was king, but instead of purple, he dressed in sackcloth, and sat not on seats of gold, but on ashes and on the ground 87. But he not only sat on the ashes, but also fed on them, as he himself says: "The bread that I eat is the ashes" (Ps. 102,10). His lustful eye filled him with tears, as he says: "I bathe my bed every night, I flood my bed with tears" (Ps 6:7). When the princes exhorted him to On Cyril's difficult statement about the sin of angels, cf. PG 33, 394-395 Those words are not properly from Scripture. According to PG 33, 396, they can be related to Isaiah 64,4: "Behold, you were angry, but we were sinners", in the context of a meditation-supplication in view of the history of Israel. Interpretation of 2 Sam 12:16. To taste the bread, he did not agree and continued his fast until the seventh day (2 Sam 12, 17-20). If the king manifested himself like this, wouldn't you, who are a simple private individual, do the same? After Absalom's rebellion, when he (the king) was offered various routes to escape, he chose to do so through the Mount of Olives (2 Sam 15:23), as if invoking in his mind the Deliverer, who from here was to ascend to heaven88. And when Shimei hurt him with harsh curses, he replied: "Let him be,"89 because he knew that he who forgives will be forgiven90. Other examples of penance

13. You see that it is a good thing to confess. And you see that it is salvation for those who convert. Solomon had also fallen (I Kgs 11:4), but what is the reason for saying: "Afterwards I did penance"91? Also Ahab, king of Samaria, was an evil worshiper of idols, of notorious wickedness, a murderer of prophets, impious, covetous of other people's fields and vineyards (I Kgs 20-21). But when he caused Naboth to perish at the instigation of Jezebel, and once the prophet Elijah arrived and wanted to threaten him, he tore his clothes and dressed in sackcloth. What then does the merciful God say to Elijah?: "Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself in my presence?" (I Kgs 21:29), as if wanting to calm the prophet's temper by inclining him towards the penitent. And he says: "I will not bring evil in his lifetime" (ibid.; for the entire episode, cf. 1 Kings 21, 17-29). And although the king, after forgiveness, would not depart from sin, God forgives him unconditionally, not because he did not know the future, but granting his mercy at the moment in which he is showing conversion. It is typical of a fair judge to issue a sentence adjusted to each of the facts.

14. On another occasion Jeroboam was standing offering sacrifices to idols on an altar: his hand was paralyzed for having ordered the arrest of the prophet who reproached him. But upon experiencing for himself the power of that man, he exclaimed: "Please appease the face of Yahweh your God" (1 Kings 13:6; cf. 13:1ff). And by virtue of this word his hand was completely restored. But if a prophet healed Jeroboam, can't Christ free you by healing you from your sins? Manasseh also committed numerous crimes: he was the one who had Isaiah killed, he contaminated himself with all kinds of idolatries and filled Jerusalem with the deaths of innocent people (2 Kings 21:16). But, taken captive to Babylon, through the experience of his own evil he used the medicine of conversion. For the Scripture says that Manasseh deeply humbled himself in the presence of the God of his fathers and "prayed to him and God agreed, heard his prayer and granted him the return to Jerusalem, to his kingdom" (2 Chron 33,12,13). If this man, who had the prophet sawed down92, was saved by conversion, will you not also be saved, who have not committed anything so serious? Trust in the possibility of conversion. Hezekiah Cyril refers here to Luke 24:50-51, the Ascension, in combination with Acts 1:12: "...they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet." More precisely: "Let him curse, for Yahweh has commanded him" (2 Sam 16, 11). Cf. in fact 2 Sam 16:12: "Perhaps Yahweh will look upon my affliction (perhaps "my fault") and Yahweh will repay me well for the curses of this day." The phrase is a translation of both the original Greek and the Latin version. It seems to refer to Prov 24, 32, but here Cyril, as PG 33,390 observes, uses a weak and complicated argument to talk about Solomon's conversion, interpreting the context of Prov 24,30-34 as such. It is a Jewish translation that mentions this form of martyrdom of Isaiah, although the data is not completely certain.

15. Do not mistrust the power of conversion without reason. Do you really want to know the power of penance? Do you want to know this very strong sword of salvation in depth and learn the value of confession?93. By conversion Hezekiah annihilated one hundred and eighty-five thousand enemies (2 Kings 19:35). And this is truly admirable, but it is little compared to the fact that through conversion he has changed the divine sentence that had already been pronounced against him. For Isaiah had told him in his illness "Give orders about your house, because you will die and not live" (2 Kings 20:1). And there were, therefore, no expectations, once the prophet had said "you are going to die." However, Hezekiah did not revoke his conversion, remembering what is written: "By conversion and calm they will be liberated" (Is 30:15)94. He turned to the wall and raising his mind from the bed to heaven (the thickness of the walls could not prevent his devout prayers), he exclaimed: "Lord, remember me!" (cf. Is 38:3), as if to say: «For my health it is enough that you remember me, you who are not subject to time, but have created the laws of life. The reason for our life is not in the origin or size of each of the stars, as some dream, but it is you who governs life and its duration according to the plans of your will. Because of the prophet's announcement (cf. Is 38:1) he (Hezekiah) had lost the hope of living, but the time of his life was extended by fifteen years, of which the receding of the sun was offered as a sign (38:8). The sun turned back for Hezekiah. And likewise the sun became absent because of Christ, not receding but going out95, thus showing the difference between Hezekiah and Jesus. But if he could annul God's sentence, can't Jesus grant forgiveness of sins? Turn away from them and mourn them in your soul; Close the doors and pray that they be forgiven you (cf. Mt 6, or), so that God quells the burning flames that spring from you, because confession96 can extinguish the fire and tame the lions. The three young men and Nebuchadnezzar

16. But if you don't believe, think about what happened to Ananias and his companions. How many sextarians of water97 were needed to extinguish a flame that rose to forty-nine cubits (Dan 3:47)? But where the flame was highest, there faith poured out as if it were a river, and they pointed out the remedy for evils: "You are just in everything you have done to us... Yes, we sin, we act wickedly" (Dan 3,27,29). And penance dissolved the flames. But if you doubt that conversion can put out the fire of Gehenna, learn from what happened to Ananias and his companions. Although some keen listener may say: "God freed them then justly." Since they did not want to worship the idol, God granted them strength and power. And since it was truly so, I will now move on to another example of conversion.

17. What is your opinion about Nebuchadnezzar? Have you not heard from the Scriptures that he was bloodthirsty and fierce like a lion? Have you not heard that he took the bones of kings out of their graves to throw them into the air? (cf. Jer 8,1ff)? Have you not heard that he took the people into exile and that he blinded the king's eyes after making him watch the slaughter of his children? (2. Kings 25, 7) And the "confession" mentioned here is the confession of faith. It must be taken into account that after the "delivery", traditio of the Symbol of Faith, there must come the "confession" of faith in the "return" or redditio of the Creed. Cyril refers to the force that the confession of faith has on the path that leads to Christian initiation. On the other hand, Hezekiah's illness, healing and subsequent song of thanksgiving also appears in Is 38. On Hezekiah cf. also Eclo 48,26. In the case of Jesus, cf. the darkening of the sun in Mc 15,33 par. The issue being addressed continues to be the confession of faith that will be made in the return of the creed. Sextary: measure of capacity equivalent to just over half a liter in our system of measurements. that destroyed the cherubs? I am not referring to the cherubs that can only be contemplated with the mind. Get this idea out of your head! I am referring to the cherubs that were sculpted, but also to the mercy seat from which God spoke (cf. Ex 25,1718,22). He also desecrated the veil of the sanctuary. Taking the censer, he took it to the temple of the idols98. He transformed all the objects of the offering, razed the temple to its foundations. He deserved innumerable punishments for the dead kings and for the saints he insulted. And since he had reduced the people to slavery and had placed the sacred vessels in the temples of idols, was he not worthy of suffering a thousand deaths?

18. You have seen the magnitude of the crimes. Turn now to the mercy of God. He (Nebuchadnezzar) was like a beast: he lived solitary and had to be beaten to be tamed. He had the claws of a lion, with which he grabbed the saints, and the manes of lions. He was, indeed, a swift and roaring lion. He ate hay like an ox and was like a donkey that did not know who had given it the kingdom99. His body was covered with dew, but he did not believe when he saw the fire extinguished by that same dew. And what happened?: "At the end of the appointed time, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven... and blessed the Most High, praising and exalting Him who lives forever" (Dan 4:31). When he recognized the Almighty and addressed these words of his grateful spirit to God, he repented of his actions, confessing his own weakness. God then restored the honor of the kingdom to him. final exhortation

19. What then? To Nebuchadnezzar, who had done so many evils, God gave, upon having confessed, forgiveness and the kingdom: and to you, if you convert, will he not give you forgiveness of sins and the kingdom of heaven, if you conduct yourself worthily? God is merciful, quick to forgive and slow to retaliate. Therefore, let no one despair of his own salvation. Peter, the prince of the apostles, denied the Lord three times before a random servant. But, touched by repentance, he wept bitterly: by crying, he manifests the intimate conversion of his heart; and for this reason he not only received forgiveness for his denial, but also preserved the dignity of an Apostle.

20. Therefore, brothers, there are multitudes of sinners who were converted and obtained salvation, you also ardently confess the Lord so that you may receive forgiveness of previous sins and, having become worthy of the heavenly gift, you may inherit the kingdom of heaven with all the saints, in Christ Jesus, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen100 Cf. a general description in Dan 1,2. It is the affirmation that power comes from God. Cf. cat. 8, no. 5. On the subject, in the New Testament, cf. Jn 19:11 and Rom 13:1-8. The editions of the catechesis of Cyril of Jerusalem frequently present a second copy of this second catechesis, deduced from the existing codices and partly based on conjectures about them (for example, PG 33,407-424). It has not been considered necessary here to offer any of these versions, because they are variants that are probably due to the fact that they are transcribed on different occasions in which the same catechesis on conversion could be pronounced. CATECHESIS III BAPTISM Delivered in Jerusalem, it deals with baptism. Take as a basis the Letter to the Romans 6:3-4: Or do you not know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? We were therefore buried with him with baptism into death, etc. (Rom. 6,3-4). They are heading towards baptism

1. "Hail, heavens, and exult, earth!"
