(Is 49,13) for those who will have to be aspergered with hyssop and who will be purified with intellectual hyssop by the strength of him who in his passion accepted the hyssop and the reed (cf. Jn 19,29). And let the powers of heaven rejoice; Let the souls that are to be espoused by the divine bridegroom prepare, for it is written "the voice of one crying in the desert: Prepare the way of the Lord" (Is 40:3; cf. Mt 3:3 par). It is not about something unimportant, nor about the ordinary and fearful union of bodies, but about the Spirit who scrutinizes everything according to faith101, delighting each one. Well, betrothals and human agreements are not always made with due judgment, since a husband always leans more quickly towards where there seems to be wealth or prestige of figure. Here, on the contrary, we do not look at the beauty of the bodies, but rather at whether there is an expert consciousness in perceiving the soul; We do not pay attention to the riches of condemnation but to those that piety has prepared. Be well disposed

2. Therefore, children of justice, direct your way of acting to John, who exhorts saying: "Rectify the way of the Lord" Jn 1:23). Remove all impediments and stumbling blocks to walk straight to eternal life. By the sincere faith of the soul, prepare clean vessels to receive the Holy Spirit. Begin to wash your clothes through conversion so that, when called to the bridegroom's bedchamber, you may be found clean. For the bridegroom calls everyone without distinction, since it is an abundant grace102. They are all brought together by the loud call of those who make the announcement103, but he later discerns who enters this wedding that was already there. Cyril seems to be alluding to the knowledge that Christ has of the intimate nature of man and, consequently, the knowledge that he who approaches Christ has of himself and others as intimately as he can through baptism. In this line it is useful to remember I Cor 2, perhaps especially 2:10-16: «For God has revealed it to us through the Spirit; and the Spirit searches everything, even to the depths of God. Indeed, what man knows the innermost part of man but the spirit of man that is in him? In the same way, no one knows what is intimate about God, except the Spirit of God. And we have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit that comes from God, to know the graces that God has granted us, of which we also speak, not with words learned from human wisdom, but learned from the Spirit, expressing spiritual realities in spiritual terms. Man naturally does not grasp the things of the Spirit of God; They are foolishness to him. And he cannot know them, since they can only be judged spiritually. On the other hand, the man of spirit judges everything; and no one can judge him. For "who knew the mind of the Lord to instruct him!" (Is 40,13). But we have the mind of Christ. Baptism is considered here as grace (cháris) or gift. prefigured104. May it not happen now that one of those who gave the name hears: "Friend, how did you get in here without a wedding dress?" (Mt 22,12). May it be granted to all of you to hear: “Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful in a little, I will put you in charge of much; Enter into the joy of your lord! (Mt 25,21). Well until now they stayed outside the door; that now everyone can say: "The King has brought me into his mansions" (Song 1:3).

«My soul exults in my God, because he has clothed me with the clothes of salvation and with the tunic of joy. He has put on me, like a husband, a diadem, as a bride adorns herself with her adornments” (Is 61:10)105. So that the soul of all of you may be found “without spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but may be holy and blameless” (Eph 5:27). I do not mean before they obtain grace (for they have been called precisely to receive the forgiveness of sins), but when grace is granted to them, there is nothing condemnable in their consciences that opposes baptism. Be prepared

3. Well, this is a great thing, brothers, and you must approach it with singular care. Let each of you stand before God in the presence of the myriads of the many armies of the angels. The Holy Spirit will seal their souls, for they will be selected for the militia of the great king106. Prepare yourselves, then, and be ready, not clothed in very white material garments, but with a soul penetrated by piety107. Do not approach this laver as if it were pure and simple water, but out of attention to the grace of the Holy Spirit, which is given together with the water. For the gifts offered on the altars of the Gentiles, being nothing other than what they are by nature, are contaminated by the invocation of idols. But, in our case, the water, when the Holy Spirit, Christ and the Father are invoked upon it, acquires the force of holiness108. Reborn in body and soul by water and the Spirit

4. Since man is composed of soul and body, purification is twofold: incorporeal for the non-corporeal part, corporal for the body. For at the same time that water cleanses the body, so the Spirit seals the soul, so that, sprinkled with the heart through the Spirit and, washed by water, also with the body we have access to God109. He will descend into the water. That is why you should not focus on the poverty of the material element, because you will have to receive salvation effectively: without The Greek expression speaks of "announcers" or, better, "criers" (the Latin version speaks of pracconum), expressly referring to those who announce the kerygma (megalophonon kerykon toné). Vine. procat., no. 3. The Jerusalem version of the Bible is taken into account, but also the text of the catechesis itself. Keep in mind what has already been said several times about "Character", referring to baptism and confirmation (or both sacraments at the same time). To understand the entire phrase, one must also include the fact that the "character" with which soldiers could be "sealed" in a troop was an expression of a soldier's commitment to his master. In Latin patristics, in which Tertullian definitively puts the term sacramentum into circulation, this term originally comes, with an important religious nuance, from the legal-military commitment contracted by the soldier with his commander. Cf. cat. 4, no. 18. Cyril is probably referring to the blessing of water prior to the actual administration of baptism. It may also simply refer to the central fact of the collation of baptism in the name of the Father, the Son and the Spirit, but the former is perhaps more likely. Cf Hebr 10:22; "...Let us draw near with a sincere heart, in fullness of faith, our hearts being purified from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water." both things you cannot receive salvation. It is not I who says it, but the Lord Jesus Christ, who has the power over this matter, for he says: "Unless one is born again"110, adding "of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God" (Jn 3:5). Nor does he perfectly possess grace who is baptized with water, but does not receive the Holy Spirit. Even if someone, being instructed in the works of virtues, does not receive the seal through water, he will not enter the kingdom of heaven111.

This statement seems daring, but it is not mine, since it is Jesus who pronounced it: you can take the proof for it from the Holy Scripture. Cornelius was a just man, considered worthy of contemplation by the angels, who had appropriately made his supplications and alms reach God. Peter came to him and the Spirit was poured out on those who believed, spoke in tongues and prophesied (Acts 10:34,44) and yet, after this grace of the Spirit, the Scripture says: "And he (Peter) commanded that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ" (10:48)112, so that, once the soul was regenerated by faith, the body would also receive grace through water. Salvation through water, in the history of Israel

5. But if anyone wants to know why grace is given through water, and not through some other element, he will find out by examining the Scriptures. Water is certainly a great thing, the most beautiful of the four fundamental elements of the world113. For the abode of angels is heaven; but the heavens are composed of water, the earth is the seat of man and the earth also has sprung from the waters: formed before the constitution in six days of all created things, "the spirit of God hovered over the waters" (Gen 1:2). The beginning of the world is water and the beginning of the gospels is the Jordan. Pharaoh's deliverance took place for Israel through the sea: deliverance from sins is obtained by the world through the washing of water in the word of God (cf. Eph 5:26). Wherever an alliance is established between anyone, water intervenes there. It was after a flood that the alliance with Noah was sanctioned (Gen 9:9). The alliance with Israel was approached from Mount Sinai, but with scarlet wool and hyssop (Hebr 9:19; cf. Ex 24:6-8)114. Elijah was taken, but not without water, since he first approached the Jordan, but then entered heaven in a chariot and transported in a whirlwind (2 Kings 2,7,11). The high priest washes first, and then offers the incense, since Aaron was washed before being made high priest (cf. Lev 8:6). Well, how would he pray for others who before Jn 3,3. The editors of the Gospel of John, according to the codices, usually prefer the version "from above." However, among the Fathers the idea of ​​the "new birth" is very common (cf I Pet 1:3). Cf the case, however, of the baptism of the martyrs in no. 10 of this catechesis. Peter's reasoning had previously been (10:47): "Can anyone deny the water of baptism to these who have received the Holy Spirit like us?" In this action of Peter, it is also the seal of baptism that reaffirms the good path that Cornelius is on, which had already been attested by the descent of the Spirit on him and his people. The entire episode and its consequences is the baptism of the first Christians from the Gentiles, in Acts 10:1-11:18. The later episode of Acts 19:1-7 bears a certain resemblance.

Mention of the philosophical conception, widespread in ancient times and already popularized rather than authentically defended at the time of Cyril's catechesis, according to which there are four elements of the world (air, water, earth and fire). The question is practically irrelevant for Christian dogma as long as it does not lead to the denial of the spiritual element of man. Allusion to fundamental elements of the world is found in cat. 9, no. 5. Evidently, in this and other statements the cosmological conception of the world is ancient. What is decisive, however, in Cyril's images is the symbolism of the baptismal water that is set out immediately below. Also allusion, according to the story of Exodus, to the rite of what would be the Eucharist starting with the Last Supper. would not have been purified by water? The font placed in the tabernacle was also a symbol of baptism115. The figure of John the Baptist

6. Baptism is the end of the Old and the beginning of the New Covenant. Well, the first important character was John, the greatest among those born of women (cf. Mt 11:11), who was the last of the prophets: "For all the prophets, as well as the Law, prophesied until John" (Mt 11:13). But he himself was the beginning of evangelical realities. It says, in effect, "the beginning of the Gospel of Jesus Christ" (Mk 1:1), indicating that it is then that "John appeared baptizing in the desert" (1:4). Although you remember Elijah, the Thesbite, who, taken to heaven, is not greater than John either. Enoch was also transported, and he is not older than John. Moses is a greater lawgiver and all the prophets are admirable, but they are not greater than John. It is not my intention to make comparisons between prophets, but both of them and of us the Lord Jesus said: "There has not arisen among those born of women one greater than John" (Mt 11:11), and he does not refer to those born of virgins, but of women. And if the comparison is made between fellow servants and the older servant, the superiority and grace of the son over the servants is much greater. Do you see what great man God chose as the giver of this grace? He was someone who owned nothing and was a lover of solitude, but he did not hate dealing with men; He ate locusts, but let his soul fly (cf. Is 40:3031), he satisfied his hunger with honey, while speaking words that were wise and sweeter than honey. He was dressed in camel hair, while giving an example of ascetic life in himself. When he was gestated in his mother's womb, he was sanctified by the Holy Spirit (Lk 1:15). In the same way Jeremiah was sanctified (Jer 1:5), but he was no longer a prophet before leaving the womb. Only John jumped for joy inside the womb (Lk 1:44) and, not seeing with the eyes of the body, recognized his Lord in the Spirit. Since the grace of baptism was great, its author had to be great as well. John's preaching

7. John baptized in the Jordan and all Jerusalem came to him enjoying the first fruits of the baptisms116. It is in Jerusalem where all good things have their beginning. You Jerusalemites know how those who approached allowed themselves to be baptized by him. “Confessing your sins,” he says (Mt 3:6). First they showed their wounds, and then he applied the medicine, granting those who believed rescue from eternal fire. If you want to be shown that John's baptism freed him from the threat of fire, listen to him himself: "Breed of vipers, who has taught you to flee from the wrath that threatens you? (Mt 3,7). So don't be a viper. But if you have ever been a breed of viper, get rid of—he means—your primitive sinful condition. For if a snake, feeling the anguish of aging, sheds its skin and, being renewed, is rejuvenated with a new body, you too must enter through the narrow gate (Mt 7:13-14) through fasting that frees you from perdition. Put off the old man with his works (Col 3:9b) and say that from the Song of Songs: "I have taken off my tunic, how can I put it on again?" But perhaps there is among you some simulator lurking for the favor of men, who Ex 40:7: "You will place the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and you will pour water into it." The font is not located inside the tabernacle itself, but in the court of the tabernacle. It is preferred to leave the plural "of baptisms" in the original, as it helps to understand the substantial difference between the "baptism of conversion" of John (Lk 3,2), which remains rather within the limits of the symbolic, and the novelty of the effectiveness of the baptism of Jesus. But it would be a mistake to ignore the real importance of John's baptism. He simulates piety but does not believe from the heart, but rather imitates the hypocrisy of Simon Magus. He does not come here to receive grace, but to sniff out what is going to be given to him. Listen also to Juan: «The ax is already laid at the root of the trees. Every tree that does not bear good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire” (Mt 3:10). Suppress simulation, because the judge is inexorable. Bear fruits of conversion

8. What then is to be done? What are the fruits of penance? "He who has two tunics, let him share them with him who has none" (Luke 3:11) 117 and "he who has to eat, let him do the same." Do you desire to enjoy the grace of the Holy Spirit, and do you not consider yourself worthy of those who are poor in sensible foods? Do you want the big things and don't communicate on the small things? Even though you have been published and have given yourself to fornication, have hope in salvation. "The tax collectors and the harlots arrive before you into the Kingdom of God" (Mt 21:31). Paul also witnesses this when he says: «Neither the impure, nor the idolaters, etc..., will inherit the Kingdom of God. And such were some of you. But they have been washed, they have been sanctified” (I Cor 6:9-11). It does not say: "Some have been," but "these have been." Sin committed through ignorance can be forgiven, but those who persist in evil will be condemned. Baptism "in the Holy Spirit and fire"

9. For greater praise of baptism I have to refer to the Son of God himself, since I can no longer say anything about men. Juan really is great, but not if he is compared to the Lord. Strong is his word, but not in comparison with the word of the Word. What is an illustrious spokesman compared to the king? He who baptizes in water is good, but what is he in comparison with he who baptizes in the Holy Spirit and fire? (Mt 3:11). The Savior baptized the apostles with the Holy Spirit and fire when “suddenly there came from heaven a noise like that of a rush of impetuous wind, which filled the entire house in which they were. Tongues like fire appeared to them and spread out and rested on each one of them; They were all filled with the Holy Spirit" (Acts 2:2-4). Martyrdom can be baptism

10. If anyone does not receive baptism, he does not obtain salvation. The only exceptions are the martyrs who, even without water, receive the kingdom. But the one who saved the world through the cross let blood and water flow from his pierced side (Jn 19:34), so that some, in times of peace, would be baptized with water, while others, in times of persecution, would be baptized with his own blood. For the Savior also gave the name baptism to martyrdom when he said: "Can you drink the cup that I am going to drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am going to be baptized?" (Mk 10,38)118. And truly the martyrs confess, becoming "a spectacle for the world, angels and men" (1 Cor 4:9); You will also confess shortly after. But it's not time yet for you to hear about this. Cyril himself makes the following observation here, as if it were a note: "That teacher was credible, since he was the first to practice what he taught and not do what his conscience prohibited." As the note of the Jerusalem Bible recalls to Mark 10:38, "according to the original force of the Greek term "baptize", Jesus will be "immersed" in a baptism of sufferings." In reality, the Christian knows that, by being baptized, he is immersed in the death of Jesus. Cf. the well-known passage Rom 6,3-11. The baptism of Jesus

11. Jesus sanctified baptism when he was baptized. If the Son of God had himself baptized, who can despise baptism without lacking piety? For Jesus was not baptized to receive forgiveness of sins (since he was free from sin), but, despite this, he was baptized to grant Divine grace and dignity to those who are baptized. For "just as children partake of blood and flesh, he also partook of the same" (Hebrews 2:14), so that, made partakers of his bodily presence, we might also have part in his grace: for this reason Jesus had himself baptized, so that we might obtain it, through communion in the same reality, together with the honor of salvation. According to the book of Job, there was a beast in the waters capable of swallowing the Jordan with its mouth (cf. Job 40:15-24). When the dragon's heads had to be crushed (Ps 74:14)119, (Jesus) descended into the water, he tied the strong one (cf. Mt 12:29) so that we would receive the power to tread on snakes and scorpions (cf. Luke 10:19). The beast was very small, but horrendous. No fishing boat could carry even a scale of its tail; perdition preceded it, infecting with its contagion those who encountered it120. Life appeared to stop death, and so that we could say that we have achieved salvation: «Where is your victory, O death? Where is your sting, O death? (1 Cor 15:55). For by baptism the sting of death is destroyed. You too will descend into the water of baptism

12. You descend into the water carrying sins, but the soul is sealed by the invocation of grace. This saves you from being absorbed by the wild beast. You have descended dead in your sins, but you ascend quickened in righteousness (Rom 6:11). If you have been grafted into a death similar to that of the Savior, you will also be considered worthy of his recurrence (Rom 6:5). For Jesus died taking upon himself all the sins of the world in order, after annihilating sin, to resurrect you in justice. You too, descending into the water, and buried in a certain way in it as he was in the tomb, are resurrected walking in newness of life. Baptism will give you the strength to fight

13. Later, when God has granted you that grace, he will make it possible for you to fight against the opposing powers. Just as he, after baptism, was tempted for forty days. And not because he couldn't win first, but because he wanted to do all things orderly and successively. You too, before baptism, feared meeting your adversaries. But after you have received grace, trusting in the weapons of justice, fight now and, if you want, announce the Gospel. After baptism, Jesus begins his task of evangelization Cf Ez 29,3, where "Pharaoh, king of Egypt, a great crocodile, reclining in the middle of his Niles" is mentioned (the image is continued in the following verses; cf. Ez 32, 1ff.). The texts of Ezekiel evoke the victory in the water over Satan. From that point "the crushed heads of the dragon" can be interpreted as the victory over the devil that is achieved through baptismal water. Cf. the description of Leviathan in Job 40,25-41,26.

14. Jesus Christ was the Son of God. However, he did not evangelize before receiving baptism. If the Lord himself administered the moments with a certain order, should we, who are servants, dare to do something outside of that order? Jesus began his preaching when “the Holy Spirit descended on him in bodily form, like a dove” (Lk 3:22). It does not mean that Jesus was the first to see him (since he knew him before he appeared in bodily form). The important thing then was that Juan saw it. Well, he says: "I did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water said to me: The one on whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining on him, that is the one..." (Jn 1:33)121. And also upon you, if you have sincere piety, the Holy Spirit will descend and the voice of the Father will descend upon you from above; not, “This is my Son” (Mt 3:17), but “He has now become my son”122. Only of him (Jesus) has it been said: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God" (Jn 1:1,). The verb is is appropriate, since the Son of God always exists. But what is appropriate for you is "it has been done now," since, to be a son, you are not one by nature, but you have obtained by adoption to be called a son. He has been from all eternity, but you acquire that grace as a gift. Convert to be baptized and receive the gift of the Holy Spirit

15. Prepare, therefore, the receptacle of your soul so that you may be made a son of God, and indeed an heir of God, a joint heir with Christ (Rom 8:17). You will achieve it if you prepare to achieve it: approaching by faith to achieve a firm conviction, leaving aside the old man. For all the evil you have done, fornication, adultery or any other kind of slander and sin, will be forgiven you. What greater sin than having crucified Christ? Well, this is also expiated by baptism. For as those three thousand who had crucified the Lord approached, Peter spoke to them123 and, when they asked: "What shall we do, brothers?" (Acts 2:37), you warned us, O Peter, of our ruin, saying: "You killed the Chief who brings to life" (Acts 3:15). What plaster will be placed on the wound? How will so much dirt be cleaned? What will be the salvation for so much perdition? He answered: “Convert and let each one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of your sins; and they will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit" (Acts 2:38). Oh unspeakable mercy of God! They do not expect any salvation, but are graced with the gift of the Holy Spirit. You see what power baptism has. If any of you crucified Christ with blasphemous words, or if anyone out of ignorance denied Him before men or if, finally, someone through his evil actions caused the truth to be mistreated, let him convert and have hope, for grace remains active. Trust in God's mercy

16. "Trust, Jerusalem: the Lord will take away your sins" (Zeph 3:14-15)124. «The Lord will cleanse the filth of his sons and daughters, with a righteous wind and a scorching wind» (Is 4:4). He will pour pure water on you and you will be purified from all your sin (cf. Ezek 36:25). The angelic choirs will come to you and say: "Who is this who comes up from the desert, leaning on her beloved?" (Song 8,5). The soul that was once a slave now counts the Lord as its beloved. And this one, upon receiving it, will exclaim: How beautiful you are, my beloved, how beautiful you are!... your teeth, a flock of Cyril does not fully transcribe Jn 1:33, which concludes: "... that is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit." Vine. below cat. 11l,9. The "three thousand" is mentioned in Acts 2:41. But the assertion that these "had crucified the Lord" presupposes the statements of Acts 2:23; "... You killed him by nailing him to the cross by the hand of the wicked." The version given of Sof responds to the way Cyril quotes the prophet. shearing sheep" (Song 4,1,2), this as a confession that has arisen from the dictates of conscience. And it is also said: "All births will be double" (Song 4:2), because it is a double grace: I mean that it is achieved by water and the Spirit, and is announced in the old and the new Covenant. May all of you, by carrying out this fast125 and keeping in mind what is said, "being fruitful in every good work" (Col 1:10), standing before the Bridegroom with a blameless heart, obtain forgiveness of sins from God, to whom be glory with the Son and in the Holy Spirit forever. Amen. It is about the fast of the forty days of Lent. CATECHESIS IV: THE TEN DOGMAS Delivered in Jerusalem, it deals with the "ten dogmas." It starts from Col 2:8: Be careful that no one enslaves you through the vain fallacy of a philosophy, founded on human traditions, according to the elements of the world and not according to Christ126. Purpose: catechesis on dogmas is necessary to avoid disorientation

1. Vice imitates virtue and tares pretend to be wheat, because in appearance they are certainly similar to wheat, but those in the know distinguish them by taste. The devil also transforms into an angel of light (2 Cor 11:14), not to return to where he was (since his heart is inflexible like an anvil, without the possibility of a new repentance), but to envelop those who lead a life similar to that of angels in the fog of blindness and the pestilent state of disbelief. Many go like wolves in sheep's clothing, but with nails and teeth of another kind: dressed in soft skin, disguising themselves in such an appearance before the simple, they spew the deadly poison of impiety through their teeth. That is why we need the grace to observe with a vigilant and sharp eye, lest, by eating tares instead of wheat, we fall into vice through ignorance or, believing that the wolf is a sheep, we become its prey. Just as it could also be that, taking him for a beneficent angel, when in reality he is the devil who is the architect of ruin, we will be devoured by him. For "he prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour," as the Scripture says (I Pet 5:8). This is why the Church makes its warnings; This is why this teaching is taught; For this reason these readings are established. In addition to good works, correct beliefs are required

2. For piety consists of two things, sacred dogmas and good works: neither is doctrine pleasing to God without good actions, nor does God accept works separated from religious beliefs. Of what use is a right feeling about God if one commits dishonest fornication? And, a The title of the catechesis perfectly expresses its content, since it is about exposing ten nuclear "contents" of the faith, which can be stated as follows: God, Christ, virgin birth, the cross, the resurrection, the second coming of Christ, the Holy Spirit, the soul, the body, the resurrection of man, the sacred Scriptures. In this enumeration, the theme of Scripture would be the eleventh of those presented. If counted this way, we are dealing with eleven, and not ten dogmas. That is why some codices speak of catechesis "of the eleven dogmas." The exposition of each of the dogmas can often in turn, according to the content, be subdivided in various ways. But these are secondary issues. More important is to note the importance given to "dogma" in these Jerusalem catechesis, prepared twenty years after the Council of Nicaea. They represent an important testimony of the dogmatic edifice that emerges from that first ecumenical council. For this reason and because the set of these catechesis always respects the dogmatic structure chronologically prior to them, but subsequent to the New Testament, Cyril's catechesis is not only an important catechetical testimony, but also a reflection of the dogmatic and objective faith (what theologians have called fides quae) of the Church of his time. More specific observations will be made in the notes that are added. As general observations, those contained in PG 33,449-454 are important. Conversely, what is the point of acting modestly—what is correct in itself if it is then impiously blasphemed? Therefore, the knowledge one may have of the dogmas is of great value. For this it is necessary to have a vigilant mind, even though there are those who obtain their loot through philosophy and vain fallacies (Col 2:8). The Gentiles seduce various realities through soft speech, for "honey drips from the lips of a whore" (Prov 5:3). And those who come from circumcision deceive those who approach them with false interpretations of sacred Scripture (cf. Tit 1:10-11), commenting on it from their childhood to their old age and growing old in ignorance of reality (cf. 2 Tim 3:7).

Heretics, for their part, deceive the humble through the softness of their language and softness of speech (cf. Rom 16:18), intertwining with the sweet name of Christ the poisoned darts of impious decrees. Of all of them at the same time the Lord says: "See that no one deceives you" (Mt 24:4). For this reason, the doctrine of faith is delivered and expositions of it are made127. It will proceed in an orderly manner

3. But before transmitting to you what belongs to the faith, I think I will do well by stating in a brief compendium the fundamental themes of the necessary truths, lest, due to the many things that must be said or due to the very duration of the entire Holy Lent, those among you who have a simpler mind lose the memory of the whole. Listing now by chapters, we will not forget what will later be discussed more fully. Those who have more perfect mental habits and more exercised senses in the distinction between good and evil should take it patiently, for they will hear a very simple exordium and a gentle introduction, so that at the same time those who need catechesis will benefit and those who already have knowledge will be happy to recover in their memory what they already knew. ABOUT GOD (dogma I)

4. As a foundation, let the truth about God 128 be firmly established in your soul. Namely, a God who is only one, not begotten129 by another, and without anyone to succeed him, who had no beginning and will never have an end, and who is himself good and just. If you ever hear a heretic say that there is someone else who is good or just, 130 realizing the heresy at once, recognize the poisoned dart. Some dared, through malevolent speech, to divide the one God: and some said that the author and owner of the soul is another than that of the bodies, teaching it foolishly and impiously. Well, how is it possible for a single man to be a servant of two masters if the Lord says in the Gospel: "No one can serve two masters" (Mt 6:24)? Therefore, there is only one God, author of both souls and bodies. One is the creator of heaven and earth, maker of angels and archangels, architect of multiple realities, Father from eternity of his only Son, Jesus Christ, our Lord, through whom he made everything (cf. Jn 1,3) the visible and the invisible (Col 1,16). The Greek original speaks of the “teaching (didaskalia) of faith” in which “exegesis” is done. Ultimately, this and the following catechesis are based, in terms of their content, on the "Symbol", the Creed in which the affirmations of the "objective" faith are grouped. As “truth” about God the Greek word “dogma” has been translated here. Or "inagento", without origin at any specific time. Perhaps it is useful to remember Mt 23:8-10 here.

5. The Father of Our Lord Jesus Christ is not limited to one place nor is he less than heaven, but the heavens are the work of his fingers (cf. Ps 8:4) and the entire earth is contained in his fists. It is both inside and outside of all things. And don't think that the sun surpasses it in luminosity or is even equal. For he who made the sun must be without comparison much greater and luminous. He has prior knowledge of future things and is more powerful than all of them, he knows everything and does everything according to his will: he is not subject to the succession of things or to what the stars indicate, to chance or to the necessity of fate. He is perfect in all things and equally possesses every kind of virtue. It neither decreases nor enlarges, but always remains the same and in the same way. He has prepared punishment for sinners and a crown for the righteous.

6. Now, since many have departed in various ways from the one God: some made the sun God in order to remain without God during the night; others to the moon so as not to have God during the day; others made other parts of the world God; some to the arts and others to food131 or their passions. Some fell ill for the love of women, others consecrated a solemnly placed image to Venus and, under this visible appearance, worshiped the vices and affections of their soul. There were those who, astonished by the brilliance of gold, judged that this and other materials were gods132. But if anyone impresses well within himself the doctrine that God is the only principle and believes in it from the heart, he will prevent the abuse and impetus of the vices of idolatry and the error of heretics133. Therefore, put this first dogma134 in your soul by faith. ABOUT CHRIST (dogma II)

7. Believe also in the one and only Son of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, God begotten of God, begotten as life from life, as light from light, like in all things to the Father,135 who did not begin to exist in time, but was begotten from eternity before all ages and before all that can be thought. He is wisdom, the power of God, and justice in person,136 and he is seated at the right hand of the Father before all ages. For he was not crowned by God, as some thought after his passion, nor did he sit at his right hand as a reward for his patience. In reality he has royal dignity from the beginning of his existence (although he has been begotten from all eternity): being God, his wisdom and his power, he sits next to the Father, as has already been said; He reigns together with the Father and governs everything with him. He lacks absolutely nothing of divine dignity137 and he has a perfect knowledge of the one by whom he was begotten as he is in turn known by the one who begotten him (cf. Jn 10:15). Vid, the poetic expressions of Is 40,12. Because of the detailed and drastic description of sin, this passage is reminiscent of what Paul makes in Rom 1:18-32. All this insistence that God is the only one recalls the biblical creed contained in the "Listen, Israel" of Deut 6:4-9. The terminology adopted at the beginning of point 2 continues to be used. "Similar in all things", homoíon katá pánta. The term "homoion" was found at the core of the condemnation of Arianism by the Council of Nicaea, not too many years before the present catechesis was pronounced. The precision of the Nicene creed in this regard consists in pointing out that Jesus Christ is of the same nature, "consubstantial" (homoousion v non homoioousion with the Father). Cyril is in accordance with the teaching of the council, as is proven by the rest of point 7. In the person of Jesus, the wisdom, power, and even the justice of God subsist in the uniqueness of his person. As "justice" Cyril uses the well-known Pauline term dikaiosyne. To put it in summary, remember what is written in the Gospels: "No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son" (Mt. 11,27).

8. But do not separate the Son from the Father nor believe, when relating them, in a "filio-paternity" as a mixture of one and the other. Believe, instead, that he is the only begotten Son of God, God-Word before all ages138. But it is not a word that, once pronounced, was lost in the air nor similar to words that lack solid and proper consistency: it is the Word-Son, creator of those who use word and reason; It is the Word that listens to the Father and speaks himself. If God allows it, we will talk about these things in due course, since we do not forget our plan, which is now to list only the topics of a necessary introduction to the faith. THE VIRGIN CONCEPTION (dogma III)

9. Also believe that the only begotten Son of God descended from heaven to earth because of our sins, assuming our humanity, subject to the same weaknesses to which we are subjected; who was born of a holy Virgin, and by the work of the Holy Spirit 139. This humanity was assumed, not according to an appearance or through some type of fiction, but in a true way. Not through a virgin, as if dragged along a canal, but having truly incarnated from her (and truly fed from her with milk), also eating and drinking truly like us. For if the assumption of human nature was a phantasm (and a visual deception), salvation would also have been a deception. (Christ was double: man in what could be seen, and God in what was hidden)140. As a man, he truly ate like us, since he experienced bodily states similar to ours; but, as God, he fed five thousand men with five loaves (Mt 14:17-21). As a man, he truly died, but as God called to life a man who had been dead for four days (Jn 11:39-44). Like God, he also walked calmly on the waters. ABOUT THE CROSS (dogma IV)

10. He was truly crucified for our sins141. But if you want to deny it, this well-known place will convince you, this blessed Golgotha ​​where we are gathered for the sake of him who was nailed to the cross: the whole world is full of the pieces into which the wood of the cross has been cut. But he was not crucified for his sins, but so that we might be freed from our own. He was then despised by men, beaten like a man with slaps (Mt 26:27). But creation recognized him as God, because, when the sun saw God subject to ignominy, he hid himself in fear, not being able to endure the spectacle (Luke 23:45). The burial Cf. catechesis 11, n. 10. In catechesis 11. The words that have just been transcribed in the last parenthesis are not found in all the codices. The insistence on the reality of the crucifixion is present everywhere in Cyril's catechesis. This insistence is even more understandable in the city where the events of the Passion had taken place.

11. He was placed, as a man, in a monument on the rock (Mt 27:60), but the stones, when they trembled, cracked (Mt 27:51). He went down to Sheol, to rescue the righteous there142. Did you perhaps want, I ask you, for the living to enjoy the grace of God without many of them being saints? That those who had been prisoners for a long time since Adam did not achieve freedom? The prophet Isaiah announced many things about him with an exalted voice. Did you not want the king to free them by descending with his announcement? David, Samuel and all the prophets were there. And even John himself, who said for his messengers: "Are you the one who is to come, or must we wait for another?" (Mt 11,3). Would you not wish that, by descending, I would free those men? THE RESURRECTION (dogma V)

12. But he who had descended into hell143 ascended again. And Jesus, who had been buried, was truly resurrected on the third day. If you ever feel harassed by the Jews, respond by reminding them that Jonah came out of the whale after three days (Jon 2:1,11; Mt 12:40). And if a dead person also came back to life through contact with the bones of Elisha (2 Kings 13:21), wouldn't the creator of men be resurrected144 much more easily? Therefore, he truly rose from the dead and, having returned to life, he was seen again by the disciples, and the twelve disciples were witnesses of the resurrection (Acts 2:32; 3:15; cf. 1 Cor 15:5), who bore witness to the resurrection not only with their words, but also going to the extent of torture and death with the hope of a true resurrection. Certainly "by the testimony of two or three witnesses a case will be established", according to Scripture (Dt 19:15; cf. Mt 18:16). And since there are twelve who testify about the resurrection of Christ, do you still not believe in it? The Ascension145

13. Once Jesus finished the course of his sufferings and freed men from their sins, he ascended on a cloud (Acts 1:9) collected again into the heavens; The angels were next to him who ascended and the apostles contemplated. But if anyone distrusts what we say, believe in virtue and by the power of the things that are now seen. For when kings die, they lose their power with their lives, but Christ crucified is adored by the entire world146. We announce a crucified man and the demons tremble. Many have been in different times nailed to The listener of the catechesis is here before the affirmation of what the creed and dogmatics will call the "descent into hell." In the affirmation of the descent into hell, a distinction must be made between the expression, as a way of speaking, of the materiality of a "descent" to the lower regions of the earth (which uses the image of the Jewish sheol) and what is really wanted to be expressed: the liberation of Christ is effective for men of any age. This is expressed by the statement that everyone was physically "waiting." But the issue, then, is the universality of redemption. In the New Testament all this is beautifully expressed in 1P. 0318ff. Keep in mind that hell comes from "inferior." In all of this this is not a statement about the state of condemnation, but rather about the universal value of Christ's death. See what was said in note 17. The affirmation, in a passive sense, of resurrecting does not indicate that Jesus was not an active agent of his own resurrection, but rather that this occurs in union with the Father. That is why the statement in Acts 3:15 that "God raised him (Jesus) from the dead" is accurate. This is further confirmation of the union of Jesus with the Abba, the Father. For a deepening of the union of Jesus and the Father, cf. the studies published by J. Jeremías, especially Abba. The central message of the Nuevo Teslamento, Salamanca 1981. The original text and the Latin version of it use the word "Assumption", but the content refers to what in the Western Church is called "Ascension", a term that is therefore used in the present translation Cf. cat. 13, nos. 3, 36, 39. a cross. But did the invocation of someone else crucified other than him make the demon flee?

14. Therefore, let us not be ashamed of the cross of Christ and, if you see someone hiding it, make the sign with it on your forehead so that the demons, seeing the royal sign, flee away in terror147. Make this sign when eating and drinking, when you sit, lie down and get up, when you talk and when you walk; In a word, in all circumstances. For he who was crucified here is now up in heaven148. Well, if, after being crucified and buried, he had remained in the tomb, perhaps one would have to blush; but he who was nailed to the cross on Golgotha, from the tomb facing the East on the Mount of Olives (Zech 14:4) ascended on the mountain to heaven (Lk 24:50-51; Acts 1:12: "From the mount called Olivet"). Descending from earth to hell149 and returning from there to us, he returned from us again to heaven, the Father hailing him and saying: "Sit at my right until I make your enemies your footstool" (Ps 110:1). THE COMING JUDGMENT (dogma VI)

15. This ascended Jesus Christ will come again from heaven, not from earth. I said "not from the earth", because many antichrists will come from the earth at this time (cf. I Jn 2:18). In fact, as you see, many have begun to say150: "I am the Christ" (Mt 24,5), after which the "abomination of desolation" will come (Mt 24,15 par.; cf. Dn 9,27; 11,31; 12,11), falsely usurping the name of Christ for themselves. But you—do me a favor—do not expect that the true Christ, the only begotten Son of God, has to come from the earth, but from the heavens, and will be seen by everyone with the maximum brilliance and the maximum radiance, surrounded by an escort of angels, to judge the living and the dead. Thus he will obtain the celestial kingdom, everlasting and devoid of any end. Be sure of all this and be cautious when many say that the end of the kingdom of Christ is near. THE HOLY SPIRIT (dogma VII)

16. Believe also in the Holy Spirit and think of him what you have accepted from the Father and the Son, and not according to those who teach erroneous things about him151. Learn therefore that this Holy Spirit is one and, furthermore, undivided and omnipotent. When doing many things, however, it is not divided. He knows the mysteries, he scrutinizes everything, even to the depths of God; descended on the Lord Jesus Christ in the form of a dove (cf. Lk 3:22), he had been active in the law and the prophets, but now he also seals your soul on the occasion of baptism 152: all rational nature now needs his holiness and, if anyone dares to blaspheme against him, he will not be forgiven either in this world or in the next (Mk 3,29 par.). Together with the Father and the Son he possesses the honor and Cat. 13, no. 16. Cat. 13, no. 4 Vid. above, note 17. It is probably an allusion to the fact that, until the time of Cyril of Jerusalem, the history of heresies had already had time to write some of its pages in Christianity. With which Cyril affirms the identity of nature of the Holy Spirit with the Father and the Son. The moment of baptism is presented by the original text as a kairós, that is, as a saving opportunity. On the other hand, the use of the verb "seal" (again, sfragidsein) refers to what was previously pointed out several times about the theology of "character", referring to both baptism and the gift of the Spirit and confirmation. Cf. Procatochesis, note 36. glory of divinity; Thrones and dominions, principalities and powers also need him153. For there is only one God, Father of Christ; and there is one Lord Jesus Christ, the only Son of God; and one Holy Spirit, who sanctifies and deifies everything, and who spoke in the Law and the Prophets, in the old and in the new Covenant.

17. Always have this sign in your mind, because all this is being announced to her in a summary way; But if God allows it, we will explain everything more fully, according to our strength, demonstrating it according to the Scriptures. For, regarding the divine and holy mysteries of faith, nothing should be transmitted without the Holy Scriptures, nor should things that are simply probable and supported by arguments constructed with artificial words be recklessly adduced. And do not think, therefore, that I am going to proceed in this way, except by proving from the Scriptures what I announce to you. For this faith, to which we owe our salvation, does not receive its strength from comments and disputes, but from demonstration through Holy Scripture. ON THE SOUL (dogma VIII)

18. After the knowledge of this venerable, glorious and most holy faith, you must also know yourself: Who are you?154. As a man, you have been made composed of soul and body and, as was said shortly before,155 God himself is the author of your soul and your body. You must also know that you have a free soul that is God's masterpiece, made in the image of its creator: immortal because of God who grants it immortality; a living being endowed with reason and free from corruption because of the one who gave him all this; with the ability to do what you want. For you do not sin because of the position of the stars when you were born156 nor do you see yourself fatally entangled in fornication, nor, as some rave, does the conjunction of the stars force you to fall into lasciviousness against your will. Why, not wanting to recognize your own evils, do you attribute your guilt to the innocent stars? And do not speak to me, after all this, about the astrologers, for the Scripture says of them: "Let those who write the letter from heaven come now and save you," to add a little further down: "Behold them there like blades of straw, which will be consumed by fire; They will not be able to escape from the arms of the flames” (Is 47,13,14). 19. But also learn this: before the soul came into this world, it committed no sin. But having come innocent, we now sin voluntarily157. Do not think that I am misinterpreting that: "But if I do what I do not want..." (Rom 7:16), but remember that: "If you want, if you are docile, you will eat the goods of the earth; If they do not want to and rebel, they will be devoured by the sword" (Is 1:19-20) and, on the other hand: "As they offered their members to the service of impurity and iniquity for iniquity, so now let them give their members to the service of justice for holiness" (Rom. 6:19). Remember also what the Scripture says: "As they did not see fit to keep the true knowledge of God..." (Rom 1,28) and "whatever of God can be known, is manifest in them" (Rom 1,19) and, on the other hand, "they have closed their eyes" (Mt 13,15, quoting Is 6,9-10). By applying to the Holy Spirit everything that is said about the Son, what is said about the triumph and supremacy of Christ in Col I:16 and Eph 1:2 is logically also attributed to him. Also in this it is observed that, although Cyril of Jerusalem is not, properly speaking, creative in Trinitarian theology, he is at least a good witness to it.

The topic was already mentioned in catechesis 3, no. 4. Ibid. At this time, as at other times, the catechisms demonstrate against astrology and the belief in horoscopes. Vine. cat. 6, nos. 27, 28. Remember God when he rebukes and says: “I had planted you with the choice stock, all legitimate seed. Well, how have you changed into a bastard vine branch? Jer 2,21).

20. The soul is immortal. And all souls are alike: both men and women. Only the members of the bodies are different. There is no class of souls that are sinful by nature and others that act properly, since they all act according to their will and the free will of each one, while there is no diversity in the substance of the souls and it is similar in all of them. Anyway, I realize that I have said a lot of things and that we are running out of time. But what should come before salvation? Won't you be able to put in a little effort to gain strength against the heretics? And don't you want to know the detours along the way so as not to recklessly fall off the cliff? Those who teach you these things do not intend to obtain the slightest benefit from your learning them. And you, who are the one who learns them, should you not willingly accept the multitude of things that are said?

21. The soul is free and master of itself. The devil can certainly suggest, but he cannot force her to act by depriving her of her will. When the thought of fornication comes to you, you admit it if you want, but not if you reject it. Well, if you necessarily had to commit fornication, why would God have prepared Gehenna? If by nature he does what is right, and not freely, for what purpose would God have ordained ineffable rewards? The sheep is meek, but it has never been crowned for its meekness, since that meekness does not come from the determination of its will, but from its way of being. ABOUT THE BODY (dogma IX)

22. You have already heard, dear, enough things about the soul; If you can, listen now also about the body. And do not think what some say that the body was not made by God, and that they believe that the soul dwells in it as in a vessel that is foreign to it, inclining for this reason to the practice of fornication158. What is it that they reproach the admirable body? What is lacking in decency and harmony? What lacks aesthetics in its structure? Should they not take into account both the splendid configuration of the eyes and the oblique position of the ears, to be able to hear without difficulty, or the sense of smell capable of distinguishing odors or even soft aromas, or the double capacity of the tongue to taste things and to be able to speak, without forgetting the lung capacity to breathe air incessantly? Who gave the heart its continuous movement? Who tied the nerves to the bones so wisely? Who allocated a part of the food to the repair of the forces of nature, allocating The author wants to defend, with reason, the dignity of the body, trying to prevent a fair valuation of the soul, the most specific and characteristic of created man, from being detrimental to the somatic reality of man. The later teaching of the substantial unity of soul and body will explain all this more clearly, in addition to the better knowledge we have today of New Testament anthropology with its concepts of soma, psyche, etc., especially in the letters of Paul. On all this, the study by F.P. can be usefully consulted. FIORENZA and J.-B. METZ, Man as a unity of body and soul, Mysterium Salutis II/2, Madrid 1970, 661715. The interest of this paragraph of the catechesis is focused especially on defending that, since the body is a reality of man with full dignity, "it is not for fornication, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body" (I Cor 6,13). another to defecation, modestly covering the less noble parts? Who is it that made weak human nature able to perpetuate itself through a simple union?

23. And don't tell me that the body is the cause of sin159. Well, if the body is the cause of sin, why don't the dead sin? Place a sword to the right of a man who has recently died, it will not kill anyone. Now all kinds of beauties can parade before a recently dead young man; he will not experience any lasciviousness. Because? Because the body does not sin of itself; It is the soul that sins through the body. The body is like the instrument of the soul, as if it were clothing and its shelter: it becomes unclean if it is the one that moves it to fornication; but if it is united to a holy soul, it becomes a temple of the Holy Spirit. And it is not I who say this, but the apostle Paul: "Do you not know that the body is the sanctuary of the Holy Spirit, who is in you?" (I Cor 6,19). Respect, therefore, your body as a temple of the Holy Spirit. Do not stain your flesh with fornication; Do not dirty this beautiful dress of yours. But if you have made it dirty, wash it now for the sake of penance: do it while there is still time.

24. Regarding chastity, pay attention above all to the order of monks and virgins160, who live in the world a life similar to that of angels, but also listen to all the people of the Church. And, having your name written in the evangelical books because of the purpose of purity, take care that it does not later have to be erased because of the clumsiness committed.

25. Nor should you, if you perfectly fulfill the duty of chastity, conceit yourself in front of those who, united in marriage, follow an inferior state of life. I Cor 7:5); These such offer their pure bodies, along with their clothing, in the assemblies of the Church, since they married not to enjoy the passions, but for the procreation of children.

Lord, so that the Lord also respects the body. Nourish it (the body) with food to live and give it adequate care, but not so that it indulges in pleasure. About food

27. These should be the rules about food; In fact there are many who have problems with that question. For some deal without problems with what is sacrificed to idols, others abstain, for reasons of practicing the ascetic life, from some of the things offered and condemn those who eat them161, and thus the souls of some are stained in different ways with respect to food (I Cor 8,7), by ignoring the valid causes for eating or abstaining. We fast from wine and abstain from meat, not because we hate them for religious reasons, but in the expectation of gratuitousness, so that, despising what is sensible, we enjoy the spiritual and true banquet. So also that, sowing now in tears, we may reap the harvest of joy in the world to come (cf. Ps 126:5-6). Therefore do not despise those who eat, for they take food because of the weakness of their bodies; Nor do you rebuke those who drink a little wine because of their stomach and their frequent illnesses,162 nor condemn them as sinners; Nor do you hate meats, for the Apostle had known some such when he said that "they prohibit marriage and the use of foods that God created to be eaten with thanksgiving by believers" (I Tim 4:3). Therefore, if you abstain from these things, do not do it as if it were abominable, for if it were so you would not obtain grace; Rather, leave them, even if they are good, for the most authentic thing that is proposed to you, which is much better.

28. Completely avoid eating what was offered to idols, since it is not that I say this today, but that the Apostles themselves and, at that time, even James, bishop of this Church, cared about such foods; for the apostles and presbyters wrote an epistle to all the Gentiles with the purpose of abstaining first and foremost from what was sacrificed, but also from blood and what was drowned (Acts 15:20-29)163. Well, many men Explaining the problem (Rom 14,1-15,13; I Cor 8; 10,14-33), Paul, even having the criterion that it does not matter to eat meat previously sacrificed to idols, wants everyone's opinions to be respected. Cf. p. e.g., Rom 14:3: «Let him who eats not despise him who does not eat; and let him who does not eat not judge him who eats. The phrase is taken from the actually different case of 1 Tim 5:23. Cyril seems to consider the importance that the prescriptions of the Jerusalem assembly still have for his time. This (Acts 15:5-35) met to resolve whether the adoption of circumcision and the Jewish Law were a prior step to the entry of Gentiles into the Church. But, basically, the issue that was discussed was whether Pauline preaching (the "gospel of Paul") was fair, according to which the justification of the sinner was not achieved by works (and, in them, the works of the Law), but by faith. The topic, capital in Paul, is addressed in great detail, especially in his letters to Gal and Rom. Peter's moderating role was decisive in the assembly (Acts 15:7-12) in favor of man being justified freely in Christ. Without denying this, but because of James, culturally and religiously very close to Jewish observances, a solution of some compromise was adopted, "not to impose on you any burdens other than these indispensable ones: abstain from idols, blood, strangled animals and impurity" (Acts 15:28-29). Apart from the question of "impurity", which in all probability refers to fornication and whose moral rejection is normal, it is logical that the other prescriptions very soon fell into disuse, especially in the Churches of the West, in which very soon after the central years of Paul's preaching there would no longer be a question that the Jewish law had expired in all its liturgical and legal aspects.

But it does not seem strange that in the Church of Jerusalem, due to a certain historical memory that Cyril's catechesis seems to reflect, a certain respect for that circumstantial Jerusalem decree was still maintained. It could be said, on the other hand, that in the present catechesis the influence of Pauline theological anthropology is not as present as it could be. For some details on this passage from the catechesis, cf. PG 33,491-492, note 1 of fierce nature that live like dogs, lick the blood like wild beasts and swell from drowned animals. But you, who are a servant of Christ, observe this when you eat to do so piously and religiously. That's enough about food. About the dress

Wear a simple dress, and not as decoration but to cover what you need; not to delight you with pleasure, but to warm you in winter and modestly cover your body; but do not fall into the unnecessary complication of clothing, with the pretext that you have to cover yourself, or any other foolishness. ON THE RESURRECTION (dogma X)

30. Please use this body moderately; Know that you will have to be resurrected from the dead to be judged precisely with that body164. But if any thought of distrust comes to you, as if it couldn't happen, judge by other things about yourself that don't seem real either. Well, tell me yourself, think about where you were a hundred years ago or more. And, if you started from being such a small and vile reality, how is it that you have reached such development with such harmony of your external figure? Can He not bring into existence what did not previously exist, be able to resurrect what has already been and died? Will he who each year, on our behalf, raises the wheat that, once sown, perishes and rots, have difficulty in resurrecting ourselves for whom he himself resurrected? You see how the trees now remain for so many months without fruit and without leaves; but all of them, after the winter, come back to life after having been as dead. Will we not be, much more and much more easily, called back to life? Moses' staff was transformed, by God's will, into something very different from itself, a serpent. Can not then the man fallen into death be restored to himself?

31. Do not listen to those who say that this body does not resurrect, because it will resurrect. Isaiah is a witness to this when he says: "The dead will rise, and those who are in the graves will rise" (Is 26:19)165 and, according to Daniel: "Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awaken, some to eternal life, others to shame, to eternal horror" (Dan 12:2). For the rest, the resurrection is for all men, but it will not be the same for all. Well, we will all receive eternal bodies, but not all of them are equal. The righteous will receive it to eternally join the choir of angels, and the sinners will eternally suffer the penalties for their sins. The baptism

32. For all this, the Lord, out of his goodness towards men, granted them the conversion of baptism, so that, throwing away most of the weight of sins, and even all the burden (cf. Hebr 12:1), by obtaining the seal through the Holy Spirit we might become heirs of eternal life. 33. All this is taught to us by the Scriptures of the old and the new Covenant, inspired by God. One and the same is the God of both alliances, who in the old one preannounced that Christ would manifest himself in the new one and who led us through the Law and the Prophets as a pedagogue to Christ. “Before faith came, we were shut up under the supervision of the Law” (Gal 3:23), and “the Law has been our teacher until Christ. But if you ever hear any of the heretics denigrating the Law or the prophets, reply to him with that salutary word that says: "Jesus did not come to abolish the Law, but to fulfill it." Why do you waste time pitifully on dubious and controversial issues? Read the Holy Scriptures, that is, these twenty-two books of the Old Testament that the seventy-two interpreters translated168.

34. After Alexander, king of the Macedonians, died, dividing his kingdom into four principalities, Babylon, Macedonia, Asia and Egypt, one of those who reigned in Egypt, Ptolemy Philadelphus, a prince who was a great scholar of letters, collected books from all places. He heard his librarian Demetrius Phalereus speak about the Scriptures of the Law and the Prophets. He rightly thought that books are not obtained by force, but that one wins over their possessors rather by gifts and friendship. Knowing that, by violent force, what is given against one's will is often corrupted by deception, while what is taught spontaneously is given in all sincerity, he sent numerous gifts to the then high priest Eleazar to adorn the temple of Jerusalem, bringing six men from each of the twelve tribes of Israel to it. Later, in order to verify whether or not the books were inspired by God, seeking to ensure that the interpreters sent did not agree with each other, he had them place each of them in their own rooms where the Lighthouse of Alexandria is located1694, ordering each one to translate the entire Scripture. They finished the work within seventy-two days, and the king gathered all the versions, prepared in separate places and without contact between the authors, verifying that they completely coincided not only in terms of meaning, but in the terms themselves. The work, then, was not a verbal creation nor an artifice of human sophistry, but a version of the Holy Scriptures, dictated by the Holy Spirit and with the inspiration of that same Spirit. The phrase, on the lips of Jesus, is: "Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law and the Prophets" (Mt 5:17). Inauthentic biblical books, although the expression is especially applied to the so-called "apocryphal gospels." These are books not accepted in the biblical canon. Furthermore, the LXX version was highly appreciated by the NT authors themselves, who frequently use it. 35. Read, then, the twenty-two books, but do not want to know anything about the Apocrypha. Meditate and study only those, which are the ones that in the Church we read with certain confidence; Much more prudent and pious than you were the Apostles, as well as the ancient bishops of the Church who transmitted them to us; Therefore, you, who are a child of the Church, do not violate its laws. Meditate seriously on the twenty-two books of the Old Testament, whose names strive to commit to memory just as I will tell you now. The first five are the books of the Law, of Moses: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy. Then, the book of Joshua and that of Judges, the seventh and which is considered together with Ruth. Of the remaining historical books, the first and second of the Kingdoms are considered one among the Hebrews, and the same is true of the third and fourth170. That of Esther is the twelfth book. These are the historical ones. Five are written in verse: Job, the book of Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and the Song of Songs, which is the seventeenth book. Five prophetic books follow: a book of the Twelve Prophets 172 and the Epistle 173, plus the books of Ezekiel and Daniel, the twenty-second of the Old Testament.

Saturday and do not consider pure or clean foods that are in themselves indifferent. but above all you will hate all meetings of offending heretics; Put all the means to favor your soul with fasting, alms and reading divine oracles so that, through temperance and the observance of sacred dogmas, you may enjoy, for the time you have left to live in the flesh, the only salvation, which is granted by baptism. And thus, assigned by God the Father to the heavenly host, you also deserve the crown of heaven: in Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen. CATECHESIS V FAITH Delivered in Jerusalem, on "faith." The starting point is Hebr 11:1-2: «Faith is a guarantee of things hoped for; the proof of realities that are not seen. For her our elders were praised»175. The passage from the order of catechumens to that of the faithful

1. The greatness of the dignity that God has granted them by making them pass from the order of catechumens to that of the faithful is expressed by the apostle Paul when he says: "Faithful is God, by whom they have been called into communion with his son Jesus Christ" (I Cor 1:9). But, if God is called "faithful", you also receive this adjective as you have grown in dignity. For just as God is called good, just, omnipotent (as well as lord of all) and creator of all things, he is also called "faithful." Think, therefore, to what dignity you are promoted, since you will have to participate in this divine appellation.

2. Here you are looking to see if there is anyone among you who is already faithful in the depths of his conscience 176. Well, "a faithful man, who will find him?" (Prov 20:6). It is not about revealing your conscience to me, since you must be judged in human circumstances, but about showing the sincerity of your faith to the God who searches the loins and the hearts (cf. Ps 7:10) and "knows the thoughts of man" (Ps 94:13). A faithful man is certainly a great thing, and he is richer than all the rich even though he is deprived of all riches177, and all this precisely because he despises them. For those who are rich externally, although they possess many things, are tortured by their internal poverty: the more things they gather, the more they are mortified by the desire to possess what they lack. But the faithful man - and this is the most admirable thing - is rich in his poverty knowing that the only thing necessary is to clothe and feed himself and, content with this (I Tim 6,8), he despises riches. Faith generates communion and trust and is an expression of them

3. Nor should we think that the prestige of faith only exists among those of us who protect ourselves under the name of Christ, but rather that everything that is done in the world, even by those who are far from the Church, is penetrated by faith178. Through faith, two strange people are united by nuptial laws; people who are strangers to each other enter into the communion of bodies and The theme of this catechesis is usually defined as "on faith and the symbol," but it is often called "On faith." A symbol in use in the Church of Jerusalem is transcribed after this catechesis. Cf. 1 Cor 4,2-4. Prov 17, or, according to the version of the Seventy. The lines that follow have a more direct objective of explaining that there is also a human faith, in contracts, etc., which is used here to give an explanatory idea of ​​what faith can be in the Christian sphere. The entire rest of paragraph 3 reveals, on the other hand, quite clearly the awareness of the distinction that exists between the Christian and those who live outside the Church. property through the faith that is present in the marriage contract. Agricultural work is also supported by a certain faith, since those who do not have hope of receiving fruits do not begin to work. Men travel the sea with faith when, trusting in a small log, they exchange the solidity of the earth for the agitation of the waves, surrendering themselves to uncertain hopes and showing a confidence more sure than any anchor. Finally, men's businesses rely on trust, and this not only happens among us, but also, as has been said, among those who are unrelated to our affairs. For, although they do not accept the Scriptures, they have their own doctrines that they accept with confidence179. Strength of faith in diverse situations

4. Today's reading also calls you to true faith, indicating the way by which you can please God, as it points out that "without faith it is impossible to please Him" ​​(Hebrews 11:6). But how will man resolve to serve God if he does not believe in him as a rewarder? How will a girl maintain her purpose of virginity or a young man be chaste if they do not believe in the unfading crown of chastity? Faith is the eye that illuminates the entire conscience and favors insight, since the prophet says: "If they do not believe, they will not understand"180. Faith, according to Daniel, closes the mouths of the lions (cf. Hebr 11:33), since the Scripture says of it: "They took Daniel out of the den and no wound was found on him, because he had trusted in his God" (Dn 6:24). Is there anything more terrible than the devil? For against him we have no other kind of weapon than faith (cf. 1 Pet 5:9): an incorporeal shield against an invisible enemy, who launches multiple spears and shoots with arrows those who, in the dark night, are not vigilant. But, although darkness reigns and the enemy is not in sight, we have faith as armor, as the Apostle says: "always embracing the shield of faith, so that with it you can extinguish all the fiery darts of the Evil One" (El 6:16). The devil often throws the fiery dart of voluptuous desire, but faith extinguishes it by illuminating our judgment and lightening our mind181. Faith in the story of Abraham, Father of nations

5. One could talk very broadly about faith and there would never be enough time to finish talking about it. But, from the figures of the old Law, Abraham will suffice for us, since we have been adopted as sons also by his faith (cf. Rom 4:11 b). He was not justified only by his works, but also by his faith (James 2:24; cf. 2:14-26) 182. For he had done many things correctly, but he had never been called "friend of God" until after he believed183, and Philosophical doctrines, religions, sects, etc. Cf. Is 7,9, version of the Seventy. Regarding the difficulty of the verse, the note from the Jerusalem Bible is very useful, in summary.
