On the subject, the works of O.H. are very interesting. Pesch and F. Mussner contained in the exposition of dogmatics Mysterium Salutis, t. IV/2, Madrid 2 1984 Gen 15,6: "And he believed in Yahweh, who counted it to him as righteousness." His entire performance reached its consummation through faith. By faith he abandoned his relatives; By faith he left country, region and home (Hebr 11:8-10). And, as he was justified, you also will be justified184. His body was already exhausted, but he would later receive children: being old himself, he had an elderly wife, Sarah, but with no hope of children. Well, it is to this old man to whom God promises a future offspring. But he "did not waver in his faith when he considered his body no longer in strength" (Rom 4:19), but heeded the power of the one who promised it to him, "because he counted him worthy of faith who had assured it to him" (Hebrew 11:11). Therefore, as from dead bodies and contrary to what was thought, he received a son (cf. Hebr 11:12; Rom 4:18-22).

Later, upon receiving the order to offer the son received (Gen 22), even though he had heard that "through Isaac a descendant will bear your name" (Gen 21,12b), he offered his only son to God, because "he thought how powerful God was even to raise from the dead" (Hebr 11,19). And after having tied his son and placed him on the wood, he certainly sacrificed him of his will, but he recovered his son alive through the goodness of God who placed a lamb in the same place to replace his son. And so, truly having faith, "he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the faith that he possessed when he was uncircumcised" (Rom 4:11, which uses Gen 17:11), once he had accepted the promise that he would become the father of many nations (cf. Gen 12:2-3); 15,5,18; 17.5; Rom 4:11)185.

6. Let us now see how Abraham was the father of many nations. Clearly it is of the Jews, according to the descent of the flesh. But if, in explaining the prophecy, we paid attention to carnal descent, we would be forced to misunderstand the oracle; for he is not, according to the flesh, the father of us all. However, the example of his faith made us all children of Abraham (cf. Rom 4:12). Why so? Among men it is incredible that someone should rise from the dead, just as it is equally incredible that offspring should sprout from a sterile womb. But when it is announced that Christ, who was crucified on the tree, rose from the dead, we believe it. By the likeness of faith we become adopted children of Abraham. And then, after faith, we receive the spiritual seal. We are circumcised at the washing by means of the Holy Spirit, but not in the foreskin but in the heart, according to what Jeremiah affirms: "Circumcise yourselves for Yahweh and remove the foreskins from your hearts" (Jer 4:4) or, according to the Apostle, from whom these expressions are: "By circumcision in Christ... Buried with him in baptism" (Col 2:11-12), etc. Again, the strength of faith

7. If we keep this faith, we will see ourselves free from condemnation and adorned with all kinds of virtues. For faith has power to keep men walking on water. Peter was a man similar to us, made of flesh and blood and fed with the same foods. But when Jesus said to him: "Come," by faith "he began to walk on the water" Rom 4:23: "And the Scripture says not only for him that it was reputed to him, but also for us, to whom faith must be imputed...". On the events of the OT as a figure or "type" of Christian realities, cf I Cor 10:1-13. Paul's entire conception of Abraham's faith is related to the Christian's faith process. If we look at Rom 4, we see that like Abraham, the Christian receives, in the kerygma and in the process of catechization leading to baptism, a promise to which, like Abraham, he responds with faith. The circumcision that Abraham receives when his faith has been sufficiently proven, is an image, that is, also a "seal" (the sphragis of the New Testament and the catechisms of Cyril) of the baptismal sign or the sacramental "character" of baptism, which has already been spoken of so many times. Ultimately, the process of Christianization of man until the seal of baptism becomes active in him is no faster than the mature habit of faith in Abraham. (/Mt/14/29-31), having on them a firmer foundation than any other in faith; the weight of the body was suppressed by the agility of faith. And while he believed, he walked with firm steps on the waters; but when he doubted, he began to sink (14:30). By moving away and gradually diminishing faith, he was dragged to the bottom. When Jesus realized the difficulty, he, who is able to heal the intimate afflictions of the soul, exclaimed: "O man of little faith, why did you doubt?" (14.31). And with the strength of him, who took his right hand, with which he recovered his faith, led by this hand by the Lord, he continued walking on the waters as before. The Gospel indirectly speaks of the latter when it states: "They got into the boat..." (14:32). It does not say that Peter climbed up after swimming, but it insinuates that he walked the distance he traveled to Jesus and, after crossing it again, got into the boat.

8. Faith has so much energy to not only save those who believe, but also to save each other through the faith of others. Well, that paralytic from the city of Capernaum did not have faith, but those who transported him or introduced him through the roof did have faith. The soul of the sick person suffered the illness together with the body. Do not think that I am afraid that he will accuse me, for the same Gospel says: "Jesus seeing," not his faith, but "their faith, says to the paralytic: Get up."186 Those who carried him (the paralytic) were those who believed and healing came to the one who was paralyzed187. Some have been saved by the faith of others

9. Do you want to know even more surely that some are saved by the faith of others?: Lazarus died and one day, a second day and a third had passed; The dead man's nerves had weakened and putrefaction was already taking its toll on his body. How could he believe a four-day dead man and beg for a liberator? But what the deceased lacked in life, his sisters made up for. Well, one of them, when the Lord arrived, bowed at his feet and, when he said: "Where have you put him?" and she replied: "It has already stinked for four days", he exclaimed: "If you believe, you will see the glory of God" (Jn 11:17 ff). It is as if he were saying: take the place of the dead when it comes to faith. And the faith of the sisters was so powerful as to remove the dead man from the jaws of Hadeas. Thus, having faith in one another, they were able to raise the dead. And you, having faith in yourself, will you not benefit much more? But if you have no faith, or little faith, the Lord is gracious to become kind to you when you are converted. With simplicity and from the heart, simply say: "I believe, Lord, help my unbelief" (Mk 9:23). But if you believe that you have faith, even if it is still imperfect, it is necessary that you also say with the Apostles: "Lord, increase our faith" (cf. Luke 17:5). Well, you already have something in you, but you will receive something of the much that is contained in it. "Objective" faith together with faith as an attitude

10. By name faith is unique, but it is actually of two kinds. There is a kind of faith that refers to dogmas, which includes the elevation and approval of the soul with respect to some Mt 9,2. In fact, in the aforementioned verse, Jesus' words to the paralytic are: "Take heart, son, your sins are forgiven!" The words "Get up, get on your mat, and go home" appear in v. 6, after Jesus' controversy with those around him. Not all codices seem to attribute paragraph 8 to the text of the catechesis of Cyril of Jerusalem, but, at least in part of the paragraph, to a commentary by Cyril of Alexandria on the fourth gospel. But here the paragraph is transcribed following the state of the text as it appears in PG 33,515 (cf ibid, note 1). affair. This brings usefulness to the soul, as the Lord says: "He who hears my Word and believes in him who sent me has eternal life and does not incur judgment" (Jn 5:24) and, furthermore: "He who believes in him (in the Son) is not judged" (Jn 3:18), "but has passed from death to life" (Jn 5:24)188. Oh great goodness of God towards men! The righteous pleased God with the work of many years. But what they achieved by striving in the service of God for a long time, this Jesus grants to you in the narrow margin of a single hour. If you believe that Jesus Christ is Lord (Cf. Rom 10,9; Phil 2,11) and that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved (Rom 10,9; cf. Rom 1,4 ff; cf. I Cor 12,3) and you will be taken to paradise by the one who brought the good thief into it (Lk 23,43). And you do not distrust that this can be done, because the one who saved the thief on this holy Golgotha ​​after a single hour's faith, the same one will save you too as long as you believe. The charismas that spring from faith

11. But there is another kind of faith, which is given by Christ by granting certain gifts. «For to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom; to another, the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit; to another, faith, in the same Spirit; to another, charismas of healing...» (1 Cor 12,8,9). This faith, given as a grace by the Spirit, is not only dogmatic, but creates possibilities that exceed human forces. But whoever has this faith will say "to this mountain: 'Move from here to there,' and it will move" (Mt 17:20). And when someone, when saying this, "believes that what he says will happen" "and does not waver in his heart" (Mk 11:23), he will receive that grace. Of this faith it is said: "If you have faith like a mustard seed" (Mt 17:20). For the mustard seed is very small in volume, but endowed with a force like fire and, planted in a narrow space, it makes large branches grow and develops, being able to shelter the birds of the air (cf. Mt 13:32). In the same way, faith also works great things in the soul in very quick moments. Well, once the light of faith has been infused into him, he makes an image about God and thinks about what he is like to the extent that he can understand him. It encompasses the ends of the earth and, before the consummation of this world, already sees the judgment and the granting of the promised goods. Have, then, this faith that is in you and refers to him, so that from him you may also receive that which is in him and that acts above human forces189. The confession of faith in the Symbol

12. When learning and confessing the faith190, you must embrace and keep as such only that which is now delivered to you by the Church with the protective fence of all Scripture. But, since not everyone can read the Scriptures - some are prevented by inexperience and others by their occupations - so that the soul does not perish through ignorance, we summarize the entire dogma of faith in a few verses. I want all of you to remember it with those same words and to recite it to you in When Cyril has indicated that "there is a kind of faith that refers to dogmas", that faith is conceived as the act by which whoever believes confidently places himself in the hands of God and accepts everything that he manifests, in addition to trusting him with his existence. This second aspect is underlined by the three quotes from the Gospel of John that appear shortly below. In paragraph 11, faith will be understood, although related to the previous one, rather the fact that God freely distributes his gifts for the good of all. These and other aspects spring from the unique trunk of faith. The language of catechesis seems to imply that the charismas, perhaps because of what is often extraordinary about them, are as if "more difficult" and as if they depended on God to a greater extent than "dogmatic faith." Naturally, this would require greater precision of language. Here by "faith" we must understand the Creed or symbol of faith that must be memorized for redditio or return. your interior with all interest, but not writing it on tablets, but recording it by heart in your heart191. And when you think about this and meditate on it, be careful that nowhere does anyone of the catechumens hear what has been given to them. I charge you that you receive this faith as a viaticum for the entire time of your life and that, outside of it, you do not receive any other: even if we ourselves underwent a change, and spoke things contrary to what we now teach or even if a contrary angel, transformed into an angel of light (cf. 2 Cor 11:14), wanted to mislead you. For "even if we ourselves or an angel from heaven were to announce to you a gospel other than that which we have announced to you, let it be anathema!" (Gal 1,8)192. The faith that you are now hearing in simple words, retain it in your memory; considers when appropriate, in the light of the Holy Scriptures, the content of each of its statements.

This sum of faith has not been composed by men arbitrarily, but, having selected the most important statements from all of Scripture, they compose and give content to a single doctrine of faith193. And just as the mustard seed develops numerous branches from a tiny grain, so this faith also encompasses in a few words, as in a womb, all the knowledge of piety contained in both the Old and the New Testament. Therefore, brothers, consider and preserve the traditions that you now receive and engrave them in the depth of your heart (cf. 2 Thes 2:15). At this moment Cyril seems to give the Symbol, but it is transcribed after completely finishing the catechism and separately. The Jerusalem Symbol is not found directly in the text of the catechesis. Jealously guard the faith that is given in the Symbol

13. Piously watch that the enemy nowhere attacks anyone because they are passive or lazy; Let no heretic corrupt anything that has been given to them. Because faith194 is like money that we had lent them and that is returned to the lender. But God will ask them for a reason for the deposit. I "conjure you," as the Apostle says, "in the presence of God, who gives life to all things, and of Jesus Christ, who bore such solemn testimony before Pontius Pilate, to preserve without stain this faith which has been delivered to you until the Manifestation of our Lord Jesus Christ"195. The prohibition of the material writing of the Creed, frequently insisted upon in the first centuries of Christianity, was done to prevent it from falling into pagan hands. The content of the creed was also part of the discipline of the arcana and should not even be shown to the catechumens, considered here as such those who had not reached the catechesis on the Symbol. "Anathema" can mean "target of curse." Cyril adds "for you" (: "... be anathema to you"). Paul insistently insists on the idea in 1:9. It can also be understood as "teaching of the faith", which seems to clearly understand that the creed and dogmatics are a source of teaching, didaskalia, of the faith. Perhaps it can be understood as "the Symbol of Faith" or the Creed, but perhaps rather the proclamation of the Creed as a profession of the faith that one has come to have. He quotes above all 1 Tim 6:13-14, but the "conjuration" belongs to 5:21 and the "preserve", in plural, is an adaptation to the plurality of listeners of the catechesis. The "Manifestation" (epifaneia) is a term to express the coming in glory of Jesus Christ at the end of history, which Paul and wide circles of the early Church believed perhaps chronologically close. «Manifestation that in due time will make evident the Blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and the Lord of lords, the only one who possesses immortality, who dwells in an inaccessible light, whom no human being has seen nor can see. To him honor and power forever. Amen". (1 Tim 6,15-16) JEROSOLIMITAN SYMBOL The holy and apostolic faith, given to those who are to be enlightened so that they can confess it196. I. We believe197 in one God198, Father199 almighty200, author of heaven and earth 201, of everything visible and invisible202. II.

And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only Son of God 203, born of the Father and true God before all ages, through whom all things were made204. III. That he came in flesh205 and became man from a Virgin and by the work of the Holy Spirit206. IV. He was crucified and buried207. V. He rose again on the third day208. VI. And he ascended into heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father209. VII And he will come in glory210 to judge the living and the dead211: his kingdom will have no end212. VIII. And in the Holy Spirit Paraclete213, who spoke through the prophets214. This Symbol of Faith or Creed is deduced from different places in Cyril's catechesis. It is the result of the elaboration explained in Migne PG 33,533-535. On the editorial vicissitudes of the present version, cf ibid., 523-531. The designation "apostolic" shows that the contents of the faith expressed here coincide, although the formulation may seem different, with those that the apostles preached. The biblical quotations added in Migne are also respected here, except for some secondary retouching. Cf Jn 14,1. Is 45,18; 1 Cor 8,6. Rom 8:15-16. For example, Jer 32:19. Cf. Ps 136. Gen 1:1-2:25 contains the two classic accounts of creation. Cf. Col I,16. Jn 1,18; 3.16. Particularly illustrative is Jn 1:1-2; cf. I Jn 1,1. 1 Jn 4,2. Cf Lk 1,35. Cf 1 Cor 15,3-4. Experts generally agree that I Cor 15:3-4 most likely transcribes a confession of faith prior to the writing of the letter. From this it would be clearly deduced that the custom of fixing or gathering in the creeds or symbols of faith ("symbol" = concept = meeting or compendium) the essential Christian affirmations dates back to the most ancient times of the Church. Apart from the evangelical stories, cf. 1 Cor 15. Mc 16,19. Cf Acts 1,9. Mt 25,31. Cf. 1 Thes 4,16-17 Cf. Lk 1,32. Jn 16,5-15. 2 Pe 1,19-21. IX And ​​in a baptism of conversion215 for the forgiveness of sins. X. And in the Church, one, holy, catholic and apostolic216. XI. And in the resurrection of the flesh217. XII. And in eternal life218. The meaning of "one baptism" in these ancient creeds is that of "one" or "one baptism." The idea that is expressed with this uniqueness is that baptism cannot be received more than once, even if one has subsequently fallen into heresy. It was a serious problem of the ancient Church, in response to which it clearly decided the uniqueness of baptism.

"Baptism of conversion" or penitence expresses that baptism effectively signifies and seals the conversion of man. The so-called "four notes" or characteristics of the Church. Again, I Cor 15. The expression "eternal life", applied to the life of the future world, appears frequently in the NT: for example, Mt 25:46; cf. Jn 5,29; I Cor 15 CATECHESIS VI THE LORDION OF THE ONE GOD Delivered in Jerusalem, "about the monarchy of God" (or the lordship of the only God), based on "I believe in one God", but also dealing "about heresies." The reading is from Is 45,16,17 (LXX): «Be renewed with me, O islands! Israel will be saved by Yahweh with perpetual salvation. "You will never be embarrassed or insulted again." Joint glorification of Father, Son and Holy Spirit

1. Blessed be God, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ (2 Cor 1:3). Blessed also is his Only Begotten Son (Rom 9:5). Every time you think of "God", you think of the "Father", to celebrate in an undivided way the glorification of the Father and the Son together with the Holy Spirit. For the Father does not have one glory and the Son another, but only one and identical glory (and together with the Holy Spirit). And it is really about the only begotten Son of the Father so that, when the Father is glorified, he also communicates the glory to the Son, together with him. For if the glory of the Son springs from the honor of the Father219, in turn, when the Son is glorified, the Father of such goodness is honored with the greatest honor. Praise to the only God

2. But if the mind understands things very quickly, the tongue proceeds laboriously with the words and with the enunciation of intermediate propositions. The eye also encompasses a numerous chorus of stars in one fell swoop, but when someone wants to explain which is the morning star, which is the evening star, or which is each one of them, they need many words. In the same way, thought encompasses, in a very rapid instant, the land, the sea and all the ends of the world; but what is expressed in an instant is only expressed with very broad words. And all of this that we have just explained is a great example, although still poor and weak. For of God we do not say what is due, but rather what each one knows, although it is what human nature perceives and how much our weakness can bear. For we do not say what God is, but we innocently confess that we lack detailed knowledge about him 220; Well, as far as God is concerned, it is great science to confess ignorance. Therefore, "Sing with me to the Lord, let us sing together to his name" (Ps 34:4), all together, since it is not enough for just one to sing. Even if we all meet at the same time, it is not enough for what we have to do. And I am not referring only to those who are here, because even if all the members of the Church were together. Probable borrowing from Prov 17,6 The terms in which Cyril expresses himself here are not excessively precise, but he moves within the scope of what is sometimes described as "negative theology", in view of the fact that we know more about God what he is not than what he is. In any case, the fundamental statement now wants to be this: since what we do not know is infinitely more about God than what we can express, it is good for man to confess his limits in the knowledge of God, that is, the same limitations of the theological office. universal present and future, would not, however, be sufficient to praise the Shepherd according to his dignity. Praise to God from the smallness of man

3. Great and honorable was Abraham, but great for men. And when he approached God, he said naively, confessing the truth: "I am earth and ashes" (Gen 18:27)221. And he did not say "earth", then remaining silent, so that it would not seem that he was referring to something big, but he added "and ashes" to imply something with little solidity and easy to dissolve. Is there anything weaker and weaker than ash? Compare, for example, the ashes with a house, and the house with a city, the city with a province, the province with the territory of the Romans and the territory of the Romans with the entire world and, finally, the entire earth, with all its details, with the sky that envelops it in its lap: in proportion to the sky, the earth is like the center of a wheel compared to its entire extension. Such is the comparison between earth and heaven. But, furthermore, the sky we observe is the first, which is less important than the second, and this less than the third. These are what Scripture called heavens222, but this does not mean that this is their exact number. But even if you perceived all the heavens with your intelligence, even they would not be enough to praise God as he is, and not even if they resounded louder than thunder. But if all the greatness of the heavens is not capable of celebrating God as much as he deserves, can "the earth and the ashes", the smallest and most meager of all things, be able to sing to God a hymn worthy of him or speak with dignity of the God who "sits on the terrestrial globe, whose inhabitants are like grasshoppers" (Is 40:22)?

4. Whoever tries to talk about God, first expose the limits of the earth. You inhabit the earth, but you do not know the limits of this earth that is your home: how can you understand its author properly within yourself? You see the stars, but not their author. First list those that you can see and then you will know the invisible one, who "counts the number of the stars, and calls each one by name" (Ps 147:4). The water recently fallen in heavy rains made us lost; Now count the drops that have fallen in this city. But I'm not saying in this city: count, if you can, those that fell on your roof for an hour. No, you can't: recognize your helplessness. From there you will learn the power of God: "He attracts223 the drops of water" (Job 36:27), which are spilled throughout the world and not only in this one but at all times. God's work is the sun, really something big, but minimal when compared to the entire sky. Well, look first towards the sun and then, with more curiosity, seek the Lord. «Do not seek what is deeper nor investigate what is stronger than you: limit yourself to knowing what has been commanded you» (Eccl 3,22 LXX). In the original Greek text, "earth" rather than dust, which would perhaps be a better biblical version. But "earth" is more suitable for the continuation of Cyril's speech. The apostle Paul, referring to his personal experiences, relates in 2 Cor 12:2: «I know of a man in Christ, who fourteen years ago... was caught up to the third heaven. The Jerusalem Bible adds: "That is, to the highest of heaven." In general, Paul and Cyril in our text use ancient cosmology, generally geocentric, to describe what interests them. In the present catechesis these digressions are used simply to explain the smallness of the human being (cf. Ps 8:4-5), for which the starting point was Abraham's expression in Gen 18:27. In Cyril's text, "numbers" or "counts" instead of "attracts" what best adapts to what is being exposed. The Son and the Holy Spirit know the Father and reveal him

6. Some will say: Is it not written: "The angels (of children) always see the face of my Father who is in heaven" (cf. Mt 18:10). But the angels see God, not as he is, but insofar as they can grasp him224. For Jesus himself is the one who says: «No one has seen the Father, except he who has come from God; He sees the Father" (Jn 6:46). The angels see it as far as they are capable and, as far as they can, the archangels 225 and, in a more excellent way than the first, also the thrones and dominions, to whom they are inferior in dignity. In reality, only the Holy Spirit can, together with the Son, see God as he is. For "he searches everything and knows everything, even to the depths of God" (I Cor 2:10); so that it is true that even the only begotten Son, as appropriate, also knew the Father together with the Holy Spirit, since it says: "No one knows the Father well except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son wants to reveal him" (Mt 11:27). He sees God, as he should, and reveals him, with the Holy Spirit and through the Holy Spirit, to each one according to his ability. On the other hand, the Son also participates in divine eternity, together with the Holy Spirit, who "from all eternity" (2 Tim 1:9) was begotten without effort and knew the Father, the begetter knowing the begotten. But, as for the angels, their knowledge being limited - for as we said, it is the Only Begotten who, according to his ability, reveals to them (God) together with and through the Holy Spirit, that no man should be ashamed to confess his ignorance. Now I am speaking and anyone else will do so in due course, but we cannot express in words how all this happens: how could I explain the one who gave us the power to speak? I have a soul, but I cannot clarify its characteristics. To whom he granted me my soul, how can I explain it? There is only one, eternal and infinite God. Properties of God

7. For our piety, only one thing is enough: to know that we have God: the only God, the God who exists from eternity, without any variation in himself, unbegotten, stronger than any other and whom no one expels from his kingdom. It is designated by multiple names, it can do everything and remains unchanged in its substance. And not because he is called good, just, omnipotent, "God of hosts"226, he is therefore variable and diverse, but, being one and the same, he performs innumerable divine operations. And he does not have more of one part and less of another, but in all things he is like himself. He is not only great in goodness, but inferior in wisdom, but he is similar in wisdom and goodness. Nor is it that he partly sees and partly is deprived of vision, but rather that he sees everything, hears everything, and understands everything. It is not that, like us, he partly understands things and partly ignores them: this way of speaking is blasphemous and unworthy of the divine personality. It knows in advance what exists, is holy and exercises its power over everything; He is better, greater and wiser than all things. The reader may have certain doubts here as to whether Cyril admits with certainty, or to what extent, what the faith of the Church later affirmed with absolute certainty about the intuitive vision of God (that is, "as he is", without intermediaries or images). But this interpretative doubt does not prevent the general understanding of this paragraph 6. Of course, intuitive or direct vision of God does not mean that any creature, not even angels, grasps everything that God is. "God of hosts": this is how the expression "Sabaoth" is translated here, transcribed from Hebrew by Cyril in the same Greek text, as in the Latin liturgy the expression "Dominus Deus Sabaoth" ("Lord God of hosts") was preserved until the liturgical reform of Vat. II, but which has its origin in the vision of Isaiah in his vocation (Is 6:3). form or figure. For "you have never heard his voice, nor have you ever seen his face," says the Scripture (Jn 5:37). Therefore Moses also says to the Israelites: "Be very careful of yourselves, since you did not see any figure" (Dt 4:15)9. For if the mind cannot imagine something that resembles it227, can it perhaps penetrate into what is proper to its person? Errors about God

8. Many imagined many things, but they all made mistakes. Some thought that fire is God (cf. Wisdom 13:2), others that God is like a winged man because of what is written: "Hide me in the shadow of your wings" (Ps 17:8)228. They have forgotten our only begotten Lord Jesus Christ who, referring to himself, cries out in an identical way to Jerusalem: "How many times have I wanted to gather your children, as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and you have not wanted to!" (Mt 23,37). For by indicating with the name of the wings the power of someone who protects, these, in a misunderstanding and falling into human habits, valued in the human way the one who is inscrutable. Others did not hesitate to point out seven eyes to him, because of what is written: "The seven eyes of the Lord, looking over all the earth" (Zech 4,10, LXX); but if the seven eyes were placed around him differently, God would see things in part, but not totally. But to say this about him would be blasphemous and insulting. For it must be believed that God is perfect in everything, according to that word of the Savior: "Your heavenly father is perfect" (Mt 5:48): perfect in seeing, perfect in his power, perfect in his greatness, perfect in his foreknowledge, perfect in goodness, perfect in justice, perfect in kindness: not limited to one place, but the author of places; existing in all places, but not limited to any. "The heavens are my throne" - and the one who stands out is the one who sits - "and the earth is my footstool" (Is 66:1; cf. Acts 7:49). His power reaches, however, to the lower regions of the earth. The greatness of God, source and origin through Christ of all reality

9. He is the only one who is present everywhere, seeing everything, understanding everything, building everything through Christ. For "everything was made through him, and without him nothing was made that exists" (Jn 1:3; cf. Col 1:15 ff). He is the maximum and indeficient source of all good, river of benefits, eternal light that shines without ceasing, insurmountable strength destined for our weaknesses, whose name we cannot even hear. Job says: "Do you intend to reach the depths of God, to reach the perfection of the Almighty?" (Job 11:7). If not even his great and small works can be covered, can he who did it all be covered? "What eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has it entered into the heart of man what God has prepared for those who love him" (Is 64:3, quoted according to I Cor 2:9). If what God has prepared exceeds the capacity of our thoughts, can we perhaps include in our minds the one who prepared it? «O abyss of wealth, wisdom and knowledge of God! How unfathomable are his designs and his ways untraceable! » says the Apostle (Rom 11:33). And if his judgments and his ways cannot be understood, can he himself be understood? Dt 4:15-16 points out: "Be very careful of yourselves: since you did not see any figure on the day that Yahweh spoke to you at Horeb out of the midst of the fire, do not go perverted and make them any sculpture of any representation whatsoever: male or female figure." The prohibition aims to prevent the deification of human works as idols. In Cyril's catechesis it appears in the context that God is infinitely greater than any representation that can be made of him. Cf cat. 9, no. 1. Various types of idolatry

10. God being, therefore, as great, and even more so229; Since the good and great God is so immense, man is not afraid to say to a stone sculpted by him: "You are my god" (Is 44:17)230. "Great blindness, that from such majesty fell into such great indignity and vileness!" Tree that God made, grown with the rains and then, burned by fire, turns into ashes; and this, I say, they call god, while the true God is despised231. The perversity of idolatry has flourished. Even the cat, the dog and the wolf have been worshiped as if they were God; and also the lion, devourer of men, has been worshiped instead of the God who loves them so much. The serpent and the dragon have also been worshiped, emulators of the one who threw us out of paradise, while the one who created paradise has been despised. Even—it's embarrassing to say it, but I'll say it—some have worshiped the onion. Wine has been given to gladden the heart of man (cf. Ps 104:15). Well, instead of God, Bacchus is worshiped232. God made wheat saying: "Let the earth produce vegetation: herbs that bear seeds and fruit trees that bear fruit, of their kind, with their seed inside, on the earth" (Gen 1,111)233, with the intention that the bread would strengthen the heart of man. Why, then, has Ceres been worshiped? Fire is also lit to this day by the collision of two stones. Why, then, is Vulcan considered the creator of fire? Idolatry, polytheism and errors about God

11. And where did the Greeks' error of admitting a plurality of gods come from? God is incorporeal. Whence, then, are rapes and adulteries imputed to those whom they call gods? 234. I do not mention the transmutations of Jupiter into a swan; and I blush when I refer to the transformations into gold, because the anointed are unworthy of God. The god of the Greeks has been considered convicted of adultery, but if he is, let him not be called God. They also tell of those whom they call their gods, their deaths, their disasters and their fulminations. Do you see what so much majesty has come to? Wasn't the reason why the Son of God descended from heaven to heal so many wounds real? Was the coming of the Son to know the Father in vain? 5. God is abusively considered the father of many things, but by nature and in truth he is the Father of his only Son, our Lord Jesus Christ. CATECHESIS VIII OMNIPOTENCE AND PROVIDENCE OF GOD Delivered in Jerusalem, on the word "almighty" (who has everything under his power).
