Fundamental theme: the omnipotence of God, provident Father

1. Because we believe in one God, we reject all error about a plurality of gods, using these weapons against the Gentiles and against all the resistance of the heretics. But by adding “one God the Father,” we fight against those who come from circumcision, who deny the Only Begotten Son of God. Well, as was said yesterday, even before we explain what refers to our Lord Jesus Christ, simply by having said Father, we already wanted to indicate that he is the Father of the Son. Thus, in the same way that we understood that God exists, let us also think that he has a Son. But to this we now add that he is all-powerful (that he has all things under his power). We affirm this for the sake of the Gentiles, the Jews and the heretics. God, present and active in everything

2. For some of the Gentiles said that God is the soul of the world. Others, for their part, said that he only has power over the heavens, but this does not reach down to the earth. Some also, carried away by a similar error, perverting the meaning of "O Yahweh, your love in the heavens, your truth to the clouds" (Ps 35:5)256, limited the providence of God to the clouds and the sky, but alienating from God what is on earth. They forgot the psalm: "If I ascend to the heavens, there you are; if I lie down in the sun, there you are" (Ps 139:8). For if there is nothing beyond heaven, and since hell is below the earth, surely he who governs what is below also reaches the earth. Various aspects of the power of God

3. But the heretics, on the other hand, as stated above, did not know a single omnipotent God. For omnipotent is he who dominates over all things and has everything subject to his power. And those who say that (God) is lord of the soul, but not of the body, thereby affirm that neither of the two realities is perfect, since each of the two lacks the other. And if someone has power over the soul, but not over the body, why would he be omnipotent? To understand this catechesis, it is important to take into account the surrounding intellectual and religious environment: different statements are made against the Manichaeans, who emphasize the intrinsic evil of at least part of creation, and also against the Arians, who question the equality, in terms of nature and dignity, of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Keep in mind, furthermore, that the statement made that God is "almighty" has in the original Greek the semantic meaning of the one "who dominates over all things" (pantocrator), which in turn facilitates the relationship between omnipotence and God's providence. Cf. also Ps 57:11 and 108:5. And where would be the omnipotence of the one who dominated over bodies, but not over spirits? However, it is true that God declares convicted those of whom he says: "Fear rather the One who is able to destroy soul and body in Gehenna" (Mt 10:28). For if he does not have power over both, how could the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ subject both to punishment? And how can he, invading a body outside his power, deliver it to Gehenna if he does not first bind the strong man to plunder his trousseau?257. God exercises his dominion even allowing the devil's action

4. But the divine Scripture and the dogmas of truth have known a single God, who has many things subject to the rule of his power, but allows many things because he wants to258. For he also exercises his dominion over the worshipers of idols, but he endures them because of his patience; He also has the heretics who reject him under his power, but he tolerates them with his long-suffering. He also has the devil under control, but he accepts it with his tolerance. And he does not suffer from helplessness as if he were defeated (God). Well, from always, (the devil) was also among the creatures of God, who was not the one who deceived him - that would be something unworthy - but other angels, who are also creatures. He allowed him, however, to live for two reasons: so that, upon defeating him, he would feel greater shame and so that men would receive the crown259. Oh providence of God full of wisdom, who assumed that perverse will to grant salvation to those who believed. When he took advantage of the hostile intention of Joseph's brothers to carry out his plans, allowing them to sell his brother out of hatred, he took the opportunity to appoint the governor whom he wanted260. In a similar way he agreed to fight with the devil so that the victors would be crowned; Thus, once the victory was achieved, the devil, defeated by those who are inferior to him, would cover himself with greater shame. Men, on the other hand, would be ennobled in a distinguished way after having defeated the one who had once been an archangel. God also reigns over sinful man

5. Nothing, then, is removed from the power of God. The Scripture says of him: “Everything is his servant” (Ps 119:91). All reality is truly his servant, although in this reality his only Son and his Holy Spirit are not counted261. And all those creatures that are servants serve Vid. Mc 3,27 par.: «But no one can enter the house of the strong and plunder his trousseau, if he does not first bind the strong; then you can plunder your house. The Gospel text, difficult to interpret, must be understood from its context: the devil, even armed with his own strength, can be defeated in man by the power of God, so that the strong one - in this case, the devil - has his prey snatched away (cf. Is 49:24-25). All this, however, seems to be forced into Cyril's text, which in any case applies the passage to the reality of God's omnipotence. With this, a clear distinction is made between what is God's will and what He simply allows. What God allows without being the object of his will can exist both in the field of the physically existing (including here, therefore, also physical evil: illness, etc.) and in that of moral evil (for example, when God allows individual sin or of some men against others). In this case, without God wanting it, allowing it or tolerating it, he knows in the mystery of his designs how he can use for the good of men the evil that he did not want. God's goodness is by nature incompatible with his supposed will for evil. This is originally the question that gives rise to the Theodicy. The crown of victory to his merits. Vine. the entire story of Joseph in Gen 39-48. This affirmation that the Son and the Holy Spirit are placed outside the rest of the servant reality is perhaps intentionally anti-Arian, since it seeks to affirm the equality in dignity of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, without any of these two being subject or subordinate to the Father. to the Lord through the only Son in the Holy Spirit262. God, then, rules over all of them and endures murderers, thieves, and libertines by his patience, so that, having determined the time in which he will give to each one according to his merits after the truce of a lasting time, without having returned their hearts to conversion, they are condemned with greater severity. Kings of men are those who rule in the world, although not without having received power from above (cf. Jn 19:11).
Nebuchadnezzar once experienced this when he said “that his empire is an eternal empire and his power lasts from generation to generation” (Dan 4:31). Right use of money

6. Riches, gold and silver are not from the devil as some think 263. "The entire world of riches belongs to a faithful man, but he who is not faithful does not even have an obol"264. But no one is more unfaithful than the devil, as God clearly said through the prophet: "The silver is mine and the gold is mine!" (Ag 2,8), "and I give it to whomever I want" (Lk 4,6). The only thing you have to do is use it well. You shouldn't criticize money anymore. But when you misuse something that is good without wanting to blame your own administration, you direct your complaint impiously against the creator. "I was hungry and you gave me food" (Mt 25:35): there is no doubt that it was your own riches. "I was naked and you covered me" (Mt 25:36): your money intervened in this. Do you want to know that riches can be the door to the kingdom of heaven?: "Sell what you have, give it to the poor and you will have treasure in heaven" (Mt 19:21). What one possesses is in itself good 265

7. I have said these things because of the heretics, who condemn property, money and bodies to anathema. Well, I neither want you to be a slave to riches nor, on the other hand, to see them as enemies, since they have been given to you by God as help. Therefore, do not go around saying from time to time that the money is from the devil, for even if he says: "I will give you all this because it has been given to me" (Luke 4:6), someone can nevertheless refute even those words, since a liar cannot be believed. Perhaps, however, daunted by the power of whoever was present, he told the truth, since he does not say: "I will give you all this because it is mine," but "because it has been given to me." He did not usurp the property, but rather declared an encomienda and simple administration entrusted to him. Appropriately, the interpreters wonder if he lied or told the truth. Conclusion: the power of the Lord God

8. Therefore, there is only one omnipotent Father God, whom many heretics have dared to attack with insults: they have not been afraid to revile the Lord of hosts who sits on the cherubim266. They have dared to slander the Lord Adonai267 with blasphemies, they were not deterred, Vid. later cat. X, no. 9. A rigorism that considers wealth in itself to be evil is condemned here. Currency worth much less than one cent. The phrase is taken from Prov 17,6 LXX. At least this is one of the issues raised in this issue. 7. Although wealth is completely relativized, it is not condemned in itself, which means that Cyril is very far from what the Cathar movements, etc., will always be in the history of the Church. Cf. Is 6,2-3 (mention of "seraphim"); Salt 80.2. The Adonai formula is above all to address God: "My Lord!" (cf. Gen. 18:3). to insult with them the one whom the voices of the prophets celebrate as almighty God. You, however, worship the one almighty God, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ268. Flee from the error of polytheism; Also escape from any heresy and say, according to what is in the book of Job: «I would appeal to God for myself, I would expose my cause to God. He is the author of great and unfathomable works, of wonders without number" (Job 5,8-9), and that of "honor comes from the Almighty"269, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen. The formula is from Rom 15:6: "... glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ." The edition of PG 33,635 refers here to Job 36,22, which both in the Hebrew Bible and in LXX reads: "Look, God is sublime in his power, who is a master (or: powerful) like him." But it is preferred in this case to leave the text of the catechesis as it is. CATECHESIS IX GOD CREATOR OF ALL THINGS Delivered in Jerusalem about "creator of heaven and earth, of everything visible and invisible." The reading is from Job: "Who is this who tarnishes my plan, retaining the words in his heart and thinking he is hiding from me?" (Jb 38,2 LXX)270. You cannot see God directly in this life

1. It is not possible to see God with the eyes of the flesh: for what is incorporeal cannot enter with these eyes. This was also testified by the only begotten Son of God when he said: “No one has ever seen God.” For even if someone interprets what is written in Ezekiel as if he had a direct vision, listen to what the Scripture says: "He saw the likeness of the glory of the Lord" (Ez 1:28), not to the Lord himself, but to "the likeness of the glory", nor directly to the glory as it really is. But, having beheld only a likeness of glory, but not the glory itself, he fell to the ground for fear (ibid.). But the contemplation of the likeness of glory aroused in the prophets the fear and concern that God would take their lives if anyone tried to contemplate it directly, according to what "man cannot see me and continue to live" (Ex 33:20)271 For this reason God, out of his great goodness, has spread the heavens as a veil of his great goodness so that we do not perish. This word is not mine but the prophet's, who says: "Ah, if you would rend the heavens and come down—the mountains would melt before your face" (Is 63:19). And why do you wonder if Daniel fell to the ground after having contemplated the likeness of glory? On one occasion Daniel saw Gabriel, a servant of God,272 and immediately his spirit was troubled and he fell on his face. The prophet did not hesitate to respond until the angel took the form of a man (cf. Dan 8:17 and 10:15-16). And if Daniel's vision aroused fear in the prophets, would they not all have perished if God himself had allowed himself to be seen as he is? Knowledge of God through creatures

2. We have not been given to know the divine nature with bodily eyes; but through the works of God we can gain an idea of ​​his power, according to what Solomon says: "For from the greatness and beauty of creatures one comes, by analogy, to contemplate their Author" (Wisdom 13:5) 273. He does not simply say that the creator is deduced from creatures, but he added: by analogies274. Well, God's words are a complaint, from the wisdom of the Creator, against the petulance of man. The note from the Jerusalem Bible to this verse is also not wasted on this occasion. The angel Gabriel. Wisdom 13:1-9 is one of the best-known biblical passages that expose the possibility of reaching God through creatures, the fruit of divine power. It is worth remembering that, although Paul uses this way of arguing relatively little, his indications on the matter in Rom 1:19-20 are well known, verses surely inspired by Wisdom 13:1. Wis 13:6 may also have inspired the writing of Acts 1 7:27. More literally: "analogously" or "in an analogous manner", with which, using Cyril an abstract philosophical term, not simple equality or identity between God and creatures is established, but rather analogy, which the Christian philosophical tradition has so well known how to distinguish from univocity and ontological equivocation. God seems all the greater to each one the greater the contemplation of creatures acquired by man. And the more he has subjected his own mind to contemplation, the greater the knowledge and image he has of God himself. It is not possible to fully understand God

3. Do you want to know that it is not possible to encompass the entire nature of God? Those three young men who were on the way to the fire exclaimed, celebrating God with praise: "Blessed are you, who fathom the abysses, who sit on cherubim" (Dan 3:55). And now I ask you: "Tell me what the nature of the cherubim is and then think about what it is like for him to sit on them." For his part, the prophet Ezekiel, as far as possible, gave a description of them saying: "They each had four faces" (Ez 1:6): the first, that of a man; the second, of a lion; the third, an eagle; the last, of a bull (cf. Ezek 1,10). Also "each one had six wings" (Is 6:2) and eyes on all sides, and they moved as on a wheel in four directions (cf. Ezek 10:11-12). However, even after this description of the prophet, we cannot understand everything through reading. For if we cannot even comprehend the throne which he has described, how can we comprehend the invisible and ineffable God who sits upon it? It is certainly impossible to intimately scrutinize the nature of God, but glory and honor can be paid to the one we know through his works. Again, the true relationship between God the Father and God the Son

4. These things are said to you in the consecutive and orderly manner of faith275. And since we say: "We believe in one God, the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth, of everything visible and invisible," we thus remember that he is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ and that he is the same one who made heaven and earth276. In this way we are protected against the deviations of heretics alien to God, who have dared to insult the most wise creator of all this world: they see with the eyes of the flesh, but are deprived of the understanding of the mind. God's foresighted wisdom in creating

5. What do you have to criticize in this greatest work of God? They should have been filled with amazement when contemplating the celestial curvatures, thus worshiping him who made the sky as a vault and from the fluid nature of the waters formed the substance of the sky. For God said: "Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters" (Gen 1:6). God said it only once and it remains without falling. The sky is water, but the beings nailed to it, the sun, the moon and the stars, are made of fire. But how do these igneous beings move in water?277 If anyone has doubts because of It refers to the order in which the statements of the Creed are found. By reaffirming the reality of God as "Father of our Lord Jesus Christ", insisting once again, at the same time, that he is the creator of everything, the Christological and Trinitarian teaching of Nicea is once again highlighted. It is worth noting, when it comes to understanding what Cyril's catechesis teaches about creation, that one thing is the fundamental affirmation contained in the two accounts of the creation of the book of Genesis (in 1,1-2,4a and 2,4b-25) that the world does not have its origin in itself, but in God, and another different issue is the way in which the description of the universe is made in those same chapters and, in general, in ancient authors, biblical or extrabiblical, or in the Christian authors of antiquity themselves. The exposition of the universe, as is also the case of Cyril, places the earth and not the sun at the center. The sun, moon and stars, in this same painting, are little more than mere very interesting decorations of the "cosmos." However, this does not in any way invalidate the biblical affirmation of the contrary natures of fire and water, remember the fire that, in the time of Moses, burned in the midst of the hail (cf. Ex 9:23) and consider the most wise disposition of God in creation. Well, since the waters were necessary for the further progress of the earth, he prepared a sky of water at the highest point so that, when the celestial regions needed irrigation by rain, the sky would be prepared and disposed for it by its nature. The admirable order of the universe, the seasons and the world

6. So what? Shouldn't we be amazed at the construction of the sun? For, appearing with the modesty of a vessel, it contains enormous energy: appearing in the East, it emits light to the West. The psalmist said, describing his morning outings: "And he, like a bridegroom coming out of his bedchamber" (Ps 19). The way, at once splendid and gentle, in which it begins to shed its light on men was sweetly described. And when the sun is in the middle of the day, we often flee from it because of the excessive heat, but at its rise it has made everyone happy when it makes its appearance as "the husband." Consider the position of the sun, which is completely appropriate, although it has not been established by him himself, but rather by the one who determined its course with his command. In summer it is at its maximum height, the days become longer, giving men the opportunity to do their jobs. In winter, however, it limits its range, so that the cold season is not prolonged but rather that the nights, becoming longer, help men to rest and so that the earth produces its fruits. See also how the days follow one another in the proper order: they lengthen in summer and shorten in winter, but in spring and autumn days of similar length become pleasant; and they make the nights the same way. Of all of them the psalmist says: "Day to day delivers the message, and night to night delivers the news" (Ps 19:2). It is as if they cried out before some heretics who do not want to hear and, in the midst of their admirable order, they said that there is no other God than the one who created and arranged the confines of the world, putting everything in order. The wise rhythm of day and night

7. Let no one mention those who say that one is the creator of light and another is the creator of darkness278. Remember the words of Isaiah: “I (Yahweh) shape light and create darkness” (Is 45:7). Why then are you angry with these? Why do you endure so badly the time that has been given to you as a rest? The servant would not get any rest from his work from his masters if the darkness of the night did not bring him respite. And how is it that so often, tired from the day's work, it is at night that we recover? And the one who worked the day before, in the morning appears robust and agile from the night's rest. And what better than night to lead to wisdom? For we meditate on it very often when it comes to God; In it we dedicate ourselves to reading and contemplating the divine oracles. When does our mind strive most tenaciously to sing the psalms or to pour out our supplications?279. Isn't it when it's night? And when, if not at night, do we remember fundamentally, which is also true here of Cyril as of the entire Christian tradition: the universe owes its origin to something greater and different from it, which we call "God." Again, the Manichaeans, and again an allusion to their conception of the eternal struggle between the two also eternal and antagonistic principles of good and evil. It may be a simple allusion to the environmental ease of addressing God in prayer and in the silence of the night, but it is also very likely that Cyril had in his mind the prayer vigils, frequent in the Palestinian churches of his time (cf. PG 33,646, note 7). our sins more frequently? Let us not admit, therefore, perversely, that there is another author for darkness, since experience shows that they are also good and very useful. The light of the stars, the sun and the moon

8. It would be appropriate for these (those mentioned) to be amazed and admire not only the greatness of the sun and the moon, but also the orderly dances and free movement of the stars, which nothing disturbs as long as each one of them appears at the opportune moment. And how some are a sign of summer and others of winter: some indicate the beginning of sowing and others that of the sailing season. And it is precisely the navigator, who moves in the immensities of extensive waves, who directs his ship by observing the stars. Of all this Scripture clearly says: "Let there be stars in the heavenly firmament, to separate the day from the night, and let them serve as signs for solemnities, days and years" (Gen 1:14), but not for fables about astrology and genealogy280. Also notice how beautifully God is giving us the light of day little by little. Well, we do not see the sun rising suddenly, but first a limited light appears so that, by preparing the pupils, they can capture the increasing strength of the sun's rays. Also consider how it mitigates the darkness of the night with the softness of the moon's glow. God, Lord of the elements and natural phenomena

9. Who is the father of rain? Who made the dew drops? Who concentrated the vapor in the clouds, ordering them to hold the water of the storms? And doesn't it make clouds dressed in an aerial radiance approach from the north, while depending on the moment it makes their appearance and shape change into figures different from the world or from any other genre? Who is there who can knowingly number the clouds? It is said about this in the book of Job: «Who has the skill to number the clouds? Who tilts the wineskins of heaven? (Job 38,37). And that other thing: "He counts the clouds with his wisdom" (26,8 LXX) and the clouds are not "an opaque veil" for him (cf. Job 22,14). A large amount of water is contained in the clouds, but they do not break, since they fall to the ground in perfect order. Who is it that brings the winds out of their deposits? (cf. Ps 135,7). Who is it, as we said before, that produces the dew drops? (cf. Job 38:28). What uterus does ice come from? (38,29). Because, although it is a watery substance, it has the properties of stone. Sometimes even water becomes "snow like wool", but other times it submits to the will of the one who "spreads the frost like ashes" (Ps 147:16). But sometimes it turns into a stone substance. And of course he subjects and governs the water according to his will. The nature of water is unique, but it is endowed with multiple power and effectiveness. The water in the vines is wine that gladdens the heart of man, in the olive trees it is oil that gives shine to the face of man and bread that strengthens the heart of man (cf. Ps 104:15), as it is also capable of becoming all kinds of fruits. Tit 3:9 expressly recommends avoiding “foolish discussions and genealogies”; Perhaps the warning in 2 Tim 3:7 against some "who are always learning and are not able to come to the full knowledge of the truth" refers to similar issues. Paul's frequent allusions to the pseudo-religious environment, especially in Col 2, reflect the environment in which the New Testament Church had to develop, in which very different conceptions of the divine competed and in which it was very easy to see oneself simply in an atmosphere of widespread relativism. This atmosphere still persists in late antiquity in the middle of the 4th century, when Cyril's catechisms were delivered. Variety of creation

10. Given this, what should be done? Should we utter insults against the Maker of the world or should we rather worship Him? And I do not speak of the hidden things of his wisdom. Rather, I would like you to contemplate spring, retaining the variety of its flowers that are all the same and at the same time different: the purple of the rose and the sublime whiteness of the lily. Well, although both come from the same rain and the same soil, who is it that makes them different and builds them? I would also like you to consider what skill of the sole craftsman it is that makes trees of the same kind sometimes serve to provide shade and sometimes to spread different fruits. One part of the vine is destined for burning, another to become shoots, another to foliage, another to forks and, finally, a last to grapes. Also be amazed, in a reed, at the breadth of space that its author put between its knots. In the same terrain, snakes, donkeys, trees, food, gold, silver, copper, iron, stone emerge. One is the substance of the waters, and from them come the species of fish and birds, so that some swim in the water while the birds fly in the air. The immensity of the sea, dominated by the Creator

11. "There is the sea, great and with wide arms, and in it, the innumerable teeming with animals, large and small" (Ps 104, 25). Who can expose the beauty of the fish that live there? Who the magnitude of cetaceans or the nature of amphibian animals that live both on arid land and in water? Who can explain the depth and depth of the sea or the immense force of the waves? He remains, however, within the limits set for him by the one who told him: "You will reach this point, no further..., here the pride of your waves will be broken" (Job 38:11). The mandate imposed on him is clearly explained by the fact that the waves, when they retreat, leave a visible line on the shores. Those who see it are thus indicated that the sea will not go beyond the established limits. The sublime flight of birds

12. Who can capture the nature of the birds of the sky? How is it that some have a tongue that is expert in singing, while others have a great variety of colors in their feathers and some, like birds of prey, remain, in mid-flight, motionless in the air? For it is by God's command that "the falcon takes flight, spreads its wings toward the south" (Job 9:26). What man perceives how "the eagle soars" to "the heights" (39,27). For if with all your ability to think you cannot realize how the birds rise high, how then can you encompass with your mind the author of all things? Diversity and teachings from the animal world

13. Who has simply known the names of all the wild animals? And who has realized the nature of each of them and their strength? But if we don't even know their names, how can we understand their author? One was the precept of God, by which he said: "Let the earth bring forth living animals of every kind: beasts, serpents, and terrestrial vermin of every kind" (Gen 1:24). By a single command, the various kinds of animals sprang up, as from a single source: the meekest sheep, the butcher lion. For their part, diverse movements of irrational animals reflect a variety of human inclinations: the fox, for example, expresses human perfidy; the snake, those who hurt their friends with poisonous darts; the horse that neighs, to voluptuous young people281. However, the diligent ant serves to stimulate the negligent and the lazy. For when someone, in his youth, lives in apathy and idleness, the same irrational animals stimulate him according to the same reproach recorded in Scripture: "Go where the ant, lazy one, look at his wanderings and you will become wise" (Prov 6,6). Well, when you see that she stores food for the opportune time, imitate her and collect for yourself as treasures, for the future life, the fruits of good works. On the other hand: "Get to work and learn what a worker she is" (Prov 6,8 LXX)282. Observe how, going through all kinds of flowers, it produces honey for your service, so that you too, going through the Holy Scriptures, may obtain your eternal salvation and, satisfied by them, say: "How sweet is your promise to my palate, sweeter than honey to my mouth!" (Ps 119,103). Diverse qualities of wild animals

14. Is not the Creator worthy of all praise? Or is it that, because you do not know the nature of all things, must created beings be useless? Can you, perhaps, come to know the qualities of all herbs? Or are you able to learn the usefulness of what comes from any animal? Well, it is true that even poisonous vipers come from certain antidotes for the health of mortals. But you will tell me: snakes are a horrible thing. Fear the Lord and he cannot harm you. The scorpion gains strength when it stings: fear the Lord and it will not sting you. The lion is thirsty for blood: fear the Lord—as Daniel once did (Dan 6:23)—and (the lion) will remain calm with you. The strength of the animals themselves is truly to be admired: some stab with their sting, while the strength of others resides in their teeth; There are those who fight with their claws; Finally, the strength of the basilisk lies in its gaze. By the various qualities of his work you can, therefore, understand the capacity of the Creator. The same wonder of the human body

15. But there is another thing that you do not know: there is something very different between yourself and the animals that are outside of you, because you can enter within yourself and know the Creator by your own nature. For what is there in your body that is worthy of rebuke? Practice continence and nothing in your limbs will be bad. At first Adam is naked in paradise together with Eve. For its members, of course, it was not worthy of disgrace or rejection. Therefore, the cause of sin is not the members, but those who misuse them283. Wise is, however, the one who created the members. Who is the one who prepared the space of the womb for the procreation of children? Who gave life in him to the inanimate fetus? Who made the connection of the nerves and bones and surrounded them with skin and flesh? Who has made it so that, as soon as it is born, the child takes milk from its mother's breasts as from its source? How is it converted? Somewhat distantly, there could be an allusion here to Jr 5:8 and its context. Referring to the comparison with the activity of bees. After the description of the fall, Gen 3:7 points out that “then both of their eyes were opened, and they realized that they were naked; and sewing fig leaves together they made girdles." The evident intention of the sacred text is to make present that it is precisely because of the sin that is in man that he is tempted to misuse the entire created reality, including his own body. But neither his body nor his members are inherently bad. infant into child and the child into a young man, later into a man and, finally, he himself becomes an old man, without anyone being able to notice that it is at precise moments when these changes occur? How is part of the food converted into blood, part integrated into the flesh itself, and part discarded? Who is it that makes the heart move with continuous movement? Who so wisely protected the softness of the eyes with the movement of the eyelids? For certainly the great books of doctors hardly dealt sufficiently with the admirable structure of the eyes. Who made the distribution of the breath throughout the body? You see there, oh man, the wisdom of the author who made it all284. Conclusion: God from his works

16. Our words have already explained all this in sufficient detail, although overlooking many things and also leaving others, especially of a disembodied and invisible nature, so that you hate those who insult the wise and good craftsman. And from what has been said and read, which you yourself will be able to remember and meditate on, you will understand in an analogous way, due to the magnitude and beauty of the creatures, their author (cf. again Wisdom 13:5). Piously bowing your knee before the author of all things, sensible and rational, visible and invisible, with an expression of gratitude, remembrance and blessing, you will praise God with your lips and your heart saying: “How numerous are your works, Yahweh! You have done everything with wisdom” (Ps 104:24). To you the honor, the glory and the magnificence now and forever and ever. Amen. Since almost the beginning of this issue. 15 ("what is there in your body that is worthy of rebuke?..."), there is a variant of the transmitted text, contained in the codex of a supposed homily of Saint Basil. For the interest of the variant, it is also translated in this note according to the text offered by PG 33,655-658: «What is it that has been reflected in your body that is reprehensible? Come out and say it. Moderate your thinking nothing bad will come out of your members. Each one of them has been made for our use. Guide your reflection toward piety and follow divine commands, for no member sins when he acts or submits within the scope of the things for which he was made. If you do not want it, your eye does not look depravedly nor does your ear hear what does not suit it; Nor does the hand take hold of anything improperly nor do the feet lead to injustice; neither do you take affection for another's things nor commit fornication nor desire your neighbor's wife. Suppresses deviated thoughts from the heart. Realize how you were made by God and you will give more thanks to the one who formed you. To begin with, Adam was naked while he was delighting in paradise, but, upon receiving the command and not keeping it, he improperly extended his hand (not because the will was in the hand, but because, with the desire of his soul, he extended his hand to where it should not be). Thus he fell into disobedience, depriving himself of the goods he enjoyed.

In the same way, the members are not a cause of sin for those who use them, but rather the fact that the spirit feels unduly induced, according to what the Lord said: "For from the heart come evil intentions, murders, adulteries, fornications" (Mt 15:19) and other similar things, for all of which you would want to use your members when they had been admirably placed at the service of the soul and placed as servants of reason. You must rule them and govern them by the action of piety. Restrain them with the fear of God. Subdue them docile with the desire for temperance and fasting, and they will never rise up against you by exercising their tyranny: rather they will protect you, leading you to a great victory against the devil, while you wait for the unfading and eternal crown of victory..." This variant, however, does not seem to cancel the text that continues after note 14. CATECHESIS X ONE LORD JESUS ​​CHRIST About "And in one Lord Jesus Christ." It starts from the passage of 1 Cor 8,5-6: «For although they are called gods, either in heaven or on earth, so that there are many gods and lords, for us there is only one God, the Father, from whom all things come and for whom we are; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things are and through whom we are”285. The Son, door to reach the Father

1. Those who have been taught to believe in "one God, the Father almighty," must also believe in the only begotten Son. For "anyone who denies the Son does not possess the Father" (I Jn 2:33). “I am the door” (Jn 10:9), says Jesus. "No one comes to the Father except through me" (Jn 14:6). If you deny the door, the knowledge that leads to the Father will remain closed to you. "No one knows the Father well except the Son and anyone to whom the Son wants to reveal him" (Mt I 1,27b). For if you deny him who reveals, you will remain in ignorance. A sentence in the Gospels says: «He who believes in the Son has eternal life; He who refuses to believe in the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains on him” (Jn 3:36). The Father is outraged when the only begotten Son is deprived of his honor. A king considers it serious that someone insults a simple soldier. Therefore, if one of the most honorable people, colleagues or friends, is treated indecently, one's own anger is inflamed the more. And if someone reviles the only Son of the King, who will appease and soften the Father of the only begotten Son who is so moved? It is in the Son that the designs of God are fulfilled

2. If anyone, therefore, wants to be pious towards God, let him worship the Son; Otherwise, the Father will not admit his worship. The Father exclaimed from heaven saying: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Mt 3:17). The Father came together in the Son. If you do not also find your pleasure in him, you will not have life. Do not let yourself be carried away by the Jews, who evilly and cunningly say, yes, there is only one God. But, along with this recognition that there is only one God, it also recognizes that there is an only Son of God. I have not been the first to say this, but about the person of the Son the psalmist says: "I am going to announce the decree of Yahweh: He has said to me: 'You are my Son: today I have begotten you'" (Ps 2:7). for example, to what is exposed in Paul's famous kerygmatic preaching in Antioch of Pisidia: "We also announce to you the Good News that the Promise made to the fathers, God has fulfilled in us, the children, by resurrecting Jesus, as it is written in the psalms: 'You are my son, and today I have begotten you'" (Acts 13:33; cf. its context). The quote made here by Acts is from Ps 2:7, a passage to which no. 2 of this catechesis. what the Jews say, but what the prophets speak. Are you surprised that they despise the voices of the prophets when they themselves stoned them and handed them over to death? Various denominations of Christ in Scripture

3. You believe "in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son of God." We say “one Lord Jesus Christ,” because it is a unique filiation; We say "single," so that its multiple activity, which is expressed through diverse names, does not lead you to impiously speak of diverse children. It is called a "door" (Jn 10:7), but do not think, because of this name, that it is a wooden door, but rather a rational one, alive and aware of who passes by. It is called "the way" (Jn 14:6), but not because it is trodden by the feet, but because it leads to the Father. She is called a "sheep", but not devoid of reason, but by her precious blood she cleanses the world of its sins: she is brought before the shearer and knows when it is appropriate to remain silent (cf. Acts 8:32; see Is 53:78). But this same sheep at the same time changes his name to shepherd when he says: "I am the good shepherd" (Jn10,11) 3. He is a sheep by his human nature, but he is a shepherd by the love for men that shows his divinity. But do you want to know how we refer to rational sheep? The Savior says to the apostles: "Behold, I am sending you out like sheep in the midst of wolves" (Mt 10:16). It is also called "lion" (cf. Gen 49:9)4, but not because it is a devourer of men, but rather because with such a name the royal dignity of nature itself is shown and its own vigor in which it can rely. He is also called a lion in opposition to the "adversary, the Devil", who "prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour" (I Pet 5:8). For the Savior comes, not changing his natural meekness, but like the mighty lion of the tribe of Judah (cf. Rev 5:5), bringing salvation to those who believe and crushing the adversary. It is called a "stone", not inanimate nor extracted with human hands (cf. Dan 2:34), but a "cornerstone" (cf. Ps 118:225; cf. Mt 21:42 par), in which whoever believes will not be confounded (cf. Is 28:16). More denominations of Christ

4. He is called "Christ"6, although he has not been consecrated by human hands, but rather anointed by the Father for an eternal priesthood superior to the things of men (cf. Acts 4:27). He is counted among those who have died, but without remaining among the dead7, like all the others in Hades (cf. Acts 2:31), but the only free one among those who died. He is called "Son of man" (Mt 16:13); not like each one of us, who have had our birth on this earth, but as one who will come on the clouds to judge the living and the dead (Mt 24:30)8. He is called "Lord", not in an abusive way, like the "lords" among men, but as one who has a natural and eternal power9. He is called "Jesus" with an appropriate name10, which refers to his work as a doctor11. He is proclaimed "Son"12, who did not become so by adoption, but rather by nature he was begotten. There are truly many denominations of our Savior. But don't let this multitude of names make you think of a multitude of children. And do not think, because of the errors of the heretics, that they say that one is the Christ, but another is Jesus, and another is the door, and so on. Right faith warns you against all this: in one Lord Jesus Christ. Although there are many different denominations, what is understood under them is a single reality. Jesus Christ, Savior and Lord

5. He acts as Savior differently according to each person's circumstances. For those who need joy, he is the vineyard (cf. Jn 15:1). For those who need to enter, he is the door (Jn 10:7). For those who have to present their supplications, he has been constituted "sole mediator" (1 Tim 2,5) and "High Priest" (Hebr 7,26). But, in turn, he becomes a sheep in favor of sinners to be sacrificed in their place (Is 53:6-7). Everything is done for everyone, remaining what he is according to his nature. For remaining thus and holding a son's dignity that is not subject to any mutation, he descends to our weaknesses as an excellent doctor and kind teacher. And this being in truth the Lord, who has not acquired the lordship for his own benefit, but rather possesses by nature the dignity of that lordship13. He is not abusively called our "Lord", but truly is: when by the will of the Father he dominates over his own creatures. We exercise a right of dominion over men equal to us in honor and who are subject to the same weaknesses: we often rule over those who surpass us in age and it is not unusual for a young man to rule over older servants. But in our Lord Jesus Christ there is no such kind of dominion. For in the first place he is Maker and then Lord: first he has done the will of the Father, and it is only later that he dominates over the things he has made. Christ, always in union with the Father

6. "Christ the Lord"14 is the one who "was born in the city of David"15. And do you want to know that Christ the Lord is with the Father before becoming man16, so that what is said you not only accept by faith, but also have proof from the Old Testament? Look for the first of the books, Genesis, where God says: "Let us make human beings", he does not say in my image, but "in our image" (Gen 1:26). And after Adam was made, he says: "So God created human beings in his own image" (1:27). He did not, therefore, restrict the divine dignity to the Father alone, but also referred jointly to the Son, thus declaring that man is not simply the work of God, but also of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is also true God. This is the same Lord, who cooperates with the Father, as he also did in the matter of Sodom, according to what is said in the Scripture: "Then Yahweh rained sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah from Yahweh." And on another occasion, he showed himself to Moses as soon as he was able to see him (cf. Ex 3:2.6; 33:18-20; 34:5-6). For the Lord is kind and always descends indulgently to our weaknesses. Christ, appeared to Moses

7. And so that you may know that it is he himself who appeared to Moses, accept this testimony from Paul: “For they drank of the spiritual rock that followed them; and the rock was Christ" (I Cor 10:4) and, furthermore (referring to Moses): "By faith he left Egypt" (Hebr 11:27), shortly after having said: "counting the shame of Christ as greater riches than the treasures of Egypt" (Hebr 11:26)18. And Moses says to him: "Please let me see your glory" (Ex 33:18). Don't you see that even then the prophets saw Christ, although to the extent that they were capable of it? "Let me see you," cried Moses. But God tells him: "Man cannot see me and continue living" (Ex 33:20). Therefore, since no one could see the face of divinity, he adopted the face of man so that, seeing him, we might live19. But when he wanted to show it with brilliance, that is, when his face "shone like the sun", "the disciples fell face to the ground full of fear" (Mt 17:2-6). Therefore, if the face of his body did not shine as much as he could but as much as the disciples were able to endure, how could anyone look at the majesty of divinity? “Great is what you desire, Moses,” says the Lord. «I give my approval, however, to your unsatisfied desire. "I will also do this which you have just asked of me" (Ex 33:17), to the extent that you can grasp it.» «Look, there is a place next to me; you will stand on the rock. And when my glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by. Then I will remove my hand, so that you can see my back; but my face cannot be seen" (Ex 33,21-23) 20 The presence of Christ among the Israelites, invoked by Moses

8. Keep firmly, because of the Jews, everything I am going to say. For it was our purpose to show you that, next to the Father, was the Lord Jesus Christ. Because the Lord says to Moses: "I will make all my goodness pass before your sight and I will pronounce before you the name of Yahweh" (Ex 33:19). He who is the Lord in person, whom does he call Lord?21. You see how, although in an obscure way, he taught the pious doctrine about the Father and the Son. And furthermore, in the words that follow it is written22 “Yahweh came down in the form of a cloud and stood there by him. Moses called on the name of Yahweh. Yahweh passed before him and exclaimed: "Yahweh, Yahweh, God merciful and gracious, slow to anger and rich in love and faithfulness, who maintains his love for thousands, who forgives iniquity, rebellion and sin, but does not leave them unpunished; who punishes the iniquity of the fathers on the children and on the children's children to the third and fourth generation." Then, according to what follows, Moses, falling to the ground on his knees and worshiping the Father before the Lord, whom he called, says: "May my Lord deign to come from among us" (Ex 34:5-9, for everything together). Christ is, like the Father, Lord of all

9. You thus have a first demonstration. Admit another one that is obvious. «The Lord said to my Lord: 'Sit at my right'» (Ps 110:1). The Lord says these things to the Lord, not to the servant23. But it is about the Lord of all things, his own Son to whom everything was submitted (cf. 1 Cor 15:2728; Hebr 2:8). «But when he says that "everything is subjected", it is evident that he excludes Him who has subjected all things to him» (1 Cor 15:27)..., «so that God may be all in all» (15:28). Lord of all is the only begotten Son: he is the Son of the Father, submissive to him and who has not usurped his sovereignty, but has received it spontaneously and naturally. Well, neither the Son stole it from the Father nor has the Father felt envy of the Son by giving him the domain. It is this same one who says: "Everything has been handed over to me by my Father" (Mt 11:27). But it has not been given to me as if it had previously lacked it24, although I preserve it carefully without impoverishing its largesse. More about the lordship of Christ

10. Therefore, the Son of God is "Lord." Lord born in Bethlehem of Judah, according to the words of the angel to the shepherds: "I announce to you great joy...: a savior has been born to you today, in the city of David, who is Christ the Lord" (Lk 2:10-11). Of which, in another place, one of the Apostles says: "He has sent his Word to the children of Israel, announcing to them the Good News of peace through Jesus Christ who is Lord of all" (Acts 10:36). And when he says "everything", do not subtract absolutely anything from his sovereignty, because both the angels and the archangels, "the Principalities, the Powers" (Col 1:16) or any other of the created realities named by the apostles, everything has been submitted to the lordship of the Son. He is Lord of the angels, as you have in the gospels: «Then the devil leaves him. And behold, angels came and ministered to him” (Mt 4:11). It does not say "they helped him", but rather "they served him", that is, they carried out a servile job. And when he was going to be born of the Virgin, Gabriel then served him, who thus converted his own dignity into service (cf. Luke 1:26 ff.). When he had to go to Egypt to destroy its idols25, an angel again appeared to Joseph in a dream (cf. Mt 2:13). Having risen after his crucifixion, an angel announced it and, like a diligent servant, said to the women: "Now go immediately and tell the disciples: 'He has risen from the dead and will go before you to Galilee; there you will see him': I have already told you" (Mt 28:7). As if to say: I have not neglected the assignment; I testify that I have told you this so that, if you neglect it, the fault will not be mine but that of those who have been negligent. Thus, then, that is the only Lord Jesus Christ, about whom the reading that was proclaimed26 contains these words: “For although they are called gods, either in heaven or on earth, so that there are many gods and lords, for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things come and for whom we are; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things are and through whom we are” (I Cor 8:5-6). Aaron and Joshua, figures of Christ priest and savior

11. Jesus Christ is called by a double word: Jesus, because he grants salvation; Christ, because he possesses the priesthood27. Realizing the situation perfectly, the divine prophet Moses called two very chosen men with these names: Ausés, his successor in leadership, whom he called Jesus, changing his name, and his own brother Aaron, adding the name of Anointed29; In this way, through these two excellent men, he represented the royal power and the pontifical power that were to be united in the only Jesus Christ who was to come. For Christ is high priest in the likeness of Aaron, if it is true that "Christ also did not appropriate the glory of the High Priesthood, but he had it from the one who said to him:... You are a priest forever, like Melchizedek" (Hebr 5,5.6). And in many things Joshua, son of Nun,30 was an image of him, since the leadership over the people had its beginning in the Jordan31, where Christ also began to evangelize once he received baptism (Mt 3:13). The son of Nun made twelve parts of the entire inheritance (Joshua 14:1-5) and Jesus sent twelve apostles of the truth as preachers to the whole world (Mt 10). As an image (of Jesus), he (Joshua) protected the prostitute whom he had believed (Joshua 2:1 ff; 6:17 cf. Hebr 11:31). But the true32 exclaims: "Truly I say to you, the tax collectors and the harlots reach the Kingdom of God before you" (Mt 21:31). Before the cry of joy, although that was only an image, the walls of the city of Jericho collapsed (Joshua 6:20), and because of the word of Jesus: "Not one stone will be left here upon another" (Mt 24:2), what opposes us fell, the temple of the Jews. And not because Jesus' sentence was the cause of the collapse, but this fall was caused by the sin of the wicked. Jesus, Savior, named after the angel

12. Unique is the Lord Jesus Christ, an admirable name indirectly announced by the prophets. For the prophet Isaiah says: «Look, your salvation is coming; Look, his salary accompanies him” (Is 62:11)33. But Jesus, in Hebrew, means "savior"; However, the grace given to the prophets, foreseeing the twisted sentiment of the Jews towards the destruction of the Lord, concealed from them the true denomination so that they could not, knowing it too soon, lay in wait against it in a more insidious manner. But Jesus was clearly called that way, not by everyone, but by the angel, who did not come by his own initiative, but by the authority of God, and said to Joseph: "Do not be afraid to take Mary your wife with you because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. She will give birth to a son, and you will name him Jesus” (Mt 1:20-21). And when giving a reason for this name, he immediately added: "For he will save his people from their sins" (1:21b). But you have to understand how someone who has not yet been born can have a people, and in reality it already existed before being born. This is what the prophet says about him: "Yahweh called me from his mother's womb: from my mother's womb he remembered my name" (Is 49:1)34. That is why the angel predicted that he would be called Jesus. As these words must also be understood from Herod's snares: "He hid me in the shadow of his hand" (Is 49:2). The Savior who heals

13. Thus, "Jesus" means "savior" in Hebrew, and in the Greek language, "healer."35 In reality he is a doctor of souls and bodies, and a healer of spirits: he heals those who are blind in their sensitive eyes, but he also brings light to minds: he is a doctor of those who are visibly lame, and he also directs the feet of sinners to conversion when he says to the paralytic: "Sin no more" (Jn 5:14) and: "Take up your mat and walk" (5:8)36. For since because of the sin of the soul the body had been given over to paralysis, he first healed the soul in order to later also bring the medicine to the body. Therefore, if someone's mind is stiffened by the disease of sins, there is a doctor there. But if someone has little faith, tell him: "Help my unbelief" (Mk 9:23). And if anyone is plagued by bodily illnesses, do not be distrustful, but draw near, and you will also receive a remedy, and recognize that Jesus is the Messiah. Eternity and immutability of the priesthood of Christ

14. The Jews grant that Jesus is something more, but they deny that he is the Messiah. For this reason the Apostle says: "Who is the liar but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ (1 Jn 2:22)?" But Christ is the high priest with a non-transferable priesthood37. He did not begin to be a priest at the time nor does he have any successor in his pontificate, just as you heard us speaking on Sunday in the assembly33 about "according to the order of Melchizedek" (Ps 110,4; cf. Hebr 5,6)39. He has not obtained the pontificate by bodily succession nor has he been anointed with earthly oil,40 but he comes from the Father before the ages; and he is all the more excellent than others who has been a Priest through an oath: «For the others were made priests without an oath, while this one was made priest under an oath by Him who said to him: "The Lord has sworn and will not repent..."» (Hebr 7,20b-21a). For the security of the matter the will of the Father was sufficient. But this security has been doubled by adding an oath to the will: "So that through two immutable things by which it is impossible for God to lie, we may be more powerfully encouraged" (Hebrews 6:18)41 who welcome Jesus Christ, the Son of God. Despite the announcements, Christ was rejected

15. The Jews rejected this Christ when he arrived42, but the demons confessed him (cf. Luke 4:41). Nor was the patriarch David unaware of it when he said: "I will prepare a lamp for my anointed" (Ps 132:17). Some have understood this lamp as the splendor of prophecy; others have understood by this lamp the flesh taken from the Virgin, according to what the apostle says: "We carry this treasure in earthen vessels" (2 Cor 4:7). The prophet did not ignore Christ when he said: "Announcing his Christ to men" (Am 4:13 LXX). Moses had also known him, Isaiah had known him, and Jeremiah had also known him: none of the prophets did not know him. Even the demons themselves recognized it. "He warned them," and, it is added, "because they knew that he was the Christ" (Lk 4:41). The princes of the priests ignored it, but the demons confessed it. While the chief priests did not recognize him, the Samaritan woman announced it, saying: “Come see a man who has told me everything I have done. Is it not the Christ? (Jn 4:29). Universality of Christianity

16. This Jesus Christ is the "High Priest of future goods" (Hebr 9:1 1), who by the greatness of his divinity communicated his same name to us all. When someone is king, he does not communicate to others the name of his royal dignity. But Jesus, the Christ, Son of God, deigned to call us Christians. Truly, some will say, it is something new. This name "Christians" had not been heard before, and sometimes opposition is aroused to new things simply because they are new. The prophet addressed this when he said: "He will give his servants a new name such that whoever wishes to be blessed on earth will wish to be blessed in the God of Amen..." (Is 65:15-16)43. Let us ask the Jews: do you serve God or not? Show me, if anything, your new name. For in the time of Moses and the other prophets you were called Jews and Israelites, and likewise after the return from Babylon and until our days. Do you perhaps have a new name? But we, serving the Lord, have a new name: and it is really new, a new name that "will be blessed on the earth": this name has taken over the entire earth, just as the Jews are limited to the confines of a single region, but the Christians are spread throughout the world. What they announce is the name of the only begotten Son of God. Paul, announcer of the Gospel after having persecuted Christians

17. Do you want to know that the apostles knew and announced the name of Christ, and that rather they had Christ himself in them? Paul tells his listeners: "...since you want proof that Christ speaks in me" (2 Cor 13:3). Paul announces Christ saying: "We do not preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as His servants through Jesus" (2 Cor 4:5). But who is it that speaks thus? The one who was previously a pursuer. Oh great miracle! He who was once a persecutor now announces Christ. And for what reason? Earned for money? But there was no one to persuade him with such arts. Or had he seen him personally on earth and was acting out of reverence and modesty? In reality he had already gone to heaven. He (Paul) had set out as a pursuer and, after three days in Damascus, the one who was dedicated to persecuting became his crier (Acts 9:1-25). By virtue of what? Some call witnesses from their house for family things, but I have brought you as a witness someone who had previously been an enemy. Do you still have doubts? Great is certainly the testimony of Peter and John, but it could be considered with some suspicion, since they were relatives (of Christ). But when someone who was once an enemy now faces death for the same thing, there is no longer any room to doubt the truth. Conversion of Paul to Jesus Christ. Fertility of his writing activity

18. While speaking of these things, one is pleasantly surprised by the admirable design of the Holy Spirit that the letters of others should be very few in number, but he granted Paul, who had previously been a persecutor, to write fourteen. And it is not that he restricted that grace in Peter and John, as if they were minors. None of that, but to affirm the undoubted authority of the doctrine, he granted someone who had previously been an enemy and persecutor to write widely so that we would all have a certain faith. Certainly everyone was amazed at Paul and said: "Isn't this the one who in Jerusalem fiercely persecuted those who called on that name, and hasn't he come here with the goal of taking them all to the high priests?" (Acts 9:21). "Do not surprise them," says Paul, I know that for me "it is hard to kick against the sting" (Acts 26:14)44. I know that "I am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I have persecuted the Church of God" (I Cor 15:9), but "out of ignorance" (I Tim 1:13). For he believed that the preaching of Christ was the ruin of the Law: he did not know that he had come to fulfill the Law, not to annul it (cf. Mt 5:17). "And the grace of our Lord abounded to me all the more" (I Tim 1:14). Countless testimonies and witnesses of Christ

19. Dear ones, there are many testimonies about Christ45. From heaven the Father testifies about the Son (cf. Mt 3:17; 17:5); the Holy Spirit testifies by descending bodily in the form of a dove (Lk 3:22); the archangel Gabriel testifies announcing the gospel to Mary (Lk 1,26-38); testifies the Virgin Mother of God (ibid.); testifies to the happy place of the manger (Luke 2:7). Egypt is a witness, which welcomed the Lord in body when he was still a very small child. Simeon is a witness, who took him in his arms and said: "Now, Lord, according to your word, you can let your servant go in peace, because my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the sight of all people" (cf. Lk 2:28-31). And Anna, the prophetess, a very pious continent (and widow)46 who led an ascetic life, also testifies of him (Luke 2:36-38). John the Baptist testifies, the greatest of the prophets (Jn 1,15; 1, 19 ff) and the first of the New Testament, who in a certain way connects both Covenants within himself, the old and the new47. Among the rivers the Jordan is a witness, among the seas, that of Tiberias. The blind, the lame, the dead, called back to life, bear witness. The demons bear witness saying: "What do we have with you, Jesus of Nazareth?... I know who you are: the Holy One of God" (Mk 1:24). The winds restrained by his power testify (Mt 8:23-27); The five loaves distributed among five thousand men testify (Mt 14,1321). This is testified to by the holy wood of the cross, which is seen among us to this day and which has filled almost the entire world with the pieces that some, through their faith, have taken from it. The palm tree that provided palm trees to the children who at the time welcomed Christ with praise testifies in the valley (Jn 12:13). Gethsemane testifies as also showing Judas to those who understand what happened (Mt 26:47 ff.). This holy mountain, Golgotha, standing out above the rest, also testifies by being seen; The holy sepulcher and the stone placed next to it to this day also bear witness (cf. Mt 27:60). The sun that is now shining is a witness for having experienced an eclipse in passion. Witness was also the darkness that on that occasion extended from the sixth hour to the ninth hour (Lk 23:44). Witness is the light that illuminated from the ninth hour until the evening. Witness is the holy mountain of Olives from which he ascended to the Father (Acts 1,912).

Also witnesses are the storm clouds that welcomed the Lord48. Likewise the heavenly doors that welcomed the Lord, of which the psalmist says: "Lift up, doors, lift up the lintels, eternal doors, so that the king of glory may enter!" (Ps 23,7). Those who had previously been enemies also testify, of whom we must now remember the blessed Paul, who for a certain time lived in enmity, but (later) exercised his ministry in a lasting way. The twelve apostles testify, that they preached not only with words but also with their own torments and their death. The shadow of Peter testifies, who in the name of Christ healed the sick (Acts 5:15); The handkerchiefs and aprons testify that through Paul they also carried out healings with the power of Christ. The Persians, the Goths and all the converted Gentiles are witnesses who do not hesitate to face death for him49 whom they did not see with the eyes of the flesh. The demons testify, exorcised to this day by the service of the faithful. With so many witnesses, faith becomes evident

20. Many, diverse and different are the witnesses. Will faith then be refused to a Messiah proven by so many testimonies? If anyone, therefore, has not believed before, believe now; But if you have already believed, receive a greater increase in faith: believing in our Lord Jesus Christ, know from whom you receive the name of your name. You have been called a Christian: may not our Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, be blasphemed for your sake, but may your good works shine before men, so that men who see them may glorify in Christ Jesus, our Lord, the Father who is in heaven (Mt 5:16), to whom be glory now and forever and ever. Amen...

2. Cf. on the Christological interpretation of this psalm at the end of the previous note. But it is the entire psalm that must be understood Christologically, especially as it relates to the drama of the passion and the messianic lordship. That is what explains its very frequent use in the writings of the New Testament.

3. For the entire allegory of the Good Shepherd, cf Jo 10:1-21. 4 This admits the Christological interpretation of the "lion of Judah": the Messiah had to be, and Jesus in fact is, from the tribe of Judah. 6. "Christós" is a Greek verbal adjective, which means "anointed" and translates the Hebrew "Messiah", with the same meaning. When Mt 1:16 speaks of "Jesus, called Christ" he means to indicate that in Jesus the Messiah awaited throughout the history of salvation that God has established for centuries with all humanity has been recognized, but taking shape in the history of Israel. In Christ God has placed his Spirit (cf. Is 42:1). Jesus of Nazareth is the one whom "God anointed with the Holy Spirit and with power", according to the version of Is 61:1 offered by Acts 10:38. According to Luke 4:17-21, Jesus interprets Is 61:1-2 seeing the words of Isaiah fulfilled in himself. For all these reasons, Jesus is the most explicit and clear personification and presence of God in the world. Jesus is, therefore, definitively the "Christ", "Messiah", "anointed" of God for the salvation of man.

8. Mt 24:30, on the definitive coming of the Son of Man at the end of time: "Then the sign of the Son-of-Man will appear in heaven, and then all the races of the earth will beat their chests and will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with great power and glory." The image of the "Son of Man" is of an apocalyptic nature, that is, as a description of contours it is blurred; but the term, used in Dn 7:13-14, serves, precisely in its imprecision, to express something that goes far beyond its literal meaning. The excellent note of the Jerusalem Bible to Dan 7:13 speaks of a sense of the expression "Son of man" that is both collective and individual (based on Dan 7:18.22) since "the Son of man is identified in some way with the saints of the Most High: but the collective sense (also messianic) extends the personal sense, since the Son of man is at the same time the head, the representative and the model of the people of the saints." And he adds the same note: "That is why Saint Ephrem thought that the prophecy refers first to the Jews (the Maccabees), then, above them, and in a perfect way, to Jesus." For all these reasons it can perhaps be said that the title of Son of man or of man, applied to Jesus, is useful to indicate, in Jesus Christ, the definitive image of man, his reality and his history. These biblical speculations on Christian anthropology are probably not alien to the statements of I Cor 15:47: "The first man, coming out of the earth, is earthly, the second comes from heaven."
