35. The expression can be translated as "the centuries", literally "eons", according to the Greek. It can, therefore, also designate the "ages" of the world, the eras and the epochs. CATECHESIS It starts from the passage of Isaiah: «Yahweh spoke again to Ahaz saying: "Ask for yourself a sign from Yahweh your God..." (7,10-11), and: "Behold, a maiden is with child and is going to give birth to a son, and she will name him Immanuel"» (7,14), etc.1 The Son of God has become man

1. As students of purity and disciples of prudence, let us celebrate with chaste lips the God born of the Virgin. Those of us who consider ourselves worthy of feeding on the rational lamb2, let us eat both the head and the legs3, meaning divinity through the head and humanity through the legs. Those of us who listen to the Gospels listen to the theologian John, who after writing: "In the beginning was the Word and the Word was with God, and the Word was God" (Jn I,1), later added: "And the Word became flesh" (1,14). Nor should one worship a simple man4 nor only God without reference to humanity. For if Christ is God, as is the case in reality, but does not assume human nature, we do not have salvation. Let him therefore be worshiped as God, but also believe that he has put on human nature. Nor is it acceptable to be called man leaving divinity aside, nor does it lead to salvation to separate humanity from the confession of divinity. Let us acknowledge the presence of the king and the doctor. Jesus is a king who will bring salvation by girding himself with the cloth of humanity and having healed what was sick. As a perfect teacher of children, he became a child with them "to teach the simple prudence" (Prov 1:4). The bread from heaven has come down to earth to feed those who are hungry. Do not reject the one in whom the prophecy of the incarnation is fulfilled

2. But the Jews, when they reject him who has come, wait for him who is to come harshly: they repudiated Christ, but they will welcome, led into error, the impostor who comes. Thus the word of the Savior will become true: “I have come in the name of my Father, and you do not receive me; If another comes in his own name, him you will receive” (Jn 5:43). It would be great to ask this question to the Jews: is the prophet Isaiah telling the truth or a lie when he points out that Immanuel will be born of a virgin? (cf. Is 7:14). It is not surprising that they accuse him of being a liar, since it is customary for them not only to accuse prophets of lying, but even to stone them. Now, if the prophet spoke the truth, point out who the Emmanuel is. Even more: will he who is to come, and for whom you wait, be born of a virgin or not? If he is not born of a virgin, you accuse the prophet of falsehood. And if you expected this to happen in the future, why do you reject it when it has already happened? True full humanity and virginal conception of Christ

3. The Jews will be brought out of their error when they allow it5, and the Church of God will be glorified, since we truly welcome the God who is the Word made man. This has happened, not by the will of a man and a woman, as the heretics say, but that man was made of a virgin and by the Holy Spirit, as the Gospel says. And not in appearance, but in truth. And I would like you to realize that now is the time to convey the doctrine that he has received human nature from a virgin. Now you will receive the proof of this reality. The error of the heretics is multiple, since they totally denied that he had been born of a virgin6; others granted the reality of her birth, but not from a virgin, but from the union of a man and a woman. Others say that it is not the Messiah God who has become man, but a deified man7. These dared to say that not a pre-existing Word became man, but that a man with his own merits was crowned (like God)8. We will face the objections

4. But remember the things that were said yesterday about divinity. He believes that the only begotten Son of God is the one who in turn was born of the Virgin. Believe the evangelist John when he says: «The Word became flesh, and took up residence among us. He is truly the eternal Word, begotten of the Father before all ages, although in time he has taken flesh for our sake. Many are against this and say: What happened so seriously that God descended to humanity? To which it can be said: "Then she appeared9 on earth, and lived among men" (Bar 3:38). Or (they ask themselves): is it possible for a virgin to give birth without a man? When we find ourselves, therefore, being widely contradicted and facing battle on various fronts, it is necessary that we annihilate all of this through the grace of Christ and through the discourses that we offer here. The Son assumed the flesh of the most excellent of creatures

5. Let us ask ourselves, in the first place, why Jesus came. And do not notice my reasoning, which could perhaps be contradicted by sophistry. Now, if you do not accept the testimonies of the prophets about each of these things, you will not believe what we say. If you do not learn from the Scriptures what refers to the Virgin, the place, the time and the manner, neither do you receive testimony from any man10. Well, some suspicion may fall on this one who is now here and instructs you, but on the one who pronounced the prophecies, a thousand years ago and even longer, who can have reluctance if he is in his right mind? Therefore, if you seek the cause of the coming of Christ, simply go to the first book of Scripture. In six days God made the world. But this exists for man. Let the sun shine with its splendid brilliance: it was made to shine in favor of man. All animals were made for our service; and the herbs and trees were created for us to use. They are all good creatures11, but none of them is the image of God except man alone. A simple order made the sun, while man was formed by the hands of God: "Let us make human beings in our image, in our likeness" (Gen 1:26)12. And if honor is paid to the wooden image of an earthly king, how much more should be done to the image of God? But this, the most excellent of God's creatures, who was happy in paradise, was expelled from there by the envy of the devil (Gen 3,23-24; Wis 2,24). The enemy was happy to see prostrate the one whom he had envied. Do you perhaps want to be like that enemy who was happy? He had not dared to approach the man because of his strength, but because he was weaker, he approached the woman when she was still a virgin. It was after his departure from paradise that "the man knew Eve, his wife" (Gen 4:1). Sin had spread across the earth

6. His successors in human progeny were Cain and Abel, and Cain was the first murderer. Later the flood took place because of the multiplication of the wickedness of men13. Fire from heaven fell on the inhabitants of Sodom because of their wickedness (cf. Gen 19). In later times God chose Israel, but it too fell into perversion and the chosen people were mortally wounded: Moses was on the mountain before God, and the people, instead of God, worshiped a calf (Ex 32:1-6). While the law of Moses said: "You shall not commit adultery" (Ex 20:14), a man dared to sin by entering a place of prostitution (cf. Num 25:1-9). After Moses, prophets were sent to take care of Israel. But when they brought the medicine, they lamented, overcome by the force of the disease, in such a way that some of them cried out: "Woe to me, the faithful have disappeared from the earth, there is no righteous person left among men!" (Mic 7,2); or also: «They are all misguided, en masse perverted. There is no one who does good, not even one” (Sa 14:3). And, in turn: «Yahweh has a dispute with the inhabitants of this land, because there is no faithfulness nor love nor knowledge of God in this land; but perjury and lying, murder and theft, adultery and violence, blood following blood” (Hos 4:1-2). And: "They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons" (Ps 106:37). They occupied themselves with sacred sorceries and with the vanity of their shames. Thus it says: "On pawned clothes they lie down next to any altar" (Am 2:8; cf. Deut 24:12-13). Gravity of sin

7. Very great was the wound of humanity. From her feet to her head there was nothing whole in her. There was no place for gauze, oil or bandages. Then, amid lamentations and fatigue, the prophets said: "Who will bring salvation to Israel from Zion?" (Ps 14:7). And, on the other hand: "Let your hand be on the man of your right hand, on the son of Adam whom you strengthened for you, we will no longer depart from you." (Ps 80,18-19a). And another prophet begged, saying: "Yahweh, bow down your heavens and come down!" (Ps 144,5). The wounds of men are stronger than our remedies. "They have torn down your altars and put your prophets to the sword" (1 Kings 19:10). It is not possible to avoid evil; To avoid it, you need you14. God comes to men, even if he is not welcomed

8. The Lord heard this plea of ​​the prophets: the Father did not ignore our race on the road to destruction and sent his Son from heaven as Lord and as doctor. One of the prophets says: «The Lord whom you seek will immediately come to his Temple – the place where you stoned him – (Mal 3:1)15. Then, another of the prophets hearing this, said to him: "If you announce that God is coming for salvation, do you speak in secret?": "Go up to a high mountain, joyful messenger to Zion; Cry out with a powerful voice, joyful messenger to Jerusalem, Cry out without fear. Say to the cities of Judah: 'There is your God. There comes the Lord Yahweh with power'” (Is 40:9-10). But, on the other hand, the Lord Himself says: “Behold, I come to dwell within you, declares the LORD. Many nations will join Yahweh on that day” (Zech 2:14-15). But the Israelites rejected the salvation that I offered them: "I come to gather all nations and languages" (Is 66:18), but "he came to his house, and his own did not receive him" (Jn 1:11). And, when you come, what do you give to the Gentiles: "I come to gather all the nations... I will put a sign on them" (Is 66:18-19). For, because of my combat on the cross, I will give each of my soldiers a sign to have on their foreheads16, and another prophet said: "He bowed the heavens and came down, a thick cloud under his feet" (Ps 18:10). But the one who came down from heaven remained unknown to men. The birth of the Messiah was planned

9. At another time, Solomon, hearing his father David speak of these things, after having built that admirable temple, and seeing from afar the one who was to come to it, said: "Will God truly dwell with men on the earth?" (1 Kings 8:27). David's response, in a psalm dedicated to Solomon, was affirmative: "It will fall like dew on the fleece" (Ps 72:6)17. Rocío, because of its celestial origin; on the fleece, because it is about humanity. And the dew falls on the fleece silently, just as the Magi, ignorant of the mystery of the Nativity, said: "Where is the King of the Jews who has been born?" (Mt 2:2), and a Herod disturbed by the one who had been born inquired and found out "about the place where the Christ was to be born" (2:4). Signs of humility of the victorious Messiah

10. And who is he who came? He says in what follows18: "It will last as long as the sun, as the moon from age to age" (Ps 72:5). Another of the prophets says in turn: “Exult without restraint, daughter of Zion, shout for joy, daughter of Jerusalem! Behold, your king comes to you, righteous and victorious” (Zech 9:9). Many are the kings. Who are you referring to, prophet? Give us a sign that other kings do not have. If you are referring to a king dressed in purple, there are already others who have this privilege in clothing. Whether it is that he is surrounded by an escort of soldiers or that he is sitting in golden chariots, others also have these badges. Give us a sign of this king whose coming you announce. The prophet responds by saying: "Behold, your king comes to you: righteous and victorious, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, a young donkey" (ibid.), but not on chariots. Here is the unique and singular sign of the king who arrives19. Jesus is the only one among kings who, riding a donkey that has not yet carried any burden, enters Jerusalem amid acclamations like a king. And what does this king do when he arrives?: "And you, in the blood of the covenant, brought the prisoners out of the lake that had no water" (Zech 11:11). In the same place where the catechisms are given, the Messiah was crucified

11. It was, of course, probable that he was sitting on a colt. But rather give us a sign about what this king who now comes relies on. Do not offer a sign that is far from the city, lest we not notice it. Show us a sign that is very visible to the eyes so that, even when we are in the city, we can see it right here. To this the prophet responds by saying: "His feet will be planted on that day on the Mount of Olives, which is opposite Jerusalem, to the east" (Zech 14:4). Is there anyone who does not see this place, even if they are inside the city?20. The messianic signs of miracles and judgment of the elders of the people

12. We have two signs, but we want to see a third. Tell what the Lord will do when he comes. Another prophet says: «Look, your God is coming an avenger, it is God's reward, he will come and save you. Then the eyes of the blind will be taken off, and the ears of the deaf will be opened. Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will shout for joy" (Is 35:4-6). Also tell us another testimony. You say, prophet, that the Lord will come performing signs like never before (cf. Jn 15:24a). In what other way do you say that it has been manifested?: "The Lord enters into judgment of the elders of his people and their leaders" (Is 3:14). This is the main sign: the Lord is judged and has to endure it, by his servants, the elders. Allusion to the fear of seeing God directly

13. When the Jews read this, they do not realize it; The ears of his heart have been closed so as not to hear. But we believe in Jesus Christ "who came in the flesh and became man" and whom, otherwise, we would not have been able to perceive21. Since we cannot see God as he is or enjoy him, he became what we are so that we would have the ability to enjoy him. Well, if we do not have the ability to see perfectly the sun, which was made on the fourth day, can we see God, its author? The Lord descended in the fire on Mount Sinai, but the people could not bear to see him, but "they said to Moses: Speak to us, and we will be able to understand you, but do not let God speak to us, lest we die" (Ex 20:19). And, on the other hand: «What man has heard like us the voice of the living God speaking from the middle of the fire, and has survived? (Dt 5,2). For if you hear the voice of God, he is calling for death22 and, if you realize that it is God himself, how can he not attract death? Why are you amazed "if Moses himself said: 'I am terrified and trembling'" (Hebrews 12:31)23? God becomes man to be better understood

14. What would you want then? May he who came for salvation become a cause of death for us because we could not bear his presence? Would it not be better for him to adapt his grace to our capacity? Daniel could not stand the presence of the angel, and would you stand the direct vision of the angels of the Lord? When Gabriel appeared, Daniel fell to the ground (cf. Dan 10:9). What was he like and what was the appearance of the one who appeared?: "His face was like the appearance of lightning, his eyes like torches of fire" (it does not say "like a furnace of fire"), "and the sound of his words like the noise of a multitude" (10:6), but not like that of "twelve legions of angels" (cf. Mt 26:53). However, the prophet prostrated himself on the ground and, as the angel approached, he said: "Do not be afraid, Daniel", stand up and lift up your spirit, for "your words were heard" (cf. Dan 10:12). And Daniel says: “I stood up fearful”24. However, he did not respond until a hand touched him (cf. 10:10). And after the one who appeared transformed into what looked like a man, then Daniel began to speak. And what did he say?: Lord, when I see you, my insides have turned. There will be no strength in me, because your breath did not remain in me. If the vision of the angel robbed the prophet of his voice and his strength, would the appearance of God himself allow respite? And, says the Scripture, until he saw him in the form of a man, a new creation did not take place in Daniel. Therefore, once our weakness had been demonstrated by experience, the Lord assumed what was necessary for the good of man. In fact, the man was eager to hear someone like him speak. The Savior clothed himself in that nature with similar qualities so that men could be taught more easily. The Son becomes flesh to save man

15. But there is also another reason. Christ came to be baptized and thus sanctify baptism. He came to work miracles walking on the waters of the sea (cf. Mt 14:25). But, before his coming in the flesh, "the sea saw him and he fled, the Jordan receded" (Ps 114:3): the Lord assumed a body that was sustained in the sea and which the Jordan welcomed with fear. And this is one reason. But there is another one: through the virgin Eve death appeared. It was, therefore, appropriate that through a virgin, or rather coming from a virgin, life should sprout, so that, as the serpent deceived that one, Gabriel could bring the good news to this one. Men, by abandoning God, created images of human form. But since a human-looking fiction was deceptively worshiped as God, God became truly man to undo the deception. The devil used the instrument of the flesh against us. Aware of this, Paul says: "I notice another law in my members that fights against the law of my reason and enslaves me..." (Rom 7:23). But with the same weapons with which the devil fought us, with those same ones we have been saved. The Lord took from us what is like us, to bring salvation to human nature. He assumed our likeness to grant greater grace to what was in a deficient situation and so that sinful human nature could become a participant in God. “Where sin abounded, grace abounded all the more” (Romans 5:20). It was fitting that the Lord should suffer for us, and the devil would not have dared to approach him if he had known him: "for if they had known her23, they would have crucified the Lord of glory" (I Cor 2:8). Therefore, the body was thrown to death so that, when the dragon believed that it would devour it, it would actually vomit out even those it had already devoured26. «It will consume death definitively. The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from all faces..." (Is 25:8). The incarnation is the fulfillment of the Law and the Prophets

16. But did Christ become man in vain? Are our teachings the fruit of quackery and fallacies of human ingenuity? Aren't the Holy Scriptures our salvation? Are not the predictions of the prophets? I have been entrusted to keep this deposit27 immobile and that no one should move you from it. Believe that God has become man. And it was really shown that it was possible for him to become a man. And if the Jews refuse to believe beyond their own faith, let us agree with them on this: What do we announce again when we say that God has become man if you yourselves say that Abraham gave hospitality to the Lord (cf. Gen 18:3). Do we preach insolently when Jacob says: "I have seen God face to face, and my life is saved" (Gen 32:31). The same Lord who ate with Abraham (Gen 18:8) is the one who ate with us. What do we say, then, that is unusual? We also have two witnesses who were with the Lord on Mount Sinai: Moses was in the cleft of the rock (Ex 33:21-23) and Elijah was also at the entrance of the cave (I Kgs 19:9). Both were present when he was transfigured on Mount Tabor and pointed out to the disciples the departure that he would make to Jerusalem (Lk 9:30-31)28. The incarnation was possible, as previously demonstrated. There are now more demonstrations, which can be left to the curiosity of scholars. The Savior came during Roman domination in Palestine

17. Furthermore, we had promised them that in our words we would give an account of the place and time of the coming of the Savior. And we must not end up as prisoners of a false promise, but we must say goodbye to you, leaving you sufficiently protected as candidates of the Church. Let us investigate, therefore, the time in which the Savior came, since his coming is still recent, although someone denies it. Furthermore, yesterday as today, Jesus Christ is the same, and will always be the same" (Hebrews 13:8). Moses says prophetically: "I will raise up for them, from among their brothers, a prophet like you" (Dt 18:18)29. Let's leave the "like me" for the moment, which will be explained in its place. But when did that expected prophet arrive? Go, he says, to the things I have written. Investigate Jacob's prophecy to Judah: "Your brothers will praise you, Judah" (Gen 49:8), and, a little further down, in order not to recite it all: "The staff, the staff of command, will not leave Judah from between your legs, until tribute is brought and to whom the nations pay homage" (Gen 49:10)30. A sign of the coming of Christ was that the Jews lost their independence. If they had not been subject to the Romans at that time, Christ would not have come. If they had had a prince from the lineage of Judah and David, the expected one would not have come either. I feel hesitant even to mention their own institutions, which refers to the patriarchs and their lineage, topics that I gladly leave to those who know them. Now, he who comes as desired by the nations, what sign does he bring with him? He says immediately afterwards: "he ties his donkey to the vine." You realize that it is the colt that Zechariah (9:9) already spoke eloquently about. Everything will happen in the days of a great empire

18. But you also look for other testimony about the time. He (the Lord) has said to me: «You are my son; today I have begotten you” (Ps 2:7). And, a little further down: «With an iron scepter you will break them»31. I said on another occasion that the Roman Empire is called a rod of iron32. In what remains of him we can reflect on Daniel. Well, by describing and interpreting the image of the statue to Nebuchadnezzar, he also explains to him the entire vision of it (Dn 2:2745; cf. 46-49) and announces that the stone, which has been detached from the mountain "without the intervention of any hand" (3:34), will dominate the entire world. He also speaks very clearly in this way: "In the time of these kings, the God of heaven will raise up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, and this kingdom will not pass to another people" (3:44)33. More details about the time of the coming of the Messiah

19. WEEKS-YEARS/DANIEL: But we seek an even clearer exposition of the time of his coming. In fact, man is hardly induced to believe - he does not believe in what he is told if he does not openly achieve an exact calculation of years. What, then, are the circumstances of the time and the time itself? When there are no longer native kings of Judah, then the foreigner Herod will reign. Therefore, the angel who speaks to Daniel says (and write down for me now what he says): "Understand and comprehend: From the moment the order went out to rebuild Jerusalem, until a Prince Messiah, seven weeks and sixty-two weeks" (Dan 9:25)34. Sixty-nine weeks of years are four hundred and eighty-three. He affirms, therefore, that four hundred and eighty-three years after the reconstruction of Jerusalem, and when there are no longer proper leaders, a foreign king will then come in whose time the Messiah will be born. Darius the Mede built Jerusalem35 in the sixth year of his reign (Ezr 6:15)36, in the first year of the sixty-sixth Greek Olympiad. Among the Greeks, the games that are usually held every four years are called the Olympiad. This was due to the day that is achieved every four years by adding the remains of hours left over by the solar movement each year. Herod was king in the one hundred and eighty-sixth Olympiad, the fourth year. Therefore, from the sixty-sixth Olympiad to the one hundred and eighty-sixth with one hundred and twenty Olympiads and a little more. And these one hundred and twenty Olympics make a total of four hundred and eighty years. The other three missing years, necessary to complete the number of weeks, fit into the interval between the first and fourth years. Therefore, you already have a demonstration from Scripture, which says, as already explained, that the time from the order to rebuild Jerusalem to Christ is sixty-nine weeks (cf., already above, Dan 9:25). Here you have this demonstration of the moment, although there is no shortage of other interpretations of the prophecies about the weeks of years in Daniel37. Details about the place

20. But listen now to the place of the promise. Micah says: "But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, although you are the least among the families of Judah, from you will come me one who will rule in Israel, and whose origins are of old, from the days of old" (Mic 5,1) 38. As for places, being from Jerusalem as you are, you already know what is written in Psalm 132: "Look: we have heard of her that she is in Ephrathah39, we have found her in the Fields of the Forest! (Ps 132,6). Well, until a few years ago it was a place populated by forest. You have heard, on the other hand, Habakkuk, who says to the Lord: "In the midst of the years make her revive, in the midst of the years make her known!" (Hab 3,2). And what will be, O prophet, the sign that the Lord is coming?: "In the middle of two lives you will know him." With this he clearly alludes to the Lord: when you come in the flesh, you will live and you will die; But when you rise from the dead, you will live again. But from what part of the region of Jerusalem must it come? From the east or from the sunset, from the north or from the south? Tell us in detail. He answers very clearly and says: "God comes from Temán"—but by Temán he means the South40—"the Holy One of Mount Pharaoh, with shadows and clouds"41, which the psalmist said in the same sense: "We have found Him in the Fields of the Forest!" (Ps 132,6). virgin birth

21. Then we ask from whom it will come and how it will come. This is taught to us by Isaiah: "Behold, a virgin42 is pregnant and will give birth to a son, and she will name him Immanuel" (Is 7:14). The Jews, who since ancient times tend to reject the truth, argue against this and say that it is not written virgin, but girl. But, even if I grant this, I find that the truth lies in asking: if a virgin is raped and screams for help, does she do so after or before being raped? Therefore, if Scripture says somewhere: "The betrothed girl perhaps cried out and there was no one to help her" (Dt 32:27), is this not said of a girl who is a virgin?43. And so that you know more clearly that virgins in Holy Scripture are also called "girls", listen to the book of Kings about Abishag, the Shunammite, which says: "The young woman was extraordinarily beautiful" (I Kgs 1:4). And it is known that this is the virgin who was chosen and brought to David (1,3). The sign offered to Ahaz does not refer to his son Hezekiah, but to a virgin, in the future

22. But the Jews reply: what was said to Ahaz referred to Hezekiah. Let's read the Scripture: "Ask for yourself a sign from Yahweh your God in the depths of Sheol or in the highest" (Is 7:11). But it must be a sign that causes admiration and is indisputable. A sign had been the water brought out of the rock (Ex 17:6), the sea parting (14:21) or the sun receding (2 Kings 20:11)44 and other similar things. But what I have to say is greater evidence against the Jews45. Isaiah spoke of all this when Ahaz was king, which he was for sixteen years, a period in which this prophetic oracle took place. The contradiction of the Jews is refuted by his successor, King Hezekiah, son of Ahaz, who was twenty-five years old when he acceded to the throne (2 Kings 18:2). But since the prophecy was made in the period of sixteen years,46 it is at least nine years before the prophecy that Hezekiah of Ahaz was born. There is no need, therefore, for the prophecy to refer to him who had already been born even before his father Ahaz began to reign. Furthermore, Isaiah does not say that a virgin "was" pregnant, but rather—as a prediction—that she "will be." David's lineage is eternal

23. We have already seen clearly that Christ is born of a virgin. Now we will have to explain what this virginity is like. «Yahweh swore to David, and he will not repent: "I will establish the fruit of your womb on your throne45" (Ps 132:11), and also: "I will establish his lineage forever, and his throne as the days of heaven" (89:30). It will remain forever like the moon, a faithful witness in heaven" (Ps 89:36-38). You see that it is talking about Christ, not Solomon, since his throne did not remain like the sun. But if someone disagrees because Christ did not sit on David's wooden throne, let us remind him of this sentence: "The scribes and the Pharisees have sat on the seat of Moses" (Mt 23:2). It does not refer to a chair of wood, but to the doctrinal authority. Do not look for the throne of David in a wooden one, but in the royal power. As witnesses of this accept the children who shouted: "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!" (Mt 21,9). The blind also say: "Have mercy on us, Son of David!" (Mt 9,27). And Gabriel clearly announces to Mary: "The Lord God will give him the throne of David, his father" (Lk 1:32). And Paul: "Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, descended from David, according to my gospel" (2 Tim 2:8). And, at the beginning of the epistle to the Romans, it says: "Born of the line of David according to the flesh" (Rom 1:3). Welcome, therefore, the one who was born of David, in accordance with the prophecy: "On that day the root of Jesse47 will be raised as a banner for the people, the Gentiles will seek it" (Is 11:10).

24. But the Jews are greatly enraged by these things. Isaiah had also foreseen this when he said: “They will be burned, food for the fire. For a creature has been born to us, a son has been given to us” (Is 9:4-5). Realize that he was first the Son of God and then he was given to us. A little further down it says: "His peace will have no end" (9,6). The Romans end themselves, but the kingdom of the Son of God has no end. The Persians and the Medes had an end. But the Son of God has no end. And then it continues: "...on the throne of David and on his kingdom, to restore and consolidate it" (ibid.). From David arose, then, the holy Virgin. The virgin birth is insisted upon

25. It was fitting, then, that he who is most pure and master of purity should arise from a pure bed. For if everyone who holds the priesthood with Jesus abstains from women, how could Jesus be born from a man and a woman? "Yes, you brought me out of the womb," it is said in the Psalms, "you gave me confidence at my mother's breasts" (Ps 22:10). Pay attention to "you took me out of the womb": this means that he came out and was born from the womb and the flesh of a virgin, but without the work of a man, in a different way from that of those who are born according to the nuptial law. It is the flesh of man that God assumes

26. He is not afraid to assume the flesh of members of which he is the architect. But who is it that tells us this? The Lord says to Jeremiah: "Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you" (Jer 1:5). And he who, in making men, touched their members without being ashamed of it, will he be ashamed to create, for his own sake, this holy flesh which is the mantle of his divinity? It is God who in the womb, to this day, shapes human fetuses, according to what was written in Job: “Did you not pour me like milk and curdle me like cheese? You clothed me with skin and flesh and woven me with bones and sinews” (Job 10:1011). There is nothing abominable in the workmanship of man as long as it is not stained by adultery and lasciviousness. He who made Adam also made Eve; With divine hands both man and woman were made. None of the members of the body was made abominable from the beginning. Keep silent, then, all the heretics who accuse the bodies and those who made them49. We, on the other hand, will remember Paul's sentence: "Do you not know that your body is a sanctuary of the Holy Spirit, who is in you"? (1 Cor 6:19). Furthermore, the prophet predicted about the person of Jesus: "My flesh is theirs" (Hos 9:12 LXX)50. And, in another place, it is written: "Therefore he will abandon them until the time when she who is to give birth gives birth" (Mic 5:2)51. And what will be the sign of this?: "She will give birth and the rest of her brothers will return to the children of Israel." And what are the nuptial pledges of the Virgin, the holy wife?: "I will espouse you to me in fidelity, and you will know Yahweh" (Hos 2:22). And Elizabeth, speaking of the same thing, says something similar: "Happy is she who believed that the things that were spoken to her from the Lord would be fulfilled!" (Lk 1,45). Against the objections of the Greeks

27. But both the Greeks and the Jews disturb us, saying that it was impossible for the Messiah to be born of a virgin. Let us, first of all, stop the mouths of the Greeks for their fables. Those of you who maintain that stones that are thrown can transform into men52, how do you say that it is impossible for a virgin to give birth? Those of you who fable that a daughter was born from a brain53, do you affirm that a son cannot come out of the womb of a virgin? Those of you who falsely affirm that Bacchus came out of Jupiter's thigh, as if it were a pregnant womb, how is it that you reject our truth? What I say is unworthy of the present audience. But we say this so that you reject the Greeks, who deny themselves with their fables. Sarah's birth and other prodigies with Moses and Aaron make us understand the miracle of virginal conception

28. To those who come from circumcision, argue like this: what is more difficult, for a barren old woman to give birth or for a virgin who is in the flower of her age to do so? Sarah was sterile and, no longer having her period (Gen 11:30; 18:11), she gave birth outside of her natural capacity (cf. Gen 21:2). Therefore, if it is possible for a barren woman to conceive in an unnatural way, also, beyond nature, a virgin can be a mother. So either you reject both or you admit both. Well, God himself is the one who did that and this. You will not dare to say that this is possible for God, but this is impossible. And what, for example, is so natural about a man's hand changing its appearance in the space of an hour, but then regaining its appearance again? How is it, then, that Moses' hand became white as snow, but instantly returned to its previous state? (see Ex 4,6-7). And you say: it is God who has brought about the change. And if God can do this, can't he also do that? And that sign was intended for the Egyptians (Ex 4,8-9), but this one has been given to the entire world. What work is more difficult, O Jews, for a virgin to give birth or for a rod to become a living being? Confess that, in the time of Moses, a rigid rod took on the appearance of a snake that caused fear to Moses himself. So the one who previously held the rod fled from it afterward as from a dragon, for he really was one, but in reality he fled, not because of what he was holding but from fear of the one who had caused the change54. If, then, eyes came out of the rod that could see, could not a child be born, God willing, from a virginal womb? And I do not mention now that Aaron's rod produced in a single night (cf. Num 17:23) what other trees produce in the space of many years. For who does not know that a rod without bark, even if planted in the middle of a river, will never germinate? But God is not at the service of the trees, but is the author of nature. And a fruitless, dry and barkless rod blossomed, germinated and bore nuts as fruit (cf. ibid.). And he who granted to the rod - in the face of a priesthood that was only a type, that is, a figure of another55 - fruit beyond its capacity, would he not grant childbirth to a virgin because of the true high priest? The birth of Eve is also miraculous

29. All these examples are very remarkable. However, Jews dispute them. And they do not assent to these examples of the rod if they are not convinced by admirable births of the same kind and not natural ones. Ask them, then, in this way: of whom was Eve born in the beginning? What mother made her if she lacked her? But Scripture says that it was made from Adam's rib (Gen 2:22). But if Eve was made from the rib of man without needing a mother, could not a child be born from the womb of a virgin without the help of a man? Women are subject to men to procreate56. For Eve had been born of Adam, not being conceived by a mother, but coming from a man as if he had given birth to her: the debt of this grace was repaid by Mary when, by the power of God, not by a man but by herself, she conceived intact and by the power of the Holy Spirit. The very creation of man is a miracle

30. But there is another much better example. Although it may seem astonishing that some bodies are generated from others, it is, nevertheless, possible. And it is more astonishing that man is made from the dust of the earth57. And it is even more admirable that from a mass of mud the eyelids and the light of the eyes appear, and that from a little mud the solidity of the bones, the softness of the lungs and the various types of limbs are born. All of that is admirable. And that a clay that has come to life travels the world anywhere and builds, and that it teaches and speaks, carries out factory work or performs government tasks, all of this is worthy of admiration. Therefore, ignorant Jews, where did Adam come from? Has not God molded his admirable figure by taking dust from the earth? What then? If the mud becomes an eye, will not a virgin give birth to a son? What seems most impossible to human judgment nevertheless becomes reality. And shall not what is possible by itself be realized? Married without having broken her virginity

31. Let us remember, brothers, these glories and use them as throwing weapons. Let us not follow those who heretically teach a coming of Christ only in appearance or debatable58. Let us also reject those who say that the birth of the Savior took place from a man and a woman, who have dared to say that He was begotten of Joseph and Mary, based on what is written: "He took his wife with him" (Mt 1:24). Let us remember Jacob, who, before taking Rachel, said to Laban: "Give me my wife" (Gen 29:21). As she, before sanctioning the nuptials, was already called Jacob's wife simply because she was betrothed to him, so Mary was also called Joseph's wife because of the betrothal. Observe the careful way of speaking of the Gospel when it says: "In the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent by God to a city in Galilee called Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph" (Luke 1:26). And, in turn, when talking about the registration and that Joseph went up to register, what does the Scripture say?: "Joseph also went up from Galilee... to register with Mary, his espoused wife, who was with child" (Lk 2:4.5). And, although she was pregnant, he did not simply say "his wife," but his "betrothed wife." “God sent his Son,” says Paul, not made of man and woman, but only “born of a woman” (Gal 4:4), in this case, of a virgin. That a virgin is simply called "woman" is something that we already showed before. From a virgin was born who made virgin souls. The multiple witnesses against heresy

32. You are amazed at what has happened. But the same person who gave birth to him was also amazed. Well, he says to Gabriel: "How will this be, since I do not know a man?" And he responds: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you and the power of the Most High will overshadow you, so the one who is to be born will be holy and will be called the Son of God" (cf. Luke 1:34.35). It is a pure and uncontaminated conception. For where the Holy Spirit blows, every stain disappears. The virgin birth of the Only Begotten in the flesh is free from impurity. And if the heretics are against this truth, the Holy Spirit will convince them of it after the anger of the power of the Most High who covered the Virgin with his shadow (Luke 1:35): he will confront them on the day of judgment with his face turned towards Gabriel. The place of the manger that welcomed the Lord will be confusion for them (cf. Lk 2:7). The shepherds who then received the good news will bear their testimony (Luke 2:10 ff.), and also the army of angels who praised, celebrated, and said: "Glory to God in the highest and on earth peace to men in whom he delights" (Luke 2:14). Likewise the temple to which he was taken after forty days (Luke 2:22) "also to offer as a sacrifice a pair of turtledoves or two pigeons" (2:24). Simeon, who then "took him in his arms" (2:28), and the prophetess Anna, who was there (2:36 ff.), will also testify. He who is born of the Virgin is a true man. Praise of chastity

33. Before the testimony of God, together with that of the Holy Spirit and with the words of Christ: "Why do you want to kill me (Jn 7,19), me, who am a man who has told you the truth (cf. 8,46b)?", let the heretics who are against their humanity be silent. Well, they contradict him when he says: "Handle me and see that a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have" (Luke 24:39). May the Lord born of the Virgin be adored and may the virgins know the honor and crown of their own institution. The order of monks also recognizes the glory of purity. Well, we men are not deprived of the dignity of integrity. Christ fulfilled the time of nine months in the womb of the Virgin, but the Lord was a man for thirty-three years, so that if a virgin boasts for a time of nine months, much more can we glory for a multitude of years. Dignity of chastity and virginity

34. Let us all run by the grace of God the race of chastity, "the young men and the maidens, the elderly along with the children" (Ps 148:12), not following lasciviousness, but praising the name of Christ. Let us not ignore the glory of purity, since it is an angelic superiority and a task that goes beyond man: let us respect the bodies, which in due time will shine like the sun. Let us not stain such a worthy body with such low passions. Sin is something small and lasts only a limited time, but its shame lasts for an eternity of years. Those who follow purity are angels who walk the earth. The virgins have a part with the Virgin Mary. Eliminate all striking adornment, all dangerous looks and any dress and perfume that attracts base passions. As for all, let the perfume be prayer, the odor of good works and the sanctification of bodies, so that the Lord born of the Virgin, may also say of us, men who have kept his integrity and women who have received the crown: "I will establish my dwelling in your midst... I will walk among you, and I will be a God to you, and you will be a people to me" (Lev 26:11, 12; cf. 2 Cor 6:16; Apoc 21,3; Ez 36,28; Jer 31,31-34). To whom be glory forever and ever. Amen...

1. This catechesis deepens in the confession of the divinity and humanity of Christ. The prophecies of the old Alliance are also seen fulfilled in Christ. The virginal conception of Christ, which is discussed at great length, gives rise to Cyril to also praise virginity, celibacy and monastic life.
2. This strange expression refers to Christ.

3. Allusion to the complete ingestion of the paschal lamb, a figure of Christ, according to Ex 13:9; "You shall not eat any of it raw or cooked, but roasted, with its head, its legs and its entrails."
4. In the person of Jesus.
5. The virginal conception of Christ was already addressed in cat. 4, no. 9.

6. The expression "totally" seems to refer to the fact that the humanity of Christ could not even be said to be more than apparent. The heretical opinion according to which the humanity of Jesus would be only an appearance has been qualified in the history of Christian theology with the technical term "docetism" (from "dokein", to seem or appear). Docetism, in its various variants, manifested itself among Gnostics and Valentinians. The theology of Apollinaris of Laodicea is not foreign to him, who denies the human soul of Jesus and points out that his intellectual functions would lie only in his divinity. Other variants of Docetism survive in Monophysitism, which was maintained for a long time despite being condemned in Chalcedon (c. 451). In this way, contrary to the denial, in Arianism, that Jesus is God like the Father, in the Docet conceptions a full humanity of Jesus is not affirmed. It was the Council of Constantinople that, in the year 381, following in the footsteps of Nicaea, solemnly affirmed the full human reality of Jesus Christ. In the present catechesis, since the topic is the incarnation of Christ, Cyril moves in the line later drawn by the Council of Constantinople. On the other hand, the confession that the conception of Christ was virginal was the theme especially of the Council of Ephesus, in the year 431, although the Church already expressed that conviction in much earlier times. On these issues it is important to remember the history of the ecumenical councils of ancient times. Pedagogically, the corresponding chapter of J.L.'s Christology is quite interesting.
