And the arm of Yahweh, to whom was it revealed? (53.1). And, in what follows: "He was led like a lamb to the slaughter" (53,7), etc. 1. The cross is what freed all men

1. In any action of Christ the Catholic Church glories. But the height of these glories is the cross. Paul, knowing the matter, says: “As for me, God forbid I should glory except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ! (Gal 6:14). It was undoubtedly admirable that a man blind from birth regained his vision in Siloam (cf. Jn 9). But how did this affect all the blind people in the world? It is great, and beyond all nature, that Lazarus, dead for four days, was resurrected Un 11,39.44). But this is a grace that only reached him. What did this have to do with all those around the world who were dead for their sins? (cf. Eph 2,1 ff; cf. Rom 3,23). It is admirable that five loaves gave food, as if it flowed from five sources, to five thousand men (cf. Mt 14:21). But what is this compared to those around the world who were subjected to the hunger of ignorance? (cf. Am 8:11). It is admirable that a woman was totally freed after having been bound by Satan for eighteen years (cf. Luke 13:10-13). But look at us all, who are bound by the chains of our sins. Instead, the crown—or even the glory—of the cross illuminated those blinded by ignorance, freed those bound by sin, and rescued all men. Jesus has rescued all men

2. Do not be surprised that the entire world has been redeemed. For it was not a simple man, but the only begotten Son of God, who died for this cause. Certainly, the sin of a single man, Adam, could introduce death into the world. But if through the fall of one death reigned in the world, why should it not reign much more through the justice of one?2. And if at that time, because of the wood from which (our fathers) ate, they were expelled from paradise (cf. Gen 3:22-24), will not those who believe now, through the wood of Jesus, enter paradise much more easily? If the first man, made from the earth, brought death to all, will not He who made him from the earth (Gen 2:7), being himself life (Jn 15:5 ff.), give him eternal life? If Pinchas, inflamed with zeal, by killing the perpetrator of the crime, appeased the wrath of God (cf. Num 25:711), will Jesus, without killing anyone, but giving himself as a ransom (I Tim 2:6), not undo the wrath against men (cf. Rom 1:18)? In the absurdity of the cross, and even more so since Jesus is innocent, there is salvation

3. May we not be ashamed of the cross of the Savior, and even glorify ourselves in it. For the word of the cross is scandal to the Jews and foolishness to the Gentiles, but for us it is salvation (cf. I Cor 1:18-25). «It is foolishness for those who are lost; but for those who are saved—for us—it is the power of God” (1:18). For, as has been said3, it was not a simple man who died on our behalf, but God, the Son of God made man. But then the dead lamb, according to the teaching of Moses, threw the Exterminator away4. Now, will not the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world (Jn 1:29) free much more of sins? Also the blood of an irrational sheep showed health. And will not the blood of the Only Begotten bring salvation in a greater measure? If anyone does not believe in the power of the crucified one, question the demons themselves5. And if someone does not believe in the words, believe in the clear things. There are many who have been crucified throughout the world, but the demons are not afraid of any of them. But before Christ, crucified for us, the demons are terrified when they simply see the sign of the cross, because those others crucified were killed for their own sins, but he for those of others. He is "he who committed no sin, and in whose mouth no guile was found" (I Pet 2:22; cf. Is 53:9). It was not Peter who said this, which could arouse the suspicion that he wanted to be pleasing to the teacher, but rather it was Isaiah who had said it, who had not been physically present (before Jesus), but in spirit had foreseen his coming in the flesh. But why do I add only the testimony of the prophet? He counts among the witnesses Pilate himself, who sentenced him saying: "I have not found in this man any of the crimes of which you accuse him" (Luke 23:14). And when he handed it to him, washing his hands, he said: "I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man" (Mt 27:24). And there is also another witness of the innocence of Jesus, the thief who went first to paradise, who rebuked his companion and said: "We are right, because we have deserved it with our actions; On the other hand, this man has done nothing wrong (Lk 23:41), since you and I were in his judgment»7. reality of the crucifixion

4. Thus, Jesus really suffered for all men. The cross is not a fiction, because in that case the redemption would also be something fake. Death was not something apparent, but an indisputable reality. If this were not the case, salvation would simply be a fable. If death had been only apparent, those who said would be right: "Lord, we remember that that impostor said while he was still alive: 'In three days I will rise again'" (Mt 27:63). The passion was, therefore, real: he was truly crucified, and we are not ashamed of it; He was crucified and we do not deny it. Rather I glory in it when I say it. Well, if I deny it now, the Golgotha ​​that we have so close here will argue against me8. He will argue against me the wood of the cross, which in small pieces has been distributed from that place to the whole world. I confess the cross once I have known the resurrection. Well, if he had not gone beyond the cross, perhaps he would not have confessed it and would have hidden it together with the teacher. But since the resurrection has followed the cross, I am not ashamed to proclaim it9. Condemned without any sin

5. He was crucified, who, like everyone else, lived in the flesh, but not with similar sins. Well, he was not led to death by the greed for riches, since he was a master of poverty and the renunciation of goods. He was not condemned for his libidinous passion, he who said clearly: "Everyone who looks at a woman lustfully has already committed adultery with her in his heart" (Mt 5:28). He did not strike or wound anyone in arrogance, but to whomever he struck he showed the other cheek (5:39). And he did not despise the Law, but brought it to its fullness (5:17). He did not accuse the prophets of falsehood, since he was the one who had been announced by them10. He did not defraud in payments, since he healed without charge and free of charge. He did not sin in any way, neither in word nor in deed nor in thought. «He who committed no sin, and in whose mouth no guile was found; the one who, when insulted, did not respond with insults; When he suffered, he did not threaten...» (I Pet 2, 22-23; cf. Is 53,9), who did not come to the passion forced, but of his own will. And to whom he told him to have compassion on himself, he said: "Depart from me, Satan" (Mt 16:23). He voluntarily went to passion without shying away from it

6. Do you want to convince yourself more that he came of his own free will to passion? All the others, who are unaware of their destiny, die unwillingly, but he predicted of his own passion: "The Son of Man is going to be handed over to be crucified" (Mt 26:2). Do you know why he, who loved men, did not refuse death? So that the world would not be lost for its sins. "Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over and will be crucified" (see Mt 20:18-19). And, on the other hand: "He confirmed his will to go to Jerusalem"11. Do you want to know clearly that the cross of Jesus is glorious? Don't listen to me, but to the one who says so. It was Judas who handed him over, full of ingratitude towards the one who had invited them. He soon left the table after drinking the chalice of blessing, but he went from this drink of salvation to shedding the blood of the righteous. "He who ate my bread lifts up his heel against me" (Ps 41:10)12. Shortly before, his hands received the blessings (or the pieces of the blessed bread), and immediately afterwards he plotted his death for the money for which he had agreed to betray. When he was caught in it and upon hearing "You said it" (Mt 26:25), he went out again. Then Jesus said: "The time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified" (Jn 12:23). Do you see how he knew that his own cross was glory to him?13. If Isaiah, being sawn14, does not believe that this is shameful, will Christ, who dies for the world, consider it a disgrace? "The time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified" (Jn 12:23): not because he lacked glory before. For he had been glorified "with the glory that was at your side (in Jesus' phrase) before the world was" (Jn 17:5; cf. 17:24). But from eternity he was glorified as God; now, however, he was glorified in the crown of suffering. He did not lose his life unwillingly nor was he killed without his strength, but voluntarily. Listen to what he says: "I have power to give it (life) and power to recover it again" (Jn 10:18). I give in to enemies voluntarily, because if I didn't want to, it wouldn't happen. He came to passion by his free will, rejoicing in the exemplary work and even more for the crown he would receive and for the salvation of men. By not being ashamed before the cross, he brought salvation to the entire world. And it was not a vile man who suffered, but God made man fighting for the reward of his obedience. The suffering Messiah, a new teaching before the Gentiles

7. But the Jews are against it, always prepared for contradiction and slow to believe. That is why the prophet that has been read15 said: "Lord, who has given credit to our preaching?" (Is 53,1). The Persians believe, but the Hebrews do not. "Those who received no message from him will see him, and those who heard nothing will understand" (Rom 15:21, taken from Is 52:15). And those who reflect on it will reject what they think about. They reply to us and say: Is it that God suffers? And were there no human forces greater than the Lord's own force? Read the Lamentations: Jeremiah, complaining about you, wrote in them things truly worthy of regret. He saw your perdition and contemplated your fall. He lamented the ancient Jerusalem, because for the one that now exists there will be no tears16. That one crucified the Messiah, but the present one worships him. In the Lamentations it is said: "Our vital breath, Christ the Lord, was imprisoned in our corruption"17. But am I using imaginary expressions? The text speaks of Christ the Lord, taken prisoner by men. What will happen then? Tell me, prophet. And he answers: "In his shadow we will live among the nations!" (Lm 4,20b). But he points out that the grace of life will no longer be in Israel, but among the Gentiles. Listen and find out the testimonies of the Passion in the Scriptures

8. But since they contradict us in multiple ways, let us, albeit briefly, present, with the grace of the Lord, some testimonies of the passion. Because everything that concerns Christ has been written: nothing is ambiguous nor has anything been left unrecorded; Everything has been written in the testimonies of the prophets, and not on tables of stone, but clearly described by the Holy Spirit. So, when you hear the gospel account of Judas' actions, shouldn't you pay attention to this testimony? You heard that Christ's side was pierced by a spear. Shouldn't you examine that this is also written? (Jn 19,24-37). You heard that he was crucified in the garden. Shouldn't you check that this has been written? (Jn 19:41). You heard that it was sold for thirty pieces of silver. Won't you listen to the prophet who spoke about it (cf. Mt 26:15 and Zec 11:12b). You heard that he was given vinegar to drink. Also learn where this is written (cf. Jn 19:29 and Ps 69:22b). You heard that the body was buried inside a rock covered with a stone (Mt 27:60). Will you not accept the testimony of the prophet on this matter (cf. Is 53:9)? You heard that he was crucified among thieves (Mt 27:38). Shouldn't you also find out if that was written18? You heard that he was buried (Mt 27:59-60). Shouldn't you find out if somewhere there was written about his burial (Is 53:9)? You heard that he was resurrected. Shouldn't you investigate if we deceive you with these teachings? Although "my word and my preaching had nothing of the persuasive speeches of wisdom" (1 Cor 2:4). Sophistic artifices are not constructed here19, but rather they are undone. This is not a war of words, which sometimes prove useless, but rather "we preach a crucified Christ" (I Cor 1:23), which had been previously preached by the prophets. And now you, as you welcome these testimonies, seal them in your heart. But, since we are very numerous and now lack more time, let us be allowed at this moment to listen to some things that are of greater importance. Understand our argument and take the trouble to find out the rest. And may your hand not only be extended to receive, but also to act (see perhaps Ecclesiastes 4:31). God gratifies everything. "If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all" (James 1:5), and he will receive it from him.
Who, moved by your supplications, grants us, those of us who speak to you, to be able to do it and, to you who listen, to believe20. Facts about the betrayal of Judas

9. Let us seek, therefore, the testimonies about the passion of Christ. We have decided not to make a purely contemplative exposition of the Scriptures, but rather to convince ourselves, through certain data, of those we believe. Before you received the testimonies about the coming of Jesus21. It is also written that he walked on the sea (Ps 77,20: "Your path was through the sea!"; Job 9,8b: "He trodden the back of the Sea") and you have received the testimony of various healings. I will begin, then, at the beginning of the Passion: Judas was a traitor, he arrived as an adversary and there he was speaking peacefully while plotting hostilities. The Psalmist says of him: "My friends and companions depart from my wound, my loved ones from a distance remain" (Ps 38:12). And also: "His words, softer than oil, are naked swords" (Ps 55:22), or: "Hail, Rabbi!" (Mt 26,49). At that moment he handed over the Master to death without taking into account the warning of the one who said: "Judas, with a kiss you hand over the Son of man!" (Luke 22:48). It is as if he rebuked him with this: "Remember your name," since Judas means "confession." You made a pact, you received the money. «O God of my praise, do not remain mute!

22. Mouth of the wicked, mouth of deceit, open against me. They speak to me with a lying tongue, they surround me with words of hate” (Ps 109:1-3a). But you heard23 that even some of the chief priests were there and that he was bound before the city gates. Keep in mind what the psalm says about the time and place: "They return in the evening, they howl like dogs, they prowl the city" (Ps 59:7,15).

10. Listen, then, also about the thirty pieces of silver: "I said to them, 'If it pleases you, give me my wages; if not, leave it alone'" (Zech 11:12), and what follows24. You owe me25 the grace of healing the blind and the lame. And what I receive is different: instead of gratitude, outrage; instead of worship, insult. You see how Scripture knew the future in advance: "They weighed my wages: thirty shekels of silver" (Zech 11:12). Oh prophetic word of literal precision! Oh immense and certain wisdom of the Holy Spirit! Well, he didn't say ten or twenty, but expressly and exactly "thirty", as they really were. Tell also, prophet, where this payment went. Will the one who received it retain it or return it? And, after returning it, where will he fall? In fact, the prophet says: "So I took the thirty shekels of silver and cast them into the house of Yahweh, into the furnace" (Zech 11:13). Compare the Gospel with the prophecy: «Then Judas,... harassed by remorse, he says,... threw the coins into the Sanctuary; then he retired", etc. (Mt 27,3.5).

11. But I try to suppress an apparent ambiguity here26. For those who reject the prophets argue that the prophet says: "I cast them into the house of Yahweh, into the furnace" (Zech 11:13). And the Gospel, on the other hand: "They saw them in the Potter's Field" (Mt 27:10). But pay attention to how both things are true. The Jews, that is, those who were then princes of the priests, seeing that Judas repented and exclaimed: "I sinned by giving up innocent blood" (27:4), reply: "To us, what? You'll see" (ibid.). Does it have anything to do with you, who crucified him? Let him see who received and returned the crime money. And those of you who have done it will have nothing to do with it? Then they say among themselves: "It is not lawful to put them into the treasury of offerings, because they are the price of blood" (27:6). Your mouth condemns them, since the price is abominable and the crime is also abominable: if you fulfill justice by crucifying Christ, why do you not accept the price? But we wondered: How come there is no disagreement between the gospel that says "Potter's Field" and the prophet who mentions "the furnace"? In reality, not only those who work with gold or only those who work with coins have a kiln, but also potters have a kiln for clay. They separate the finest and thickest soil, straining what will be used to separate it from the pebbles and choosing plenty of moldable material, they then knead it, thus preparing what will be cooked. Why, then, are you surprised if the gospel speaks, more clearly, of the "Potter's Field," at the same time that the prophet pronounced his prophecy in an enigmatic way, whereas prophecies are often contained in enigmas? The judgment and mockery of Jesus

12. "Then they seized him, took him away, and made him enter the house of the High Priest" (Luke 22:54). Do you want to know and see that this is also written? Isaiah says: "Woe to those who deliberate depravedly among themselves saying: Let us bind the righteous, because it is uncomfortable for us" (Is 3,9.10 LXX). Certainly: "Woe to those!" Let's look at this. Isaiah was cut in two, but the people later received health. Jeremiah was thrown into the mud of the cistern (38:6), but in this way the wound of the Jews was healed, because, being a sin against a man, it was lighter. But the Jews did not sin against a man, but against God made man. "Woe to them!" But, "let us bind the just," we said. Will he not be able to untie himself, will someone reply, who freed Lazarus from the bonds of a death that had already lasted four days? (Jn 11,39.44) and the one who freed Peter from the iron chains of prison (Acts 12,7). The angels were ready saying: "Let us break their bonds" (Ps 2:3)27, although they abstain from violence because God wanted to suffer this. He was also brought to trial among the elders (Mt 26:57). He already had a testimony of this: "Yahweh sues the elders of his people and their leaders in judgment" (Is 3:14).

13. But when the High Priest questioned him, he became indignant upon hearing the truth (Mt 26:62-63) and one of the worst of his servants slapped him. That face, which had once shone like the sun (Mt 17:2), endured being broken by wicked hands, and others approached spitting on the face of the one who had healed the man blind from birth through saliva (Jn 9:6). "Is this how you repay Yahweh, you foolish and foolish people?" (Dt 32,6). And the prophet, astonished, says: "Who believed our news?" (Is 53,1)28. It is truly incredible that God, the Son of God and the arm of Yahweh29 are exposed to these things. But, so that those who are saved do not refuse to believe in this, the Holy Spirit predicts it from the person of Christ when he exclaims (for he was the one who spoke then and later became present): "I offered my back to those who beat me" (Is 50:6)30. And Pilate, once scourged, handed him over to be crucified (Mk 15:15): «I offered... my cheeks to those who pulled my beard. I did not hide my face from insults and spittle” (Is 50:6). As if to say: anticipating that they were going to hit me, I didn't even twist my cheek slightly. How would I strengthen the disciples against the death they had to face for the truth if I myself was terrified by it? I had said: "He who loves his life loses it" (Jn 12:25). If I loved life, how would I give lessons without doing what I teach? Therefore, he, being God, endured to suffer these things from men so that we men would not be ashamed after suffering such things from men because of him. You see that these things have been widely predicted by the prophets. But, as I said before, we overlook many testimonies of Scripture because of the little time available. But if someone investigates everything carefully, none of the things concerning Christ will be left without its corresponding testimony. Before Pilate and Herod

14. Bounded, Caiaphas came to Pilate. Wasn't this also previously written? "And tying him up, they brought him as a present to King Jarim" (Hos 10:7 LXX)31. But some of you will argue angrily: "Pilate was not king (also omitting many other details). How, then, "binding him, they brought him as a present to King Jarim"? But read the Gospel: "When Pilate heard that he was from Galilee,... he referred him to Herod"32. Herod was then king and was in Jerusalem (cf. Luke 23:7). And observe the diligent diligence of the prophet, since he says that he was sent in place of gifts, because "on that day Herod and Pilate became friends, since before they were at enmity" (Lk 23:12). It was appropriate that he who was to bring peace to earth and heaven pacify, as first of all, those who condemned him. For it was the same Lord, "who reconciles the hearts of the princes of the earth" (Job 12:24)33. Accept the precisions and authentic testimony of the prophets. More about the trial of Jesus

15. Admire the Lord whom they judge. He agreed to be carried by the soldiers and have them circle around him while Pilate was "sitting at the tribunal" (Mt 27:19). He, who is seated at the right hand of the Father, stood while he was judged. The people freed by him from the land of Egypt, and many other times from other places, shouted against him: "Crucify him, crucify him!" (Jn 19,6). Why so, O Jews? At this, the prophet exclaims stupefied: "Against whom do you open your mouth and stick out your tongue?" (Is 57,4). The Lord himself relates in the prophets: “My inheritance has behaved toward me like a lion in the forest: it harassed me with its voices; That is why I hated it” (Jer 12:8). I did not expel her, but they expelled me. That is why I say consistently: "I have abandoned my home"34. The attitude of the Servant during the trial

16. When judged, he was silent, so that Pilate was suffering and said: «Do you not answer anything? What do these testify against you? (Mt 26,62). Not because he knew the man who was being judged, but because he feared what his wife's dream meant for him (Mt 27:19). And Jesus was silent. The psalmist says: "I am like a man who does not hear, nor has an answer on his lips" (Ps 38:15). And furthermore: "But I am like a deaf man, I do not hear, like a mute man who does not open his mouth" (38:14; cf. Is 53.7). You've heard this too, if you remember.

17. But the soldiers around him mock him. For them, the Lord is an object of ridicule and they make fun of him. "They see me and shake their heads" (Ps 109:25). The kingdom is glimpsed in an image: they mock, but they bend their knee (Mt 27:29); Some soldiers nail him to the cross, but first they place a purple cloak on him (27,28) and a crown on his head. Of what is it, if not thorns? (27,29). He is proclaimed king of all by the soldiers. It was also appropriate that Jesus was crowned in figure by the soldiers, so that is why the Scripture says in the Song of Songs: "Go out and see, daughters of Zion, Solomon the king, with the diadem with which his mother crowned him" (Song 3:11). That crown was a mystery, since it was the destruction of sins and the absolution of the sentence of condemnation. The curse of the fig tree

18. Adam received the condemnation: "Cursed be the ground because of you... It will produce thorns and thistles for you" (Gen 3,17.18). That is why Jesus took the thorns on himself, to undo the curse; and for this reason he was buried in the ground, so that the land that had been cursed might receive a blessing instead of a curse. At the time of the first sin, fig leaves were girded (Gen 3:7). That is why Jesus ended the signs with a fig tree. Well, when he had to go to his passion, he struck the fig tree with a curse (cf. Mt 24:32 ff.). He did not refer to every fig tree, but to that one alone, saying in an image: "May no one ever eat fruit from you!" (Mc 11,14): the condemnation is undone. And the time when the fig trees cover themselves with leaves is precisely when there is no food. Who does not know that in winter time the fig tree does not bear fruit, but only has leaves? Was Jesus unaware of what everyone knew? No, he knows what he is searching for, although he is unaware that he will not find anything, extending his curse only to the leaves35. Jeremiah, image of Jesus despised

19. Once we have approached the things of paradise, I certainly admire the truth of the figures36. In paradise the fall occurred, and in the garden salvation; sin came from the tree, but sin came to the tree37; In the afternoon, when the Lord was walking, they looked for a hiding place (Gen 3:8), and it is in the afternoon when the thief is introduced by the Lord into paradise (Luke 23:43). But someone will tell me: think, see if you can show me the wood of the cross through the prophets, because I will not assent if you do not show me a prophetic testimony. Well, listen to Jeremiah and be convinced: "And I was like a meek lamb led to the slaughter, not knowing..." (Jer 11:19). Also read this question that, as I said, Jesus asks: «Do you not know that in two days is the Passover; and the Son of man is going to be handed over to be crucified? (Mt 26,2)38. Was it he who ignored it? "And I was like a meek lamb led to the slaughter, not knowing..." (Jer ibid.). But what is the sign? Understand John the Baptist when he says: "Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world" (Jn 1:29). Was he, who knows thoughts, ignorant of events? And what did they say?: «... they plotted plots against me: 'We want to put wood in their bread'» (Jer 11,19b LXX)39. If God considers you worthy of it, later you will learn that his body showed, according to the gospel, the figure of bread. So, "come, we want to put wood in his bread, let us erase him from the land of the living, and his name will not be mentioned again"40. Life is not destroyed. Why do you tire them with useless work? Your project is vain. May his name be blessed forever, may it last as long as the sun! (Ps 72,17). And that life was hanging on the tree, Moses says it lamenting: "your life will be before you as if hanging by a thread, you will be afraid night and day, and you will not even feel safe in your life" (Dt 28:66). And what was read recently: "Who gave credence to our news?" (Is 53,1). Salvation from the wood of the cross

20. This figure was illustrated by Moses crucifying the serpent, so that whoever had been bitten by a live serpent, upon looking at the bronze serpent, would obtain salvation by believing (Num 21:4-9). And if the crucified bronze serpent grants salvation, will not the Son of God nailed to the cross grant salvation? Salvation always comes through a log. In the time of Noah, life was preserved by a wooden ark (Gen 7:23). And when Moses stretched out his staff over the sea, he withdrew out of reverence for the one who touched it (Ex 14:16-21). And if Moses could do so much with his staff, will the cross of the Savior be ineffective? I leave aside, in honor of brevity, many other figures. However, he made the water sweet at the time (Ex 15:25), and water flowed from the side of Christ on the tree (Jn 19:34)41. More about water and blood from the side

21. The first of Moses' signs is water and blood. And this first of all was the last of Jesus' signs. First, Moses transformed the river into blood (Ex 7:20) and Jesus, finally, made bloody water flow from the side. Perhaps because of the two voices, on the one hand that of those who judged him, and on the other that of those who cruelly shouted. Or, perhaps, because of those who believed or those who disbelieved. For while Pilate said: "I am innocent", others shouted: "his blood is on us..." (Mt 27,24.25). Both things gushed from his side: water, perhaps in reference to the judge, and blood, taking into account those who were screaming. But it can also be understood like this: blood for Jews, water for Christians. For those, insidious, condemnation by spilled blood; for you, who now believe, salvation by water. Nothing has happened in vain. The interpreters of Scripture42, our Fathers, have transmitted to us another explanation of the matter: in the gospels they speak of a double force of the baptism of salvation. One, through water, which is granted to those who are enlightened43, and another which in times of persecution is given to the martyrs through their own blood. Blood and water flowed from the Savior's side, confirming the grace of the confession made by Christ44 both in baptism and in times of martyrdom. But there is also another cause of that on the side. The beginning and head of sin was the woman, who was formed from one side. But once Jesus came, to grant forgiveness to both men and women, the side was pierced in the women in order to undo the sin. Glory on the cross

22. But if someone digs deeper, they will also find other causes, although what has been said is sufficient both for the lack of time and for not tiring their ears, although one should never experience fatigue from hearing the triumphs of the Lord, above all, in this thrice-holy Golgotha, since some only hear, but we also see and touch45. Let no one get tired. With the same cross he takes up arms against his adversaries. Make faith in the cross the banner against contradictors. When you have to argue about the cross against those who do not believe, first make the sign of the cross with your hand and the enemy will remain silent. Don't be ashamed to confess the cross. For in it the angels glorify themselves saying: "I know that you seek Jesus, the Crucified" (Mt 28:5). Could you not, O angel, say: "I know whom you seek, my Lord." But "I," he says with confidence, "have known him crucified." The cross is, therefore, triumph and not ignominy. Salvation is in the Crucified

23. For the rest, let us return to what we wanted to show through the prophets. The Lord was crucified and you have received the testimonies. You see the place of Golgotha...46. You acclaim, assenting to what is said: be careful not to deny it on occasion during times of persecution. May the cross not be joy for you only in times of peace: have the same faith in times of persecution, so that it does not happen that you are a friend of Jesus in times of peace and an enemy in times of difficulties. Now you receive the forgiveness of your sins and the generous graces of the King's spiritual gift. When war breaks out, fight hard for your king. Jesus, who had sinned nothing, has been crucified for you. And will you not allow yourself to be crucified by him who was nailed to the cross for you? It is not you who gives grace, because you received it first. What you do is return it by paying the debt to the one who was crucified for you on Golgotha. But Golgotha ​​means "Place of the Skull" (cf. Jn 19:17). Who prophetically named that place Golgotha, where Christ the head suffered the cross? As the Apostle says: "He is the image of the invisible God" (Col 1,15) and, a little further down, "He is also the Head of the Body, of the Church" (1,18) and, in turn: "the head of every man is Christ" (I Cor 11,3) and also, "He is the Head of every Principality and of all Power" (Col 2,10). The Head suffered in the “Place of the Skull.” Oh great name and full of prophetic meaning! Well, almost the name itself warns you as if to say: do not look at the crucified one as a simple man. For he is "Head of every Principality and all Power." He who has been nailed to the cross and who has the Father as his head is the "Head of all Power": for "the head of man is Christ... and the head of Christ is God" (1 Cor 11:3). Other details of the Passion predicted by the prophets

24. Christ was therefore crucified for us. The trial was held at night and in a cold environment, which is why they lit some embers (Jn 18:18). He was crucified at the third hour (Mk 15:25). From the sixth hour there was darkness until the ninth hour (Mt 27:45). And again there was light from the ninth hour. Are these things also written? Let's search. So Zechariah says: «On that day there will no longer be light, but cold and ice (because Peter was warming himself). It will be a unique day, known only to Yahweh" (Zech 14:6-7). What's happening? Didn't he know other days? But “this is the day that Yahweh has made” (Ps 118:24), the day of the patience of the Lord, “known only to Yahweh; there will be no day and then night” (Zech 14:7). What is the enigma that the prophet narrates? That day does not consist of day and night. What will we call it? The Gospel interprets it with its narration. "There will be no day." For the sun did not shine, as usual, from east to west, but from the sixth hour to the ninth hour there was darkness in the middle of the day. So there was darkness involved. But God had called the darkness "night." Therefore, there was no distinction between day and night: neither was the light total, so that it was called "day", nor could it be called "night" because everything was darkness, but the sun shone after none. The prophet announces this, because after he said "there will be no day and then night" (14:7), he adds: "in the evening there will be light" (ibid.). Do you realize how accurate the word of the prophets is and the truth of the things predicted?

25. But do you want to know exactly the time when the sun went dark, fifth, eighth or tenth hour? Tell it clearly, O prophet, to the unbelieving Jews: When did the sun set? In fact, the prophet Amos says: "On that day, says the Lord Yahweh, I will cause the sun to set at noon" (there was darkness from the sixth hour), "and in broad daylight I will cover the earth with darkness" (Am 8:9). What is this distribution of time, O prophet, and what is the day?: "I will turn your festival into mourning" (Am 8:10). In fact, this was happening in the unleavened bread and at the Passover festival (Mk 14:1). And later he says: "I will do it as the mourning of an only son and its end as a day of bitterness" (Am 8,10c). On the day of Unleavened Bread and on the feast of women they lamented and cried (Lk 23:27), while the apostles, hidden, were overcome with pain. Admirable, then, is the prophecy. The mantle and tunic

26. But, someone will say, give me another sign. What other note is characteristic of all this? Jesus was crucified. He used a tunic and a mantle. But the soldiers divided the mantle among themselves after dividing it into four parts. However, they did not tear the tunic because, torn in that way, it would have been of no use, but rather the soldiers cast lots among themselves (Jn 19:23-24). They divide the cloak and draw lots for the tunic. Wasn't that also written? Well, the eager psalmists of the Church47, who imitate the angelic armies, know this and celebrate God with continuous praise. Those who are considered worthy of this, chant at this holy Golgotha48 and say: "Divide my garments among yourselves and draw lots for my tunic" (Ps 22:19). That draw was the draw for the soldiers. The purple cloak

27. When he was being judged by Pilate, he was dressed in red, they covered him with a purple cloak (/Mt/27/28). Is this also written? Isaiah says: "Who is this that comes from Edom, from Bozrah, with red-dyed clothing?" (Is 63,1). As if to say: who is this that is dressed in purple to shame him? Well, that's what Bozrah sounds like among the Hebrews49. "And why is your dress red, and your clothing like that of a winemaker?" (63.2). And he responds by saying: "I stretched out my hands all day toward a rebellious people who follow a wrong path in pursuit of their thoughts" (Is 65:2). The cross of Christ and its saving effectiveness

28. He stretched out his hands on the cross to encompass the ends of the world. For the central place of the earth is here, on Golgotha. And it is not my word, but that of the prophet who says: "Author of salvation in the midst of the earth" (Ps 74:12). He extended his human hands, with the sole help of which and with his mind behind them he gave consistency to heaven (cf. Ps 33, óa). They were fixed with nails so that, nailed to the wood and annihilated the sins of men that their humanity carried upon themselves, at the same time sin would die and we would be resurrected in justice50. For as through a man came death, so also through a man came life (cf. Rom 5:1221): through a man, the Savior, who suffered death voluntarily. Remember that: "I have power to give it (life) and power to recover it again" (A 10:18). The prophetic charisma of Israel, a barren vineyard, in the Church

29. He endured these things when he came to save everyone. But the people paid him badly. Jesus says: "I thirst" (Jn 19,28), he who gave them water from a rough rock (Ex 17,1-7) and demands the fruits of the vineyard he planted (Jer 2,21; Is 5,2). But from what vineyard? By its nature, it would be the one that existed since the holy Patriarchs, but it is actually the one that, due to temptation, comes from Sodom that reaches the thirsty Lord with vinegar through a soaked sponge placed on a reed (cf. Jn 19:29). This fulfills the saying: "For his vineyard is the vineyard of Sodom and the plantations of Gomorrah" (Dt 32:32a)51. And also: "They have given me poison for food52, in my thirst they have watered me with vinegar" (Ps 69:22). You see the insight of prophetic prediction. And what was the gall they put in my mouth like? "They gave him, he says, wine with myrrh" (Mk15:23). Myrrh, with a taste of gall and a little bitter53. «Is this how you repay the Lord?» (Deut 32,6). Is this what you offer, vineyard, to the Lord? Isaiah already complained precisely about you, saying: "My friend had a vineyard on a fertile hill" (Is 5:1)54. And, in short: "He waited, he says, for it to bear grapes" (5,2). I was thirsty and wanted it to give wine, "but it gave thorns55. You see the crown with which I have been redeemed. What will I do next? (ch. Is 5,5): "I will forbid the clouds to rain on it" (5,6). It no longer has clouds, that is, it no longer has prophets, since it is in the Church where the prophets have been, as Paul says: "As for the prophets, let two or three speak, and the rest judge" (1 Cor 14:29). And further: «He (Christ) himself gave to one to be apostles; to others, prophets” (Eph 4:11)56. Agabus was a prophet, who tied his hands and feet (Acts 21:10-11). Jesus, outraged on the cross, between the two thieves GOOD-THIEF: 30. About the thieves who were crucified with him (cf. /Lk/23/32) it has been said: "He was numbered with the rebels" (Is 53:12). Both were wicked at first, but one ceased to be so. But the other despised the laws until the end, without humbling himself for his salvation, since while he was nailed by hand, his tongue still blasphemed. The Jews shook their heads, insulting the crucified man and fulfilling what was written. "They see me and shake their heads" (Ps 109:25; cf. Mt 27:39 ff; Luke 23:39-43). They made fun of him along with the others, but one of them rebuked the other: for him the end of his life and the beginning of his amendment coincided. He gave his soul and received, before others, salvation.

After rebuking his companion, he said: "Jesus, remember me" (Lk 23:42), my words are addressed to you. Leave it to him, for the eyes of his mind are blind, but "remember me." I am not saying that you remember my works, because I am afraid of them. Every man tends to join kindly with those who are his companion on the road. I am your companion on the path to death: remember me, I am your companion. I do not say: now "remember me", but "when you come with your Kingdom" (ibid.). Mercy for the "good thief"

31. What energy, O thief, illuminated you? Who taught you to worship him who had been insulted and crucified with you? Oh eternal light, which illuminates those who lie in darkness (see Luke 1:79)! He heard, of course, precisely: "Trust"58. Not because your works should be the basis of your confidence, but because there is a king willing to grace you. It was a request for something very far away, but grace came very quickly: "I assure you, today you will be with me in paradise" (Lk 23:43), since today you have heard my voice and have not hardened your heart (Ps 94:8). Very quickly I pronounced sentence against Adam. And I forgive you very quickly. He was told: "In the day you eat of it, you will surely die" (Gen 2:17). You, however, today have listened to faith, and today you will receive salvation. He fell through a tree, and you are introduced, through a tree, into paradise. Do not fear the serpent, for it will not drive you out: it has already fallen from heaven (cf. Luke 10:18). Nor am I telling you: today you will leave, but "trust: today you will be with me in paradise", you will not be rejected. Do not fear the flaming sword (cf. Gen 3:24), for it is the one that fears the Lord. Oh immense and ineffable grace! Abraham the believer has not yet entered, and the thief is already entering. Moses and the prophets have not entered yet, but the thief does enter. Before you, Paul was amazed at this saying: "Where sin abounded, grace abounded all the more" (Rom 5:20). Those who have endured the heat (cf. Mt 20:12) have not yet entered, but the one who arrived at the eleventh hour has entered (20:6). Let no one murmur against the owner, who says: "Friend, I am not doing you any injustice... Can't I do what I want with mine?" (20,13.15). The thief wants to do righteous deeds, but death worries him. I do not focus so much on works, but I accept your faith. I'm picking the lilies; Come, let me feed you in the gardens (cf. Song 6:2). I have found the lost sheep and I carry it on my shoulders (Luke 15:5). He really believes, since he said: «I have gone astray like a lost sheep (Ps 119,176). “Jesus, remember me when you come with your Kingdom” (Lk 23:42). The definitive and eternal priesthood of Jesus Christ

32. I already told my wife about this garden in the Song of Songs59, saying these things to her: "I have now entered into my garden, my sister, my bride" (Song 5:1). In fact, where he was crucified there was a garden (Jn 19:41). And what do you deduce from there? That "I have taken my myrrh with my balm" (Song 5:1), which is fulfilled when he drinks myrrhed wine and vinegar (Jn 19:29 par.), and, after drinking them, he says: "It is finished" (Jn 19:30). The mystery has reached its fullness. What was written has been fulfilled. Sins have been dissolved, then, “when Christ arrived as High Priest of future goods, through a greater and more perfect Tent, not made by the hand of man, that is, not of this world. And he entered the sanctuary once for all, not with the blood of goats or bulls, but with his own blood, achieving eternal redemption. For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of cows sanctify with their sprinkling those who are defiled, in order to purify the flesh, how much more the blood of Christ...! (Hebrews 9:11-14). And, on the other hand: "Having therefore, brothers, full security to enter the sanctuary60 by virtue of the blood of Jesus, by this new and living way, inaugurated by him for us, through the veil, that is, through his own flesh..." (Hebrews 10:19-20). And since the flesh, its own veil, was affected by dishonor, that is why the veil of the temple, which was a figure of the future, was rent, as it is written: "At this, the veil of the Sanctuary was rent in two, from top to bottom" (Mt 27:51). And absolutely nothing remained of him. And since the Lord said: "Your house will be left deserted" (Mt 23:38), the house itself was destroyed61. Christ gives himself to the Father

33. The Savior endured these things, “making peace with what is on earth and in heaven through the blood of his cross” (Col 1:20). For we were enemies of God because of sin, and God decided that it was appropriate for the sinner to die. Therefore, one of two things was necessary: ​​either that God, consequently, caused everyone to perish, or that with his mercy he annulled the sentence passed. Observe, however, the wisdom of God: he preserved both the firmness of the sentence and the effectiveness of goodness. Christ, "on the tree, bore our sins in his body, so that, dead to our sins, we might live for righteousness" (I Pet 2:24; cf. Is 53:12; 2 Cor 5:21; Rom 6:11,18). It is not that the one who died for us lacked courage: he was not just one of those sheep, nor was he just a man, nor simply an angel. It was God made man. The iniquity of sinners was not as great as the justice of him who died for us62. We do not sin as much as he who gave his life for us stood out for his justice, who gave it up when he wanted and took it back when he wanted (Jn 10:18). Do you want to know how he did not give up his life under duress or force, and that he did not give up his spirit against his will? He addressed the Father saying: "Father, I put my spirit in your hands" (Lk 23:46; cf. Ps 31:6), to put it briefly now, "and having said this, he expired", but he did not remain that way for long, because he quickly rose from the dead. Death and burial

34. The sun was eclipsed (Lk 23,44) because of the "sun of righteousness" (Mal 3,20)63, "the rocks were split" (Mt 27,51) because of the intelligible rock, "the tombs were opened" (Mt 27,52) and the dead were raised (52b) because of him who was free among the dead, he set free the "captives of the pit in which there is no water" (Zech 9:11). Therefore, do not be ashamed of the crucified one, but say with confidence: "And yet it was our ailments that he bore and our pains that he endured!... and with his bruises we have been healed" (Is 53:4.5). Let us not be ungrateful towards the benefactor. And, furthermore: «For the rebellions of his people he has been wounded; and his grave was placed among the wicked and his grave with the rich” (53:89). That is why Paul says clearly: "Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, and was buried, and rose again on the third day according to the Scriptures" (1 Cor 15:3-4). The tomb excavated in rock

35. But we want to know clearly where he was buried. Was a tomb built? Does it stand out from the ground like royal tombs? Has a monument been made with stones attached to each other? What was put on him? Give us, prophets, a description of the tomb and tell us where the body was placed and where we will look for it. And they respond: "Remember the rock from which you were hewn, and the hollow pit from which you were dug" (Is 51:1). You have in the Gospels: "In a tomb dug in the rock" (Lk 23:53), "in a tomb that was dug in the rock" (Mark 15:46). And furthermore, what? What is the door of the monument? There is, on the other hand, another prophet who says: "They suffocated my life in a pit and threw stones on me" (Lam. 3:53). I, the “cornerstone, chosen, precious” (1 Pet 2:6), am hidden among the stone for a short time; "stone of scandal" for the Jews (1 Pet 2:8) and of salvation for those who believe. Thus, the tree of life is planted in the earth, so that the earth, which had been cursed, would obtain the blessing and the dead would be freed. The strength of the sign of the cross

36. Let us not be overcome by the shame of confessing a crucified person. On your forehead, as a gesture of trust, make the sign of the cross with your fingers, and that for everything: when we eat bread or when we drink, when we enter and leave, before going to bed, when we sleep and when we get up, when we walk and when we are still. It is a great protection: free, for those in need; It does not cost effort, for the weak, and, as it has been given by God as a grace: a sign of the faithful and fear of the demons, whom in it "he publicly exhibited, incorporating them into his triumphal procession" (Col 2:15). Well, when they see the cross, the image of the crucified person comes to mind. They fear him who crushed the heads of the dragon (cf. Ps 74:14)65. Because it is free, do not despise this sign: rather venerate our benefactor in it. The historical reality of the cross of Christ

37. And if you ever intervene in an argument and run out of arguments, may your faith remain in you unshakable. Because with the teaching you have received you can reduce the Jews to silence through the prophets and the Greeks based on their own fables. Well, the latter worship those who have died from lightning. But when lightning appears, it does not usually strike at random. And if they are not ashamed to worship those whom God has rejected, will you, who have been loved by God and are his son, be ashamed to worship him who has been crucified for you?
