He also receives another testimony from Psalm 88, when it is Christ who prophetically says: "Yahweh God of my salvation, before you I cry day and night" (Ps 88,2) and, shortly after: "I am like a finished man: relegated among the dead" (88,5-ó). He does not say "I am a finished man", but "like a finished man": he was not crucified because he lacked strength, but voluntarily. Nor did death come to him due to involuntary weakness. "You have cast me into the depths of the pit" (v. 7). And what was the sign of this?: "You have taken my acquaintances away from me."9 In fact, his disciples fled (Mt 26:56). «Do you work wonders for the dead?» (Ps 88:11). And, shortly after: "But I cry out to you, Yahweh, early in the morning my prayer goes to meet you" (v. 14). Don't you see how the time circumstances of both the passion and the resurrection are also clarified? The place of the resurrection, on the outside of the city

9. But from what place did El Salvador resurrect? It says in the Song of Songs: “Arise, my beloved, my beautiful one, and come away” (Song 2:10). And in what follows: "In the cleft of the rock" (2:14). He speaks of the crack in the rock, the entrance that was then before the door of the tomb of the Savior15 and that was excavated in the same rock, as is usually done at the entrances to tombs. It can no longer be seen today because, when all the current ornamentation was placed, that shelter was removed. Before the current structure of the monument, of royal magnificence, there was a cavity before the rock. But where is the rock in which that cavity was located? Is it perhaps in the middle of the city or close to the walls and ends? Or in the old walls or in the antemurals? For it says in the Song of Songs: "In the cavity of the rock by the outer wall" (Song 2:14 LXX). It took place at Easter time

10. When was the Savior resurrected? In the summer season or another? Also in the Song of Songs, very close to what has just been quoted, it says: «For, look, the winter has already passed, the rains have stopped and they are gone. The flowers appear on the earth, the time for pruning has arrived" (Song 2:11-12a LXX). Is it that the earth is now full of flowers and the vines are pruned? You realize how he said winter was over. Well, when the Xanthic 16 month arrives, spring immediately comes. But at this time the first month of the Hebrew calendar falls and the festival of Passover is celebrated there, which before was in image and figure, and is now the true one. This is the time of creation, for it is then that God said: "Let the earth produce vegetation: herbs that bear seeds and fruit trees that bear fruit, of their kind, with their seed inside, on the earth" (Gen I, I I). And now, as you see, all kinds of grass are already germinating. And in the same way that when God then made the sun and the moon, he distributed the course of the days and nights between them, so a few days before was the time of the equinox. And then God said: "Let us make human beings in our image, in our likeness" (Gen 1:26). And really what he received was in the image and likeness of God, but he darkened and darkened it through disobedience. But at the same time he suffered this loss, reparation also took place. After man was created, he was expelled from paradise for his disobedience, but at the same moment he who believed was introduced into it through obedience17. Salvation was at the same time as the fall. When "the flowers appear... and the time for pruning has arrived" (cf. Song 2:12 LXX). Buried after death, Jesus appears to the disciples

11. The burial place was a garden, and a vine was planted. He had said: "I am the vine" Jn 15:1. It is placed on earth so that the curse that was introduced because of Adam would be eradicated. The earth was condemned to produce thorns and thistles. But the true vine arose from the earth so that what was said could be fulfilled: "Truth will spring from the earth, and justice will appear from the heavens (Ps 85:12). And what will he who is buried in the garden have to say?: "I have taken my myrrh with my balm" (Song 5:1). And also: "Myrrh and aloes, with the best balms" (4:14). But these are the symbols of the grave, and in the Gospels it is said: "They (the women) went to the tomb carrying the aromas that they had prepared" (Lk 24:1). «Nicodemus also went... with a mixture of myrrh and aloes» (}n 19,39). And they are also said afterwards: "I have eaten my bread with my honey" (Song 5,1 LXX). The bitter, before the passion, and the sweet after the resurrection. Then, returning to life, he entered through doors that were closed (John 20:19). But they refused to believe, because they thought they saw a spirit (Luke 24:37). But he said to them: "Handle me and see" (Luke 24:39; cf. 37-41). "Put your fingers in the nail hole" as Thomas demanded (Jn 20:24-29). And "as they did not quite believe it because of their joy and were astonished, he said to them: "Do you have anything to eat here?" They offered him part of a roast fish” (Luke 24:41-42). There you see how what was said has been fulfilled: "I have eaten my bread with my honey." Women, quick to the grave

12. But before entering through the closed doors, those very good women endowed with virile strength were looking for him, husband and doctor of souls. Those blessed ones arrived at the tomb and were looking for him who had already risen (cf. Mt 28:1-6). Tears flowed from their eyes when in reality it was time to rejoice and sing in chorus for the resurrected One. Mary came looking for him, as it is in the Gospel (Jn 20,1 ff.) and did not find him; He then heard it from the mouths of the angels and finally saw Christ (20:11-18). Weren't these things already recorded in writing? For it is said in the Song of Songs: "In my bed I have sought the love of my soul." But at what moment?: "In my bed, at night, I have searched for the love of my soul." Mary, he says, arrived “while it was still dark” (Jn 20:1). «In my bed, at night, I have searched for the love of my soul. I looked for him and did not find him” (Song 3:1). And in the gospels it is also Mary who says: "They have taken my Lord, and I do not know where they have put him" (Jn 20:13). But the angels present undid this ignorance by saying: "Why do you seek the living among the dead?" (Lk 24,5). He did not rise alone, but taking other dead with him. But she didn't know it. In reference to her when she addresses the angels, the Song of Songs says: "Have you seen the love of my soul?" We had barely passed—that is, the two angels—when I found the love of my soul. I seized him and I will not let him go" (3:3-4). Appearance to the women

13. After the vision of the angels it was Jesus who announced himself. The Gospel says: «At this, Jesus met them and said to them: 'God preserve you!' And they came near and took hold of his feet” (Mt 28:9). They grabbed him so that this could be fulfilled: "I have seized him and will not let him go" (Song 3:4). The woman was weak in body, but virile in spirit. The waters did not quench love nor did the rivers overwhelm it (cf. Song 8:7). The one sought was dead, but the hope of the resurrection had not been extinguished. And the angel said to them again: "Do not be afraid" (Mt 28:5). I'm not saying that you don't fear the soldiers, but that you don't be afraid. Let them feel fear, so that, instructed by experience, they may bear witness and say: "Truly this was the Son of God" (Mt 27:54). But you should not fear, because "perfect love casts out fear" (I Jn 4:18). "And now go at once and tell his disciples," etc. (Mt 28,7). "They left the tomb in haste, with fear and great joy" (28:8). Is this also written? In fact, the second psalm says, enunciating the passion of Christ: "Serve Yahweh with fear and rejoice in trembling before him" (Ps 2:11 LXX). “Rejoice,” for the Lord who has risen, but “in trembling” because of the earthquake and the angel who appeared with a flash of lightning. Jesus is resurrected, although the tomb was sealed and guarded

14. The chief priests and the Pharisees sealed the tomb after telling Pilate, but the women saw the Risen One. And Isaiah, who knew, on the one hand, the futility of the high priests and, on the other hand, the strength of faith of women, says: "Women, who come from the vision, make haste, for there is not a people that has understanding" (Is 27:11 LXX). The high priests are devoid of intelligence, and the women are seeing with their own eyes19. And when the soldiers went to them telling them everything that had happened (Mt 28:11), they warned them: «Say: 'His disciples came at night and stole him while we were sleeping'» (28:13). Isaiah also correctly predicted this, speaking as for them: "Speak flattering things to us, contemplate illusions" (Is 30:11). But he has risen and risen, but they bribe the soldiers with monetary donations (28:15). But the soldiers do not need to convince the current emperors now. Well, the soldiers of that time betrayed the truth with money, but the current emperors built this holy Church of the Resurrection of God the Savior, in which we are and which they embellished with silver and gold, ornamenting it with altars also with gold, silver and precious stones. "And if the matter reaches the ears of the procurator, we will convince him and avoid complications" (Mt 28:14). They persuaded him, but not the whole world. And how is it that, when Peter left prison, his guards were condemned (Acts 12:19), while those who guarded Jesus were not punished? In reality, the penalty was imposed on them by Herod, since they had no excuse for ignorance, but these others, who knew the truth and hid it for money, were respected by the high priests (cf. Mt 28:15). A few Jews then believed the fable, but the entire world believed in the truth. Those who hid the truth were buried in oblivion, but those who welcomed it appeared in public light moved by the strength of the Savior. This one not only rose from the dead, but also took with him other dead, of whose person the prophet Hosea clearly says: "In two days he will give us life, on the third day he will raise us up, and in his presence we will live" (Hos 6:2)20. The apostles, witnesses of the resurrection, are also Hebrews

15. Since the Holy Scriptures do not convince the Jews, who do not obey, and since they themselves contradict the resurrection of Jesus, it would be best to speak to them like this: Why, while you affirm that Elisha and Elijah have raised the dead (cf. 2 Kings 4,20 se; 1 Kings 17,17-24) do you obstinate them against the resurrection of our Savior? Or is it that those of us who currently live are not of any use to the witnesses from then? Seek, therefore, witnesses of that time21. If what happened at that time is written, this is also written. Why do you accept one of the things and reject the other? The Hebrews wrote down those previous events. But all the apostles were also Hebrews. Why, if they are Jews, do you not believe them? Matthew, when writing his gospel, did so in the Hebrew language22. Paul, the preacher was “a Hebrew and a son of Hebrews” (Phil 3:5). And the twelve apostles were all Hebrews. Subsequently, the fifteen bishops of Jerusalem have been, in unbroken succession, also all Hebrews. Why then, while you admit what is yours, do you think that what is ours, which has been written down by Hebrews of your race, should be rejected? The resurrection of Jesus is a greater miracle than those worked by Ella and Elisha

16. But it is impossible, someone will say, to resurrect the dead. But Elisha performed resurrections again and again, both while he was alive (2 Kings 4:20 ff.) and after his death (2 Kings 13:21). If we believe that a corpse thrown to the ground was resurrected upon contact with Elisha, who was lying there dead, did not Christ rise from the dead? Furthermore, the one who was dead was resurrected and touched Elisha, but the one who raised him remained, however, dead, as he was before. But the dead man of whom we speak was resurrected and many other dead people who had not even touched him were resurrected: «Many bodies of deceased saints were resurrected. And coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they entered the Holy City—it is clearly the city in which we are23—and appeared to many” (Mt 27:52-53). Elisha certainly raised a dead man, but he did not manage to dominate the world; Elijah raised a dead man, but the demons did not submit in Elijah's name. However, we do not miss the prophets, but we celebrate with greater magnificence the one who is their Lord. In reality, we do not exalt what is ours by diminishing that, since that is also ours. Rather we reconcile faith in what is ours with their things24. Jonah, image of the death and resurrection of Jesus

17. But they insistently say: It is a recently deceased person who has been resurrected by a living person, but show us that it is possible for a three-day dead person to be resurrected and for a man who has already been buried for three days to be called back to life. But, if we are looking for such proof, the Lord Jesus provides it to us in the gospels when he says: "For in the same way that Jonah was in the belly of the whale three days and three nights, so also the Son of man will be in the bosom of the earth three days and three nights" (Mt 12:40; cf. Jon 2:1). And when we carefully investigate the story of Jonah, the similarity with our own story is great. Jesus was sent to preach conversion: Jonah (1:2 es) was also sent (to the same thing). But this one, not knowing the future, flees: the other, on the other hand, agreed to announce the penance of salvation. Jonah slept in the ship, and he did so deeply (1:5) while the sea was rough due to the storm: also, when Jesus was sleeping, the sea was rough for certain purposes (Mt 8:2425), so that later the power of the one who was sleeping would be recognized (8:27). They said: «What are you doing here asleep? Arise and call upon your God! Perhaps God will care for us and we will not perish” (Jon 1:6). And here they say to the Lord: "Lord, save us!" (Mt 8:25). There they said: "Call on your God!" And here; "save us!" He says: "Grab me and throw me into the sea, and the sea will calm down for you" (Jn 1:12). He "rebuked the winds and the sea, and great prosperity ensued" (Mt 8:26). The former ended up in the belly of the whale (Jon 2:1), but the latter descended of his own free will to the place where death swallowed men. He voluntarily descended so that death would vomit up those it had swallowed, according to what is written: "I will rescue them from the grip of sheol, I will rescue them from death" (Hos 13:14).

18. Having reached this part of the discourse, let us consider whether it is more difficult for a buried man to come out of the ground. Or does a man not fall apart and corrupt in the belly of a cetacean, swallowed in the warm viscera of a living being? Who ignores that there is so much heat in the belly that it even melts the bones that are devoured? And Jonah, after living three days and as many nights in the whale's belly, wouldn't he be corrupted and undone? Since the nature of all men is identical, and he cannot live without breathing the air, how could he live three days without it? The Jews respond and say: Together with Jonah, when he was agitated in Sheol, the power of God descended. God thus gave life to his servant by granting him his power. And couldn't God give that power to himself? If that was credible, this is also credible; and if this cannot be believed, neither can that. Both things seem equally credible to me. I believe that Jonah was protected, because "with God all things are possible" (Mt 19:26). I also believe that Christ rose from the dead. I have multiple testimonies of this reality, both from the Holy Scriptures and from the Risen Lord himself, all valid to this day: the one who descended into hell only returned accompanied by many25, since he descended to death and many bodies of the saints who had died were resurrected by him (Mt 27:52). In the abyss, victory over death

19. Death was terrified when it saw that someone different was descending into hell who was not bound by the chains of this place (cf. Acts 2:24). For what reason, guardians of hell, did you fill them with dread at the sight of it? (cf. Job 38:17 LXX). Did a blatant fear overcome you? He fled death and that flight revealed his fear. The holy prophets came. Moses the lawgiver, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, David and Samuel, Isaiah and John the Baptist, who says and testifies: "Are you the one who is to come, or must we wait for another?" (Mt 11,3). All the saints that death had swallowed have been redeemed. What had to be is that the King who had been preached was actually the liberator of the best omens. That is why someone among the righteous has said: “Where is your victory, O death? Where is your sting, O death? (1 Cor 15:55). It is the author of victory who has liberated us26. More information about Jonah as an image of the dead and resurrected Christ

20. Jonah was a figure of this our Savior praying from the belly of the cetacean saying: "From my anguish I cried to Yahweh and he answered me: from the bosom of sheol I cried, and you heard my voice" (Jan 2:3). He was inside the whale, but he says he was in hell: he was a figure of Christ, who at the time would descend to hell27. And shortly after, speaking prophetically with complete clarity about the person of Christ, he says; "I descended to the roots of the mountains" (2:7). What mountains are you talking about if you are in the belly of the whale? The thing is that I know - he says - that I am the image of the one who will be placed in the tomb excavated in stone. When Jonah was in the sea, he says: "I descended to the earth" (2:7 LXX), thus being an image of Christ, who descended to the bowels of the earth (Mt 12:39-40)28. He also foresaw the fraud of the Jews by inducing the soldiers to lie and telling them: "Say that they stole it" (cf. Mt 28:13). He foresaw this by saying: "Observing vain and false things, they abandon mercy toward them" (Jan 2:9, better LXX). In fact, one who had compassion on them came, and was crucified and resurrected after having given the gift of his precious blood on behalf of Jews and Gentiles. They, however, say: "Say that they stole it," thus observing vain things and falsehoods. Isaiah also says of his resurrection: "He who brought up the great shepherd of the sheep from the dead, in the blood of an eternal covenant" (Is 63:11)29. He added the word "great" so that he would not be counted among the shepherds of the category of the previous ones. The appearances of the Risen One

21. With all these prophetic data, let faith awaken in us. Fall those who fall through infidelity according to their whim. You, on the other hand, have stood firm on the rock of faith in the resurrection: may no heretic ever drag you to denigrate the resurrection. For, to this day, the Manichaeans say that the resurrection of the Savior was simulated and not true. We also have Paul, who writes30: “Born of the lineage of David according to the flesh” (Rom 1:3); and continues: "... by his resurrection from the dead" (1,4)31. And, on the other hand, he directs his words against them saying: «Do not say in your heart "Who will ascend to heaven?" that is, to bring Christ down; or: "Who will go down into the abyss?", that is, to bring Christ up from the dead» (Rom 10:6-7). Likewise, in another place, warning us, he writes: "Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead" (2 Tim 2:8). And also: «And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is empty, your faith is also empty. And we are convicted of being false witnesses of God because we have testified against God that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise” (1 Cor 15:14-15). And, in what follows he says: «But no! “Christ was raised from the dead as the firstfruits of those who fell asleep” (15:20). "He appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve" (15:5). If you do not accept the faith of just one, you have twelve witnesses there. "Afterwards they appeared to more than five hundred brothers at the same time" (15:6). If they didn't believe those twelve either, let them listen to these five hundred. "Then he appeared to James" (15:7), his brother33, the first bishop of this parish34. If this important bishop saw the resurrected Jesus Christ, do not deny your faith, you who are his disciple. But if you say that James bore witness because he was his brother, "in the end he also appeared to me" (15:8), Paul, his enemy. How can you question the testimony of one who has been your enemy and now announces it? Before I was a persecutor (cf. I Tim 1:13) and now I announce the resurrection. People and material objects, witnesses of the resurrection

22. Many are the witnesses of the resurrection of the Savior. It was night and there was a full moon, the sixteenth night35. The rock of the tomb that welcomed Christ and the stone that resisted the Jews in his face: that stone saw the Lord, the stone that was removed from its place (Mt 28:2), it bears witness to the resurrection lying there to this day. The angels of God, present there, bore witness to the resurrection of the Only Begotten (Lk 24,4 ff.). Peter and John, Thomas and all the other apostles, some of whom ran to the tomb (Jn 20:4) and saw the grave linens in which he had been wrapped and which had been left there after the resurrection (20:6-7). Others touched his hands and feet and contemplated the marks on the nails (20:27). And they all received at the same time the breath of the Savior and the power to forgive sins by virtue of the Holy Spirit (20:22-23). The women who clung to his feet observed the magnitude of the earthquake and the brilliance of the angel who was there (28:2-5), as well as the linen cloths that wrapped him and that, upon resurrection, he left there. The soldiers and the money given to them are also witnesses (Mt 28:15), the place, which can still be seen, and the holy building of this Church, built, for the love of Christ, by the Emperor Constantine, of happy memory, and which, as you see, is so beautified. Other testimonies of the resurrection and ascension

23. Also the one who was resurrected in his name, Tabitha, is a witness of the resurrection (cf. Acts 9:40). Well, who will stop believing in the resurrection of Christ, when his very name raised the dead? Also the sea, as you already heard36, is a witness to the resurrection of Jesus. Witnesses are the capture of the fish, the burning embers and the prepared meals (Jn 21,6.9). Peter also testifies, who had previously denied him three times, but later confessed him three more times, receiving the commission to feed the spiritual sheep (21:15-17). To this day there is the Mount of Olives, which shows the eyes of the faithful who it is who ascended on the cloud and who is the door to ascension to heaven. In Bethlehem he had descended from heaven, but he ascended to heaven from the Mount of Olives. From there he came to the men to engage in combat and it is here where he is crowned after his fight. You have, therefore, numerous witnesses, you have this same place of the resurrection and you have the place of the ascension, located, from our position, to the East. You have as witnesses the angels who testified there and the cloud that rose. And also to the disciples who came down from there (cf. Acts 1:9.12). The ascension37

24. The order of the doctrine of faith already warned us to also talk about the ascension, but the grace of God arranged things in such a way that yesterday, which was Sunday, you heard, to the extent of our strength, talk about this. It was because, by the grace of God, the readings of the liturgical meeting contained what related to the ascension of our Savior to heaven. What we said was addressed to all people and because of the multitude of faithful gathered. But, above all, yesterday we talked about this thinking about you. We want to see now if you listened to what was said. For you know that faith teaches you to believe in him "who was raised on the third day, and ascended into heaven, and is seated at the right hand of the Father." I think you will remember what we said, although, without too much insistence, I will remind you of what we said. Remember that in the Psalms it is written clearly; "God ascends with acclamations" (Ps 47:6). The divine Powers cried out to each other: "Doors, raise up their lintels" (Ps 24:7), etc. Keep in mind the other psalm: "You have gone up to the heights, leading captives" (Ps 68:19)33. And remember the prophet, who says: "He who builds his purple fins in the heavens" (Am 9, or). And all the other things that were said yesterday because of the contradictions of the Jews. Arguments in favor of the possibility of Ascension

25. For when they have opposed, judging it impossible, the ascension of the Savior, remember what is said of the translation of Habakkuk (Dan 14:33-39). For if Habakkuk was transported by the angel taking him by the hair of his head, much more the Lord of the prophets and angels, ascending in a cloud from the Mount of Olives, was able to prepare his way to heaven and by his own power. Also keep other similar things in your mind, keeping in mind that greatness is from the Lord, who does such wonders: those were carried away and this is the one who "upholds all things" (cf. Hebr 1:3). You remember that Enoch was translated (Gen 5:24), but Jesus ascended. Remember the things that were said yesterday about Elijah: that Elijah was taken in a chariot of fire (2 Kings 2:11), but the chariot of Christ was "the chariots of God, by thousands of myriads"; and that Elijah was taken to the east of the Jordan (2,1 1.14-15) while Christ ascended to the east of the Kidron torrent; that he ascended "as towards heaven" (2 Kings 2, 11 LXX) but Jesus did so "to heaven"; and that the first had told his disciple that he would give him two parts of his spirit39, but Christ has granted his disciples such a great participation in the grace of the Holy Spirit that they do not possess it only for themselves, but also by the laying on of hands they grant it to those who believe in him (Acts 8:14-17). The Supereminent Glory of Christ

26. When you have fought against the Jews and have conquered them with these comparisons, then draw near to the surpassing glory of the Savior: while they are servants, he is the Son of God. You will see how much he stands out when thinking that the Servant of Christ40 was taken up to the third heaven. For if Elijah reached the first heaven and Paul reached the third (2 Cor 12:2)41, it is evident that the latter achieved greater dignity. Don't be ashamed of your apostles. They are not less worthy than Moses nor inferior to the prophets, but they are good to the good and better than the good. Well, Elijah was truly taken to heaven, but Peter has the keys to the kingdom of heaven after hearing that: "Whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven" (Mt 16:19). Elijah was taken to heaven, but Paul to heaven and paradise (it was good that the disciples of Jesus received a more abundant grace): «He heard ineffable words that man cannot pronounce (2 Cor 12:4). But Paul descended again, and not because he was unworthy to live in the third heaven, but—after receiving gifts that surpass the human condition—abandoning that honor and after announcing Christ, to suffer death for him and obtain the crown of martyrdom. The rest of this argument, which I argued yesterday in the Sunday assembly, I have now ignored, since for intelligent listeners this single mention is enough. The Son is seated from eternity next to the Father

27. Remember also the things that I have often said about the Son sitting at the right hand of the Father. This is what is contained in the sequence of statements of faith: "he ascended into heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father." Let's not ask ourselves so much about the "reason" for this sitting, because it surpasses our intelligence. Nor let us rely on those who perversely maintain that, after the cross, the resurrection and the return to heaven, the Son then began to sit at the right hand of the Father. For "sitting" was not an acquisition for him, but he is seated next to the Father for what he is42. The prophet Isaiah, contemplating this throne before the coming in the flesh of the Savior, states: "I saw the Lord sitting on a high and elevated throne," etc. (6.1). For "no one has ever seen the Father" (Jn 1:18; cf. I Tim 6:16)43. Whom the prophet then saw was the Son. And the psalmist says: "From the beginning your throne is established, you have always existed" (Ps 93:2)44. As there are many testimonies of all this (the throne is evidently eternal), what has been said is enough, given the lateness of the hour. Importance of Salt 110.1: «The Lord said to my Lord...». Other testimonials

28. /Sal/109/110/01/Cyril: We will try to summarize some of the things said on this topic of the Son being seated at the right hand of the Father. Psalm 110 says openly: "The Lord says to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool" (110:1). When the Savior confirms this in the gospels, he points out that David did not say these things on his own, but said them by inspiration of the Spirit of God. He (Jesus) says it with these words: «For how does David, moved by the Spirit, call him Lord, when he says: "The Lord said to my Lord, sit at my right hand..."» (Mt 22:43-44). And in the Acts of the Apostles, on the day of Pentecost, Peter standing with the eleven and speaking to the Israelites, he remembers with the same words this testimony of Psalm 110 (Acts 2:34).

29. We must also bring to mind some other similar testimonies about the Son being seated at the right hand of the Father. In the Gospel according to Saint Matthew it is written: "I declare to you that from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power..." (Mt 26:64). The apostle Peter writes things consistent with this, mentioning: "... through the Resurrection of Jesus Christ, who, having gone into heaven, is at the right hand of God..." (1 Pet 3,21,22). And the apostle Paul writes to the Romans saying: «Christ Jesus, who died; even more so is he who is risen, who is at the right hand of God..." (Rom 8:34). And, writing to the Ephesians, he expresses himself in this way: "... according to the effectiveness of his mighty power, which he displayed in Christ, raising him from the dead and seating him at his right hand in heaven" (Eph 1:19-20), in addition to what follows. He instructed the Colossians in this way: "Therefore, if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God." And in the Epistle to the Hebrews it says: "After purifying sins, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high" (Hebrews 1:3). And on the other hand: «To what angel did he ever say: "Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool"» (1:13; cf. Ps 110:1). Furthermore: "He, on the contrary, having offered one sacrifice for sins, sat down at the right hand of God forever45, waiting from then on until his enemies were made his footstool" (Hebrews 10:12-13)46. I Thes 4:17) in due time. To him be glory forever. Amen...

1. The theme of catechesis is the resurrection of Jesus Christ. Only at the end, very briefly, do they touch on ascension and "he sits at the right hand of the Father." In general, the present catechesis has a very marked apologetic character towards the Jews, but also towards Manichaeans and others. This explains the insistence on numerous details relating to people, places, moments and other circumstances. For a modern reader it is very important to attend to the Christian conception of man that is explicitly or implicitly derived from Cyril's words. Various issues will be commented on in the notes to the text. PG 33,823 VII, account of the codices used.

2. Is 66:10 and its context refer primarily to Jerusalem, within an apocalyptic tone that suggests clear attitudes of joy and hope. Naturally, all of this makes much more sense from the reality of the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

3. The strong apologetic character of the catechesis, indicated in note I, is also a defense of a quite positive nature: an attempt is made to defend, especially against the Jews, the reality of the resurrected Jesus Christ, but the impression that the reader receives is not simply that of being on the defensive like someone who is besieged by a multitude of counter-reasonings. Rather, it is, as a whole, an impressive display of biblical texts. The objective is not an artificial stitching of some texts with others, but to show that multiple layers of Scripture point towards the resurrection of Christ, even in minute details. It is something similar to what, for example, the Gospel of Matthew intends when it so many times points out that "so that what was said in Scripture might be fulfilled" (or the same thing is said with other similar expressions). Ultimately, here also underlies the general idea - in this case moving, however, in the area of ​​the resurrection - that Scripture finds its fulfillment and its fullness in Christ, in whom all biblical statements are filled with meaning.

The words of Ps 16:4 are interpreted by Cyril as spoken by Christ - it is very common in the patristic tradition to understand numerous psalms as spoken in the first place by Christ, which frequently acquires a more accentuated prophetic meaning. Thus, in this case, when Jesus' accusers point out that their king is the Roman Caesar - when, in reality, they hated the imperial occupation - they are disavowing Jesus. This is what would have been prophetically said in Ps 16:4.

20. Probably the clearest text in the New Testament about how Jesus, in his resurrection, "dragged", that is, made many others experience the resurrection with him, is Eph 4, 7-11, especially due to the use made of Ps 68,19: 7 "To each of us has been granted divine favor in proportion to the gifts of Christ 8That is why it says: "He went up to the height, took captives and gave gifts to men" (Ps 68:19). 9What does "he ascended" mean if not that he also descended to the lower regions of the earth? 10This one who came down is the same one who ascended above all the heavens, to fill everything. 11 He himself 'gave' some to be apostles; to other prophets; to others, evangelizers; to others, pastors and teachers...». The descent "into the lower regions of the earth" is the descent into hell already spoken of. But what is interesting here is the idea of ​​the "ascension" (vv. 9 and 10) argued through the quote from Ps 68:19, whose historical context is different, but which here is applied to the victory of Christ in: "Going up to the height, he took captives." It is the idea that is liturgically expressed as that "in the death of Christ our death has been conquered and in his resurrection we have all been resurrected" (Paschal Preface, Il). By conquering death and rising again to the Father, Christ has taken free with him all the captives of sin and death, making them new men. It is the effect of the "justification" of the sinner (cf. Rom 4:25, which describes Christ as "who was handed over for our sins (Is 53:6), and was raised for our justification." The Pauline ideas about "faith", "resurrection", "justification" are fully relevant in this entire context to complete sometimes simply apologetic conceptions of the resurrection. It must also be taken into account that the resurrection of Jesus It is not only his recovery as "revived." It is a Jesus who possesses a new vital principle and with which all Christians are called to be associated: "... Knowing that Christ, once risen from the dead, dies no more, and that death no longer has dominion over him" (Rom 6:9). resurrected in man (6:11; for Paul's detailed explanations, cf. I Cor 15).
21. The argument is: The witnesses of the resurrection of Jesus are of value to us if the testimonies of the resurrections that took place through Elijah and Elisha are of value to you.

When the catechesis affirms that Elisha "did not manage to dominate the world" or that "the demons did not submit in the name of Elijah" despite the resurrection events narrated, it is implicitly saying something essential: the resurrection of Christ is not only, as has already been indicated, "living again." Cf. the previous note 20. In this sense, the resurrection of Jesus is qualitatively different from what are the resurrections of the daughter of Jairus (Mt 9,18-19, 23-26 par), of the son of the widow of Naim (Lk 7,11-17) or of Lazarus (Jn 11,1-44), since the resurrection of Christ is definitive and marks the beginning of a new humanity.

31. Rom 1:3-4 is important for a summary understanding of the reality of Jesus Christ. Paul speaks, at the beginning of the epistle, of the Gospel "3 concerning his Son, born of the seed of David according to the flesh, 4 constituted the Son of God with power, according to the Spirit of holiness, by his resurrection from the dead." In the context of catechesis, it is interesting to emphasize here that the life and ministerial activity of Jesus are a path or process in which he reaches the full manifestation of his power as the Son of God when he arrives at the Resurrection ("constituted Son of God with power") in union with "the Spirit of holiness", in the unity with which and with the Father his entire existence has meaning, which only in terms of creaturely weakness can be understood in his humanity ("born of the lineage of David, according to the flesh. Naturally, this does not prevent the Son of God from always having the same dignity through eternal generation from the Father.

32. In the decisive moments in which it is said that, after his resurrection, Jesus "appeared" to the apostles or to others, the verb is "ophthe" which, because it is a passive aorist, must be translated as "he was made to be seen" and, in this case, "he made himself seen" or "he let himself be seen." This slight linguistic appreciation reveals something important: the initiative to allow oneself to be found and, ultimately, to "appear" corresponds exclusively to the Risen One. H.U. von BALTHASAR, using the words of H. SCHLIER (which will be transcribed here in quotation marks) expressed it perfectly: «Unanimously there is talk of encounters with the living Christ. "The encounter that the witnesses experience comes from him. That encounter - word and sign, greeting and blessing, call, interpellation and teaching, consolation and instruction and mission, founding of a new community - is pure gift" (so far Schlier). As in human encounters, the senses of those who experience it also come into play: they see and hear, touch and even taste... But the emphasis does not fall on sensible experiences, but only on the object. And this, the living Christ, shows himself from himself. This is the meaning of the "ophthe" that appears in decisive texts (I Cor 15,3 ff: four times; Luke 24,34 in the meeting with Simon; Acts 13,31; regarding the appearances to Paul, Acts 9,17, 16,9, 21,16)" (H.U. von BALTHASAR. op. cit., in note 27, 780).

48. For details, cf. supra, note 20. CATECHESIS behold, in the clouds of heaven he came like a Son of man..." (7:13) in addition to what follows1 The two comings of Christ2.

1. We announce the coming of Christ, but not just one, but also a second, much more magnificent than the previous one. The first carried with it a meaning of suffering, this other, however, will carry the diadem of the divine kingdom. For almost all things are double in our Lord Jesus Christ. His birth is double: one, from God, from all eternity; another, of the Virgin, in the fullness of time. Its descent is also double: the first, silent, like rain on fleece (Ps 72:6); the other, manifest, still future. At the first coming he was wrapped in sashes in the manger (Luke 2:7); in the second he will be clothed with light as a garment (cf. Ps 104:2a). In the first "he endured the cross, without fear of ignominy" (Hebrews 12:2), in the other he will come glorified and escorted by an army of angels (cf. Mt 25:31). We do not think, therefore, only of the past coming; We are also waiting for the second one. And, having proclaimed in the first: “blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord” (Mt 21,9), we will say the same in the second (cf. Mt 23,39); and, going out to meet the Lord with the angels, we will acclaim in worship: "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord." The Savior will come, not to be judged again, but to call to his court those for whom he was brought to trial. He who before, while being judged, remained silent (Mt 27:12) will refresh the memory of the evildoers who dared to insult him when he was on the cross and will say to them: "This you did and I kept silent" (Ps 50:21) 3. Then, for reasons of his gracious providence, he came to teach men with gentle persuasion; On that other, future occasion, whether they want it or not, men will necessarily have to submit to his reign.

2. The prophet Malachi speaks of both comings: "Suddenly the Lord whom you seek will enter the sanctuary" (Mal 3:1). There is the first coming. Regarding the other, it says like this: The messenger of the alliance that you desire: see him coming in, says the Lord of hosts. Who can resist the day of his coming? Who will be left standing when he appears? It will be a smelter's fire, a washerman's lye: it will sit to melt and purge" (3:1-3). And in the lines that follow the Savior Himself says: "I will come to you for judgment, and I will be a quick witness against sorcerers and against adulterers, against those who swear falsely," etc. (3.5). Therefore, wanting to make us more cautious, Paul says: «If anyone builds on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw, each person's work will be revealed; The Day will reveal it, which will be revealed by fire” (I Cor 3:12-13)4. Writing to Titus, Paul also speaks of these two comings in these terms: “The grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all men; teaching us to renounce impiety and worldly desires, and to lead from now on a sober, honest and religious life, awaiting the happiness we hope for: the glorious appearance of the great God and our Savior, Jesus Christ” (Titus 2:11-13). There he expresses his first coming, giving thanks for it; but also the second, the one we wait for. For this reason, in our profession of faith, as we have received it by tradition, we say that we believe in him “who ascended into heaven, and is seated at the right hand of the Father; and he will come again with glory to judge the living and the dead, and his kingdom will have no end.” The present condition of the world will pass

3. Therefore, our Lord Jesus Christ will come from heaven. He will certainly come towards the end of this world, on the last day, with glory. Then the consummation of this world will take place, and this world, which was created at the beginning, will be renewed again. Well, since corruption, theft, adultery and all kinds of sins have been poured out on the earth and blood is shed again and again (see Hos 4:1-2). This present world will disappear so that this dwelling is not filled with iniquity and to give rise to another more beautiful one. Do you want to see a demonstration of this from Holy Scripture? Listen to the prophet Isaiah: "The heavens are rolled up like a book, and all their army pales as the branch of the vine pales, like a withered fig leaf" (Is 33:4). And the Gospel says; "The sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall from the sky" (Mt 24:29). Let us not be sad, therefore, as if only we had to die, because the stars also die, although perhaps they will rise again. The Lord will make the heavens fold and not to make them perish but to make others more beautiful. Listen to the prophet David when he says: “Of old, you founded the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands; They perish, but you remain” (Ps 102:26-27). But someone will say: He openly declares that they will perish. Listen to how he says “they will perish,” because from what he says next it is clear: “They all wear out like clothes, like a garment you change them, and they change” (102:27). In a similar way to how it is said that man perishes, according to that: "The righteous perishes, and there is no one who pays attention" (Is 57:1), even though the resurrection is expected. Thus, we also hope for a resurrection from heaven. "The sun will turn into darkness and the moon into blood" (J13,4; Acts 2,20; cf. Mt 24,29). Let those who have converted from the Manichaeans know this and do not make gods of the stars nor impiously think that Christ will one day lose his light. Listen again to the Lord, who says: "Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away" (Mt 24:35), because creatures are not of the same value nor do they have the same destiny as the words of the Lord. We will talk about what is to come and its signs

4. Therefore, visible things will pass and those expected to be better than these will arrive, but let no one look with curiosity as to what the moment will be. Well, he says: "It is not for you to know the time and the moment that the Father has set by his authority" (Acts 1:7). Don't dare determine when these things will happen or remain lazily dozing. Well, he also says: "Be ready, for when you do not think, the Son of Man will come" (Mt 24:44; cf. 42). But since it was convenient for us to know the signs of the consummation and since it is Christ whom we wait for and so that we would not die disappointed and be led astray by the Antichrist of lies, the apostles, impelled by a divine motion and in accordance with the wise designs of God, approach the true Master and say to him: "Tell us when this will happen, and what will be the sign of your coming and the end of the world" (Mt 24:3). We hope you will come a second time, but "Satan disguises himself as an angel of light" (2 Cor 11:14). Therefore, keep us safe, so that we do not worship another in your place. And he, opening his divine and blessed mouth, says: "See that no one deceives you" (Mt 24:4). You also, those who now hear, look at him now as if you were seeing him with the eyes of your mind and listen to him as someone who is telling you the same things: "See that no one deceives you." These words warn everyone to direct their minds to what is going to be said. For it is not a story of things past, but of things to come, and it is a prophecy of what will surely happen. And it is not that we prophesy, for we are unworthy of it, but that we proclaim in this assembly what is written and explain its signs. You will see which of these things have already taken place and which are still to come. That way you can prevent yourself. First sign: the false messiahs

5. «See that no one deceives you. For many will come, usurping my name and saying, “I am the Christ,” and will deceive many” (Mt 24:4-5). These things have already happened in part. Well, this was already said by Simon Magus, and Menander and other heads of heretics6 enemies of God. But others will also say it in our time and after us. Wars and natural disasters

6. Second sign: "You will also hear of wars and rumors of wars" (Mt 24:56). Is it, or not, the war in the current era of the Persians against the Romans over Mesopotamia? Does "nation against nation and kingdom against kingdom" rise or not (Mt 24:7)?7. "There will be great earthquakes, pestilence and famine in various places" (Luke 21:11). This has already happened. And, in turn: "There will be fearful things and great signs from heaven" (Iba). "Watch, therefore," he says, "because you do not know what day your Lord will come" (Mt 24:42). Betrayal and hatred as signs of the end

7. But of the coming of the Lord we look for a sign that is our own, that of the Church: that is, one that belongs to the Church, since we who are part of the Church seek it. But the Savior says: "Many will then be scandalized and will betray and hate each other" (Mt 24:10). If you hear that bishops are against bishops, clerics against clerics,8 and that peoples turn against each other, do not be disturbed: Scripture has already predicted it before. Don't put your attention on what is happening now, but on what is written. And even if I, who am instructing you, perish, that does not mean that you have to go to death with me, but it is necessary that the listener become better than the teacher and that the one who arrives last becomes the first (cf. Mt 20:16), since the Lord also receives those who arrive at the eleventh hour (Mt 20:6-7). And if betrayal occurred among the apostles, are you surprised that there is also hatred between brothers among the bishops? And this signal is not only among the bosses, but among the masses. For it says: "And as iniquity increases more and more, the charity of the majority will grow cold" (Mt 24:12). Will any of those present boast that their friendship with their neighbor is sincere and without pretense? Isn't it very common for lips to kiss, faces to smile, and hilarity to be seen in the eyes, while inside he who speaks in peace plots deception and plans evil? (cf. Ps 28:3). Before the end, the Gospel will have been preached to all nations

8. You also have this sign: «This Good News of the Kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the entire world, as a testimony to all nations. And then the end will come” (Mt 24:14). And almost the entire world is already filled with the doctrine of Christ9. Apostasy and the Antichrist

9. And what will happen next? It says in what follows: "When you therefore see the abomination of desolation announced by the prophet Daniel10, erected in the Holy Place (let him who reads understand)" (Mt 24:15). And, in turn: "Then if anyone says to you, 'Look, the Christ is here or there,' do not believe him" (Mt 24:23). Brotherly hatred then makes way for the Antichrist. The devil prepares divisions between people so that, when he arrives, he will be welcomed more favorably. May it not happen that anyone present or any servants11 anywhere joins the enemy. Writing about this, the apostle Paul gave a clear sign when he said: First the apostasy must come and the ungodly Man, the Son of perdition, the Adversary who rises above all, who bears the name of God or is an object of worship, must be revealed, to the point of sitting himself in the Sanctuary of God and proclaiming that he himself is God. Don't you remember that I already told you this when I was with you? You know what it is that holds him back now, so that he may manifest at his opportune time. Because the mystery of impiety is already at work. If only he who now restrains him is removed from the midst, then the Wicked One will be revealed, whom the Lord will destroy with the breath of his mouth, and annihilate with the Manifestation of his Coming. The coming of the Wicked will be marked by the influence of Satan, with all kinds of miracles, signs, deceitful wonders, and all kinds of evil, which will seduce those who are to be condemned (2 Thes 2,3b- 1 Day)12. That's it Pablo. Certainly, defection now occurs, since men have departed from the right faith: some affirm that the Son is Father and others that he has been brought into existence from nothing. And in other times the heretics were clearly perceptible, but now the Church is full of hidden heretics. Men have distanced themselves from the truth and feel the desire for new things (cf. 2 Tim 4:3-4): Are these words artificially composed to persuade? Everyone listens sweetly: are they perhaps words for the conversion of the spirit? Everyone actually moves away. Many have departed from right doctrines and are more inclined to choose evil than to apply themselves to good. It is, therefore, apostasy, and we must now wait for the enemy. In part he already began to send his precursors to come later ready to collect the loot. Take care of yourself, then, O man, and secure your soul.

The Church now conjures you (2 Tim 4:1) in the presence of the living God (cf. 1 Tim 6:13) and announces to you in advance, before it happens, what refers to the Antichrist. We do not know if these things will happen in your time or if they will happen after you, but the best thing is that, knowing them, you take precautions. Don't be fooled

10. But Christ, the only begotten Son of God, will no longer come from the earth. If someone comes saying that he has appeared in the desert, do not go out (cf. Mt 24:26). Acts 1:11) and not alone, as before, but with a great company, surrounded by a multitude of innumerable angels (cf. Jude 14). Nor imperceptibly like the dew on the shoot (Ps 72, or), but resplendent like lightning. And further: "You will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with great power and glory 13. He will send his angels with a loud trumpet" (Mt 24:30-31), etc. The Antichrist, product of the devil

CATECHESIS XVI THE HOLY SPIRIT (I) Delivered in Jerusalem on: «And in the Holy Spirit, Paraclete, who spoke for the prophets". The reading is taken from I Cor 12,1-4: "Concerning spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be in ignorance..." And, later: "There are different charisms, but the Spirit is the same" (12,4), etc.

1. We truly need spiritual grace to speak of the Holy Spirit, although we will never be up to the task, because it is impossible. We will try, however, to present naturally what we draw from it in Holy Scripture. In the Gospels we speak of great fear when Christ openly says: "Whoever speaks a word against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, neither in this world nor in the next" (Mt 12:32)2. And we must seriously fear that someone, by speaking out of ignorance or misunderstood piety, will earn damnation. Christ, judge of the living and the dead, announced that such a man will not obtain forgiveness. And if someone offends you, what hope do you have? We will talk about what is said about the Holy Spirit in Scripture

2. The gift of grace of Jesus Christ is necessary, both for us to speak properly and for you to hear intelligently. For penetrating intelligence is necessary not only for those who speak, but also for those who hear, so that it does not happen that they hear one thing and wrongly understand another. We will speak, therefore, about the Holy Spirit only what is written and, if something is not written, let curiosity not make us nervous. It is the same Holy Spirit who spoke through the Scriptures: he said about himself what he wanted or what we could understand. Therefore, let us say the things that were said by him, because with what he did not say we will not dare. Present since ancient times, he is equal in dignity to the Father and the Son

3. There is only one Holy Spirit Paraclete. And just as there is only one God the Father, and there is no second Father, and only one only begotten Son, who has no other brother, so there is only one Holy Spirit, and there is no other Holy Spirit who is equal in honor of him3. It is, therefore, the Holy Spirit, the maximum power, divine and ineffable reality. For he lives and is rational, a sanctifier of all things that God has done through Christ. He illuminates the souls of the righteous. He is also in the prophets and he is also, in the new Alliance, in the Apostles. I hate those who have the audacity to isolate the action of the Holy Spirit. For there is only one God the Father, Lord of the old and the new Covenant. And one Lord, Jesus Christ, who prophesied in the old and has come in the new. And only one Holy Spirit who announced Christ through the prophets and who, after Christ arrived, showed him4. There is no talk of three gods nor should Father, Son and Holy Spirit be separated.

4. Therefore, let no one separate the old Covenant from the new Covenant: let no one say that there is one Spirit, while here there is a different one5, since this offends the Holy Spirit himself, to whom honor is paid together with the Father and the Son and who is, in baptism, included within the Holy Trinity. For the same only begotten Son of God clearly said to the apostles: "Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit" (Mt 28:19)6. Our hope is placed in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. We do not announce three gods. Be silent, then, the Marcionites7, because, together with the Holy Spirit, through one Son, we preach one God. Faith is undivided and piety is inseparable8. We neither separate the Holy Trinity, as some do, nor do we, like Sabellius, create confusion9. But we piously recognize a unique Father, who sent us a Savior, the Son, We recognize a unique Son, who promised that he would send the Paraclete from the Father (cf. Jn 15:26). We recognize the Holy Spirit, who spoke through the prophets and at Pentecost descended on the apostles in a kind of tongues of fire (Acts 2:3), in Jerusalem, in the church of the apostles, the one above10. Here we have all kinds of prerogatives. Here Christ and the Holy Spirit descended from heaven. And it was very convenient that, in the same way that we said the things that refer to Christ and the place of Golgotha ​​on Golgotha ​​itself, so we also spoke of the Holy Spirit in the church above. But since the one who descended there participates in the glory of the one who was crucified here, that is why it is in this place that we will speak of the one who descended there. Pious worship does not admit separation. We will expose the heresies

5. The purpose, then, is to say some things about the Holy Spirit. Not, of course, to expose his person in detail11, since that is impossible, but to point out, about him, various aberrations of some so that we are not, ignoring them, carried away by them. We also want to delimit the paths of error so that we advance along a real path. And if we carefully examine something that has been said by the heretics, let it fall again on their heads, but let us remain immune, both we who speak and you who listen.

6. For the most impious heretics in all matters also sharpened their tongue against the Holy Spirit, daring to say infamous things, as Irenaeus wrote in his books Against Heresies12. Some were not afraid to say that they themselves were the Holy Spirit. The first of whom is Simon, whom the Acts of the Apostles calls "Magician." Once expelled, he did not hesitate to teach such things13. The so-called "gnostics" are also impious and have said other things against the Spirit, and the Valentinians have likewise spoken perversely14. But the criminal Manes dared to say of himself that he was the Paraclete sent by Christ. According to the prophets or the New Testament, there have been those who imagined that both were the Holy Spirit. His error—or rather his blasphemy—is very great. Hate such men, therefore, and flee from those who blaspheme against the Holy Spirit, for whom there is no remission. How are you going to join those who lack all hope, you who now also have to be baptized in the Holy Spirit? If he who joins himself with a thief and goes on raids with him is subjected to torture, what hope will there be for he who confronts the Holy Spirit? Against the Marcionites and the Gnostics

Let us hate men worthy of hate. Those whom God leaves aside, let us leave them. With all confidence, let us also say about heretics: «Do I not hate, Yahweh, those who hate you? 11. Let what has been said about these expelled people be sufficient. But now let us return to Holy Scripture, and drink water from our vessels and from the fountain of our wells (cf. Prov 5:15). Let us drink of the living water “which springs up to eternal life” (Jn 4:14). "He said this referring to the Spirit that those who believed in him would receive" (7:39).
