These are not rivers perceptible by the senses and that irrigate, in a simple and vulgar sense, the earth that contains thorns and logs, but rather those that give light to souls: "But the water that I give him will become in him a fountain of water springing up to eternal life" (4:14). It is another kind of water, which lives and flows: it flows on those who are worthy of it. The Spirit distributes his gifts among everyone

12. WATER/GRACE GRACE/WATER: And why have you given the name water to the grace of the Spirit? Because all things consist of water, since water is what makes plants and animals; because storm water comes down from the heavens. It always falls in the same way and in the same form, although the effects it produces are multiform: a single source waters the entire garden. And a single and identical storm descends upon the whole earth, but it becomes white in the lily, red in the rose, purple in violets and hyacinths, and diverse and varied in different kinds of things. In one way it exists in the palm and in another in the vine, but it is all in all things, since (water) is always the same and without variation. And, even if it changes in a storm, it does not change its way of being, but rather it adapts to the shape of its recipients, becoming what is necessary for each of them. Thus the Holy Spirit, being one and unique, and also indivisible, distributes grace "to each one individually according to his will" (cf. 1 Cor 12:11). And just as a dry tree produces buds when it receives water, so also the sinful soul, when through conversion it has been graced by the gift of the Holy Spirit, produces the clusters of the Holy Spirit. And although he is one and only, he nevertheless works, by the will of God and in the name of Christ, multiple effects: he uses the tongue of one for wisdom and enlightens the mind of another with the gift of prophecy; To the latter he grants the power to expel demons and to the former the gift of interpreting the Holy Scripture; of some it strengthens temperance23 and teaches another about mercy24; others are taught to fast or to endure the exercises of the ascetic life; others, to despise the things of the body, and there are those who prepare for martyrdom. He is diverse in each one, but he is never different from himself. As it is written: “To each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common benefit. For to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit; to another, the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit; to another, faith, in the same Spirit; to another, charismas of healing, in the one Spirit; to another, power of miracles; to another, prophecy; to another, discernment of spirits; to another, diversity of languages; to another, the gift of interpreting them.
But all these things are worked by one and the same Spirit, distributing them to each one individually according to his will" (I Cor 12:7-11)25 Various meanings of the word "spirit

13. But since many diverse things have been said in Holy Scripture about the Holy Spirit, with a single and common name, and it may be feared that someone will confuse them out of ignorance because they do not know to which spirit what is written there refers, it is necessary to point out certain sure characteristics of the Spirit whom the Scripture calls Holy. For just as Aaron is called "Christ"26 and also David, Saul and others are called "Christs," and yet the true Christ is unique, so also, once the name "spirit" is attributed to various realities, it is wonderful to see who is called, for some peculiar reason, the Holy Spirit. Well, there are many things that are called "spirit", because an angel is called "spirit", our soul is called "spirit" and the wind that blows is called "spirit"27. Also a great virtue is called "spirit" and an impure action is called "spirit." Even the Demon, the Adversary, is called "spirit." Be careful, therefore, when you hear these things, that, because of the similarity of the denomination, you do not confuse one thing with another. For of our soul the Scripture says: "Its breath exhales, it returns to its clay," and of the soul it says in turn: "It shapes the spirit of man within" (Zech 12:1)28. And of the angels he says in the Psalms: "He makes his angels spirits and his servants a flame of fire"29. And of the wind he says: "The east wind is such that it destroys the ships of Tarshish" (Ps 48:8). And further: "As a tree is shaken by the wind in the forest." And: "Fire and hail, snow and mist, stormy wind, executor of his word" (Ps 148:8). And of good doctrine the Lord Himself says: "The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and are life" Un 6:63), that is, they are spiritual30. But the Holy Spirit is not something that is exhaled by speaking with the tongue, but rather someone alive31, who allows us to speak with wisdom, being himself the one who expresses himself and speaks. The Holy Spirit suggests, speaks and teaches

14. Do you want to notice how he creates words and speaks? Philip, by revelation from an angel, went down the road that led to Gaza, when the eunuch arrived. And the Spirit said to Philip: “Come near and stand beside that chariot” (Acts 8:29). Do you see how the Spirit speaks to those who hear him? And Ezekiel says this: "The spirit of Yahweh broke into me and said to me, 'Say, Thus says Yahweh'" (Ez 11:5). On the other hand, "the Holy Spirit said" to the apostles, who were in Antioch: "Separate Barnabas and Saul for me now for the work to which I have called them" (Acts 13:2). You see the Spirit that is alive, that secretes and that calls, and that sends with power. And Paul says: "I only know that in every city the Holy Spirit testifies to me that prisons and tribulations await me" (20:23). He is the one who sanctifies the Church, her helper and her teacher, the Holy Spirit, teacher, of whom the Savior said: "He will teach you everything", and he did not only say "he will teach you", but also "he will remind you of everything that I have told you" (Jn 14:26). For there are not some teachings of Christ and others those of the Holy Spirit, but clearly the same. Paul testified in advance of the things that were to happen, so that, through prior knowledge, the spirit might feel firmer. And these things have been told to them by that sentence: "The words that I have spoken to you are spirit" (Jn 6:63), so that you do not think that this (the Spirit) is only something that we say, but solid doctrine. The devil, spirit of evil and sin

15. The word "spirit" also refers to sin, as we have already said, but for another opposite reason, that is, as they say: "with a spirit of fornication they went astray" (Hos 4:12 LXX). The demon is also called a spirit, an unclean spirit, but with that adjective "unclean." For each spirit is given an addition, which designates its own characteristic. If we say "spirit" to the human soul, we add "of man" (I Cor 2:11). If it is said about the wind32, it is spoken of "a stormy wind" (Ps 107:25). When it designates sin, it says "spirit of fornication." If he refers to the devil, he calls him “unclean spirit,” so that we know what is being talked about particularly in that case and do not believe that he is talking about the Holy Spirit. No way! Well, this name "spirit" is a general and common name, and what does not have a thick and dense body is called, in a generic way, spirit. But since demons do not possess such, they are called "spirits." But there are very diverse spirits. For the impure demon, when it enters the soul of man (and God save all souls from this evil, both those who are here and those who are absent), arrives like a wolf swallowing blood and ready to devour, launching itself against the sheep. It is a very cruel arrival, and very serious for the one who suffers it. The mind becomes dark with a dense fog. It is an unjust attack by someone who invades another's property, since he strives to abuse, doing violence (Mk 9:17-18), a foreign body, using it as if it were his own. It causes the fall of those who remain standing, related as they are to the one who fell from heaven (cf. Lk 10:18); he tangles his tongue and twists his lips; instead of words, he spews foam. Man is plunged into darkness and, when the eye is open, the soul sees nothing through it. Full of misery, man convulses in fear of death. Really, demons are enemies of men and mistreat them dirtyly and without mercy. The strength and illumination granted by the Holy Spirit

16. The Holy Spirit is not such. Far be it from you this thought! Well, on the contrary, here we are in the realm of good and salvation. First of all, his coming takes place in meekness and softness, and he is perceived with that softness and with fragrance, since his yoke is very light. The bright rays of light and science warn of their arrival. It comes with the feelings of a true protector. He comes to save, heal, teach, warn, strengthen, console and illuminate the mind: first, that of the one who welcomes him and, second, his works and those of others. And in the same way that someone who was previously in darkness, when he then looks at the sun, suddenly receives light in his bodily eye and distinguishes what he did not see clearly before, so is he who has been considered worthy of the gift of the Holy Spirit: his spirit is illuminated and, placing himself beyond the human, he now sees what he did not know. His body prostrated on the ground, his soul contemplates the heavens as in a mirror. Like Isaiah, he sees “the Lord sitting on an exalted and elevated throne” (Is 6:1). Contemplate, like Ezekiel, the one who “was on the heads of the cherubim” (Ez 10:1). He sees, like Daniel, “thousands of thousands” and “myriads of myriads” (Dan 7:10). Being little as a man, he sees the beginning and the end of the world, and discerns the passage of time and the succession of kings. And it's not that he has learned this, but he is a true provider of light. A man may be confined within walls, but the force of his knowledge extends widely to contemplate even what others do. The power that the Spirit gives to discern the hidden

17. Peter was not present when Ananias and Sapphira sold their possessions. But he was present by the Spirit, and said, "How did Satan fill your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit?" (Acts 5:3). He was neither an accuser nor a witness. Where had he come to know about the fact? «Is it that while you had it it was not yours, and once it was sold you could not have the price? Why did you determine in your heart to do this? (Acts 5:4). An illiterate man, Peter, knew by the grace of the Spirit what not even the wise men of the Greeks had come to know. You also have a similar example in Elisha. When he had cured Naaman's leprosy for free, Gehazi33 took a payment, collecting the value of another's work, and placed the money received from Naaman in a dark place (cf. 2 Kings 5:20 ff.). But darkness is not dark for the saints (cf. Ps 139:12)34. Well, after returning, Elisha (as well as Peter) asks him: "Tell me, have you sold the field for so long?" (Acts 5,8): "Where do you come from, Gehazi?" (2 Kings 5,25). (cf. 2 Kings 5:27) I have fulfilled the command of him who told me: "You received it freely; give it freely" (Mt 10:8). that happened elsewhere. You see how it not only suppresses ignorance, but even gives infused knowledge, and you see how the Holy Spirit illuminates the souls. The Holy Spirit also illuminated the prophets.

18. Isaiah lived almost a thousand years ago. He looked upon Zion as a poor tent. However, the city was still standing, embellished by a large number of public squares and clothed in its dignity. It is said, however: "Zion will be a field to be plowed" (Mic 3:12), foreshadowing what has been accomplished in our days. Observe the accuracy of the prophecy, for it says: "The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shelter in a cucumber orchard, like a besieged city" (Is 1:8). And this place really is now full of cucumber orchards. Don't you see how the Holy Spirit illuminates the saints?35. Don't let the similarity of the name drag you to other things. Maintain instead what is exactly the truth. The Spirit, who suggests voluntary chastity and poverty, protects man and gives him his gifts

19. If on any occasion, when you are resting, thoughts about chastity or virginity come to you, it is he who is instructing you. Does it not often happen that a young woman, already prepared for the consummation of marriage, does not agree because he36 suggests virginity? Does it not happen very often that a conspicuous man in public life despises riches and dignity instructed by the Holy Spirit? Or that many times a young man, seeing a graceful figure, closes his eyes so as not to see and escape disgrace? Why do you think that happens? The Holy Spirit has instructed the mind of man, since the desires of greed are so many in the world, there are Christians who follow voluntary poverty. For what reason? By the inner command of the Holy Spirit. The holy and good Spirit is a precious reality. We are properly baptized in the Father, in the Son and in the Holy Spirit. With his body man fights with many fierce demons37. And often a demon that many could not restrain with iron chains is contained and dominated by words of supplication. A simple breath from the exorcist turns into fire against the invisible enemy. We have, therefore, from God a helper and protector, a great teacher of the Church and a great fighter on our behalf. Let us not be afraid of demons or the devil, because he who fights for us is greater: let us simply open the doors to him, because "he goes everywhere looking for the worthy" (cf. Wisdom 6:16)38 and looking for someone to give his gifts to. The strength of the Holy Spirit in difficulties

20. But he is called Paraclete because he consoles, strengthens with his exhortations and helps us in our weakness39, "because we do not know how to ask to pray as we should; but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings that cannot be expressed” (Rom 8:26), that is, before God, as can be seen from the matter itself. Often someone, a victim of insults for the sake of Christ, unjustly suffers contempt. Martyrdom and torment threaten everywhere: fire and the sword, beasts and the precipice. But the Holy Spirit suggests: "Wait in Yahweh" (Ps 27:14), man. What happens to you is little, but what will be given to you is great. After suffering for a short time, you will be eternally in the company of angels. "The sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed in us" (Rom 8:18). The Spirit describes to man the kingdom of heaven, shows him the paradise of delights, and the martyrs, present in the sight of their judges but already in paradise in terms of their energy and power, can thus despise the harshness of what they see. The Spirit allows us to bear witness in favor of Jesus

21. Do you want to know how the martyrs gave their testimony with the power of the Holy Spirit? The Savior tells the disciples: "When they take you to the synagogues, before the magistrates and the authorities, do not worry about how or what you will defend them with, or what you will say, because the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very moment what should be said" (Lk 12:1 1-12). For it is impossible to suffer martyrdom to bear witness to Christ if one does not suffer with the strength of the Holy Spirit. Well, if "no one can say "Jesus is Lord!" but with the Holy Spirit" (1 Cor 12:3), who will give life for Jesus if not in the Holy Spirit? Enlighten all Christians of any condition and of any people

22. Great, omnipotent in his gifts and admirable is the Holy Spirit. Think how many are sitting here, how many souls we are. The Spirit acts in a way appropriate to each one. He is in the middle of everyone and sees each one's situation. He also sees thought and consciousness, and also what we talk about and what we turn over in our minds. What I have just said is great and yet it is still little. I would like you to consider, by illuminating your mind, how many Christians there are in this entire parish and how many there are in the entire province of Palestine. Also expand your mind from this province to the entire Roman Empire and turn your gaze from there to the entire world: the peoples of the Persians and the nations of India, the Goths and the Sauromatas, the Gauls and the Hispanics, the Moors, the Africans, the Ethiopians and others whose names we do not even know: there are many, in fact, people whose names have not even come to our knowledge. Look at the bishops of any town, at the priests, the deacons, the monks, the virgins and the lay people, and observe who it is that governs them, presides over them and grants them their gifts. How, throughout the world, one is gifted with modesty, one with perpetual virginity, another with the desire to give alms, another with interest in poverty, and finally with another, the ability to put enemy spirits to flight. And just as light, with a single ray, illuminates everything, so also the Spirit illuminates those who have eyes. Therefore, if anyone complains that grace is not given to him, let him not accuse the Spirit, but his own unbelief. Angels, powers and all creatures need the Spirit

23. You see the power it exercises in the entire world. Don't let your mind stay at ground level, but rather ascend to the top: go up in your thoughts to the first heaven and contemplate the many thousands of angels that are there. If you can, rise with your thoughts to a higher height: contemplate the archangels and contemplate the spirits, see the virtues, the principalities, the powers, the thrones and the dominions40. God has given the Paraclete as prefect, teacher and sanctifier of all of them. Elijah, Elisha and Isaiah among men need him. And among the angels, Michael and Gabriel. None of the created things equals him in honor. For all classes of angels and all armies together lack parity and equality with the Holy Spirit. All of them are covered and obscured by the extremely good power of the Paraclete. If any of them is sent to carry out a ministry41, he searches even the depths of God, as the Apostle says: «The Spirit searches everything, even to the depths of God. Indeed, what man knows the innermost part of man but the spirit of man that is in him? In the same way, no one knows what is intimate about God, except the Spirit of God" (I Cor 2:10-11) In union with the Father and the Son, the Holy Spirit distributes his gifts

24. He, in the prophets, announced Christ; he acted in the apostles; He, to this day, seals souls in baptism. The Father gives himself to the Son, and the Son communicates of himself to the Holy Spirit42. It is Jesus himself, not me, who says it: "Everything has been handed over to me by my Father" (Mt 11:27). And of the Holy Spirit he says: "When he, the Spirit of truth, comes... He will give me glory, because he will receive what is mine and will announce it to you" (Jn 16:13-14). The Father, through the Son and together with the Spirit, gives everything. There are not some gifts from the Father, others those from the Son, and others those from the Holy Spirit. For there is one salvation, one power and one faith, God the Father is one, his Son is one and the Holy Spirit Paraclete is one. And it is enough for us to know these things. Do not diligently inquire into nature or substance. Well, if it was something that had been written, we would say it. But let's not dare with what has not been written. For our salvation it is enough for us to know that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit exist. About the seventy elders who helped Moses

25. This Spirit descended, in the time of Moses, upon the seventy elders. (But let the breadth of the discourse, dear ones, not cause you boredom. The same one of which we speak gives strength to each one of us, to those who speak and to those who listen.) This Spirit, as I said, descended on those seventy elders who were under Moses. But I tell you this to prove that he knows everything and acts everything as he wants. Seventy elders were selected. «Yahweh came down in the cloud and spoke to him. Then he took some of the spirit that was in him and gave it to the seventy elders” (Num 11:25). And the Spirit was not divided, but each one received something of his grace, distributed according to his ability and his power. Those present were in fact sixty-eight, and they prophesied, but Eldad and Medad were not there. But to make it clear that it was not Moses who granted anything, but rather the Spirit who worked, Eldad and Medad also prophesied, who had been called, but had not come (cf. Num 11:26-30). The same sign of the laying on of hands for the old and the new Covenant

26. Joshua, son of Nun, Moses' successor, was amazed at this, and coming to Moses he said, "Have you heard that Eldad and Medad are prophesying?" They were called and they did not come. «My lord Moses, forbid it» (11:28). But he said to him: I cannot forbid it, for it is a heavenly grace. I will not stop you, because I also have that grace. I don't think you said this out of envy. Do not be consumed with zeal for me because they have prophesied while you have not yet prophesied. Wait a while: "If only all of Yahweh's people would prophesy because Yahweh would give them his spirit!" (11.29). Prophetically he added "because he gave them his spirit." Well, he certainly hasn't given it now either, and you don't have it yet. So, didn't Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph have it? Didn't those who lived before him have it? However, it is very clear that "when God gave them his spirit", which is as if he were saying: to everyone. And yet the gift of grace is now private and restricted, whereas then it was poured out and abounded. In reality, what was meant was what would happen to us at Pentecost, since he also descended among us. But it had also previously descended on many. For it is written: "Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid hands on him" (Dt 34:9). You see the same sign everywhere, in the old and the new Covenant. In the time of Moses the spirit was granted by the laying on of hands. To you, who will be baptized, grace must come. I do not tell you how nor do I anticipate the moment43, Presence of the Spirit in characters of the old Alliance

27. He also came to all the righteous and prophets. I mean Enos, Enoch, Noah and the rest, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. That Joseph also had the spirit of God (cf. Gen 41:38) is something that Pharaoh himself had already discovered. You have already heard about Moses and the wonderful things he did by the Spirit. The mighty Job and all the saints also had it, although we will not mention the names of all of them now. He was the one who, in the construction of the Tabernacle, filled Besalel and his skilled companions with wisdom (Ex 31, 1-6).

28. In the strength of this Spirit, according to what we have in the book of Judges, Othniel was judge (Judges 3:10), Gideon was strengthened (6:34) and Jephthah achieved victory (11:29). Deborah, a woman, engaged in battle (4-5) and Samson, while he was still acting justly and did not grieve the Spirit, did things greater than human strength44. In the books of Kings we clearly find, about Samuel and David45, how they prophesied in the Holy Spirit and were chief prophets. And Samuel was called "seer" (I Sam 9,9.11). But David says eloquently: “The spirit of Yahweh speaks through me” (2 Sam 23:2). And, in the Psalms: "Do not take your holy spirit from me" (51:13). And in turn: "May your spirit, which is good, guide me across a flat land" (143,10). And, as we have in the Chronicles, Azariah, under King Asa, and, under Jehoshaphat, Jahaziel, were blessed with the Holy Spirit (2 Chron 15:1; 20:14). And also Zechariah, who was stoned to death (2 Chron 24:20-21; cf. Mt 23:35 ff.). And Ezra says: "You gave them your good Spirit to instruct them" (Neh 9:20)46. Concerning Elijah, the one who was taken, and Elisha, both bearers of the Spirit and achievers of admirable things, it is clear - although we now overlook it - that they were filled with the Holy Spirit. And in other prophets

29. And if someone goes through the books of both the twelve47 and the other prophets, they will find many testimonies about the Holy Spirit. Micah says: "I, however, am filled with strength through the spirit of Yahweh" (Micah 3:8). And Joel: "It will come to pass after this that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh" (3:1). And Haggai says: "...according to the word that I covenanted with you when you left Egypt, and my Spirit remains in your midst: do not fear" (2:5). Similarly, Zechariah: "However, accept my words and my commands, which I command in my Spirit to my servants the prophets" (Zech 1:6 LXX). And so on, other things. In Isaiah and Ezekiel

30. Also Isaiah, the most eloquent preacher: “The Spirit of Yahweh will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and strength, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of Yahweh. And it will inspire him with the fear of Yahweh” (11:2-3). By this he means that he (the Spirit) is one and indivisible, but the effects he produces are diverse. And also: «Behold my servant whom I uphold, my chosen one in whom my soul delights. I have put my spirit on him (Is 42:1). And also that: «I will pour out my spirit on your offspring (44,3). And further: "Now the Lord Yahweh sends me with his spirit" (48:16). Or: “As for me, this is the alliance with them, says Yahweh. My spirit that has come upon you..." (59,21)49. And, in turn: "The spirit of the Lord Yahweh is upon me, because Yahweh has anointed me..." (61,1)49. And also, speaking against the Jews: "But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit" (Is 63:10) and: "Where is he who put his Holy Spirit in him?" (63.11). You also have in Ezekiel—if you are not already tired of hearing—what has already been remembered: «The spirit of Yahweh broke into me and said to me: 'Say: Thus says Yahweh'» (Ez 11,5). But the "burst upon me" must be understood correctly, as meaning charity and clemency. In a similar way to how Jacob, once he found Joseph, "fell on his neck" (Gen 46:29) and how, in the Gospels, that loving father, upon seeing his son returned, "moved, ran, fell on his neck and kissed him profusely" (Lk 15:20). And, also in Ezekiel: "The spirit lifted me up and took me to Chaldea, where the exiles were, in vision, in the spirit of God" (Ez 11:24). And you already heard other things before, when we talked about baptism50: "I will sprinkle you with pure water... and I will give you a new heart, I will put a new spirit in you" (36,25.26). And, shortly after: "The hand of Yahweh was upon me, and by his spirit Yahweh brought me out" (37:1). In Daniel

31. He put wisdom into the soul of Daniel, so that a young man would be a judge of elders. The chaste Susanna had been condemned as impudent. Nobody defended her. Who would have snatched her from the hands of the leaders? She was taken to death and was already in the hands of the executioners (Dan 13:41-45). But his helper appeared, the Paraclete, the Spirit who sanctifies every intelligent creature. “Hang in there,” he told Daniel. «You, who are young, argue against the old who are stained by the corruption of the sins of the young. For it is written: "He raised up the holy spirit of a young man" (13:45). And, briefly summarizing, that pure girl was saved by Daniel's sentence. We have summarized this case, since there is no time to explain everything. Even Nebuchadnezzar recognized that the Holy Spirit was in Daniel, since he referred to him as "Daniel..., in whom resides the spirit of the holy gods" (Dan 4:6)51. He said one thing true and one thing false. That he had the Holy Spirit was true, but not that he was "chief of the wise men." For he was not a magician, but a knower of things by the Spirit. In fact, before (Dan 2:31ff.) he had explained the vision of the image that he had seen and that he did not understand. "Explain to me, he says, the vision, because I, who saw it, do not understand it." You see there the power of the Holy Spirit, because those who saw do not understand, and those who did not see knew and interpreted. In the following catechesis we will talk about the Holy Spirit in the New Testament

32. We would be inclined to collect many testimonies from the Old Testament and to explain more clearly what concerns the Holy Spirit. But there is little time left and it is advisable that you not have so much to listen to. Therefore, content with what was mentioned about the old Covenant, we will return, if God allows it, in the following catechesis to what is missing from the New. May the God of peace gift you all with spiritual and heavenly goods through Our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit (cf. Rom 15:30). To him be glory and power forever and ever. Amen52...

1. The present catechesis and the following one, which were held during or around Holy Week, are an excellent testimony of the progress of the theological consciousness of the Church regarding the Holy Spirit, who at all times, even when clearly distinguished, is equated in dignity with the Father and the Son. Catechesis provides extensive information on opinions and heretical currents regarding the Holy Spirit, but it also positively exposes the teaching of Scripture about him. In this aspect, the catechesis is dedicated more than anything to the Old Testament, while the XVII exposes mainly the New Testament doctrine.

2. The quote from /Mt/12/32 is reproduced exactly as it appears in Cyril's text. But the full text of the verse is: “And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven; But whoever says it against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, neither in this world nor in the next. When interpreting the verse, one should not start from whether or not there are sins that cannot be forgiven, but from the problem of a possible existential closure of man. At this moment - and it will be explained throughout this catechesis and the next - the starting point is that man's access to Jesus Christ (and through him to the Father) is not done with the eyes of the flesh or with intelligence but by virtue of the action of the Spirit, who in the plan of salvation - regardless of whether man is aware of it or not - is the one who, through grace, makes man have access to God and the salvation that he offers him. He who "blasphemes against the Spirit", thus closing himself off from the action of God in him - whether or not one is reflectively aware of the work of God in him is a secondary question - thus closes himself to the path of salvation towards his existence. This is something that should be taken into account at least as a warning. The theme of the "sin against the Holy Spirit" has been exposed with remarkable clarity in the encyclical Dominum et vivificantem of John Paul II, stating that ""blasphemy" does not consist in the fact of offending the Holy Spirit with words; It consists, on the contrary, in the refusal to accept the salvation that God offers to man through the Holy Spirit, who acts by virtue of the sacrifice of the Cross. If man rejects that "convincing about sin", which comes from the Holy Spirit and has a saving character, he at the same time rejects the "coming" of the Paraclete: that "coming" that has been accomplished in the paschal mystery, in unity through the redeeming power of the Blood of Christ. The Blood "that purifies the dead works of our conscience." »We know that a fruit of this purification is the remission of sins. Therefore, he who rejects the Spirit and the Blood remains in "dead works", that is, in sin. And the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit consists precisely in the radical refusal to accept this remission, of which the Spirit himself is the intimate dispenser and which presupposes the true conversion wrought by him in conscience.

If Jesus affirms that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit cannot be forgiven either in this life or in the future, it is because this "non-remission" is linked, as its cause, to "non-repentance", that is, to the radical rejection of conversion. Which means the refusal to turn to the sources of Redemption, which, however, remain "always" open in the economy of salvation, in which the mission of the Holy Spirit is carried out» (Dominum et vivificantem, no. 46; the Spanish edition of PPC, Madrid, 1986, year of the appearance of the encyclical, has been cited).

3. In somewhat broad language, it is a clear confession of the Trinitarian faith. Regarding the Father and the Son, the phrase recalls I Cor 8:6: «For us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things come and through whom we are; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things are and through whom we are. The XVI and XVII catechisms aim to speak of the Holy Spirit in such a way that in the listeners he is equated, in his dignity, with the Father and the Son. This expresses the maturity of the dogmatic conscience of the Church.
4. Mt 3,16 (Mc 1,10; Lk 3,22) show this union of Jesus with the Spirit, in the same way that he also appears united to the Father. It is from there that Jesus will begin his public activity.

5. It seems that in some historical moments some spoke, for the Old and New Testaments, of several "Fathers", several "Christs" and several "Spirits", although these are things that are too far from our mentality. See different testimonies about the Marcionites, Manichaeans, Gnostics, etc. in PG 33,921-922, note 3.

6. These words from Mt 28:19 probably reflect, written decades after the earthly Jesus, an expressly Trinitarian formula of baptism that perhaps cannot be understood as a literal expression of Jesus. But this is not an inconvenience if we take into account both 1) the value of all the texts of Scripture, which has the value of divine Word without necessarily having to prepare a record of historical accuracy, and 2) the rectitude of the use of a Trinitarian formula in the action of baptizing.

7. Marcion (ca. 85-ca. 160) had defended a total opposition between a God of the Old Testament, rigid, legalistic and just, and the God of the New Testament, reflected only in the theology of Paul and what of it is found in Luke. Marcion was a talented organizer and his preaching offered a rigorous sense of morality, both characteristics that, together with his strong personality, gave him numerous followers. He was excommunicated, upon conviction of the lack of relationship between his teachings and the apostolic faith, in Rome in the year 144.
8. Faith and piety that are directed to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, since the three must not be separated, are directed to a single God.

9. 42. This statement represents in some way the internal life of God: the Father begets the Son (and the Son thus proceeds from the Father). The Spirit comes from the love between the Father and the Son. The theological tradition of the Western Church has pointed out, especially from the influence of Carolingian theology, that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son. In this way the famous expression Filioque ("and of the Son") was added to the Creed of the Latin Church. This addition, rather than a direct theological justification, has its origin in the interest in pointing out, contrary to the Arian conception, the equality of the Father and the Son in terms of their dignity, and thus, in this case, it is affirmed that the Holy Spirit comes from both (theologians have called "processions" the fact that the Son proceeds from the Father, and the Holy Spirit from the Father and the Son). The Eastern tradition, for its part, has preferred to express itself by saying that the Holy Spirit comes from the Father through the Son. This, leaving aside the anti-Arian controversy - which should no longer be necessary - is perhaps even more accurate. It is thus more adequately expressed that the Son is also the mediator of the Holy Spirit and, at the same time, that it is the Holy Spirit who leads us to Jesus Christ (cf. I Cor 12:3) and, through him, to the Father. Ultimately it is an even more Christ-centered conception and also expresses more clearly that the Father is at the beginning of everything. Cyril of Jerusalem fits, logically, within the Eastern Trinitarian theological conception. An acceptable practical exposition of the relationship between Father, Son and Holy Spirit is given, based on various biblical data, in cat. XVII, no. 19. Other details in PG 33,951, note 1. It is interesting, on the other hand, to remember that, on the feast of Pentecost in 1981, John Paul II, in the recitation of the Creed in St. Peter's Basilica, suppressed the words "and of the Son" in a meeting with Catholic and Orthodox bishops. Cf. the religious information magazines for the month of June of that year. CATECHESIS XVII THE HOLY SPIRIT (II) Delivered in Jerusalem, it finishes what was left about the Holy Spirit. The reading is taken from the First Epistle to the Corinthians: “For to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit; to another word of knowledge..." (I Cor 12,8 ff.).1 We will stop at fundamental points of the New Testament

1. In the previous catechesis we offered, as far as our strength allowed, a small part of the testimonies referring to the Holy Spirit. In the present, as soon as we are allowed, we will touch, God willing, on what remains to us, that is, what refers to the New Testament. Already then, in order not to go too far in speaking, we set limits to our task—because we would never finish talking about the Holy Spirit—and now we will give an account of a small part of what remains. We do not naively attempt to cover the little we will say with the multitude of what can be gleaned from Scripture. Nor will we use human reasoning and inventions today—it should not be done—but it will be enough for us to recall the sentences of the Holy Scripture. It is the safest procedure according to the blessed apostle Paul, who says "... of which we also speak2, not with words learned from human wisdom, but learned from the Spirit, expressing spiritual realities in spiritual terms" (1 Cor 2:13). We do things similar to pedestrians and sailors, who, having in mind the goal of a very long journey, hurry on purpose, but tend, due to human limitations, to stop in different cities and ports. One God the Father, one Son, one Holy Spirit

2. For although there have been divisions when it comes to disputing about the Holy Spirit, he nevertheless remains undivided, since he is one and the same. Likewise, when we talked about the Father, we mentioned, on the one hand, the supreme and only power of his person, and on the other, how he was called "Father" and "Almighty" and, furthermore, creator of all things3 but this distribution of catechesis did not mean a division of faith. The purpose of piety and our religiosity was also unique when we spoke of the only begotten Son of God, when we taught both what refers to his divinity and what concerns his humanity. In this way when we distributed in various questions what had to be said about our Lord Jesus Christ, we preached an undivided faith in him. Therefore, even now, even though we have divided the catechisms about the Holy Spirit, it is an undivided faith in him that we announce. For the Holy Spirit is one and the same, since "all these things are worked by one and the same Spirit, distributing them to each one individually according to his will" (1 Cor 12:11), but he remains without division. For there is no other Paraclete other than the Holy Spirit, but he is unique and identical although with different names: living and subsistent4, who speaks and acts. He is a sanctifier of all creatures endowed with reason that God has made through Christ, angels and men. Various denominations, but one Spirit

3. But let some not believe, due to their ignorance and the diversity of denominations of the Holy Spirit, that these are diverse spirits, and not a single and identical one, the only one that exists. For this reason, the Catholic Church, which ensures your safety, transmitted in the confession of faith that we believe "in one Holy Spirit Paraclete, who spoke through the prophets": so that you could realize that certainly the denominations can be many, but there is only one Holy Spirit. Of those many denominations we will now talk to you about some. The relationship of the Holy Spirit to the Son and the Father

4. It is called Spirit according to what we have read: "For through the Spirit the word of wisdom is given to one" (1 Cor 12:8). And he is called the Spirit of Truth, according to what the Savior says: "When he, the Spirit of truth, comes..." (Jn 16:13). He is also called the Paraclete, as he also said: "... because if I do not go, the Paraclete will not come to you" (16,7). And that it is a single and same reality, which is called by different names, is clearly explained by what I will immediately say. Well, it has already been said that the Holy Spirit and the Paraclete are the same. But it is also said that the Paraclete and the Spirit of truth are the same: "(And I will ask the Father) and he will give you another Paraclete, to be with you forever, the Spirit of truth" (14:16-17). And also, "when the Paraclete comes, I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth" (15:26). It is called the Spirit of God, as it is written: "I saw the Spirit descending...on him" (Jn 1:32), and, in turn: "All those who are led by the spirit of God are children of God" (Rom 8:14). It is also called the Spirit of the Father, as the Savior said: "It will not be you who will speak, but the Spirit of your Father who will speak for you" (Mt 10:20). And also Paul: "I bow my knees before the Father" (Eph 3:14) and, further down: "... that he may grant you... that you may be strengthened by the action of his Spirit" (3:16). It is also called the Spirit of the Lord, as Peter says: "How have you agreed to test the Spirit of the Lord?" (Acts 5:9). It is also called the Spirit of God and of Christ, as Paul writes: «But you are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, since the Spirit of God dwells in you. He who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to Him” (Romans 8:9). It is also called the Spirit of the Son of God, as it is said: "The proof that you are sons is that God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts" (Gal 4, or). And he is also mentioned as the Spirit of Christ, as it has been written: "... seeking to discover to what time and to what circumstances the Spirit of Christ referred" (I Peter 1:11). And also: "...thanks to your prayers and the help given by the Spirit of Jesus Christ" (Phil 1:19). More denominations of the Holy Spirit

5. You will also find many other denominations of the Holy Spirit. For it is called the Spirit of sanctification, as it is written: "According to the Spirit of holiness" (Rom 1, 4)5. It is also called the Spirit of adoption, as Paul says: "For you did not receive a spirit of slaves to fall back into fear, but you received a spirit of adopted sons, which makes us cry, 'Abba, Father!'" (Rom 8:15). It is also called the Spirit of revelation, as it is written: "... may the God of our Lord Jesus Christ grant you the spirit of wisdom and revelation to know him perfectly" (Eph 1:17). He is also mentioned as the Spirit of the Promise, as it is said in the same place: "In him you also, after you... also believed in him, were sealed with the Holy Spirit of the Promise" (1:13). He is also called the Spirit of grace, when in turn he says: "he who... insulted the Spirit of grace" (Hebrews 10:29). And it is also called by many other names in the same way. You also heard clearly in the preceding catechesis that in the Psalms he is sometimes called "good" and sometimes "generous" (51:14). And in Isaiah it has been called "the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and strength, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the Lord" (Is 11:2). From all of this it can be deduced, both from the above and from what we have said now, that the denominations are really different, but the Holy Spirit is one and the same, living and subsistent, always present together with the Father and the Son. It is not uttered by words from the mouth or lips of the Father or the Son, nor by any expiration, nor is it cast into the air, but it subsists in itself6, speaking and acting itself, dispenser and sanctifier. It is not a dispensation with tear, but in harmony, and it is the only one that gives salvation, which proceeds—as we already said—from the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. I want you to remember what we recently said7 and to clearly realize that it is not a question, in the Law and the Prophets, of one Spirit and a different one in the Gospels and in the Apostles. There is only one and identical Holy Spirit, who inspired the Holy Scriptures in both the Old and New Testaments. The Holy Spirit made the virginal conception of Mary possible

6. This is the Holy Spirit who came to Holy Virgin Mary. For since it was about begetting Christ, the Only Begotten, the power of the Most High covered her with his shadow and the Holy Spirit, approaching her (cf. Luke 1:35), sanctified her for this, so that she could have within her the one by whom everything was made. I do not need many words for you to understand that this pregnancy was free of all stains and contamination, since you already learned it (cf. cat. 12, no. 25). Gabriel is the one who told her: I am a messenger and herald of what is to happen, but I do not participate in the operation. For although I am an archangel, I am knowledgeable about my order and my office. I announce joy to you, but it is not by my grace that you will give birth: «The Holy Spirit will come upon you and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; That is why he who is to be born will be holy and will be called the Son of God” (Luke 1:35). The Holy Spirit in Elizabeth, Zechariah and Simeon

7. This Holy Spirit showed its effectiveness in Elizabeth. Well, it not only acted with virgins, but also between spouses as long as it was a legitimate marriage. "And Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit" (Lk 1:41) and she prophesied. And the illustrious servant said of her Lord: "Where is it that the mother of my Lord comes to me?" (1.43). For Elizabeth called her blessed (1:45). Filled with the same Spirit, Zechariah, father of John, also prophesied saying how much good this Only Begotten would cause, adding also that John would be, by his baptism, his precursor. Simeon the just was also warned by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before contemplating the Messiah of the Lord and, receiving him in his arms, he publicly testified in the Temple about what was his part (cf. Luke 2:25-35). John the Baptist and the Holy Spirit

8. John, for his part, who had been filled with the Holy Spirit from his mother's womb (Luke 1:5), was sanctified in order to baptize the Lord, not because he communicated the Spirit but because he announced the one who did communicate it. For he says: «I baptize you with water for conversion; but he who comes after me... he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire" (Mt 3:11). "In fire", why? Because in tongues of fire the descent of the Holy Spirit took place. About which the Lord says with joy: "I have come to cast a fire on the earth and how I wish it were already lit!" The Holy Spirit in the baptism of Jesus

9. This Holy Spirit descended when the Lord was baptized (Mt 3:16) so that the dignity of the one who was baptized would not be hidden, according to what John says: "He who sent me to baptize with water said to me: The one on whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining on him is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit (Jn 1:33). But look what the gospel says: “The heavens were opened.” Opened by the dignity of the one who descended. It says: "The heavens opened and he saw the Spirit of God descending in the form of a dove and coming upon him." (Mt 3,16). It was a descent on his own initiative8. For it was appropriate, as some have interpreted, that the first fruits and gifts of the Holy Spirit, which are granted to the baptized, were shown first in the humanity of the Savior, who is the one who confers such grace9. He descended in the form of a dove—as some say, pure, innocent and simple—cooperating with their prayers in favor of the new children and the forgiveness of their sins, thus showing the image and the example10. In this way it had been predicted, in a mysterious way, that the Messiah would manifest himself in this way. For in the Song of Songs it is exclaimed about the Bridegroom: "His eyes are like doves by streams of water" (Song 5:12)11. Noah's Ark, the dove, baptism, the Holy Spirit12

10. NOE/ES NOE/J J/NOE: According to some, an image of that dove was offered in part by the one told in the story of Noah (Gen 8,8 ff.). Well, in those times, salvation and the beginning of the new humanity came to men through wood and water. The dove returned to Noah at sunset, carrying an olive branch (Gen 8:11). Thus, they say, it was the Holy Spirit who actually descended with Noah, the head of that new humanity. He (the Holy Spirit) is the one who made a unity of the wills and the genius of the diverse lineages. The different natures of the animals enclosed in the ark were an image of this diversity of interests. And after he (Christ) arrived, the spiritual wolves grazed with the sheep, because the Church feeds the calf and the bull with the lion (Is 11:6; 65:25). Today we see that the princes of the world are guided and taught by the men of the Church. Therefore there descended, as some interpret, an intelligible dove at the moment of baptism. Thus he showed that it was the same one who, through the wood of the cross, grants salvation to those who believe and who, in the evening13, would bring salvation through his death. Jesus himself speaks of the Holy Spirit and promises it to the Apostles14

11. And we must also speak of these things from another aspect. It is necessary to hear the words of the Savior about the Holy Spirit. For it says: "Unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the Kingdom of God" (Jn 3:5). And about this grace coming from the Father he says: How much more will the Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him! (Jn 11:13). And he also points out that God must be worshiped in Spirit: «But the hour is coming, and we are already in it, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, because that is how the Father wants them to be those who worship him. God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth” (Jn 4:23-24). And also: "But if by the Spirit of God I cast out demons..." (Mt 12:28), and shortly after, in what follows: "Therefore I tell you: all sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven. And whoever speaks a word against the Son of man, it will be forgiven him; But whoever says it against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, neither in this age nor in the next” (12:31-32). And he also says: «And I will ask the Father and he will give you another Paraclete, to be with you forever, the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it does not see him nor know him. But you know him, because he dwells with you and is in you” (Jn 14:16-17). And he also says: “I have told you these things while I was among you. But the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything and will remind you of everything I have told you" (14:25-26). And he says: "When the Paraclete comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness of me" (15:26). Also: "If I do not go, the Paraclete will not come to you... and when he comes, he will convince the world about sin, about justice, and about judgment" (16:7-8). And in turn, in what follows: «I still have much to tell you, but now you cannot bear it. When he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into the complete truth; for he will not speak on his own, but he will speak what he hears, and he will announce to them what is to come. He will give me glory, because he will receive what is mine and will announce it to you. Everything the Father has is mine. That is why I said: he will receive what is mine and will announce it to you” (16,1215).
I have read expressions from the Only Begotten Himself, so that you no longer pay attention to human words. The partial gift of the Holy Spirit, already on the same day of the resurrection

12. He gave the gift of the Holy Spirit to the apostles. For it is written: "Having said this, he breathed on them and said to them, 'Receive the Holy Spirit. Whose sins you forgive, they are forgiven; whose sins you retain, they are retained'" (John 20:22-23). This is the second time that the Spirit was breathed in, since the first time (Gen 2:7)15 had been obscured by voluntary sins. Now what is written was fulfilled: "He ascended, breathing in your face, delivering you from affliction" (Nah 2,2 LXX). Where did he "ascend" from? From hell16. The gospel narrates, in fact, that, after his resurrection, Jesus breathed on them (Jn 20:22). He really gives them grace now, but he will give it more abundantly later. It is as if I were saying to them: I am in a position to give it to you now, but the recipient cannot collect it. Receive for now the grace you can, but wait for a broader one. "For your part, remain in the city until you are clothed with power from on high" (Lk 24:39). Now "receive" it in part; later, in its entirety, and they will be completely bearers of it. For he who "receives" often only partially has what is granted to him. But he who dresses himself covers himself completely with the stole. Do not fear, he says, the weapons of the devil and his darts, for they will be bearers of the strength of the Holy Spirit. Remember what we said previously, that it is not the Holy Spirit that is divided, but the grace that he confers. The coming of the Spirit at Pentecost

13. Jesus then ascended into heaven and fulfilled his promise. Well, he had told them: "I will ask the Father and he will give you another Paraclete" (Jn 14:16). They were sitting waiting for the coming of the Holy Spirit. "When the day of Pentecost arrived" (Acts 2:2), here, in this city of Jerusalem—in reality, it is something that affects us, since we do not speak of what happened to others, but of the gifts that have been granted to us—, when it was, I say, Pentecost, they were sitting and the Paraclete arrived from heaven: custodian and sanctifier of the Church, rector of souls, guide of those thrown into the waves and into the storm, light of the lost, referee of those who fight and crown of the victors. The coming of the Spirit penetrates the interior of the soul

14. And he descended to clothe his power and baptize the apostles. The Lord says: "In a few days you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit" (Acts 1:5). It is not that grace has been divided or is given only in part, but that it is an integral force that has been poured out completely. For just as he who is baptized by immersion is surrounded by water on all sides, so those baptized in the Spirit are completely surrounded by it. On the other hand, the water is poured out externally to the body, but the Spirit penetrates and baptizes the hidden soul without anything being hidden from it. What are you amazed at? Take the example of matter, weak and humble, but which can be useful to the simplest. The fire, upon penetrating the interior of the iron, turns everything into fire and causes the cold metal to boil, thus beginning to shine what was black and dark. Well, if fire, a material reality, when introduced into the interior of iron, acts there without encountering obstacles, why are you surprised that the Holy Spirit penetrates into the interior of the soul? The Pentecost event in Acts 2

15. And so that the greatness of the grace that was coming would not be ignored, it sounded like a heavenly trumpet: "Suddenly there came from heaven a noise like a rush of mighty wind" (Acts 2:2), which thus gave a sign of the coming of him who grants men "to obtain by violence the Kingdom of God" (cf. Mt 11:12). And it made the eyes see tongues of fire and the ears hear the sound. And “he filled the whole house where they were” (Acts 2:2). That house became the receptacle of an intelligible wave. The disciples were sitting inside and the whole house was filled. They were baptized, “immersed”17 completely. according to the promise (cf. Acts 1:5). They clothed themselves in soul and body with a divine and healthy garment. «Tongues like fire appeared to them and spread out and rested on each one of them; They were all filled with the Holy Spirit" (2,3). They received a fire that did not burn, but was healthy and that, destroying the thorns of sins, restored its brilliance and splendor to the soul. This is the one who will soon come to you. And while he cuts and removes your sins, which are like thorns, he will make the depths of your soul shine more and give you grace, as he then gave it to the apostles. He landed on them under the appearance of tongues of fire, as if wanting to redeem their heads with spiritual diadems in the shape of tongues of fire. On a previous occasion, a sword of fire prevented entry to paradise (/Gn/03/24). Now, a tongue of fire that sought salvation returned that grace. The gift of languages

16. "And they began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit enabled them to express themselves" (Acts 2:4). The Galilean Peter and Andrew speak the language of the Persians or the Medes. John and the other apostles spoke in any language to people who came from diverse towns. For it is not now that crowds of foreign people have begun to gather from all sides, but this has already happened since that time. Where will one find such a great teacher who only by example teaches his listeners without having previously learned his language? Many years are spent, through grammar and the other arts, just to learn to speak correctly in Greek. And not everyone, however, speaks it the same way. Perhaps a rhetor18 can speak beautifully, but perhaps not a grammarian. And an expert in grammar may not know philosophical matters. But the Holy Spirit taught many languages ​​that those men had never learned. This is truly great wisdom and strength from God. Can a lack of culture for so many years on the part of those be compared with the multiple and unprecedented energy of languages? The amazement of believers

17. Stupor occurred in the crowd of those who were listening (Acts 2:6), a confusion different from the confusion that came from evil and that had occurred at Babel (cf. Gen. 11:79). Well, in that case, with the confusion of languages, a division of spirits and wills occurred when a project opposed to God was conceived19. But here the thoughts of the mind were repaired and called to unity, since pious interests were involved. By the same means by which the fall occurred, the conversion also occurred. Hence they were amazed saying: "How do each of us hear them?" (Acts 2:8). There is nothing strange that you ignore it, since Nicodemus was also unaware of the arrival of the Spirit, and it was said to him: "The Spirit blows where he wants, and you hear his voice, but you do not know where he comes from or where he goes" (Jn 3:8). And if I ever hear his voice, I don't know where it comes from. How can I explain his person? The Holy Spirit is like the new wine of the new Covenant.

18. "Others, however, said laughing: 'They are full of must!' (Acts 2:13) They told the truth but in a mocking way. For it was a truly new wine: the grace of the new Covenant. This was a truly new wine20, from an intelligible vine, which often, according to the prophets, had already borne fruit and which germinated in the New Testament. For in the same way that, to take a graphic example, the vineyard always remains the same, but according to the change of the seasons it always produces new fruits, so, although the Spirit always remains as he is, in the same way that he often manifested his strength in the prophets, he now decided on something new and admirable. Grace came to the Fathers before, but now it does so to a greater extent. For they really received a participation in the Holy Spirit. But on this occasion 21 were baptized (into it) completely and completely. The promise of the Spirit through Jesus and the prophecy of Joel are fulfilled

19. But Peter, who had the Holy Spirit, was fully aware of what he had and said: "You Jews and all inhabitants of Jerusalem," who preach Joel but do not know the Scriptures, "these are not drunks, as you suppose" (Acts 2:14-15). For they are drunk, but not as you think, but according to what is written: "They are satisfied with the fat of your House, you water them with the stream of your delights" (Ps 36:9). They are drunk with sober drunkenness, which destroys sin and gives life to the heart, completely different from drunkenness of the body. Well, this one causes us to forget the things we know, but the other one even grants the knowledge of unknown things. They are drunk with wine from the intelligible vine, he who says: “I am the vine; you are the branches" (Jn 15:5). And if you don't believe me, understand what I'm saying from the same circumstance of time. "For it is the third hour of the day" (Acts 2:15). He (Christ) had been crucified at the third hour, as Mark says (15:25). Now also22 he sent grace. For that grace and this one are not different, but he who had been crucified and had committed himself, thus fulfilled his word. If you choose to accept this testimony, hear what it says: "This is what the prophet said: It will happen in the last days, says God: I will pour out my Spirit..." (Acts 2:16-17; cf. Joel 3:1-5). But I will pour out means a copious donation, since God “gives the Spirit without measure. The Father loves the Son and has put everything in his hand" (Jn 3:34-35). And he gave him the power to grant the grace of the Holy Spirit to whomever he wishes. "I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh, and their sons and your daughters will prophesy" (Acts 2:17)... "and I will pour out my Spirit on my male and female servants" (2:18; cf. Joel 3:1-2). The Holy Spirit is no respecter of persons, since he does not seek dignities but rather the piety of the soul. Let the rich not harden nor the poor lose heart, but simply prepare each one to receive heavenly grace. Given the multitude of data, we will reduce our claims

20. There are many things we have discussed today and perhaps your ears are tired. But there are still many things left and to conclude the teaching on the Holy Spirit a third and even more catechesis would be necessary. But grant us permission for all of this, since the Easter festival is upon us. Therefore, today we will still talk about it, but we will not be able to mention everything that is in the New Testament. And we have many data left from the Acts of the Apostles, according to which the grace of the Holy Spirit acted effectively in Peter and also in all the other apostles. There are many other things in the Catholic epistles and in the fourteen epistles of Paul, of which we will now try to remove a few, as if taking them from an immense meadow, in order to bring them to memory. The power of Peter's words. Healing of the paralytic. Ananias and Sapphira

21. For in the power of the Holy Spirit, by the will of the Father and the Son, "Peter, appearing with the Eleven, lifted up his voice" (according to that: "Cry with a powerful voice, joyful messenger to Jerusalem", Is 40:9) and in the spiritual network of his words he captured "about three thousand souls" (Acts 2:41). A grace so intense acted in all the apostles that many of the Jews—who had crucified the Messiah—believed and were baptized in the name of Christ, and persevered in the apostles' teaching and prayers (cf. Acts 2:42). And on one occasion when, by the same power of the Holy Spirit, Peter and John, at the ninth hour, had gone up to the temple to pray, they healed one who had been at the Beautiful Gate, lame since his mother's womb, for forty years (3,110). Thus what was said was fulfilled: "Then the lame will leap like a deer" (Is 35, ó). With the spiritual network of his teaching, five thousand believed that day (Acts 4:4) and declared the leaders of the people and the high priests convicted of error. And this, not by virtue of their own wisdom, since they were unlettered and ignorant, but by the effectiveness of the Spirit. For it is written: "Then Peter, full of the Holy Spirit, said to them..." (Acts 4:8 ff.). And the grace of the Holy Spirit was so great that it was worked by the twelve apostles in whom they had believed, that they were one heart and one soul, but the use of their goods was common. For those who owned religiously handed over the value of their possessions and none of them was in need. Ananias and Sapphira, who tried to deceive the Holy Spirit, had to endure a suitable punishment (5, 1-11). The power of the Holy Spirit

22. "Many signs and wonders were performed among the people by the hand of the apostles" (5:12). And so much grace of the Spirit had been poured out on the apostles that, although they were simple, they caused fear (for there were those who did not dare to join them, although the people praised them). But "crowds of men and women who believed" were added to them... "to such an extent that they even took the sick out into the squares and placed them on beds and stretchers, so that, as Peter passed by, even his shadow would cover some of them. The multitude also came from the neighboring cities to Jerusalem, bringing the sick and tormented by unclean spirits; and they were all healed” (5:15-16; cf. 5:13) by the power of the Holy Spirit. Arrest and release of the apostles

23. On another occasion the twelve apostles, thrown—for announcing Christ—into prison by the chief priests, were brought out of there at night by the Angel23 contrary to what might have been expected. And they were brought from the temple to the judgment seat24, and they rebuked them, telling them boldly about Christ. And when they added that "God also gave the Holy Spirit to those who obey him" (Acts 5:32) and they beat them with ropes, they marched joyfully and did not stop teaching and announcing the good news of Christ Jesus (cf. 5:40-42). The power of the Holy Spirit in Deacon Stephen

24. But the grace of the Holy Spirit was not only effective in the twelve apostles, but also in the firstborn children of this sometimes sterile Church. I am referring to the seven deacons. These were chosen, as the Scripture says, "full of Spirit and wisdom" (Acts 6:3). One of them, Stephen, worthily called by the crown25, the first fruit of the martyrs, "a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit" (6,5), "performed great wonders and signs among the people" (6,8). Some engaged in discussions with him, "but they could not resist the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke" (6:10). Attacked with slander and put on trial, he shone with angelic radiance. For "all those who were sitting in the Sanhedrin looking at him saw his face like the face of an angel." And after having refuted, with a wise apology for himself, the Jews, who were stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, and who always resist the Holy Spirit (Acts 7:51), "he saw the glory of God and the Son of man standing at the right hand of God." But he did not see it by his own power, but, as Holy Scripture says, "filled with the Holy Spirit, he looked intently at heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God" (7:55). In the deacon Felipe. Conversion of the Ethiopian eunuch

25. In the same power of the Holy Spirit, Philip also, in the name of Christ, expelled on some occasion, in a city of Samaria, unclean spirits that made loud cries. And he healed the paralyzed and the lame, and converted a great multitude of those who believed to Christ (Acts 8:4-8). Peter and John having come down to them, they made them, by the laying on of hands, partakers of the Holy Spirit (8:14-17). Of which only Simon Magus (18-24) was deservedly deprived. At another time, called by the Angel of the Lord to set out because of that most pious Ethiopian eunuch (8:26 ff.), he clearly heard the Holy Spirit himself: "Come near and stand next to that chariot" (8:29). He instructed the Ethiopian and baptized him, and thus sent the message of Christ to Ethiopia, according to what was written: "Let Ethiopia stretch out her hands toward God" (Ps 68:32). And, caught up by an angel26, he announced the gospel to all the other cities. In the apostle Paul

26. Paul was also filled with the same Holy Spirit, after he was called by Our Lord Jesus Christ. As a pious witness to this we have the pious Ananias, who was in Damascus and said to Paul: "Saul, brother, the Lord Jesus has sent me to you, who appeared to you on the way you were coming, so that you may regain your sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit" (Acts 9:17). And he, who acted quickly, restored the use of light to Paul's blinded eyes, printing a seal27 on his soul. He thus made him a vessel of election (cf. Acts 9:15), so that he would carry before the kings and the children of Israel the name of the Lord who had appeared to him. He turned the one who had previously been a persecutor into a herald and a good servant, who carried the gospel from Jerusalem to Illyria; He filled imperial Rome with his teachings and extended his diligent will to announce the Kerygma to Spain28. He also tackled a thousand tasks and performed signs and wonders. But for now enough with what has been said. The Holy Spirit illuminates Peter

27. In the force, therefore, of the same Holy Spirit, Peter, prince of the apostles and in charge of the keys of the kingdom of heaven, in Lidda (present-day Diospolis), restored the paralytic Aeneas to health in the name of Christ (9:32-35). And in Joppa he raised Tabitha from the dead (9:36-37), who was dedicated to doing good works. And being at the highest part of the house, in an ecstasy, he saw the sky open and descending like a great canvas, in which there were numerous figures and animals, so that no one could be said to be, even a Greek, vulgar or unclean (10:14-16). Called by Cornelius, he (Peter) heard clearly from the Holy Spirit himself: «There are men looking for you. So go down immediately and go with them without hesitation, for I have sent them” (10:19-20). And to explain more clearly that those who believe among the Gentiles are also made partakers of the grace of the Holy Spirit, when Peter arrived in Caesarea and taught what refers to Christ, the Scripture says about Cornelius and those who were present: "Peter was saying these things when the Holy Spirit fell on all those who heard the Word" (10:44), in such a way that those who had come with Peter from among the circumcised were astonished and, stupefied, They said: "That the gift of the Holy Spirit had also been poured out on the Gentiles" (v. 45)29. The community of Antioch and the first mission of Barnabas and Paul

28. And in Antioch of Syria, a most noble city, the proclamation of Christ developed admirably and from the place where we are, Barnabas, "a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith" (Acts 11:24), was sent to Antioch as a collaborator of that good work. Seeing a great harvest of believers in Christ, he took Paul as his helper from Tarsus to Antioch. And as they had gathered a great crowd in the assembly, all instructed in their commands and gathered there, it happened that "in Antioch was where, for the first time, the disciples received the name of Christians (11:26). In Antioch God poured out the Spirit very abundantly. There were prophets and doctors there (13:1), with whom Agabus was also (12:28). «While they were celebrating the worship of the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said: "Separate Barnabas and Saul for me now for the work to which I have called them" (13:2). Then, after having laid hands on them, they were sent by the Holy Spirit (cf. 13:3). It is, therefore, clear that the Spirit that speaks and sends is alive, has its own subsistence and, as we said, acts effectively. The Antioch controversy and the so-called "council" of Jerusalem

29. The same Holy Spirit, who, in consensus with the Father and the Son, inspired the New Testament in the Church, freed us from the difficult burdens of the Law, I mean those that refer to the pure and impure and to foods. He freed us from the Sabbaths, the new moons and circumcision, the sprinklings and the sacrifices (cf. Rom 8:2; Acts 15:10; Hebr 9:10), which things, given for a time, were "a shadow of the good things to come" (Hebr 10:1). But when the truth has come, they have been properly suppressed. When controversy arose in Antioch by those who said that it was necessary to be circumcised and observe the rules of Moses, Paul and Barnabas were sent. The apostles, who were then in Jerusalem, with all the baggage of the law and figures, liberated the entire world through a letter they wrote. But they did not attribute to themselves the authority of a matter of such magnitude, but in the epistle they declare: "It seemed to us30 to the Holy Spirit and to us not to impose on ourselves any more burdens than these indispensable ones: to abstain from things sacrificed to idols, from blood, from strangled animals, and from impurity (Acts 15:28-29). By what they wrote they openly made it clear that, although it had been written by the apostles, who were men, it was nevertheless a command of the Holy Spirit and affected the entire world. Paul and Barnabas took him with them into all the world. The power of the Spirit in Paul's missionary journeys

30. At this point in my words, I pray for your love that you grant me permission. I also beg the Holy Spirit who lived in Paul, if it is not possible for me to achieve everything, both because of my weakness and because of the fatigue of those of you who are listening. Well, when have I worthily explained his admirable deeds in the name of Christ and by the work of the Holy Spirit? What happened in Cyprus with the magician Elymas (Acts 13:5-12) or the healing of the cripple in Lystra (14:8-10), and what happened in Cilicia (15:41), Phrygia and Galatia (16:6), Mysia (16:8) and Macedonia (16:99 ff.). Or also that of the city of Philippi (16,12 ff.). I am referring to his preaching and the expulsion, in the name of Christ, of a spirit of divination (16:16-18). Also, after the earthquake, the salvation that was given through baptism to the prison guard with his entire household (16:25-34). Likewise, what happened in Thessaloniki (17.1 ff.) or his speech among the Athenians in the Areopagus (17.22 ff.). Or his teaching work in the city of Corinth and throughout Achaia (18:1 ff.). How will I continue to say everything that, through Paul, the Holy Spirit did in Ephesus? Those who previously did not know him knew him (the Holy Spirit) through Paul's teaching. For after Paul had laid his hands on them and the Holy Spirit had come upon them, "they began to speak in tongues and to prophesy" (Acts 19:6). And so much was the grace of the Spirit upon him that not only contact with him produced salvation, but also the handkerchiefs and aprons that had been separated from him cured diseases and removed evil spirits (Acts 19:12). Furthermore, those who had dedicated themselves to the esoteric arts "gathered the books and burned them before everyone" (19:19).

31. I also go over what was done in Troas, in Eutychus, who, overcome by sleep, "fell down from the third floor" and "they found him dead" (Acts 20:9), but was returned safe and sound by Paul (cf. 20:10). I ignore the prophecy that he presented before the priests of Ephesus gathered in Miletus, to whom he explained at length: "I only know that in each city the Holy Spirit testifies to me that...", etc. (20,23 ff.). By the words "in each city" Paul was referring to the admirable things that he had done in each place and that came from the action of the Holy Spirit: by the will of God and in the name of Christ who spoke in him. By the power of this Holy Spirit, Paul also came determined to this holy city of Jerusalem, although Agabus prophesied by the Spirit the things that were to happen to him (cf. Acts 21:10). But he expounded his doctrine among the people with the confidence of Christ. Transferred to Caesarea (23:23 ff.), sitting among the judges, before Felix (24:10 ff.) or before the procurator Festus or before King Agrippa, Paul, by the Holy Spirit and with the wisdom of conquering grace, managed to get the king of the Jews himself, Agrippa, to say: "With your arguments you almost made a Christian of me" (26:28). The same Holy Spirit granted Paul that on the island of Miletus he was not injured at all when he was bitten by a viper and that he performed various cures on the sick (Acts 28:1-9). The same Holy Spirit led the former persecutor as a herald to royal Rome. He persuaded many of the Jews who lived there to believe in Christ and to those who contradicted he spoke clearly: "No wonder the Holy Spirit spoke to their fathers through the prophet Isaiah..., etc." (28,25)31. Paul himself was filled with the Holy Spirit But that Paul was filled with the Holy Spirit, and so were the other apostles like him and those who after them believe in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit32, clearly heard from him himself who in his letters writes: "My word and my preaching had nothing of the persuasive speeches of wisdom," but were a demonstration of the Spirit and power" (1 Cor 2:4). And also: "...and he who marked us with his seal and gave us the Spirit in our hearts as a guarantee" (2 Cor 1:22). And: "He who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to our mortal bodies" (Rom 8:3).

And in turn, writing to Timothy, he tells him that he has preserved the deposit of faith (cf. 2 Tim 4:6-8) "through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us" (Rom 5:5). The Holy Spirit has its own action

33. And that the Holy Spirit has his own subsistence, lives, speaks and announces what is to happen is something that we have already said many times in the things discussed previously. In a penetrating way Paul writes to Timothy: "The Spirit clearly says that in the last times some will apostatize from the faith" (1 Tim 4:1). We see this not only in ancient times, but in the divisions of our times, since heretics teach various errors that take different forms. And he also says: "... which in past generations was not made known to men, as it has now been revealed to his holy apostles and prophets by the Spirit" (Eph 3:5). And in turn: "Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says" (Hebr 3,7), and: "the Holy Spirit also bears witness to us" (Hebr 10,15). He also hails the soldiers of justice saying: “Take also the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God; always in prayer and supplication" (Eph 6:17-18). And again: «Do not make them drunk with wine, which is a cause of debauchery; rather be filled with the Spirit. Recite among yourselves psalms, hymns and inspired songs” (5, 18-19). And finally: "The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with you all." You must accept, therefore, the Holy Spirit
