34. For all of this and for many other things that have not been mentioned, it is strongly recommended that men accept the personal, sanctifying and effectively active force of the Holy Spirit. For I would lack time to speak, if I wanted to continue, of what remains to be said about the Holy Spirit in the fourteen epistles of Saint Paul, in which he taught diversely, completely and piously. But may we be granted the gift of the strength of the Holy Spirit Himself so that we may be dispensed with the things we have overlooked due to lack of time, and may you who are listening be granted a fuller knowledge of what is missing. Those among you who are scholars, learn these things through a more frequent reading of the Holy Scripture, although from the present catechesis and from what we previously discussed you have drawn a firmer faith "in one God the Father almighty and in our Lord Jesus Christ, his only begotten Son; and in the Holy Spirit Paraclete. But this term and the name "Spirit" are adopted very frequently in Scripture—since of the Father it is said: "God is spirit," as it is written in the gospel of John (4:24)—and also of the Son: "The Spirit before our face, Christ the Lord," as the prophet Jeremiah says (Lm 4:20)33. And about the Holy Spirit: "But the Paraclete is the Holy Spirit" (Jn 14:26), as has been said. Therefore, what has been piously perceived in faith also corners the error of Sabellius34. But let's return now to what is urgent and useful to you. He will seal your soul Be careful that it does not happen to you that, like Simon, you approach baptism with pretense, but your heart is not seeking the truth. We must warn you and you must be careful. Blessed are you, if you keep the faith. But if you fall due to infidelity, reject infidelity from this day on and clothe yourself with firm convictions. For when the time of baptism approaches and you go to the bishops or the presbyters or the deacons (grace is granted in all places, both in towns and cities, both by uneducated and learned, by servants and by free, since it is not a grace that comes from men, but is a gift granted by God through men), you approach the one who baptizes, but do not Do not stop your mind on the aspect of the man you see, but remember the Holy Spirit of whom we now speak.

For he is willing to seal your soul and will give you a heavenly and divine sign before which demons tremble, as it is also written: "In him you also, after you... also believed in him, were sealed with the Holy Spirit of Promise" (Eph 1:13). Approach with sincerity to receive the strength of the Spirit

36. But he tests the soul and does not throw the precious stones to the swine (Mt 7:6). If you approach with pretense, men will certainly baptize you, but the Spirit will not baptize you. But if you approach from faith, men will do what corresponds to what is seen with the eyes and the Holy Spirit will grant what is not externally visible. In the space of an hour you approach the exam or the selection of an important army. But if you do not take advantage of that time, an incorrigible evil will befall you. However, if you become worthy of grace, your soul will be illuminated and you will receive a light that you did not have. You will take weapons that are terrible for demons, so that if you do not lose them, you will have a sign in your soul and the demon will not approach you. He will flee in horror, since demons are cast out with the Spirit of God (Mt 12:28).

37. If you believe, you will not only receive forgiveness of sins, but you will also do things greater than human strength. And I hope you are also worthy of the gift of prophecy. As long as you will receive grace to the extent that you can receive it and not to the extent that I say. Well, it may be that I say small things, but you receive greater things, since faith is great in obtaining things. But the Paraclete will be primarily your guardian and defender. The Paraclete will take care of you as his own soldier, of your comings and goings (cf. Ps 121:8) and of those who stalk you. And he will give you the gifts of all kinds of graces, if you do not grieve him for sin. For it is written: "Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, with whom you were sealed for the day of redemption" (Eph 4:30). And what, then, dear ones, is caring for grace? Be prepared to receive it and, once received, do not waste it.

38. And the same God of all things, who spoke in the Holy Spirit through the prophets; who sent it to the apostles on the day of Pentecost in this place where we are, may it also send it to you and may it also protect us through it, granting its good to all of us. In this way, at all times we will produce the fruits of the Holy Spirit: love, joy, peace, patience, gentleness, goodness, faithfulness, meekness, self-control (Gal 5:22-23), in Christ Jesus our Lord. By whom and with whom, together with the Holy Spirit, be glory to the Father now and forever, forever and ever. Amen...

1. This catechesis presents a collection of data about the Holy Spirit in the New Testament, as already indicated, but the development is carried out especially by exposing the action of the Spirit in the different characters of the gospels and in the Acts of the Apostles.
2. It refers, according to the words of I Cor 2:12, to "the graces that God has granted us."
3. On these matters, cf. the cats 6, 7, 8 and 9.

4. Subsistent: the expression refers to the fact that the Holy Spirit has the characteristics of subsistence and Hypostasis (both words mean the same, with the difference that the first comes from Latin (subsistere and sub-stare) and the second from Greek (hypó-stánai). Expressed in simple words, it is as if we were saying that the Holy Spirit has its own consistency, as do the Father and the Son, but it is the own subsistence of each one. which allows us to distinguish them and recognize each one's own personality ("three distinct persons" although related to each other). The theological language of our century (especially in K. Rahner) has frequently spoken of subsistent relationships when referring to persons in God. It is interesting, when speaking of persons in the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, that it necessarily speaks of relationship and not of individuality or isolation: According to this, the concept of a human person must also include this statement: the person is such only in a necessary relationship. In this way, the individual only finds his true fulfillment when he manages to leave his isolated individuality to enter into the person of the other. In reality, the person of Jesus Christ is only understood in relation to the Father and the Holy Spirit.

5. The statement, in the context of Rom 1:3-4, refers in its proper sense to Jesus Christ: "...his Son, born of the lineage of David according to the flesh, constituted the Son of God with power, according to the Spirit of holiness, by his resurrection from the dead." The text, already mentioned above, expresses in an even broader context, Rom 1:1-7, the intimate union of the Son with the Father and the Spirit (cf. also what was said in note 4). Everything, within the framework of salvation through the resurrection and the lordship of Christ (1,4).
6. Literally: "it is subsistent." Vine note 4.
7. Cf. cat. 16, nos. 3 and 6.
8. Cf. cat. 21, no. 1.

9. The approach is clearly Christocentric: what is to be realized in Christians is evident first in Jesus, since the path of the Christian is the one that, as first of all, Jesus has traveled. If the Holy Spirit must descend on each one, it is because he first descended on Jesus (at his baptism and, before that, on Mary at her conception).
10. Jesus, manifested in baptism, is the image and example of what the Christian's journey will be.
11. That is, the words quoted from the Song of Songs would be a prophecy of the manifestation of the Holy Spirit in baptism.

12. Noah's ark, the water, the dove have always been the image of baptism. The first literary expression of this, already in I Pe 3,20-21: «... in the days when Noah was building the Ark,... they were saved through water; "To this now corresponds the baptism that saves them."
13. "At evening," like Noah's dove next to the wood of the ark. It was already afternoon when Jesus died.

14. In fact, in the New Testament, the order of events is as follows: activity and preaching of Jesus, promise of the Holy Spirit (this is especially referred to in this paragraph 11), his death, resurrection at Pentecost, when the fulfillment of the promise of the Spirit takes place. Jn 20:22, however, as indicated at the beginning of para. 12, indicates that on the same day of the Resurrection the apostles already received a communication from the Holy Spirit.
15. In creation, a breath or breath of life.
16. Remember what was said previously about the "descent into hell" after the death and burial of Jesus.

17. It has already been explained that "baptism", "baptized", have to do, etymologically, with "immersion" and "submerged". In the present expressions of Cyril there is a reference to an "immersion" in the Spirit.
18. Teacher of rhetoric or oratory.
19. The entire episode of the tower of Babel, in Gen 11:1-9.
20. Jesus himself uses the image of "new wine", for example, in Mt 9, 17.
21. In the event of Pentecost narrated in Acts 2.
22. The day of Pentecost. That is, Jesus was crucified at the third hour and the coming of the Holy Spirit on Pentecost also took place at the third hour.
23. The text of Acts 5:19 says: "the Angel of the Lord." The expression is generally equivalent, in the Old Testament, to God himself. The entire episode, starting at 5.17.
24. The princes of the priests.
25. "Stephanos" means crown in Greek. Cyril perhaps thinks of the crown of martyrdom. He is the first known Christian martyr.

26. Acts 8:39 says: "The Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away." Although in one of the textual variants it is found: "The Holy Spirit fell on the eunuch, and the Angel of the Lord snatched Philip away."
27. Again "sfragis", seal, with the same sense of the sacramental "character" that was previously explained.

28. Cyril's statement that Paul was in Spain is clear but not very specific. On the interest expressed by Paul in reaching Spain, cf. Rom 15:24. In general, there is not the slightest doubt about the force of the Holy Spirit in the itinerant missionary activity of Paul, who is among the apostles, although he does not belong to the original group of "the Twelve", who perhaps did the most for the universalization of Christianity.

29. The story in Acts 10 shows that inside the cloth "there were all kinds of animals, creeping things of the earth, and birds of the air" (v.12). Peter is invited to eat these animals with the argument that "what God has purified, do not call profane" (v.15). With this, in addition to annulling the distinction between pure and impure foods, it is also symbolically affirmed that there are no pure and impure men. Thus any man, even if he was "gentle", could receive the announcement of the Gospel. This is the meaning of the words of Cyril's catechesis in the present paragraph. Paul was especially the apostle of the Gentiles, but Peter came, through this vision, to the knowledge that salvation in Jesus Christ was intended for men of any people. The end of the episode is the baptism of the first Gentiles, the need for which is evidenced by the descent of the Spirit on those present (vv. 44-48). The entire significant episode occupies entire chapter 10 of Acts and is presented as proof that the Holy Spirit expanded the horizon of the Christian mission.

30. "It seemed to us" is more consistent with both the Greek NT and the Vulgate version. The episode to which this paragraph refers was extremely important (it completes, on the other hand, the meaning, the baptism of the Roman centurion Cornelius and the first Gentiles) since it was about elucidating whether the prior incorporation into Jewish law of those who wanted to become Christians was necessary. The response of the apostles at the Jerusalem assembly was negative. Apart from what this may have meant as approval of Paul's path and his theological conceptions (cf. Gal 2:1-10), it meant the definitive legal disconnection of Christianity from the entire world of Judaism. This freed the new faith from any aspect of ghetto confinement and allowed Christianity to adopt an air of authentic universality.

31. Except for two more epilogue verses, the book of Acts closes, quite sententiously, with Paul's quote from Is 6:9-11, preceded by Acts 28:24-25 (the events referred to take place in Rome): «Some believed because of his words and others, on the other hand, remained incredulous. When they were leaving in disagreement among themselves, Paul said this one thing: "Go find this people and say to them: You will listen well, but you will not understand, you will look well, but you will not see..."» The whole set is made up of Acts 28:24-28. This last verse also includes a rather lapidary phrase from Paul: "Know therefore that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they will hear it." With all this, Paul's drama is the same drama of Jesus, so perfectly described in Matthew and, in another perspective, in John: the rejection by the people who had so anxiously awaited for centuries. But this dramatic development of events also contributed to the universalization of Christianity.

32. Some codices add "consubstantial" here, leaving the phrase "and the Holy Spirit consubstantial", but it is very doubtful that the word is used here in Cyril's original address, since it does not appear in most of the codices. It is, quite probably, a later addition, although it is a correct precision.

33. It is a Christological interpretation of a text whose literality allows it. The Jerusalem Bible, whose version has not been adopted here to better respect Cyril's speech, translates: "Our vital breath, the anointed of Yahweh."

34. That is, since the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit have their own and distinct personality, there is no room to affirm that the three are simply different ways of presenting the one God. CATECHESIS XVIII THE UNIVERSAL RESURRECTION THE CATHOLIC CHURCH ETERNAL LIFE Delivered in Jerusalem, on that of: "And in the Church, one, holy and catholic." And about the "resurrection of the flesh." And "eternal life." The reading is from Ezekiel: «The hand of Yahweh was on me and, by his spirit, Yahweh took me out and put me in the middle of the plain, which was full of bones...'' (Ez 37, I ss.)1. The resurrection of the dead, a source of hope

1. The root of every operation is the hope of the resurrection. For the hope of the prize gives the soul strength to undertake good works. For the worker is willing to endure the work if he sees the reward for his efforts, but the spirit and body of those who do not see any reward collapse. A soldier who expects the reward of combat is ready to fight, but no one militates in favor of a king who, lacking judgment, does not reward the merit of efforts, nor is he willing to face death for that same king. Likewise, every soul that believes in the resurrection moderates and tempers itself. But she who does not believe in the resurrection gives herself over to her own perdition2. Whoever believes that the body will survive with the resurrection, takes care of what serves as a stole and clothing, and does not contaminate it with debauchery. But he who does not believe in the resurrection, gives himself over to fornication, using his own body as if it were another's. It is, of course, an important doctrine and teaching of the Church to believe in the great resurrection of the dead. This is something completely essential, whose truth, although it really clashes with the contradiction of many, can be fully proven. The Greeks are against it, the Samaritans do not believe it and the heretics destroy it. It is contradicted in multiple ways, but it is a simple and straightforward truth. Objections against the resurrection of the dead

2. This is what both the Greeks and the Samaritans oppose: once a man has perished and died, he rots and is devoured by worms. The same worms also die. And after all this has happened to the body, putrefaction and death, how then is it resurrected? Fish devour those who have suffered a shipwreck and they, in turn, are devoured by others. They eat those who fight with wild beasts, destroying them, even the bones. Vultures and crows are flying everywhere eating the flesh of the corpses thrown to the ground. How can these bodies be reunited? For it is possible that, of the birds that devoured them, one died in India, another in Persia, another in barbarian countries. The corpses of others that burned in the flames, reduced to ashes were scattered by storms or wind. How will his body be reunited? Everything is possible to God

3. For you, of course, little and weak man, the barbarian countries are far from India and Hispania is far from Persia. But for God, who has the entire world in his fist, everything is close. Do not think that God is as weak as you and therefore incapable, but rather think of your own power. Furthermore, the sun, being a small work of God, fills the entire earth with the heat of its rays. Also the air, made by God, surrounds everything in the world. But God, who is the creator of the sun and the air, is he perhaps far from the world? Suppose that various grains of seeds are mixed together—I propose weak examples to you, who are weak in faith—and suppose that you have them all in one fist. For you, who are a man, is it difficult, or rather easy, for you to distinguish what you have in your fist and put each of the seeds with those of its kind? That is, if you can discern what you have in your hand, can't God discern and restore to its place what he has in his? Consider what I say and whether perhaps it will not be impious to deny it. In the resurrection of the dead, God will do justice

4. Consider also what concerns justice and reflect on yourself. You have various servants, some of whom are good and others evil. You appreciate the good ones and you punish the bad ones. Even if you are a judge, you praise the good and punish the evil. If you, who are a mortal man, have a notion of what is just, will not God, eternal king of all things, repay each person according to justice? And it is impious to deny this, because look what I say: many murderers died in bed without having been punished. Where then is the justice of God? And often a murderer is guilty of fifty murders, but has washed away his crimes with a single capital punishment. How will he pay, then, for the remaining forty-nine murders? And you accuse God of injustice if judgment and retribution do not exist after this life. But you should not be surprised by the delay in the trial. Whoever fights in a contest, once it has concluded, receives the crown or is marked by shame, but the referee of the contest never crowns those who intervene while they are fighting, but waits to see the end of all the combatants. Then, examining the result, he distributes the victory prizes and crowns. In the same way, God, while the fight still lasts in this world, partially helps the subjects, but then grants them the rewards completely and fully. Other signs of the resurrection

5. But if, in your opinion, the resurrection of the dead does not exist, what are you doing condemning those who dig up tombs? For if the body perishes irretrievably and there is no hope of resurrection, why are tomb desecrators punished? You realize, even if you deny it with your lips, that an indelible awareness of the resurrection remains within you. Changes observed in inferior beings make the resurrection credible

6. But, for the rest, a cut tree sprouts again. Will not a man who has lost his life do the same? Even what has been cut when mowing remains on the threshing floors to be collected. And shall not the man who has been reaped in this world remain on the threshing floor?3. Also the vine shoots and the branches of other trees, when cut completely and transplanted, come to life and bear fruit. And man, for whom those things are, will he not rise again even though he has gone to earth? And if we compare different works or difficulties, what is more, giving shape from the beginning to a statue that did not exist before or restoring it to one that had lost it? The God who made us from nothing, once we already had existence but then lost it, will not be able to awaken us to life again? But you do not believe, because it is Greek, what is written about the resurrection. Instead, consider these things from the perspective of what already exists and understand it within yourself from what can be seen to this day. If desired, wheat or any kind of seed is sown. When the seed falls, it dies and rots: it is no longer useful for food. But what has rotted sprouts from there like grass and what was small when it fell now rises up very beautiful. But the wheat was created for our sake, since the wheat and other seeds were made not for themselves but for our use. And if the things that were made for us come to life after death, will we not, for whom those things were made, come to life after death?

7. It is, as you see, winter time. The trees are like dead. Where are the leaves of the fig tree? Where are the grapes on the vine? But these things that are dead in winter, even then they have their strength and, when the time comes, the force of life will be returned to them, as if awakened from death. God, perceiving your infidelity, has shown you the resurrection every year in these clear signs so that, seeing what happens in inanimate beings, you would believe regarding beings endowed with reason. Apart from this, flies and bees, often drowned in water, revive after a while and certain species of toads remain immobile in winter, but later, in summer, they wake up. To you, who think small and worthless things, these examples are presented to you. Now, he who, beyond what is natural, gives life to beings devoid of reason and despicable, will he not give the same to us, for whom he made all these beings? The supposed example of the Phoenix bird

8. But the Greeks still seek a clearer resurrection of the dead and argue that, although it is true that the mentioned beings revive, it is because in reality they had not fully suffered putrefaction and they wish to openly see an animal that has completely rotted and has been resurrected. God already knew this obstinacy of men to not believe and for this purpose he provided the bird they call the Phoenix. This, as Clement5 writes and many others know, is unique of its kind, it reaches the country of the Egyptians every four hundred years and is an example of resurrection. And it does not do it in deserted places, so that it would remain something mysterious, but in a famous city, making itself visible so that it can be touched with your hands, because otherwise no one would believe it. Well, after having built the nest with incense, myrrh and other aromas, entering it once its quota of years has been exhausted, it dies in the sight of everyone and becomes corrupted. But later, a worm sprouts from the rotting flesh of the dead bird and, as it grows, it transforms into a bird7. Afterwards, this Phoenix grows feathers. Once this Phoenix has been remade as it was previously, it flies through the air as it was before dying, clearly showing men the resurrection of the dead. The Phoenix is ​​certainly admirable, but, as a bird, it is devoid of reason and has never sung psalms to God. He has never known who the Only Begotten Son of God is. But if the resurrection was granted to an irrational animal, which does not know its own creator, will it not be granted to us, who glorify God and keep his precepts? He who created man from a humble reality can also bring him back to life

9. But since the sign of the Phoenix bird, even if we look for it a lot, is rare and they still don't give it credit, it receives another test based on the things you see every day. A hundred or two hundred years ago, where were all of us, both those who speak and those who listen? Do we not know how our bodies were formed? Don't you know how we are generated from a weak, formless and simple matter? The living man is formed from a single species and from a weak principle. And that which has no strength and is weak is transformed into compact flesh and the strength of the nerves. And also in the clarity of the eyes, in the ability of the nose to smell, in the hearing capacity of the ears, the tongue that speaks, the heart that moves, the ability of the hands to work, the agility of the feet and all the variety of members of different genders. And what is so little and weak becomes a builder of ships, a bricklayer, an architect and an operator of any art, a soldier, a prince, a legislator or a king. Will the God who made us from humble beginnings not be able to lift us up once we have fallen? Could he who gave body to such a vile reality not be able to awaken a dead body again? Will he who made what did not exist not awaken to what exists, even though he has perished? The similarity with the phases of the moon8

10. A manifest reason for the resurrection of the dead, and which is attested every month, take it also from the sky and the stars. In fact, the moon, which becomes completely absent, so that nothing is seen of it, appears new again and is restored to its old dimensions. And for a perfect demonstration of this same matter, the moon melts over the years into blood, but then regains its luminous appearance. God is the one who, in his providence, prepares these things so that you too, who are man and have blood inside you, do not deny your faith in the resurrection of the dead. So what you see on the moon, you believe will also happen in you. So use these words against the Greeks. For against those who do not accept the Scriptures you must fight with weapons not taken from the Scriptures, that is, only with reasoning and demonstrations. Well, it has not been discovered to these who Moses is or who Isaiah is, and they do not know the Gospels or Paul. Faced with the Samaritans: the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob is not a God of the dead, but of the living

11. Turn now, I beg you, to the Samaritans, who, since they only accept the Law, do not accept the prophets, the reading from which we have started, from Ezekiel, may be ineffective, since, as I said, there is no place for prophets in them. Where then shall we seek faith for the Samaritans? Let's go to the books of the Law. God then says to Moses: "I am... the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob" (Ex 3:6), who undoubtedly live and exist9. Well, if Abraham died, and so did Isaac and Jacob, this is a God who does not exist. And since when is it said that a king is king of soldiers he does not have? And who is he who shows off wealth that he does not possess? It is necessary, therefore, that Abraham, Isaac and Jacob exist so that the God of things that exist is god. For he did not say: I was their God, but I am. And Abraham says that there is a judgment, referring to the Lord: "Is the judge of the whole earth going to rule on an injustice?" (Gen 18:25). The signs of God's power in Aaron, Moses and Lot's wife

12. But the foolish people of Samaria also say against this: nothing prevents the souls of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob from continuing to live, but the dead cannot be resurrected. It is as if he were saying: it was possible for the rod of the righteous Moses to become a snake (Ex 4:3), but the bodies of the righteous will not be able to live and be resurrected. And that was done outside the laws of nature. Can this not be done, which is so in accordance with nature? Also Aaron's rod, cut and dried, flourished without contact with the waters (Num 17:23) and, although it was under cover (17:22), it produced the buds that usually sprout in the fields and, in an arid place as it was, it produced in the space of one night the fruits that frequently watered trees produce after many years. With Aaron's rod it was as if he were resurrected from the dead. Will not Aaron himself be resurrected then? To preserve the high priesthood for him, God performed the miracle on his rod. Will he not then grant the resurrection to Aaron himself? Also, by unnatural procedures, the woman was turned into salt and her flesh was transformed into salt (Gen 19:26). Can't meat simply become meat? And if Lot's wife was turned into a pillar of salt, will not Abraham's wife be resurrected? By virtue of which the hand of Moses became like snow, during the time of one hour, and was then established in its previous state? (cf. Ex 4, or-7)? Without a doubt by the power of God. And has this power, once effective, already lost its strength and effectiveness? The resurrection is possible as the creation was possible

13. Of what material was man made in the beginning, O Samaritans, the most foolish of all men? Come to the first book of Scripture, for you too have received it: "Then Yahweh God formed man of dust from the ground" (Gen 2:7). Dust becomes flesh, and will flesh not become flesh again? Should they be explained where the heavens, the earth and the seas come from? Where do the sun, the moon and the stars come from? How do birds and fish come from the waters? And the way all animals come from the earth? So many thousands of beings have been brought from nothing to existence. And we men, who bear the image imprinted, will we not be resurrected? Truly this whole matter brims with disbelief. And there are many reasons to condemn those who reject the faith, since Abraham says of God that he is "judge of the whole earth" (Gen 18:25). And it is serious that those who learn the law do not believe, since it is written there that man was formed from the earth (Gen 2:7; 3:19): it is those who read there who refuse to believe. There are no biblical arguments against the resurrection

14. And we say these things in front of those who are to be counted among the unbelievers. But for those of us who believe it is appropriate to refer to the prophets. Some, however, who use the prophets, do not believe in what they have written and claim that "the wicked will not stand up in the Judgment" (Ps 1:5)10. Or also that other thing: "He who goes down to Sheol does not go up again" (Job 7,9). Or even: "The dead do not praise Yahweh" (Ps 115:17). In doing so, they misuse what has been correctly written. Without dwelling too long and to the extent we can, it will be good to face them now. For if it is said that "the wicked will not rise in the Judgment," this means not that they will be resurrected "in the judgment," but that they will do so in condemnation. God, in fact, does not need to make many inquiries, but as the wicked are resurrected, their punishments will follow. And if it is said "the dead do not praise Yahweh", this means that in this life a space of penitence and forgiveness is created. Once death has occurred, those who have died in sin will no longer be allowed to praise, but simply to mourn. For praise belongs to those who give thanks, but lamentations belong to those who suffer stripes. Therefore, the righteous will praise, but those who have died in their sins will no longer have time to glorify God. Job and the prophets also mention it

15. Regarding the context of the words "he who goes down to Sheol does not go up again" (Job 7:9), observe what follows, for it is said: "He does not return to his house again, he does not see his place again" (7:10). For as the whole world must perish, every house must also be destroyed. How will he return to his house if the whole earth is to be made new? It would be good for you to listen to Job when he says: “One hope guards the tree: if it is cut down, it can still sprout, and it will not fail to put forth shoots. Even with aged roots in the ground, with a trunk that dies in the dust, as soon as it feels the water, it reflowers and sends out branches like a young plant. But the man who dies remains inert, when a human expires, where is he? (14,7-10). It is as if he were making someone blush and scolding them, because that is how the question "where is he?" is to be interpreted. For he says that since the tree perishes and is resurrected, will not man, for whom the trees were made, be resurrected? And so that you do not think that the text is violent, read what follows, where with questions it is asked: "Once a man is dead, can he revive?" (Job 14:14) and says: "Even if a man has died, he will live" (14:14 LXX), and immediately adds: "All the days of my warfare I would wait, until my replacement comes" and, in turn, in another place: "that my skin must lift above the earth, that it endures these fatigues" (Job 19:25-26)11. And the prophet Isaiah says: "Your dead will revive, your corpses will rise" (Is 26:19). And very clearly the prophet we have now mentioned, Ezekiel, says: “Behold, I open your tombs; I will bring them out of your graves” (Ez 27:12). And Daniel says: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awaken, some to eternal life, others to shame, to eternal horror" (Dan 12:2). Resurrections of the dead in the New Testament, in Elijah and Elisha

16. Many other passages of Scripture also testify to the resurrection of the dead. There are many other sentences and sayings about this matter. But now, as if to refresh our memory, we mention only in passing the resurrection of Lazarus four days after his death (Jn 11:39-44). Also in passing, due to the lack of time, the widow's resurrected son (Luke 7:11-16). And, without insisting, we also remember the daughter of the head of the synagogue (Mt 9:25). Remember also that the slabs were opened and many bodies of saints who had died were resurrected (Mt 27:51-53) when the tombs were opened12. But let it be remembered, first of all, that Christ rose from the dead. I have overlooked Elijah and the widow's son whom he raised from the dead (I Kings 17:19 ff.), and Elisha, who on several occasions performed similar miracles (2 Kings 4:8 ff. 38 ff.), both alive and after death. While he was alive, he brought about the resurrection by his own spirit, so that not only would the souls of the righteous be honored, but there would be faith that a deep strength existed in the bodies of the righteous. On the occasion of a corpse being placed in Elisha's tomb, the dead man, upon contact with the dead body of the prophet, came to life (2 Kings 13:21). The dead body of the prophet did what seemed proper to his soul and what lay dead gave life to a dead man: what was giving life, that same thing remained, just as before, among the dead. For what reason?: so that, if Elisha had been resurrected, the fact would not be attributed only to his soul and to show that, even when the soul was absent, there existed a certain strength and power in the body of the saints due to the just soul that had lived in it for so many years and had made use of it13. And let us not deny our faith to this fact as if it had not existed, because if the handkerchiefs and aprons, which are something external to the person, applied to the bodies of the sick, gave strength to the weak (Acts 19:12), how much more would the body of the prophet not resurrect a dead person? Resurrections in the NT. Resurrection at the end of time

17. Many other things would have to be said about this if we studied the astonishing nature of these facts according to each of their details, but they are supporting the effort of fasting in preparation for Easter and the Vigil14. Therefore, only a few things will be said above, because, by throwing a few seeds and receiving them as the good soil that you are, you will report fruit by expanding it on your own. Let it be remembered that the apostles were also raised from the dead: Peter, in Joppa, to Tabitha (Acts 9:36-42); Paul, in Troas, to Eutychus (20:7-12), and also the other apostles, although what each of them did prodigiously is not recorded in writing. Remember everything that was said in the First Epistle to the Corinthians and that Paul wrote against those who said: “How are the dead raised? With what body do they come back to life? (15.35). And of what he says: "If the dead are not raised, neither was Christ raised" (15:16). And that he calls fools (15:36) those who do not believe it and of everything that is explained in that place15 about the resurrection of the dead and of what he wrote in this vein to the Thessalonians: "Brothers, we do not want you to be in ignorance regarding the dead, so that you grieve for them like the rest, who have no hope" (I Thes 4:13), and everything that follows but, above all, that of “those who died in Christ will rise first” (4:16). The final greatness of the resurrected state

18. Observe mainly what Paul says as if pointing his finger: “This corruptible being must put on incorruptibility; and may this mortal being clothe himself with immortality” (I Cor 15:53). For this same body will be resurrected, not as it is, weak, but enduring, although it will be the same body. But it will be transformed, clothed in incorruptibility: as iron introduced into fire becomes fire or, rather, as it is known by the one who moves it, God. Therefore this same body will be resurrected, but it will not remain as it is now, but will endure forever. He will no longer need to live on the food that we use, nor on stairs to climb, since he will become "spiritual" (1 Cor 15:44)16, something admirable and whose dignity we are not able to sufficiently explain. "Then the righteous," he says, "will shine like the sun and the moon and like the brightness of the firmament" (cf. Dan 12:3 and Mt 13:43). God, who previously knows men's difficulty in believing, had already granted tiny worms that in summer they would emit luminous rays from their bodies, so that what is seen could be believed in what is expected. And of course, he who granted a part could also grant the whole. And he who made a worm shine with light, much more will he make the righteous man shine. The body will also participate in the glory or the punishment. We will resurrect, therefore, all having eternal bodies, but not all similar: if someone is just, he will receive a celestial body so that he can freely deal with the angels; But if someone is a sinner, he will receive an eternal body capable of suffering the punishment of his sins so that, burning in eternal fire, he will never be consumed. And both things are well done by God. Well, we do nothing without the body. We blaspheme with the mouth, and with the mouth we pray; we fornicate through the body, and also through the body we maintain purity; We steal with the hand, and with the hand we give alms. And likewise everything else. If the body has served for everything, it must also be a participant in the fate that will befall us in the future. Use the body correctly

20. Let us, therefore, mortify the bodies and not abuse them as if they belonged to others. Let us not say, in agreement with the heretics, that this clothing of the body is another's, but let us respect it as our own, since we must give an account to God for all the things we do with the body. Do not say: "No one sees me" (Sir 23:26) nor think that there is no witness of what you do. In fact, most of the time there is no man to witness it. But there is a witness who formed us and who does not err, and remains faithful in heaven (cf. Ps 89:38) seeing what is done. The stains of sins also remain on the body. And just as, when there has been a sore on the body, a scar remains even if some medicine has been applied, in the same way sin leaves a mark on the soul and the body and the traces of the scars remain in both. They are only suppressed by those who receive the washing17. Through baptism, God also heals the wounds of the soul and body, but let us protect ourselves in a general way against what happens to us in the future and keep this garment of the body clean and let us not lose the salvation of heaven for the slightest fornication and lasciviousness or for any other sin. Let us instead draw closer to the inheritance of the eternal kingdom of God, of which God makes everyone worthy by his grace. The resurrection of the dead is well recorded

21. Let what has been said be sufficient to demonstrate the resurrection of the dead. And the profession of faith, which we have repeated to you again, make it with all diligence and with the same words, so that it is recorded in your memory18. We will talk about the Church, one, holy and catholic

22. The Profession of Faith also contains this: <<And in a baptism of conversion for the forgiveness of sins. And in the Church, one, holy and catholic. And in the resurrection of the flesh. And in eternal life>> We already spoke about baptism and penance in previous catechesis. What we have just said about the resurrection of the dead is because of "and in the resurrection of the body." We will speak, then, of what remains to us, about "And in the Church, one, holy and catholic", in which, although many things can be said, we will be brief. The Church is Catholic, Universal, in everything

23. It is called "Catholic" because it is spread throughout the world from one end of the earth to another and since it teaches completely, and without anything missing, all the dogmas that men should know about things visible and invisible, heavenly and earthly. And also because it has subjected all kinds of men, princes and common men, learned and inexperienced, to righteous worship. And finally because it heals and cures all kinds of sins that are committed with the soul and body. She (the Church) possesses every kind of virtue, whatever its name, in deeds and words and in spiritual gifts of any kind. "Church" is "assembly"

24. "Church" is a very appropriate name because it summons everyone and gathers them together19, as the Lord says in Leviticus: "Gather the entire community at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting" (Lev 8:3). It is noteworthy that this word “ekklesíason”20 is used in Scripture for the first time in this place, when the Lord grants Aaron the high priesthood. And in Deuteronomy God says to Moses: "Gather the people so that I may make them hear my words so that they may learn to fear me" (Dt 9:10). And when he speaks of the tables21: "... in which were all the words that Yahweh had spoken to them from the middle of the fire, on the mountain, on the day of the Assembly" (Dt 9,10), as if he were saying it more clearly. On the day when, called by God, you were gathered together. The Psalmist also says: "I will give thanks to you in the great assembly, I will praise you among a multitude of people" (Ps 35:18). The true Church-assembly has become that of the Gentiles

25. The psalmist had already sung before: «In the assemblies22 bless God, the Lord from the springs of Israel (Ps 68,27 LXX). But, if it had to be this way, because of the schemes plotted against the Savior, the Jews were deprived of grace and God built a second Church, formed from the Gentiles, our holy Church of Christians, about which he said to Peter: "And on this rock I will build my Church and the gates of hell will not prevail against it" (Mt 16:8). David spoke of both Churches in open prophecy: of the first, which was rejected ("I hate the assembly of evildoers", Ps 26:5). Of the second he says, in the same psalm, that it was built: "I love, Yahweh, the beauty of your house" (26,8) and, a little later, in the same psalm: "I will bless you, Yahweh in the assemblies" (26,12). Therefore, that which was in the land of the Jews was rejected. But throughout the world the Churches of Christ are multiplying, of which it is written in the Psalms: "Sing to Yahweh a new song: his praise in the assembly of his friends!" (Ps 149,1). Accordingly the prophet said to the Jews: "I have no pleasure in you, says Yahweh of hosts" (Mal 1:10). And he immediately adds: "For from the rising sun to the setting sun, great is my name among the nations" (1:11). And of this same holy Catholic Church Paul writes to Timothy: "... so that you may know how to behave in the house of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth" (I Tim 3:15). Harshly distinguish the Catholic Church

26. But the name "Church" adapts to different realities, so that also of the crowd that was in the theater of the Ephesians it is written: "Having said this, he dissolved the assembly" (Acts 19:40). Someone also intentionally said that the "assembly of evildoers" (Ps 26:5) is the group of heretics: I am referring to the Marcionites, Manichaeans and the rest. Therefore, faith very cautiously shows you that this is what you must maintain: "And in the Church, a holy, Catholic one," so that, fleeing from those abominable groups, you always adhere to the holy Catholic Church, in which you were born again. And if you ever travel through different cities, do not simply ask where the "Kyriakón"23 is, since the other sects and heresies of the impious also strive to make their lairs presentable with the name of "Kyriakón", nor simply where the church is, but where there is a Catholic church, since this is the proper name of this holy Church, mother of us all. She is certainly the wife of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Only Begotten Son of God (for it is written: "as Christ loved the Church and gave himself up for her", etc., Eph 5:25 ff.) and offers an image and an imitation of "the Jerusalem above", which "is free; that is our mother” (Gal 4:26). Having previously been barren, she is now the mother of a numerous offspring (cf. Gal 4:27 and Is 54:1). Extended without borders by the patience of the martyrs

27. Having repudiated the first24, in the second, that is, in the Catholic Church, as Paul says, God appointed some as apostles; secondly as prophets; thirdly as teachers; then the miracles; then the gift of healing, assistance, government, diversity of languages” (I Cor 12:28) and all kinds of any virtue. I am referring to wisdom and intelligence, temperance and justice, mercy and humanity, and invincible patience in persecution. It was this, "by the weapons of justice, those of the right and those of the left, in glory and ignominy" (2 Cor 6:7-8), which redeemed, in the first place, the holy martyrs in their persecutions and anguish with diverse crowns, united together by the numerous flowers of suffering. Now, in times of peace, that suffering receives, by the grace of God and at the hand of kings and men conspicuous for the greatness of their dignity, the honors that even men of any lineage and appearance owe it. And while the power of the sovereigns of peoples distributed in diverse places has certain borders, only the holy Catholic Church has power without borders throughout the world. For, as it is written, God put peace at its end (Ps 147:14). But if I wanted to say everything on this matter, I would need a speech of many hours. "And in eternal life"

28. Educated in this holy Catholic Church by precepts and illustrious customs, we will possess the Kingdom of heaven and obtain eternal life as an inheritance. Therefore we endure all things so that the Lord may grant them to us. For the goal we have set for ourselves does not consist of limited things, but rather the achievement of eternal life, and this is our struggle. That is why we are taught in the confession of faith that, after the resurrection of the body, that is, of the dead, we also believe in eternal life, for which Christians are fighting.

29. Therefore, the Father is really and truly life, and through the Son he pours out to all, as from a fountain, and in the Holy Spirit, the heavenly gifts. Because of his kindness, the gifts of eternal life have also been truthfully promised to us men. And this cannot be denied, as if it were something impossible, faith: we must believe, not looking at our weakness, but in attention to his power: "With God all things are possible" (Mt 19:26). Daniel says that this is possible and that we hope for eternal life: "Those who taught the multitude righteousness (shall shine) like the stars for all eternity" (Dan 12:3). And Paul says: "And so we will always be with the Lord" (1 Thes 4:17). This "always being with the Lord" designates eternal life. The Savior also says it very clearly in the gospels: "And these will go to eternal punishment, and the righteous to eternal life" (Mt 25:46). Achieving eternal life by doing good

30. There are many proofs that can be given about eternal life. And for those of us who wish to obtain it, the Holy Scripture shows us the ways to acquire it. We will now adduce some testimonies from them, few due to the already prolix nature of my words, leaving the rest of what can be investigated to scholars. Well, sometimes they say that it is obtained by faith, since it is written: "He who believes in the Son has eternal life" (Jn 3:36). And this same25 says: "Truly, truly, I say to you, he who hears my Word and believes in him who sent me has eternal life" (5:24), in addition to what follows. But other times they say that it is obtained by the preaching of the Gospel, since it says: "The reaper receives the wages, and gathers fruit for eternal life, so that the sower rejoices just as the reaper" (4:36). It is also sometimes said that by the martyrdom and confession of Christ. He says, in effect: "He who hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life" (12:25). And also putting Christ before money and kinship of any kind: "Everyone who has left houses, brothers, sisters... will inherit eternal life" (Mt 19:29). And for the observance of the commandments: "You shall not kill, you shall not commit adultery,..." (19:18), as he responded to that man who approached and said: "Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?" (19,16). But, furthermore, turning away from evil works and dedicating yourself to the service of God, for Paul says: «Now, free from sin and slaves of God, you bear fruit for holiness; and the end, eternal life” (Rom 6:22).

31. There are other ways to achieve eternal life, but I have overlooked them so as not to be so abundant. Since God loves men so intensely, he has not opened one but multiple doors to the entrance to eternal life so that everyone, as long as it is on their side, can enjoy it without any impediment. Meanwhile we have briefly said these things about eternal life. They are what ultimately must be taught about faith and are its end. Hopefully all of us, those who instruct them and those who listen, will achieve it by the grace of God. There will be a preparation for the Easter ceremonies

32. Furthermore, beloved brothers, speaking of these commands exhorts all of you to prepare your soul for the reception of heavenly gifts. We have spoken to you about the holy and apostolic faith, as much as has been permitted to us and by the grace of God, in these past days of Lent. It is not that only these things could have been said, since we have overlooked many others that perhaps by better teachers would have been thought in a more sublime way. But since the day of Easter is already there, in which your charity will be illuminated in Christ by the washing of regeneration, you will be instructed, God willing, in the things that are appropriate26: with how much piety and in what order it is advisable to enter once you are called, for what reason each of the holy mysteries of baptism is celebrated and with how much reverence and order one must go from (the place of) baptism to the holy altar of God to enjoy the spiritual mysteries and heavenly powers that are distributed there27, so that, by the previous illumination of your soul by this word of doctrine, you will know through each of these details the greatness of the gifts that God has granted you. There will be mystagogical catechisms during Easter week

33. But after the holy and healthy day of Easter, beginning on the second day after Saturday28, you will enter, immediately after the liturgical assembly, into the holy place of the resurrection to hear, God willing, other catechisms29, in which you will also be instructed in the reasons and causes of each of the things carried out. You will also receive the reasons from both the Old and the New Testament: first of all, about what was said immediately before baptism, but, furthermore, how you were purified from sins by the Lord through the washing of water with the word30 and in what way, like the priests, you were made partakers of the name of "Christ"31. Or also how they have been given the sign of the communication of the Holy Spirit32. And also about the mysteries of the new Alliance, which took their beginning here33: what the Holy Scripture has transmitted to us about them and what their strength and power consist of34. And how to approach them and when and how to celebrate them. And last of all, why must you in the future live and maintain yourselves, both in words and deeds, in a manner worthy of the grace received, so that all of you can enjoy eternal life35. and these things, if it is God's will, we will explain them to them. The joy of the Church because the number of its children will grow

34. «Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord; I repeat to you, be joyful" (cf. Phil 3:1; 4:4), because "your liberation is drawing near" (Lk 21:28) and the heavenly army of angels awaits your salvation. And now we hear "the voice of him crying in the desert: 'Prepare the way of the Lord'" (Mt 3:3). But the prophet cries out: "Thirst, come to the water" (Is 55:1), and immediately, in what follows: "Listen to me and eat good things, and you will enjoy something substantial" (55:2). And not long after you will hear that extraordinary passage: "Shinden, shine, Jerusalem, for your light has come" (Is 60:1 LXX). Of this Jerusalem the prophet said: "After which you will be called the City of Justice, the faithful metropolis of Zion" (1:26 LXX) because of the Law that came from Zion and the word of the Lord that originated from Jerusalem (cf. 2:3). From here it watered the entire world like rain. The prophet also says to her about you: "Lift up your eyes and see: they have all gathered together and have come to you" (49:18). And she responds saying: "Who are these that fly like a cloud, like doves to their dovecotes?" (40.8): clouds for the spiritual and doves for simplicity. And in turn: «Who heard such? Who saw such a thing? Is a country given birth in a single day? Or is a town born all at once? Well, Zion was in pain and gave birth to her children” (66:8). All things will be filled with unspeakable joy through the Lord, who says: "I will make Jerusalem an exultation and my people a joy." May God give you joy, bless you and help you

35. May it also be said of you now: "Hail, heavens, and exult, earth!..., for Yahweh has comforted his people and has had compassion on his poor" (Is 49:13). It is because of the goodness of God, who tells them: "I have scattered your transgressions like a cloud, your sins like a cloud" (44:22). And you, honored with the name of faithful and of whom it is said: "A new name will be imposed on those who serve me, which will be blessed on earth" (65:15-16), you will say with joy: "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with all kinds of spiritual blessings, in heaven, in Christ... In him we have through his blood redemption, the forgiveness of crimes, according to the riches of his grace that he has lavished upon us” (Eph 1,3.78), etc. And also: "But God, rich in mercy, because of the great love with which he loved us, when we were dead because of our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ..." (2:4-5). And in the same way praise again the Lord, the author of good things, saying: "When the goodness of God our Savior and his love for men was revealed, he saved us, not because of works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the bath of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit, which he poured out on us generously through Jesus Christ our Savior, so that, justified by his grace, we might be made heirs of eternal life in hope" (Tit 3,4-7). "May the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, grant you the spirit of wisdom and revelation to know Him perfectly, illuminating the eyes of our hearts" (Eph 1:17-18) and keep you at all times in good works, words and thoughts. To him be glory, honor and power through our Lord Jesus Christ, with the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen...

1. This is the last of the catechesis before baptism. At the end, mystagogic catechisms are promised. The resurrection-Catholic Church order is inverse to how both realities are found in the Symbol. But it does not seem that the matter is of greater importance (cf. PG 33, 1,013-1,014). Vine. note 3 below.
2. It refers to the fact that it lacks a stimulus to do good.

3. Cf. Mt 3:12: "In his hand he has the fork and he is going to cleanse his threshing floor: he will gather his wheat into the barn, but he will burn the chaff with unquenchable fire." Cyril's expression has, in terms of the terms used, a certain similarity to that of Mt, but the evangelist rather refers to the action of Jesus, in his first coming, with respect to men. In general, it is good to keep in mind, with respect to these paragraphs, that, at first, rather than providing the biblical testimony of the resurrection, catechesis aims to oppose the attitude against Greeks and Samaritans by defending its possibility. It is especially between paragraphs 14 and 21 that a more specifically biblical vision of this fundamental hope of the Christian will be offered.
4. Also here the terms are similar to the comparison that Jesus establishes with the grain of wheat in Jn 12:24.
5. CLEMENTE ROMANO, Epistle I to the Corinthians, cap. 25 Madrid 1950 (BAC 65), pp. 249250.

6. The city refers to ancient Heliopolis. But, of course, even if Clement's authoritative quote is made, everything about the Phoenix bird, which burned and later rose from its own ashes, is something purely mythological. The Phoenix was sometimes used by ancient Christians as a symbol - but only a symbol - of the resurrection.

7. Also on this occasion, in parentheses and as a note, Cyril adds: "Do not fail to give credence to this matter, because you also know that the offspring of bees are also formed from worms and you have seen that feathers, bones and nerves emerge from the very soft eggs of birds."

8. Catechesis attempts to establish a parallel between the phases of the moon and the resurrection. More than arguments, we should talk here about examples that facilitate the acceptance of the idea of ​​resurrection. At the end of the paragraph, Cyril points out that what he is trying to do, compared to the Greeks, is not to take arguments taken from Scripture, but rather ones that can be understood from reason. Beginning in paragraph 11 when addressing the Samaritans, he will use passages from the Pentateuch, what they admit from Scripture. The later Samaritans also accepted the book of Joshua.

9. The argument that the patriarchs are alive is used by Jesus himself in favor of the resurrection: "And as for the resurrection of the dead, have you not read those words of God when he said to them: 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob?' from which the Christian affirmation of the resurrection of the dead can be understood.

10. "They will rise." The Greek text of the LXX, the one used by Cyril, also allows the translation "they will rise" (anastésontai) although it should rather be translated as "they will rise" or "they will remain standing."

11. Even more explicit - it is one of the OT texts that are classically adduced about the resurrection or, at least, about life after death - is the Hebrew text of these same verses: «I know that my Defender is alive and that he, the last, will rise above the dust. After my awakening he will lift me up next to him, and with my own flesh I will see God. And v continues. 27: "I, yes, I myself will see him, my eyes will look at him, not anyone else."

12. All the cases of resurrection mentioned are qualitatively different from the resurrection of Jesus, since "Christ, once risen from the dead, dies no more... death no longer has dominion over him" (Rom 6:9) and, therefore, they are also different from the resurrection of all men at the end of time. But they are very useful to show God's ability to raise the dead.

13. It is worth remembering, in any case, that when a saint performs a miracle or it is obtained through his intercession, it is not actually the saint who performs the miracle, but the power of God who uses him as a simple instrument.
14. Fasting is referred to, often lasting several days, during the days of Holy Week and in preparation for the Easter Vigil.
15. 1 Cor 15 is the most extensive passage in the entire Bible on the resurrection of the dead.

16. I Cor 15:42-47: «So also in the resurrection of the dead: corruption is sown, incorruption is raised; 43 Vileness is sown, glory is raised, weakness is sown, strength is raised; 44 a natural body is sown, a spiritual body is resurrected. For if there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body. 45. In fact, this is how Scripture says: The first man, Adam, was made a living soul (Gen. 2:7); the last Adam, spirit that gives life. 46. ​​But it is not the spiritual that appears first, but the natural; then, the spiritual. 47. The first man, coming from the earth, is earthly, the second comes from heaven...». BODY-ESPA/WHAT-IS: The passage shows, first of all, what was pointed out in note 12 that the final resurrection of the dead is something very different from the resurrections carried out by Jesus in the gospels or from the resurrection miracles that are performed in some passages of the book of Acts. In all these cases it is a reestablishment of the type of life that men led. According to the verses cited from I Cor 15, life will have been restored, in said miracles, but in "corruption" (corruptibility), "vileness", "weakness" and "natural body", while the resurrection promised at the end of history is a resurrection promised in incorruption, "glory", "strength", "spiritual body". With respect to the antithesis "natural body" - "spiritual body", the original Greek expressions soma psychikón-soma pneumatikón refer respectively to the human being (which is properly how the word "soma" should be understood here) with his natural life, which is provided by the psyché and, in the resurrection, to the human being, to man, penetrated by the Pneuma, the Spirit of God. That is to say, beyond what had been his own vital forces, which, on the other hand, were also a gift from God when creating him, the resurrected man of the end of time is someone vivified in his reality by the Spirit of God. This is the meaning of the expression “spiritual body” in 1 Cor 15:44.
17. The washing or washing of purification, baptism. Cf. catechesis 1,19 and 20.
18. It seems to exhort a constant profession of faith through repeated recitation of the Symbol.
19. "Ekklesía", from "ek-kalein", call or convene, means convened assembly or even convocation (from the semantic point of view).
20. An adjective derived from ekklesia, used here by Cyril, who takes it from Lev 8,3 LXX to designate the community or assembly.
21. The tables of the Law.
22. Cirilo says "in the Church", adapting it to the topic he is currently developing. 23 Greek expression, derived from Kyrios, Lord, to name an ecclesiastical building or some group of them.

24. The image of "repudiation" is taken from the order that Abraham receives from God to abandon his slave Hagar. In Hagar and in Abraham's true wife, Sarah, Paul sees, in Gal 4:21-31, the image of the historically successive alliances with Israel and the Church. Cyril's catechism is referring to all of this with the aim of allowing listeners to distinguish the characteristics ("notes") of the Church: one, holy, catholic, apostolic.

26. It refers to the practical rules on how to act in the celebration of Easter, which will include baptism, confirmation and the Eucharist, and about the attitudes that must be adopted in said celebration.
27. The distribution of the Eucharist in Communion.
28. That is, in our distribution of the week, Easter Monday.
29. They are the mystagogic catechesis, here collected between XIX and XXIII.

30. SO/EVANGELIZATION: It is perhaps a quote from Eph 5:26, which should begin in the previous verse: "... as Christ loved the Church and gave himself up for her, to sanctify her by bathing in water, by virtue of the word...". Both Eph 5:26 and the text of Cyril to which all this refers seem to mention that in baptism, as in all sacraments, there is a double element: the action performed (in baptism, washing with water) and the words used as a baptismal formula ("I baptize you..."). But perhaps Cyril's words allude to the double reality that the sacraments, in this case baptism, are not simply realities that must be administered without prior work of imparting the Word of evangelization. In fact, the Jerusalem Bible comments on Eph 5:26: "Baptism requires, for its fullness, the accompaniment of the proclamation of the Word, embodied in the evangelization of the minister and the profession of faith of the baptized...". In the case of the baptism of children, the parents and godparents, who "lend" the faith to the child in the name of the Church, must first receive the Gospel in an appropriate way.
31. Since "Christ", as has been pointed out so many times, means "anointed one."
32. In the caT. XXI. It is about Confirmation.
33. In Jerusalem, because here the celebration of the Eucharist began at the Last Supper.
34. The fourth and fifth mystagogic catechesis will be dedicated to the Eucharist.

35. A sixth mystagogic catechesis seems to be promised here, which is certainly not among those that have actually been left to us. PG 33,1.055, note 2, exposes the following assumption: either Cyril could not have pronounced it or, more likely, according to the editor of the catechesis published in PG, the five mystagogic catechesis were pronounced from Monday to Friday, while on Saturday the Sunday Eucharist in albis would have already been celebrated, in which the newly baptized left their white vestments. It would be more than likely that, since it was a Sunday homily, the planned topic would have had to be varied. Abundant moral advice is found, in any case, in the last of the mystagogic catechesis. CATECHESIS XIX (MISTAGOGICAL I) THE MEANING OF THE BAPTISMAL RITES PERFORMED (I) To the newly enlightened. The reading is taken from the first epistle of Peter: "Be sober and be vigilant" (I Kgs 5:8), etc., until the end of the letter. Introduction

1. For some time now, dear brothers and children of the Church, I have wanted to deal with these spiritual and heavenly mysteries. But, aware that faith is greater for what is seen than for what is heard, I have waited for this moment so that, finding you more prepared from what you have already experienced, I can lead you more easily to this meadow of paradise full of light and fragrance. You have already been made capable of these divine mysteries once you have been deemed worthy of the life-giving divine washing. Therefore, when the table at which you are to receive more perfect gifts is to be served to you, you can be sure that we will instruct you in all this with greater care so that you may know the strength and effectiveness that have been worked in you on the eve of baptism. The passage of the Red Sea as a figure of Christian liberation

2. RED-MAR/LBC: First of all, you entered the atrium that is before the baptistery and listened while standing towards the West. You were commanded to extend your hand and you renounced Satan as if he were present. You must know that the figure of this matter is already contained in ancient history: when Pharaoh, a harsh and cruel tyrant, oppressed the free and generous people of the Hebrews, God delegated Moses to take them out of the cruel servitude of the Egyptians. And the door jambs were smeared with the blood of the lamb so that the exterminator would overlook the houses marked by the sign. In a totally miraculous way, the Hebrew people were thus proclaimed free. And when the enemy pursued the liberated ones, the two arms of the sea joining above him, according to what is told in that amazing story, his power quickly sank into the waters of the Red Sea1. The devil has been defeated like Pharaoh was

3. But I must move from the old to the new, from the figure to the true reality. At that time Moses was sent by God to Egypt, while now Christ is sent to the world. That one, to take the oppressed people out of Egypt; Christ, to free those who are oppressed in the world under the weight of sin. Then it was the blood of the lamb that drove away the exterminator, but now it has been the blood of Jesus Christ, the spotless lamb. It has been this blood that has expelled the demons. That tyrant chased those people to the sea. Also, with the same audacity, the prince of demons shamelessly pursued you to the sources of salvation. That one was submerged in the sea, and this one disappears in healthy water. Renunciation of Satan in the baptismal rite

4. BAU/RENUNCIATION-SAS: But you heard that you were commanded to stretch out your hand as towards someone who was present and say: I renounce you, Satan. And I want to explain why you were turned towards the West, because it is necessary that I do so. The reason is that the West is the place where darkness is perceived: its power is in the darkness, being itself the darkness. Therefore, to maintain the reason of what is said in the Symbol, looking towards the west, you renounce the prince of darkness and shadows. What did each of you say while standing?: “I renounce you, Satan, you who are an evil and very cruel tyrant. I no longer fear - you said - your strength: Christ undoes it by making me a partaker of his blood and his flesh so that, through them, he destroys death with his death so that I will not be eternally subject to slavery»2. «I renounce you, clever and most subtle serpent. I renounce you who are the traitor and who, simulating friendship, conceived all iniquity by proposing the fall of our first parents. I renounce you, Satan, author and instrument of all evil. Renounce the works of Satan

5. Then, in the second formula, you are taught to proclaim:... and to all your works. It refers to the works of Satan, to everything that is sin and that needs to be renounced in the same way that, if someone escapes from the tyrant, he also completely rejects his weapons. For every kind of sin is counted among the works of the devil. Know, however, that what you say, especially in the hour of fear, is recorded in writing in the books of God. And if you ever admit anything contrary to them, you will be judged as one who has broken the alliance. You renounce, therefore, the works of Satan, that is, all actions and thoughts that deviate from reason. And to all its pomps. The shows are especially mentioned

6. Then you say:... and in all its pomp. The follies of the theaters, the horse races in the hippodromes, the hunting in the circus and other such vanities are the pomp of the devil, from which the saint, asking to be delivered, exclaims to God: "Take my eyes away from looking at vanities" (/Sal/118/119/037)3. May these vanities not fill your heart with worries when you observe the petulance of comedians, full of gossip and indecency, or when you see dances full of the fury and madness of effeminate men, nor what is seen on the part of those who, in circus hunts, expose themselves to wild beasts by caressing their unfortunate belly, since they themselves become food for merciless wild beasts. To put it more exactly, through the womb, which they recognized as the only God (cf. Phil 3:19), they throw their lives off a precipice with such unusual events. Also stay away from horse races, which are absolutely insane and are a spectacle for indolent spirits. All this is the devil's bubbles. What is sacrificed to idols

7. As the pomp of the devil, what is usually used in the festivals of idols, meats, breads and other such things that have been contaminated by the invocation of impure demons, must also be counted. For the bread and wine of the Eucharist were simple bread and wine before the invocation of the holy and adorable Trinity, but, once the invocation is made, the bread becomes the body and the wine becomes the blood of Christ; In the same way such foods, belonging to the pomp of Satan, being by nature simple and common, by the invocation of demons are profaned and contaminated4. Do not worship Satan

8. Then you say:... and to all your worship. Cult of the devil are the supplications in the temples of idols, which are made in honor of inanimate images: lighting lamps and offering perfumes to fountains or rivers; Just as some, mistaken by their dreams or deceived by demons, approached those waters, believing that they would find medicine for their bodily illnesses. And so on other similar things. Don't mix with such things. Omens, divination, omens, amulets, inscriptions on plaques, the arts of magic and the like, and anything similar to them, are all worship of the devil. Flee, therefore, from all this. For if you succumb to these things after renouncing Satan and after having joined Christ, you will experience a crueler tyrant. He dealt with you familiarly in another time and reduced you to harsh slavery. Now you will have increased it more and, if you are deprived of Christ, you will experience his subjection5. Have you not heard what the old story of Lot and his daughters tells us? (Gen. 19, 15 ff.). Was he not kept unharmed with his daughters when he climbed the mountain while his wife was turned into a pillar of salt as a perennial monument that commemorated twisted affections and a late conversion? Pay attention to yourself and do not look back with the hand of the plow (cf. Luke 9:62) and returning to the bitter taste of the things of this life. Escape, instead, to the mountain (cf. Gen 19:17) which is Jesus Christ, a stone not carved with hands and which filled the entire world (cf. Dan 2:35-45). Profession of faith has been made by turning to the region of light

9. Thus, when you renounce Satan, completely annulling any pact with him and the old alliances with hell, the paradise that God planted in the East is opened to you (Gen 2:8), from which our first father was expelled for violating God's command (Gen 3:23). A symbol of this reality is when you turned from the West to the East, which is the region of light. Then you were commanded to say: "I believe in the Father, and in the Son, and in the Holy Spirit, and in one baptism of conversion." Of all of which, as soon as the grace of God granted it to us, we have already spoken to you at length. Memory of the white garment

10. BAU/WHITE-DRESS: Therefore, keep your vigilance strengthened by these words. As it has been read, "your adversary, the Devil, prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour" (I Pet 5:8)6. In previous times death could enclose them in its dominions, but in the holy washing of regeneration God wiped away "the tears from all faces" (Is 25:8). Once the old man has been stripped away, you will no longer mourn, but will celebrate the festival clothed in the robe of salvation of Jesus Christ (cf. Rom 13:14)7.

11. And this is what was done in the outer court; But, God willing, when in the following mystagogic catechesis we enter the Holy of Holies, we will know the meaning of what is done there. To God the Father be glory, power and splendor with the Son and the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen...

1. The entire story of the passage of the Red Sea, in Ex 14:15 ff. For the passage "on dry foot" of the Israelites and the sinking of the pursuers, cf. 14,22-31. The passage through the Red Sea by Israel is perhaps the central moment of the liberation narrated in the Exodus and which, in the final writing of the second of the books of the Bible, is followed by a triumphant psalm of praise, Ex 15,1 ff. Both the proclamation of the crossing of the Red Sea and the hymn of thanksgiving ("Canticle of Moses") were soon incorporated into the Christian liturgy of the Easter Vigil, understanding, as the catechesis explains, that the crossing of the Red Sea had a value as a "figure" - types is Cyril's expression - of the liberation of those baptized in Christ. This affirms, as continues to be explained in the following paragraphs, that all the realities of the liberation of Israel are "figures" or typos of Christian liberation; especially in this case image of baptism. Cf. 1 Cor 10,1-6. Furthermore, the blood of the lamb used to mark the doors (cf. Ex 12:2123) is a figure of the blood of Christ as the true paschal lamb (cf. I Pet 1:20). Cf. also Apoc 5,9.12; 7.14.

2. Cf. /Hb/02/14-15, which expresses that man's greatest fear is death. Fear of dying is not only fear of physical death, but of all those things that kill man by not being existentially capable of accepting them: failure, illness, loss of economic capacity, risks of various types, etc. The affirmation of the text cited from Hb is that the force of the "lord of death", the Devil, capable of spurring what destroys man, has been destroyed in the death of Christ.

3. Mention is made here and in the next paragraphs of the withdrawal that the early Christians practiced with respect to public spectacles and other "vanities" of the world. The matter is mentioned, for example, in Hippolytus (The Apostolic Tradition, no. 16, regarding professions related to entertainment) or Clement of Alexandria (The Pedagogue, L. III, c. IV: "what to consecrate time").

4. The most appropriate thing, to evaluate this paragraph, is to remember Paul's teaching in 1 Cor 8-10 about the conduct of Christians with respect to meats sacrificed to idols. In itself, this meat that, once slaughtered, could be found in the markets, is nothing more than a normal food that there is no difficulty, from a moral point of view, in consuming. But, in view of the fact that "knowledge puffs up, but love edifies" (I Cor 8:1), Paul explains that the Christian who feels "strong" enough to eat what is sacrificed to idols should not scandalize the "weak" (8:7-13) who think that they are spiritually contaminated by eating such foods. Paul insists on avoiding scandal in 10:23 ff. The theme also reappears in Rom 14:1-15:13. In any case, what is always prohibited to the Christian is participation in the worship of idols, a cult with which he breaks by embracing faith in Christ.
5. All this recalls the warnings of Hebr 6,4 ff.

6. For greater fidelity to the biblical text, "your adversary" is transcribed, not "ours", which is how it appears in the original text of the catechesis. Furthermore, this catechesis has strongly pointed out the power of the Devil, from which the newly baptized have been freed; For this reason, the need for surveillance becomes more expensive.

7. For a more complete description of the newness of life, cf. Rom 13:11-14. The allusion to the "robe" in the last words of the paragraph is probably a mention of the white vestment that was imposed at baptism and that the newly baptized wore in the following days. In any case, it was about highlighting the difference between the old man and the new man. _ CATECHESIS XX (MISTAGOGICAL II) THE MEANING OF THE BAPTISMAL RITES PERFORMED (II) About baptism.
