The reading is from the Letter to the Romans from: «Or do you not know that we who have been baptized into Christ Jesus have been baptized into his death? even the words: "For they are no longer under the Law, but under grace" (Rom. 6:3-14)1.

1. The mystagogics that we have every day, that is, these teachings that explain the mysteries, are useful to us, since they always explain new doctrines and new things. But they are especially useful to you, who have been changed from the old to the new. Along these lines, I will explain to you certain things that derive from yesterday's mystagogy, so that you can learn what symbolizes what you did inside the building. The tunic and the old man

2. Immediately after you entered, you stripped them of their tunic: this was the image of the old man, of whom you had stripped them by their works (cf. Col 2:12ff.; 3:1ff. 9ff.; cf. Eph 2:110). By stripping yourselves, you left them naked, also imitating Christ naked on the cross, who with this nakedness, "once stripped of the Principalities and Powers, exhibited them publicly, incorporating them into his triumphal procession" (Col 2:15). And since the adverse powers lived in their members, it is no longer lawful for them to continue wearing that old tunic: and I am not referring to the one that is perceived with the senses, but to "the old man who is corrupted following the seduction of lust" (Eph 4:22). And may it never happen that the soul puts on again the clothing it once put off, but rather says like that bride of Christ spoken of in the Song of Songs: "I have taken off my tunic, how can I put it on again?" (Song 5,3). Oh admirable reality! Naked you were before everyone's eyes, but you felt no shame. You really bore the image of the first father Adam, who was naked in paradise and was not ashamed. The probaptismal anointing

3. And then, thus stripped, you were anointed with the exorcised oil from the hair of your head to your feet and you were made partakers of the good olive tree that is Jesus Christ. Taken from the wild olive tree, you have been grafted into a good olive tree and made partakers of the wealth of the true olive tree (Rom 11:17-24).2 Therefore, the exorcised oil was a symbol of the communication of the abundance of Christ and quickly puts to flight every vestige of adverse power. For just as the insufflation of the saints3 and the invocation of the name of God burn the demons, like a very strong flame, and put them to flight, so also that oil exorcised by the invocation of God and by prayer acquires such strength that it not only purges, by burning them, the vestiges of sins, but it even makes all the invisible powers of the Evil One flee. The entrances and exits of water, a sign and realization of death and life

4. BAU/MU-BIRTH: Then you were led to the holy pool of divine baptism, as Christ was taken from the cross to the tomb. And they were asked one by one if you believed in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. You pronounced the confession that leads to salvation4, and you were immersed three times in the water, also rising three times. Also in this you signified in image and symbolically the burial of Christ for three days. Well, just as our Savior spent three days and three nights in the bosom of the earth (cf. Mt 12:40 par), you also imitated the first day that Christ spent in the tomb by rising from the water for the first time and, with the immersion, the first night. For just as he who is in the night no longer sees, and he who moves in the day walks in the light, you, when you were immersed, as in the night, ceased to see, but when you came out, you were made as in the day. At the same moment you died and you were born, and that water became a tomb and a mother for you. What Solomon said about other things fits you perfectly; He said: "There is a time to be born, and a time to die" (Eccl 3:2). But for you it is the other way around: time to die and time to be born. And a single time has achieved both, since your birth has coincided with your death. In what sense have we passed through the death, burial and resurrection of Christ

5. BAU/PARTICIPATE-MU-RS: Oh new and unprecedented reality! We have not died or been truly buried, nor were we resurrected after we had been truly crucified, but an imitation of those things has been made in an image, and it is from here that salvation has sprung5. Christ was truly crucified, truly buried, and truly resurrected, and all of this has been given to us by grace so that, made partakers of his sufferings, we may truly obtain salvation. Oh exuberant love towards men! Christ received the nails in his undefiled feet and hands, thus enduring the pain; and now, through the communication in his pains, he is graced to me without having gone through pains or labors. Baptism grants us forgiveness of sins, adoption and participation in the sufferings of Christ

6. Let no one think, therefore, that baptism consists only in the grace of forgiveness of sins and adoption, as was the baptism of John, which conferred only the forgiveness of sins. We, on the contrary, know well that it is for the forgiveness of sins, but it also grants the gift of the Holy Spirit and is the realization7 and expression of the sufferings of Christ. Hence Paul said: "Or do you not know that as many of us as were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? We were, therefore, buried with him by baptism into death” (/Rm/06/03-04). He said this to those who were convinced that baptism certainly granted forgiveness of sins and adoption, but without them having participated, in a certain identification with it, in the true sufferings of Christ. Participators in the death and resurrection of Christ

7. So that we might learn, therefore, that all that Christ endured was for us and for our salvation—and, of course, he did not suffer it only in appearance—and that, furthermore, we are made partakers of his sufferings, Paul exclaimed vividly and forcefully: "For if we have been grafted into him because of the likeness of his death, we will also be partakers of the resurrection" (Rom 6:5). Beautifully it says “grafted”. For truly here the true vine has been planted8 and we, through the communion of baptism into death, have been grafted into it. For in Christ death truly occurred; In him the soul was truly separated from the body, the burial was also true and his holy body was wrapped in a clean sheet (Mt 27:59). All this happened to him in a real way. In you there is a resemblance of his death and his sufferings, although in salvation there is no resemblance but reality.

8. When we have sufficiently instructed you about all this, I ask you to make an effort to retain it in your memory so that I, although unworthy, can say of you: "I praise you because in all things you remember me and preserve the traditions as I handed them down" (I Cor 11:2). Powerful is God who presents you here "as the dead returned to life" (cf. Rom 6:13) to grant you to walk in newness of life (cf. Rom 6:4). To him be glory and power now and forever. Amen...

1. In the previous catechesis, the renunciation of Satan and the profession of faith were recalled, rites performed in the outer court of the temple. In the second mystagogic catechesis, the undressing of the tunic and its meaning, the pre-baptismal anointing, the questioning about faith and the triple immersion and emersion in the baptismal pool are remembered. The meaning of all these rites is explained in detail.

2. Cyril's allusion to the Pauline allegory of the olive tree and the wild olive tree does not express all the richness of the thought of Rom 11:16-24, which is in the context of Rom 9-11. The theme of these chapters of the letter is the "election", first of all, of Israel in the overall plan of the History of salvation and, secondly, after the rejection of Israel, the election of Christians in the Church. Although this second election, that of the Gentiles, does not annul the first election of the Jewish people—Paul points out that the Israelites are "the filial adoption, the glory, the alliances, the legislation, the worship, the promises and the patriarchs" and from them "Christ also proceeds according to the flesh" (Rom. 9:4-5)—the Gentiles are also called to participate in the abundant wealth that is Christ. The mentality of the catechetical action of the ancient Church includes the idea that the catechumen and the Christian have been called and chosen to be a sign to the world of the life that God gives. The newly baptized are now reminded of this reality.
3. Blow into the baptismal rite to drive away the devil. "The saints" probably refers, following the usage already attested since Paul's letters, to baptized Christians.

4. “Saving confession” perhaps responds to what is expressed in Rom 10:9-10: “For if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. For with the heart one believes to obtain justice, and with the mouth one confesses to obtain salvation. "Justification" and "confession" seem, therefore, different aspects of the process of rescue ("redemption") of man. The confession of faith gives special firmness to the salvation initially obtained by justification by which man was already fundamentally freed from sin and made a son of God by adoption.
5. Cf. catechesis 21, no. 2.
6. It was exposed in cat. 4, nos. 10-12.

7. TYPOS/ANTITYPOS: The original expression antitypos is translated as "realization", which is practically, even in Cyril's language, a technical term. In the cat. XIX, no. 2, it was said that the events surrounding the liberation of Israel from the slavery of Egypt were a figure or image, typos of what would be the definitive liberation in Christ. Antitypos of the present paragraph is rather a "counterfigure", that is, an image - insofar as in this case, baptism is a visible and "visible" sign - that at the same time effectively realizes, for those who receive baptism, the death and resurrection of Christ. With this we have the concept of what a sacrament is.

8. The "here" refers to the place of Jesus' tomb, in Jerusalem, where the catechisms are being taught. The image of the graft, on the other hand, is linked here to the allusion to the allegory of the vine and the branches, in which Jesus, according to Jn 15:1, understands himself as "the true vine." CATECHESIS XXI (MISTAGOGICAL III) THE ANOINTING WITH THE CHRISM The anointing with the chrism. The reading is from the First Letter of John, from the words "As for you, you are anointed by the Holy One and know everything" (I Jn 2:20)1 until "let us have full confidence and not be ashamed away from him at his Coming" (2:28). Baptism and gift of the Spirit

1. Baptized into Christ and clothed with Christ (cf. Gal 3:27), you have been conformed to the image of the Son of God (cf. Rom 8:29). The God who predestined us for adoption (cf. Eph 1:5) made us conformed to the glorious body of Christ2. Having become partakers of Christ (cf. Hebr 3:14), you are called, not undeservedly, "Christs."3 God said of you: "Do not touch my anointed" (Ps 105:15). You were made "Christs" by receiving the image4 of the Holy Spirit and all things for you have been made in an image, since you are truly images of Christ. And truly he, once baptized in the Jordan and after communicating the fragrance of the effluvia of his divinity to the waters, came out of them and the Holy Spirit descended to him in a visible form, settling on him as someone who was like him. In a similar way, after you came up from the sacred waters of the pool, you were given the chrism, a made image of the one with whom Christ was anointed: In reality it is the Holy Spirit. The blessed Isaiah also said about him in his prophecy, referring to the person of the Lord: “The Spirit of the Lord Yahweh is upon me, because Yahweh has anointed me. He has sent me to announce the good news to the poor..."5. In the likeness of Christ

2. Christ was not anointed with oil or bodily ointment, but the Father, making him the Savior of the entire universe, anointed him with the Holy Spirit. As Peter says: "God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit" (Acts 10:38); and the prophet David cried out, saying: “Your throne is God's forever and ever; a scepter of equity, the scepter of your kingdom; you love justice and hate impiety. Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of joy more than your companions” (Ps 45:7-8). And just as Christ was truly crucified, buried and resurrected, it is granted to you in baptism, and by divine gift, to be crucified with him, to be buried and to resurrect. And the same thing happens about chrismation: he was anointed with the intelligible oil of joy, that is, with the Holy Spirit6. It is called the oil of joy because it causes spiritual joy; and you have been anointed with ointment by being made partakers of the same lot as Christ. The effectiveness of chrismation

3. CHRISM/UNCTION UNION/CHRISM: But realize that this is not a poor and vile ointment. For just as the bread of the Eucharist, after the invocation of the Holy Spirit, is not common bread but the body of Christ, so also this holy ointment, after the invocation, is no longer a simple ointment nor, so to speak, a common ointment; Christ and the Holy Spirit are given in it, it is the presence of their divinity and effective reality7. And while the body is anointed with visible ointment, the soul is sanctified by the Holy Spirit who gives life. The various anointings and their purpose

4. BAU/ANOINTINGS: You were anointed first on your forehead, to be freed from the shame that the first man who sinned displayed everywhere8 and so that, with open face, you may contemplate the glory of the Lord as in a mirror (cf. 2 Cor 3:18)9. Then, in the ears, so that you could hear the divine mysteries, of which Isaiah said: "Morning after morning my ear awakens, to listen like the disciples" (Is 50:4); and the Lord Jesus, in the Gospel: "He who has ears, let him hear" (Mt 11:15). Then you were anointed in the nose, so that, upon receiving the divine ointment, you would say: "We are to God the good odor of Christ among those who are saved" (2 Cor 2:15). You were also anointed on your chest, so that, “put on righteousness like a breastplate,” you could “resist the wiles of the Devil” (Eph 6:14.11). For, just as Christ, after baptism and the coming to him of the Holy Spirit, defeated the Adversary (cf. Mt 4:1 ff. par), you too, after sacred baptism and the mystical ointment, clothed in the armor of the Holy Spirit, can resist against every adverse power (cf. Eph 6:10-18), which you can overcome by saying: "I can do all things through Him who comforts me", Christ (Phil 4,13). You have received the name of Christians

5. Considered worthy of this holy anointing, you are called Christians, realizing the truth of this name through the new birth. Well, before this grace was conferred on you, you were not properly worthy of this name, but rather you struggled to be Christians. Christ's descendants are also anointed

6. But you must know that the figure of this chrism (or anointing) is already found in the Scripture of the old Covenant. For, when Moses communicated to his brother God's plan to make him high priest, he anointed him after washing him with water (Lev 8:1 ff.) and he was called "Christ"10 because of a chrism or anointing that was a figure. Also when the priest promoted Solomon king, he anointed him after washing him in the Gihon (1 Kings 1,39.45). And this happened to them in figure; but to you, not in figure, but in truth, if indeed you have been anointed by the Holy Spirit. Christ is the beginning of your salvation: he is the firstfruits (1 Cor 15:23), but you reap the harvest: there is no doubt that holiness is also transmitted to the harvest.

7. Keep this chrism uncontaminated. He will instruct you about everything if he remains in you, as you previously heard the blessed John speaking about these things (cf. 1 Jn 2:27) and making various reasonings on this matter11. For this is a holy chrism, spiritual safeguard of the body and healthy custody of the soul. Already from ancient times, the blessed Isaiah prophesied saying: “It will come to pass in future days that the mountain of the House of Yahweh will be set on the top of the mountains and will rise above the hills. All nations will flock to him..." (Is 2:2). He calls the Church a “mountain,” saying that “it will be set on the top of the mountains” and that they will participate in a “feast of good wines” (Is 25:6), anointed with oil12. and, to confirm you further in all this, listen to what he says about this mystical ointment: "Transmit all this to the people: the plan that God has for all nations" (Is 25,7 LXX) 13 Being anointed, therefore, with this holy ointment, keep it in yourselves spotless and blameless, profiting by good works and pleasing the author of your salvation, Christ Jesus, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen...
1. "You know everything" has been preferred to "you all know it", partly because, according to codices, it is a possible reading and because the version used by Cyril is thus respected.

2. Perhaps Cyril somewhat anticipates the expressions of Phil 3:20-21: "But we are citizens of heaven, from where we await the Lord Jesus Christ as Savior, who will transfigure this miserable body of ours into a glorious body like his, by virtue of the power he has to subdue all things to himself."

3. Cf. a similar statement in cat. 18, no. 33; cf. an explanation in no. 6 of this catechesis. The anointing of the Spirit, which in us, as a separate sacrament, constitutes Confirmation, is called in Greek chrisma, "act of anointing" or "chrismation." The name "Christ", from the verbal adjective christós, therefore means Anointed One. Hence "Christian" is one who participates in the same anointing of Christ, whom Acts 10:38, using Is 61, I, qualifies as the one whom God "anointed with the Holy Spirit and with power."
4. Original, "antitypo." Cf. note 7 of the previous catechesis.

5. Is 61,1 ff refers directly, with great probability, to the mission of the prophet, whoever the author, since this paragraph already belongs to Tritoisaias. The present passage is an echo of the songs of the Servant (see especially Is 42,1 ff. 7 ff.; 49,1 ff. 8 ff.; 50,4 ff.) and reaches its full meaning applied to Jesus, in whom the prophetic messianic mission is fulfilled in an eminent way: vid. especially the application that Jesus makes of the text of Isaiah to himself according to Luke 4:16-21.

6. BAU/CHRISMATION: Acts 10:38, especially in its context, has a strong kerygmatic flavor. Peter's speech before the Roman centurion Cornelius, a Gentile upon whom the Holy Spirit descends and is then baptized (Acts 10:44-48), is in practice a description of the being and mission of Jesus: "...how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, and how he went about doing good and healing all those oppressed by the Devil, because God was with him." The anointing with the Holy Spirit that the Father grants to the Christian in the likeness of Christ - the Holy Spirit descends on Jesus also after his baptism in the Jordan, according to the Synoptics - also makes the follower of Christ "active." To the extent that the Christian possesses the anointing of the Holy Spirit - of which Confirmation is a specific sacrament - he can also participate in "doing good" and "healing those oppressed by the Devil."
7. "Effective reality" (energetikón ginómenon, efficiens factum in the excellent Latin version) is an expression of the conception of what a sacrament is as discussed in cat. XX, note
8. The Migne edition, op. cit., 1,091, mentions Gen 3:7-8 here as an expression of shame for the sin committed.
9. Cyril alludes to the aforementioned expression of Paul, which is found in the important context of 2 Cor 3:4-18 on the difference between the ministry of the old Law and the new Covenant.

10. That is, "anointed." Cf. Lev 4,5: «The priest anointed...». What is attempted here (as, in general, when explaining the name "Christ", Greek version of the Hebrew "Messiah", anointed) is that if Christ is the anointed of God, then also the Christian, anointed in turn as Jesus, the Christ, thus participates in the anointing of the Spirit.
11. Cf. supra, cat. 17, no. 37, on the interior action of the Holy Spirit.
12. Cf. supra, no. 2.

13. In the context of 25:7 LXX, God's project is to pour out his anointing on all nations. This recalls, on the other hand, Acts 2:16 ff. CATECHESIS XXII (MISTAGOGICAL IV) THE BODY AND BLOOD OF THE LORD About the body and blood of the Lord. The reading is from Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians: «I received from the Lord what I transmitted to you (I Cor11,23), etc.1. Institution of the Eucharist

1. Even this single teaching of Paul would be sufficient to give you certain faith in the divine mysteries. Of them you have been considered worthy and made partakers of the body and blood of the Lord. It is said of him that "on the night in which he was betrayed" (I Cor 11:23), our Lord Jesus Christ "took bread, and after giving thanks, he broke it" (1 Cor 11:23-24) "and, giving it to his disciples, he said: "Take, eat, this is my body." Then he took a cup and, giving thanks, gave it to them saying: "Drink of it, all of you, for this is my blood"» (Mt 26,26-28). So, if he is the one who exclaimed and said about the bread: "This is my body," who will later dare to doubt? And if he is the one who has affirmed and said: "This is my blood," who can ever doubt saying that it is not his blood? Faith in the body and blood of the Lord

2. On one occasion, in Cana of Galilee, he changed water into wine (Jn 2:1-10), which is related to blood. And now we will believe that he is not worthy of faith by changing wine into blood? Invited to a human wedding, he performed that admirable prodigy. Shall we not confess much more that he gave his own body and blood to the children of the nuptial bed for their enjoyment? 2. Appearances of bread and wine, but reality of the body and blood of Christ

3. Therefore, let us take it, with full conviction, as the body and blood of Christ. For in the form of bread the body is given to you, and in the form of wine the blood is given to you, so that, by taking the body and blood of Christ, you may become a partaker of his own body and blood. Thus we become bearers of Christ, distributing his body and blood to our members. Thus, according to the blessed Peter, we become "partakers of the divine nature" (2 Pet 1:4). The “scandal” of the Bread of Life

4. On one occasion, Jesus arguing with the Jews, said: "Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you" (Jn 6:53). But since those did not understand what was being said in a spiritual sense, they withdrew offended (cf. 6:60) believing that he was inviting them to eat meat3. The Eucharist, bread of the new Alliance for human health

5. There were also, in the old Covenant, the shewbread; but, since they referred to an expired alliance, they had an end. But, in the new Covenant, the bread is heavenly and the drink healthy, and they sanctify the soul and the body. For, as bread is good for the body, so the Word4 is good for the soul. The certainty of the gift of the body and blood of Christ

6. Therefore you should not consider the bread and wine (of the Eucharist) as elements without greater significance. For, according to the Lord's affirmation, they are the body and blood of Christ. Although your senses already suggest it to you, faith gives you certainty and firmness. Do not gauge things by pleasure, but be assured by faith, beyond all doubt, that you have been graced with the gift of the body and blood of Christ. The table that the Lord has prepared

7. The force of all this is explained to you by the prophet David when he exclaims: "You prepare a table before me, before my enemies" (/Sal/022/023/05). Which means: before your coming, the demons had prepared for men a contaminated, very dirty table, which exudes the power of the devil. But once you came, Lord, “you have prepared a table before me.” And when man says to God: "you have prepared a table before me," what else does it mean than the mystical and intelligible table that God has prepared for us "in the face of enemies," the opposites, that is, in the face of demons? And so it is, in effect, because that table maintained communion with the demons, but this one maintains it with God. «You anoint my head with oil»5. He anointed your head with oil on your forehead through the seal6 that you have of God, so that God may sanctify you and make you an image of what the seal expresses7. "My cup overflows." It is the chalice that Jesus took in his hands and, giving thanks, said: "This is my blood..., which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins" (Mt 26:28). The new clothes of justice

8. BAU/WHITE-DRESS: For this reason Solomon, in Ecclesiastes, wanting to point out this grace, said: "Come, eat your bread with joy" (Eccl 9,7). Spiritual bread refers; He says “come,” because he calls to salvation and gives happiness. "And drink your wine willingly" (ibid.), which refers to spiritual wine. "And let there be no lack of ointment on your head" (Eccl 9,8b): Do you see how the spiritual chrism is also designated this way? "In all seasons let your clothes be white,... for God is already pleased with your works" (ibid., 8a and 7b). Well, before you had access to grace, your works were "vanity of vanities" (Eccl 1,2)8. But, once you have taken off your old garments and put on those that are spiritually clean, you must always be dressed in these. We do not tell you that it is necessary that you always wear white, but that you clothe yourself in what is white, pure and spiritual and that you say, in accordance with the blessed Isaiah: "I will rejoice in Yahweh, my soul exults in my God, for he has clothed me with clothes of salvation, he has wrapped me in a mantle of righteousness..." (Is 61:10). Compendium on the body and blood of Christ

9. You can stay with the idea and have the most certain faith that what is seen as bread is not bread, although it tastes that way, but the body of Christ, and that what is seen as wine is not wine, although it tastes like that, but the blood of Christ. And do not forget what David said anciently in the Psalms: "... to bring out of the earth bread, and wine that refreshes the heart of man, so that he may polish his face with oil and the bread may comfort the heart of man" (Ps 104:14-15). Comfort your heart by taking that bread as spiritual and make the face of your soul happy. Covering it with the purity of your conscience and reflecting "as in a mirror the glory of the Lord", walk "in ever greater glory" (2 Cor 3:18) in Christ Jesus, our Lord, to whom be honor, power and glory forever and ever. Amen...
1. The topic is, therefore, the Eucharist, the third of the sacraments received in Christian initiation.

2. The expression "the children of the wedding chamber"—the translation could also be, strictly speaking, "the servants"—would be reminiscent, for example, of Mt 9:15: "Can the guests at the wedding become sad while the bridegroom is with them? “Days will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them, then they will fast.” It is precisely in the absence of the bridegroom or the "Husband", as the Song of Songs has so poetically expressed, when his friends and his guests, by "fasting" for the absence, nevertheless feed on the body and blood of Christ, announcing "the death of the Lord, until he comes" (I Cor 11:26). That is, the body and blood of Jesus are the Christian's food while awaiting the definitive coming of the Lord.

3. Cf. Jn 6,61-62.67. Peter's confession in the face of Jesus' rejection by "the Jews" (Jn 6:67 ff.) occupies a place in the Gospel of John similar to that of the confession, also by Peter and on behalf of the other apostles, in Mt 16:16 par. That is to say, to the extent that Jesus reveals the mystery of his person and his mission (destined for the cross in the Synoptics, Mt 16:21 ff.; given to men as the true bread of life according to Jn 6:26-66), he is only accepted by those who have been prepared by the same contact with him. Regarding the Eucharist, it can, therefore, be said that only those who have been previously instructed and disposed by the Word of preaching and contact with the God of Jesus can accept it as the living presence of the Passover of Jesus Christ the Savior. Therefore, after Christian initiation, it is a good time for a catechesis that "leads to the mystery" ("mystagogical" catechesis) of the Eucharist. The topic of the Eucharist, due to the possibility of scandal similar to that of the Jews in Jn 6, fell within the so-called "secret" or "discipline of the arcane" in the ancient Church.
4. "The Word" or "the Word", referring to the Word that is Christ.
5. Ps 23:5, of which the first half has already been quoted, says in full: «You prepare a table before me, before my enemies; "You anoint my head with oil, my cup is overflowing."
6. Cf. again what has already been said at various times about the "seal", "character", etc. (see above, Procatechesis, note 36).
7. Cf., speaking of the priest's diadem, Ex 28:36: «You will also make a sheet of pure gold and on it you will engrave as seals are engraved: "Consecrated to Yahweh"».

8. In a generic way, at the beginning of Ecclesiastes (or Cohelet, "the one of the assembly", from qahal, assembly; therefore, also "preacher"; "ecclesia" in Greek is assembly and "ecclesiastes" would be "the one in charge of the assembly" as "preacher") the Jerusalem Bible correctly points out about 1,2: "a) the determinism of the cosmos, a monotonous framework of human life, causes boredom in Ecclesiastes, contrary to the admiration and adoration expressed in Jb 38-40 or Ps 104. And more specifically about the famous expression "vanity of vanities", cited here by Cyril: «b) The term... first meant "vapor", "breath", and is part of the repertoire of images (water, shadow, smoke, etc.) that in Hebrew poetry describe human fragility. But the word has lost its concrete meaning and for Qo it only evokes the illusory nature of things and, consequently, the disappointment that they reserve for man. All this, in view of the situation of the newly baptized, makes us understand the "vanity of vanities" that are ultimately the works of man prior to baptism. CATECHESIS XXIII (MISTAGOGICAL V) THE CELEBRATION OF THE EUCHARIST From the First Letter of Peter: Reject, therefore, all malice and all deceit, hypocrisy, envy, etc. (I Pe 2,1 ff.). Transition1

1. In the previous assemblies they heard abundantly spoken, by the gift of God, of both baptism and chrismation and the taking of the body and blood of Christ. But we must now move on to what follows, by which we will put an end to the edifice of your spiritual teaching. The washing of hands, a sign of immunity from sin

2. They saw how the deacon brought the water to the priest and the presbyters who were around the altar to wash his hands. But in no way did he do it to clean bodily dirt. I say that that was not the reason, because at the beginning we did not come to Church because we had spots on our bodies. However, this ablution of the hands is a symbol that they must be cleansed from all sins and prevarications. And since the hands are symbols of action, by washing them, we signify the purity of the works and the fact that they are free from all rebuke. Have you not heard the blessed David clarifying this mystery for us and saying: "I wash my hands in innocence and walk around your altar, Lord" (Ps 26:6)? Therefore, washing your hands is a sign of immunity from sin. The kiss of peace2

3. Then the deacon exclaims: "Let us speak, and kiss each other." And do not think that this kiss is of the same kind as those that mutual friends give each other in the public square. This kiss is not that kind. For it reconciles and unites some souls with others, and guarantees them total oblivion of injuries. It is a sign, therefore, that souls merge with each other and that Catechesis exposes the different rites of the celebration of the Eucharist, after the liturgy of the Word has finished. The uninterrupted continuity is observed in the essentials and in many details of the rites if this text by Cyril is compared with older traditions, starting with the same relationship of I Cor 11,17 ff., spec. 23 ff., and continuing through the testimonies, among many others, of the Didache, Justin, Hippolytus of Rome, the Apostolic Constitutions, in addition to the numerous forms of the various Churches. In the liturgy of the Eucharist described here, the embrace of peace is held before entering into the proclamation of the anaphora. The timely express mention of Mt 5:23-24 confirms the meaning of this placement of the embrace of peace: the mutual kiss of peace expresses the reconciliation between those present in the celebration of the Eucharist before the common thanksgiving that is the Eucharistic prayer. They put down any memory of the offenses. That is why Christ said: «If, then, when you present your offering at the altar, you remember that a brother of yours has something against you, leave your offering there, in front of the altar, and go first to be reconciled to your brother; then you return and present your offering” (Mt 5:23-24). Therefore, the kiss is reconciliation and, therefore, it is holy, as the blessed Paul says somewhere: "Greet one another with the holy kiss" (I Cor 16:20); and Peter: "Greet one another with the kiss of love" (I Pet 5:14). Initial invocations at the beginning of the anaphora

4. Then the priest exclaims: "Hearts up." Well, truly, at this transcendental moment, it is appropriate to raise our hearts towards God and not direct them towards earth and earthly affairs. It is, therefore, the same as if the priest ordered everyone to put aside at that moment the worries of this life and the cares of this world, and to raise their hearts to heaven towards the merciful God. Then you respond: "We have it (raised) towards the Lord," with which you assent to the indication by the confession you pronounce. Let no one who is there, when he says: "We have it towards the Lord," have his mind filled with the worries of this life. Well, we must remember God at all times. But if, due to human weakness, it becomes impossible, at least at that moment one must try as hard as one can. It is right, on our part, to give thanks to the Lord

5. After this the priest says: "Let us give thanks to the Lord." For we must be truly grateful that when we were unworthy, he called us to such immense grace, and that, when we were enemies, he reconciled us (cf. Rom 5:10) and granted us the Spirit of adoption (Rom 8:15). Your answer is: “It is worthy and just”33. For, when we give thanks, we do something worthy and just, although he, without strictly following what is just, but going beyond it, did us good and made us worthy of such great goods. The beginning of the anaphora and the «Saint»

6. We then mention the sky, the earth and the sea; of the sun and the moon, of the stars and of every creature, endowed with reason or without reason, visible or invisible; of the angels, of the archangels, of the virtues, dominions, principalities, powers and thrones; of the cherubs endowed with many faces4; all saying that of David: "Sing with me to the Lord" (Ps 34:4). We also mention the seraphim that, in the Holy Spirit, Isaiah saw around the throne of God and that covered his face with two wings, his feet with two wings, and with two they flew saying: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts" (Is 6:2-3). Let us recite, therefore, this theology5, so that, in the communal intonation of praise, we may join the armies that are above the universe. The epiclesis or invocation of the descent of the Holy Spirit on the gifts of the altar

7. Next, after sanctifying ourselves through these spiritual praises6, we beseech the merciful God to send the Holy Spirit upon the gifts presented7, to convert the bread into the body of Christ and the wine into the blood of Christ. For what has been reached by the Holy Spirit will have been sanctified and changed. We pray for all who need it

8. But after the spiritual sacrifice, bloodless worship, has been performed on that host of propitiation, we pray to God for the peace of all the Churches, for the good government of the world, for the authorities, for the soldiers, for the friends, for those who are subject to illness, for those who are prey to affliction and, in general, we pray and offer this victim for all who have any need. Also for the deceased

9. We also remember all those who have already slept: first of all, the patriarchs, the prophets, the apostles, the martyrs, so that, through their prayers and intercession, God may accept our prayers. Then, also for the deceased holy fathers and bishops and, in general, for all whose lives were spent among us, believing that this will be of the greatest help to those for whom one prays. Usefulness of prayer for the deceased

10. I want to clarify this with an example, since I have heard many say: what good does it do for a soul to leave this world with or without sins if later mention is made of it in prayer? Suppose, for example, that a king sends those who have offended him into exile, but then his relatives, afflicted with punishment, offer him a crown: Would he not thank them with a reduction in punishments? In the same way, we also present supplications to God for the dead, even if they are sinners. And we do not offer a crown, but we offer Christ dead for our sins, intending that the merciful God will have compassion and be merciful both to them and to us. The Our Father, between the Eucharistic prayer and communion

11. PATER/CIRILO-DE-J: And, after all this, we recite that prayer that the Savior gave to his own disciples, calling God Father with a pure conscience and saying: "Our Father who art in heaven" (Mt 6:9)8. Oh great mercy of God towards men!, together with his love. To such an extent did he feel compassion for those who separated from him and established themselves in the greatest evils that he granted them the oblivion of injuries and participation in grace so that they would call him Father: "Our Father who art in heaven." For from heaven they were to be those who bore the image of heaven9, in whom God dwells and with whom he walks410.

12. "Hallowed be your name." By its nature, God's name is holy, whether we say it or not. But since, through those who sin, it is sometimes profaned, according to that "the name of God, for your sake, is blasphemed among the nations" (Is 52:5, as quoted in Rom 2:24), we pray that the name of God may be sanctified in us. And it is not that it begins to be holy because it was not previously holy, but that it becomes holy in us when we sanctify ourselves and do things worthy of holiness.

13. “Your Kingdom come” (Mt 6:10). It is the nature of the pure soul to say with confidence: "Thy Kingdom come." For whoever has heard Paul, who says: "Let no sin reign in your mortal body" (Rom. 6:12), and is aware of his purity in works, thoughts and words, will cry out to God: "Your Kingdom come."

14. "Your Will be done on earth as it is in heaven." The blessed angels of God do his will, as David said in the Psalms: "Bless Yahweh, his angels, mighty heroes, executors of his orders, as soon as you hear the voice of his word" (Ps 103:20)11. Your prayer, therefore, has this force and this significance, as if you said: "As your will is done in the angels, so be it done, Lord, on earth upon me."

15. “Give us today our necessary bread” (Mt 6:11)12, Ordinary bread is not substantial. But this bread, which is holy, is substantial, as if you were to say that it is directed to the substance of the soul. This bread does not end up in the belly nor does it enter the defecation, but is distributed among your entire being for the benefit of the body and soul. The "today" is said for "every day." As Paul also said: "Every day while this day lasts" (Hebrews 3:13)13.

16. "Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors" (Mt 6:12). We really have many sins, since we cause offenses with word and thought and do many things, deserving of condemnation. And "if we say, 'We have no sin,' we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us," as John says (1 Jn 1:8). We therefore make a covenant with God, praying that he forgive us our sins, as we also forgive our neighbors their debts. Weighing, therefore, what we receive in return, let us not hesitate or hesitate to forgive mutual offenses. The offenses that are done to us are small, light and easy to forget. But those we commit against God are great and can only be erased with the help of his sole kindness. Beware, therefore, that, for small things and nothingness directed at you, you exclude yourself from the forgiveness of sins before God.

17. "And do not lead us into temptation (Mt 6:13), Lord." Does the Lord teach us to ask that we not be tempted at all? And how is it that in another place it is said: "He who has not undergone trials knows little" (Sir 34:10)14, and also: "Consider it a great joy, my brothers, to be surrounded by all kinds of trials." But doesn't entering into temptation mean sinking into it? For temptation is something similar to a torrent that is difficult to cross. But, those who are not swallowed by temptation, go through it like skilled swimmers without being dragged by anything. But those who are not like that, sink as soon as they enter. This was, to give an example, Judas. Entering into the temptation of greed, he did not swim but sank, and drowned in body and spirit. Peter entered into the temptation of denial, but, despite having entered, he did not sink, but, crying intensely, he was delivered from the temptation. He also hears, for his part, the choir of the unscathed saints, who burst into thanksgiving upon being delivered from temptation: “You have tested us, O God, you have purged us, as silver is purged; You caught us in the net, you put a strap on our backs, you let someone ride at our head, we passed through fire and water; but then you brought us out to gain breath” (Ps 66:10-12). Don't you see the confident joy of those who have passed without having sunk? "But then, it is added, you took us out to catch our breath." That they gained breath means that they were freed from temptation15.

18. "But deliver us from the evil one." If "lead us not into temptation" meant not to be tempted in any way, he would not have added "but deliver us from the evil one"16. The evil one is the devil as an adversary from whom we ask to be liberated. And then, after finishing the prayer, you say: "Amen." By this "Amen", which means "so be it", you endorse and confirm what is contained in this prayer that God has given us. "Holy things to the saints." Invitation to communion

19. After all this the priest says: "Holy things to the saints"17. Holy are the things that are on the altar, since the Holy Spirit has come upon them. You too are holy, enriched by the gift of the Holy Spirit. And holy things are good for saints. You, furthermore, add: "There is only one saint and one Lord Jesus Christ." For really only one is holy, holy by nature; But we too are saints, but not by nature, but by participation and by the practice of works and desire. The communion of the body and blood of the Lord

20. Then you heard the voice of the psalmist who invited them, by means of a certain divine melody, to the communion of the holy mysteries and said: "Taste and see how good the Lord is" (Ps 34:9)18. But do not judge or appreciate this as a human meal: I mean, not like this, but from faith and free from all doubt. For those who taste them are not commanded to taste bread and wine, but rather what they represent in an image, but in a real way: the body and blood of the Lord. The communion of the body of Christ

21. Do not approach, therefore, with the palms of your hands extended or with your fingers separated, but, placing your left hand under your right like a throne that will receive the King, receive the body of Christ in the hollow of your hand, saying: "Amen." Add it then with eyes of holiness, taking care that nothing is lost from it. For whatever falls from you, consider it taken from your own members. Well, tell me, if someone had given you gold filings, wouldn't you take them with great care and diligence, taking care that nothing was lost and you were harmed? Will you not try with much more care and vigilance that you do not drop even a crumb, which is much more valuable than gold and precious stones? The communion of the blood of Christ

22. And after the communion of the body of Christ, also approach the cup of blood: without extending your hands, but bowing forward, thus expressing adoration and veneration, while saying "Amen", you will be sanctified by also taking the blood of Christ. And when your lips are still wet, touching them with your hands, sanctify your eyes and your forehead and the other senses. Finally, in expectant prayer, give thanks to God, who has allowed you to become a participant in such great mysteries.

23. Keep these traditions intact, and keep yourselves blameless. Do not separate them from communion or defile these sacred and spiritual mysteries with their sins. "May he, the God of peace, sanctify you completely, and may your whole being, spirit, soul and body, be preserved blameless until the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ" (1 Thes 5:23), to whom be glory, honor and dominion with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and forever and forever and ever. Amen...
